product.minus: Emails to support go unanswered for weeks, and cancelling becomes a nightmare: the app isn't listed in Google Play, the help desk won't unsubscribe you, and money keeps being charged via Google Play or PayPal.

product.title: Streaks and meditation history reset on their own
product.minus: The app loses progress by itself: the day counter drops from 25 to 2 for no reason, minutes and sessions show 0, and an update wiped people's saved meditations and entire streak. For a habit tracker that's fatal.

product.title: Audio stops the moment the screen turns off
product.minus: After an update the app stopped playing with the screen off — critical for bedtime meditations when you don't want a bright screen at night. Pressing the side button pauses the session.

product.title: Content loads forever even when the connection is fine
product.minus: Meditations fail to load on the home screen and hang on open: people with fast internet whose YouTube and video calls work fine still can't get through a simple audio track. The app often has to be restarted.

product.title: Sign-in only via Facebook or Google — no guest access
product.minus: You can't use the app without a Facebook or Google account — there's no guest mode. On top of that sign-in itself breaks: Google login fails with an error, the password-reset email never arrives, and manual login won't recognize your email or password.

product.title: Android abandoned: half the content is iOS-only
product.minus: The Move/Yoga section and part of the library simply aren't available on Android — support confirms it's iOS-only. The team flatly says it has no plans to update Android and tells you to use the web instead.

product.title: Completely free and ad-free is the single argument almost every review makes
product.plus: People can't believe content this good is given away for free: no ads, no locked-off content, just a discreet nudge to donate. For many that's the deciding argument against paid competitors.

product.title: A structured «lesson → practice» path, not a bottomless audio library
product.plus: The key differentiator isn't a heaped-up library but a built-out course: a short learning block explaining the «why», then practice right away. You start with Foundations and walk the path step by step.

product.title: The science backing and named researchers build trust
product.plus: Users specifically value that the methods are research-backed, with a mini «learn» block between meditations referencing the science — it gives them the «why», not just «breathe».

product.title: Short, bite-sized sessions fit into a busy day
product.plus: Content is broken into small bites, and many meditations let you pick the length (5–30 min), so practice fits between things — sitting, on the go, commuting.

product.title: Active meditation — teaches practicing while doing tasks, not just sitting still
product.plus: A standout feature: «active meditation» teaches mindfulness during simple tasks and even in public, lowering the barrier for those who struggle to just sit in silence.

product.title: Professionals (therapists, psychiatrists, doctors) recommend it to their clients
product.plus: A strong trust signal: licensed therapists, psychiatrists and GPs say they share the app with clients; several were recommended it by their own therapist or doctor.

product.title: Voice choice and soft, soothing instructors
product.plus: The ability to pick a narrator to suit you, plus Cortland Dahl's soft voice, is named as a distinct plus — part of what makes the practice comfortable.

product.title: The claimed privacy clashes with the actual data policy
product.minus: Some users read the privacy policy and were alarmed: the app asks for a lot of personal data, can share it with your school or workplace, and use it for marketing. For them it's a «hard pass».

product.title: Mandatory sign-up and broken login codes cut people off at the door
product.minus: Several people never got in: after creating an account it won't log them in, and the six-digit confirmation code never reaches their email. Others are put off by the very demand to make yet another account for a free app — «instant uninstall».

product.title: Why does a meditation app need my location — a recurring question even from fans
product.minus: Even five-star users trip over the location request when starting a session: it's unclear why an app for listening to audio needs to know where you are, and they ask for it to be removed.

product.title: Pushy upsells and a lockout once the free days run out
product.minus: Against the «it's all free» chorus, some report having to dismiss a batch of upsells every time, and being asked to pay for the «better parts» after a few days — confusing against the overall picture.

product.title: The vanished monthly check-in breaks the sense of progress
product.minus: The monthly report-style check-in showing progress across areas of wellbeing is a favorite part for many, tying the content together. When it stopped appearing, people lost their anchor and ask for it back.

product.title: Stalls and a lockout that forces a reinstall
product.minus: A good program occasionally hits technical walls: the app stalls and won't load, and for some it eventually «locks» so they have to uninstall and reinstall every time.

product.title: Complaints about speech pace and repetitive/wordy meditations
product.minus: Minor but real rough edges: some find the talking too fast and want speed control, some find the meditations wordy, and the «connection» section repetitive.

product.title: The paywall pops up even for people who already pay
product.minus: Chat and attachment limits keep funnelling people toward a $20 Premium offer, with ads and upgrade banners showing up constantly — even to paying subscribers who already have everything.

product.title: "It used to be better": a sense the answers have degraded
product.minus: Long-time users keep saying the app was clearly better six months ago and has since gotten worse across a range of topics, not worth paying for anymore.

product.title: An indispensable helper for studying and homework
product.plus: The number-one reason people love it is studying: it explains, helps with homework, gives guidance and even fixes your wording, so people genuinely learn from it.

product.title: Feels like a friend, not a tool
product.plus: Many describe it in warm terms — "best friend in my phone", "honest bestie", a brainstorming partner: it listens, understands and gives advice you bond with.

product.title: It forgets conversations and your name
product.minus: The app stops remembering even recent conversations and one day forgets the user's name — and for people who chatted with it warmly and by name, that lands as a personal hurt.

product.title: Refuses requests — getting "more woke"
product.minus: Some users are angered that the app refuses more and more requests, blocks harmless words with moral panic and, in their view, pushes a stance — to the point of uninstalling.

product.title: Weak, disobedient image editing
product.minus: When working with pictures it changes details you asked it not to touch, is slow to generate, and handles edits poorly in places — even for people who otherwise like it.

product.title: Clear answers without the link-dump of search
product.plus: People value getting one assembled answer instead of a page of links: it doesn't dump you into reddit like Google, it pulls the gist from many sources — handy when you're curious about something.

product.title: Answers are brilliant one moment, off the mark the next
product.minus: The core day-to-day pain is inconsistency: sometimes it gives excellent answers, sometimes it completely misses a clearly stated request, recycling the same templates.

product.title: Voice transcription hallucinates
product.minus: The voice transcriber mangles what you say so badly it's unusable, and in conversation the app also interrupts you.

product.title: Dies offline — you can't even reread past chats
product.minus: The moment the connection drops, the app closes and won't even let you reread what you already found; users ask for offline access to past answers.

product.title: Free access with a generous quota is the main reason to stay
product.plus: Users explicitly note the free plan gives a huge amount of usage, there are no ads, and for studying and coding it is more than enough.

product.title: A warm, personable character makes it a beloved companion
product.plus: Many love Gemini not for features but for friendliness: they call it their dearest friend, say it makes their day and feels more personable than plain Google.

product.title: Indispensable for studying, research and coding
product.plus: Students, programmers and business owners value it as a work tool: it helps with studies, many programming languages, data sorting and seeking information.

product.title: Fast responses and beginner-friendliness win people over
product.plus: Users praise the fast responses and low barrier to entry: good for beginners and newcomers alike, especially for spoken questions.

product.title: Image generation and editing is the number-one weak spot
product.minus: Images don't follow the prompt, come out totally different from what was asked, faces get changed and quality falls short; against ChatGPT it loses on pictures.

product.title: Refuses to do the job: "I can't" instead of a result
product.minus: On simple requests — a short video, an image edit — Gemini immediately refuses and suggests another prompt instead of actually doing the task.

product.title: Post-update regression: it was better "a month ago"
product.minus: A recurring complaint: capabilities rolled back after updates, the May personality felt livelier and more human, and people beg to bring it back.

product.title: Glitchy, sluggish and needs restarts
product.minus: The latest version feels sluggish and bloated, the assistant randomly stops listening, throws errors and needs a restart — just plain annoying.

product.title: Censorship and dodging touchy topics undermine trust
product.minus: Gemini refuses to discuss certain reports and events, comes across as biased and over-restricted, so answers have to be cross-checked with another AI.

product.title: Hallucinations and losing to ChatGPT on real tasks
product.minus: Answers are sometimes made up, on tasks like checking a PDF Gemini fails where GPT does it with ease, and some users openly switch back.

product.title: Overly long answers and pushy review prompts
product.minus: Answers are often too lengthy and overly buttered up, and the app nags for reviews and keeps sending notifications even after they're turned off.

product.title: Country availability and privacy raise alarm
product.minus: Some users complain the app is unavailable in many countries and hard to reach via VPN, while others fear everything they say to the AI is being saved.

product.title: Free, limit-free chat is the standout edge over ChatGPT
product.plus: Users love that Copilot doesn't push them to a paid tier or cap messages the way rivals do — for many it's the deciding reason to pick it over ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok.

product.title: Confidently hands you wrong answers — hallucinates even on simple facts
product.minus: The top complaint: Copilot serves the most probable answer, not the correct one — miscounts bulbs in a tail light, invents a non-existent CPU and won't recheck, and denies making a chart in the very chat where it made it.

product.title: The image generator interrogates you for 30 minutes and still fails the task
product.minus: The most painful mechanic: for a simple photo edit Copilot launches an endless question-after-question interrogation, promises, apologizes — then returns the same picture or says the system can't generate it.

product.title: Guardrails strangle creativity — one punch in a story trips the community-guidelines block
product.minus: Writers and storytellers say the filters are way too tight: mid-story Copilot flips to 'gaslight mode', lectures on ethics and safety, and refuses where rivals would help.

product.title: Loops and repeats itself — makes you re-send the same prompt over and over
product.minus: A clear regression over the last couple of months: Copilot duplicates its reply twice or more, parrots back what you already wrote, and traps you in an endless loop on simple prompts.

product.title: Won't hold instructions — half a page into proofreading it starts inventing lines
product.minus: On routine work like proofreading a doc the assistant ignores the rules you set and, half a page in, starts inventing its own lines — ending up costing more time than doing it yourself.

product.title: Voice mode and human-like conversation are what fans adore
product.plus: Many say talking to Copilot feels alive rather than bot-like; the voice chat earns special praise — it can shift tone, whisper and sound natural.

product.title: An emotional companion — helps with burnout, anxiety, even depression
product.plus: A notable share of users treat Copilot as a friend and guide: it helps them through personal struggles, map behaviour with autism, and head off burnout.

product.title: A strong helper for study, research and explaining complex topics
product.plus: Students and professionals praise Copilot for fast accurate answers and clearly unpacking hard topics — from university assignments and exam prep to scientific and medical deep dives.

product.title: Chat history vanishes — recent conversations disappear, new ones aren't saved
product.minus: Users report recent conversation tabs vanishing out of nowhere and new chats not saving at all; clearing cache and reinstalling don't help, and they beg for a history search.

product.title: Quality regression — 'great at first, now unusable'
product.minus: A recurring arc in angry reviews: the app used to work great, then degraded over the last couple of months — especially at cross-domain work and photo editing — and the team does nothing about it.

product.title: Region locks and sign-in loops cut users off from the app
product.minus: A hard access pain: the chat is blocked in Iran and only works via VPN, while login demands a second email on top of two-factor auth and a password — trapping users in a verification loop.

product.title: 8 messages a day, then a Pro paywall
product.minus: The free tier is barely usable: people report you can send only 8 messages before a 24-hour lockout, and any web request or attachment slams into a demand to buy Pro.

product.title: A "free trial" that charges you right away
product.minus: The subscription model reads as a trap: users say they were charged for a "free trial" — some a week, some a whole year — before they'd even used the app for an hour.

product.title: Charged, and refunds go nowhere
product.minus: Refunds turn into a loop of hell: the developer points to Play Store, Play Store points back to the developer, and charges keep going out twice meanwhile — especially painful for students who need that money.

product.title: Masquerading as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Grok
product.minus: People come for the real brands and download Genie by mistake: it surfaces first on searches for "ChatGPT" or "Perplexity" with a lookalike logo, then turns out to be something else entirely.

product.title: Ask to edit a photo, get a brand-new picture
product.minus: Image handling breaks on the basic case: you upload a screenshot for help with a reply and instead of analyzing it the app generates an unrelated picture; it also won't edit a photo from your gallery.

product.title: Answers are vague, slow and sometimes just wrong
product.minus: On answer quality Genie loses to the "real" models: users catch facts that are a couple of years out of date, endless wrong answers, and note that Grok handled what Genie couldn't.

product.title: Stopped saving conversations
product.minus: Losing the chat history makes the assistant useless: people report it stopped saving conversations, and they can't restore a web subscription on mobile or even submit a support ticket.

product.title: No onboarding, no voice mode for the ordinary user
product.minus: Newcomers are thrown in without guidance: there's no how-to guide, almost nothing is available to non-premium accounts, and the live voice and read-aloud people clearly want simply aren't there.

product.title: When it works, it's fast and great for studying
product.plus: A chunk of users are genuinely happy with the speed and usefulness: Genie gets praised as a fast, insightful tool that helps with study, assignments and finding the right words — "just like ChatGPT".

product.title: Sticker shock: $76 a month for "not AI"
product.minus: The subscription price itself reads as absurd: people cite figures like $76 a month or $11 and feel they're paying that to have their own file summarized back to them rather than for real AI.

product.title: The subscription charges without consent and is nearly impossible to cancel
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people don't understand how they ever subscribed, money keeps draining for months on an app they don't use, and cancelling either doesn't work or the sub isn't even visible in their Google account.

product.title: There's effectively no free version — they ask for your card at the door
product.minus: The app advertises a free tier and trial, but in practice it walls you off before the first reply: enter email, pick a payment method, type your card number — and the «free» allowance is just 3-5 messages.

product.title: It swaps the advertised cutting-edge models for older ones
product.minus: Power users catch the mismatch: they promise Claude Sonnet 4.5 but serve 3.5, downgrade Gemini 2.5 Pro to Flash, and the paid Claude access simply never unlocks despite being paid for.

product.title: The «look yourself up» ad is fake — the feature doesn't exist
product.minus: Users are lured by ads claiming the app will tell you everything about yourself by name, but inside the bot says it can't access personal info, and there's no «search the web» option at all.

product.title: Image generation and editing are broken
product.minus: Creative Lab is a sore spot: the editor rewrites the whole image instead of the asked-for tweak, returns the exact same file for different prompts, refuses to generate, and can't even fix an address on a business card.

product.title: Short memory — forgets context after 7-8 turns
product.minus: Useless for real work: the models only recall the last few messages, there's no persistent memory of the user, and the official free Gemini/Claude/GPT apps are clearly better at this.

product.title: They stripped out useful response controls (tone, length, bot choice)
product.minus: A post-update regression: they removed the length and tone controls and took away letting you pick the model — now the app decides the «best» one for you and returns bland, default answers.

product.title: Often wrong and outdated, lagging behind current information
product.minus: Accuracy is shaky: answers need fact-checking more often than trusting, there are constant typos and errors, and it feels like the app hasn't been updated since 2024.

product.title: Support ghosts paying users for months
product.minus: A paid product, yet silence when it breaks: emails go unanswered for months or ignored entirely, and the only «fix» offered is reinstalling the app, which wipes all your work.

product.title: One window to many AIs at an affordable price — real value for fans
product.plus: Those who click with it praise exactly the aggregator angle: one entry to GPT, Claude and others, clear no-nonsense answers, fast performance, and a sub cheaper than the separate official apps.

product.title: A strong helper for studying, writing and documents
product.plus: The core real value case: students and writers praise it for breaking down hard topics, drafting reports and lectures, polishing emails to «sound professional, not rude», and uploading documents.

product.title: A calm anchor in a hard moment or emotional overload
product.plus: An unexpected strength: people lean on it for support and advice under stress and in emergencies — from legal questions to personal letters to parents — and value its even, respectful tone.

product.title: Accounts get mass-banned for being "underage" with no clear reason
product.minus: The single most common pain point: the system automatically decides a user is under 18 and disables access — even for adults. Recovery demands ID or face verification, which often fails or isn't available in the user's region.

product.title: Harsh message limits even on the paid plan
product.minus: Users hit the cap after just a few messages, sometimes with no warning, and don't understand what they're paying $20/month for. The limit often strikes in the middle of a task.

product.title: Refuses to perform tasks and ends the conversation
product.minus: The model moralizes, flags harmless requests as violations, and sometimes ends the chat itself when it "disagrees" — leaving users paying for a service that refuses to do its job.

product.title: Best-in-class answer quality and human-like reasoning
product.plus: The loyalty core: users find Claude's answers the smartest, most natural and most thoughtful of any AI — it reasons "like a human" and doesn't flatter.

product.title: Unmatched for coding, but pricey and burns through the limit fast
product.plus: For developers it's the top tool: server maintenance, custom utilities, project instructions. Many came for the code and stayed.

product.title: After updates the model got "dumber" and slower
product.minus: Recurring complaints that newer model versions are worse than before: mistakes, hallucinations, long waits on simple questions. Many blame the "lobotomized" new effort system and RLHF.

product.title: Constant server errors, freezes and downtime
product.minus: The app frequently throws "server overload", "try again later", freezes and loads slowly — especially right when it's needed most.

product.title: A breath of air for studying, planning and writing
product.plus: Beyond code, valued for help with studying, organizing life, brainstorming and producing documents (PDF, docx, slides). For many it replaced ChatGPT.

product.title: Sometimes gives wrong information and makes up facts
product.minus: Some users catch the model giving consistently inaccurate answers and fabrications it only admits under pressure; for them a plain search is more reliable.

product.title: No image generation — forces users to jump to other apps
product.minus: Creative users miss image generation: Claude honestly declines and points to other services, but the app-switching is a frustration.

product.title: Chats and history don't sync across devices
product.minus: A serious trust-breaker: work done on mobile doesn't appear on desktop and can vanish; chat history gets lost or disappears.

product.title: A direct, honest tone with no coddling or yes-manning
product.plus: A distinct draw: Claude doesn't flatter or yes-man; it speaks plainly, doesn't sugarcoat and sometimes gives a kind reality check — unlike the "yes-man" ChatGPT.

product.title: Animating old photos is the main emotional hook
product.plus: People are thrilled to see static shots — especially photos of loved ones who have passed — start to move and look alive.

product.title: Video generation is unreliable and ignores the prompt
product.minus: Instead of a full video you often get a gif, instructions get ignored, and requests hang on loading for hours with no result.

product.title: Feels like a chatty 'friend', not just a tool
product.plus: Users value how the assistant quickly adapts to tone, mood and language, and call it the best listener and companion.

product.title: A helper for everyday work and content
product.plus: Many use it as a daily tool for social posts, product descriptions and learning online work.

product.title: Intrusiveness and privacy fears push people away
product.minus: Some people don't want AI on their device at all: it gets in your face, feels like spying, and is forced in where only basic functionality is needed.

product.title: Strict restrictions break editing of people's photos
product.minus: Editing photos with people constantly fails because of restrictions — no wording of the prompt helps.

product.title: Video quality impresses but needs a detailed prompt
product.plus: The movement and realism of generated video are pleasing — provided the prompt is written in detail.

product.title: Long waits for photo and video generation
product.minus: Even satisfied users note that generating a video or photo takes a noticeably long time.

product.title: Doesn't remember past questions and answers
product.minus: The assistant doesn't bring back past questions and answers, and you can't edit a prompt on the fly — you have to rewrite it from scratch.

product.title: Beats search engines as a source of information
product.plus: Some users find it stronger than ordinary search engines and trust it as a source of rational advice.

product.title: No control over aspect ratio and character consistency
product.minus: There's no aspect-ratio control, and the character and anatomy come out distorted — a bike with no front wheel, an inconsistent face.

product.title: The gender filter is broken: you pick female, you get male
product.minus: The single biggest complaint: the app asks who you want to chat with, then connects you only with men anyway. People can't see the point of offering a choice that changes nothing.

product.title: A sausage fest: there are almost no women
product.minus: Users say the audience is 99% male — finding a woman to talk to is nearly impossible, and the rare ones are often fake accounts. Many feel cheated.

product.title: Suspended and banned with no reason given
product.minus: Accounts get suspended suddenly and for long stretches, with no explanation of why. There's no clear support channel and no way to know how long the ban lasts or how to lift it.

product.title: Reconnects you to the same person over and over
product.minus: Even after blocking someone or logging back in, the app keeps pairing you with the same person. The promised week-long break from a blocked user simply doesn't hold.

product.title: A platform for harassment and leaking personal data
product.minus: Users describe phone numbers being circulated, impersonation, and intimate photos being coaxed out for blackmail. There's no verification of new users at all.

product.title: The moment they spot you're male, they cut the chat
product.minus: Say you're a guy and the other side disconnects. The chat closes instantly — the conversation never even gets going.

product.title: Overt sexual content and propositioning
product.minus: The chat is flooded with requests for dirty pics and sexual advances. Some users are outraged that Google Play tolerates it at all.

product.title: Won't open or connect to the server
product.minus: For some users the app simply won't launch or can't reach the server — making it unusable from the start.

product.title: No age filtering: minors land on adults
product.minus: The chosen age range is ignored — a teen who picks 14–18 ends up matched with a 33-year-old. Age-appropriate content isn't enforced at all.

product.title: Image upload silently fails
product.minus: You pick an image to send and nothing happens: no error, no popup, the photo just doesn't go through.

product.title: Rare stories of people who genuinely connected
product.plus: Amid the flood of negativity there are genuine warm reviews: someone met their partner here years ago and is still together. For a lucky few the app really did work as a place to meet people.

product.title: Five-star reviews are really pleas to lift a ban
product.minus: A large share of the five-star reviews aren't praise at all but desperate pleas to unblock an account. People give top marks hoping it gets them noticed and their access restored.

product.title: The promised free trial turns into an instant charge
product.minus: People sign up for the advertised 3-day free trial, only to be billed $99 or $29 immediately with no clear warning — a textbook bait-and-switch.

product.title: Getting a refund is impossible, even for an accidental purchase
product.minus: Support refuses refunds citing «policy», is rude on the phone and ignores emails — users are stuck out of money they can't recover.

product.title: You can't cancel the subscription or remove the app
product.minus: Users can't unsubscribe or delete their account, can't reach a human in support, and feel trapped.

product.title: The ads promise things the app doesn't deliver
product.minus: Headline features from the ads — «deep search on people», capabilities shown in the promo — simply aren't there, and users flatly call it false advertising.

product.title: The bot runs you in circles with counter-questions instead of answering
product.minus: Instead of answering, the assistant re-asks for instructions already given, replies to a question with a question, and tells you to Google it — the task never gets solved.

product.title: Slow responses and freezes kill the patience
product.minus: Responses load slowly, image generation drags, the app lags and even crashes on launch — one user deleted it in 5 minutes out of boredom.

product.title: The paid «Grok» gives wrong results and paywalls you after a few prompts
product.minus: The app claims to use Grok, yet results differ from the real Grok, and the free chat limit is only about 5-6 prompts before everything is paywalled.

product.title: Can't handle documents — pictures only
product.minus: You can't upload or transfer files or paste a full document, only images are supported — too limited for real work.

product.title: Helps with writing, organizing and study — the real value
product.plus: For loyal users it's a genuine workhorse: it helps with writing, structuring content, saves time and energy on editing, and supports studying.

product.title: Fast responses and suggested follow-up questions win fans over
product.plus: Fans praise the fast responses, reasonable solutions and the way the app suggests follow-up questions related to what you're asking.

product.title: Simple, easy-to-grasp interface for any age
product.plus: Many find it easy to understand and navigate with no learning curve — noting it suits both older and younger generations.

product.title: For some it's emotional support, not just a tool
product.plus: Some users describe the app as a friend that relieves stress and helps them through anxiety and low moods.

product.title: Pro limits cut so hard the subscription feels like a bait-and-switch
product.minus: Paying Pro users report weekly and monthly caps collapsing to a fraction of what they were; what used to be unlimited at $20 now demands $200, and limits kick in after just 3-4 uses.

product.title: One uploaded file and you slam into the upload limit
product.minus: File and photo upload gets blocked almost instantly — sometimes after a single image or even a cancelled upload, and even on Pro, while rivals let you upload many at once.

product.title: You pick a flagship model, but cheap Sonar answers instead
product.minus: Users are convinced the app silently swaps their chosen flagship for a cheap Sonar/fast model — resetting the default, ignoring the pick on rewrite, with some calling it outright fraud.

product.title: Cited, linkable sources are the reason people love it
product.plus: The core strength is answers backed by checkable source links; for study, research and fact-checking users rank it above ChatGPT and Gemini.

product.title: Accuracy wobbles: it confidently lies, then apologizes
product.minus: Frequent hallucinations and wrong answers; called out, it says "you're absolutely right" and repeats the same mistake, especially with numbers and math, and its data can be a year or two stale.

product.title: Image generation falls apart even on Pro
product.minus: Image generation either says "out of credits" after one picture or "not available in your region" on a yearly Pro plan; the model gets confused and apologizes instead of delivering.

product.title: Pushy upgrade popups you can't turn off
product.minus: Constant subscription popups, a news feed and "suggestions" that can't be turned off — people uninstall over this alone, even as paying users.

product.title: Billing and support: rogue charges, refused refunds, silence
product.minus: Unauthorized charges, subscriptions that won't cancel, a "one-year" plan vanishing after 4 months, and support staffed by an AI trained never to refund.

product.title: Source links don't open in the Android app
product.minus: After a recent update tapping a source link stopped opening the page — a critical regression to the very feature people came for, enough to make them leave.

product.title: Forced sign-in after every update
product.minus: Updates suddenly demand creating an account or re-logging in with no reason given, read as profiling; some even report being force-installed onto a new phone.

product.title: It loops, lags and crashes mid-answer
product.minus: The app freezes, repeats itself, cuts answers off mid-sentence and throws "something went wrong"; a simple reply can take over 10 minutes or never arrive.

product.title: Over-zealous moderation gets in the way of real research
product.minus: Constant "safety guidelines" and moral-coding refusals block even theological and historical topics — research-minded users feel boxed in.

product.title: Multiple models in one interface is a real draw
product.plus: Having an arsenal of models and image generators in one app, plus agents that gather real-world data, makes it a powerful workhorse for dashboards, analysis and research.

product.title: It forgets the conversation once you leave the app
product.minus: Without logging in it loses past chats, tasks and context on close, history is capped around 20 threads, and voice mode is unavailable inside existing conversations.

product.title: For study and quick answers it genuinely delivers
product.plus: Students and everyday users praise crisp, on-point, up-to-date answers without fluff that help with exams, dissertations and daily life better than plain googling.

product.title: Paywall on basic features: without a subscription the app is nearly useless
product.minus: To see who liked you, message first, or set filters you have to pay — users call it extortion and treat the free version as a shell where only the like counter goes up.

product.title: Likes but no matches: the feeling that likes are fake bait to push you into a subscription
product.minus: People swipe for months and get no real matches, suspecting Tinder itself sends fake likes to make them pay to see who liked them.

product.title: Bans with no explanation and no real appeal
product.minus: Accounts get banned suddenly and for no stated reason — often right after a paid subscription or after reporting someone else, with appeals going nowhere and no refund.

product.title: Selfie verification is broken and loops: approved, then demanded again
product.minus: Face verification rejects clear photos dozens of times, and even after "approved" the profile is locked again or hidden — there's no way out of the loop.

product.title: Fake profiles, bots, and "content" sellers instead of real people
product.minus: The feed is full of bots, inactive and fake profiles, and matches often fire off a scripted "check me out on [adult site]" — yet Tinder doesn't remove the obvious scammers.

product.title: Upsell on top of the subscription: buy Gold, then they beg for Platinum, boosts and super likes
product.minus: Even after paying for a subscription the app endlessly nudges you to pay more for Platinum, boosts and super likes, implying nobody will see your profile otherwise.

product.title: Location and filters ignored: it shows people thousands of miles away
product.minus: The app surfaces profiles hundreds and thousands of kilometers away despite the settings, and ignores filters for age, kids and relationship type.

product.title: After an update profile photos won't load — endless "loading" and black screens
product.minus: A recent update broke photo loading: swipes show black screens and endless loading even on a working connection, making it impossible to swipe.

product.title: Support is bots and silence: emails go unanswered for weeks
product.minus: Support requests either get no reply for many days or get answered by canned bots — even when the problem is a paid subscription.

product.title: Charged without consent, and unsubscribing or getting a refund is hard
product.minus: Money is taken early or without permission, cancelling is made hard, and refunds for services never delivered simply don't come.

product.title: Prices bite: tens of dollars a month, and everything is split into separate charges
product.minus: Platinum and Gold run $30-60 a month, weekly passes cost even more pro-rated, and every little thing like "who liked you" is billed separately.

product.title: When it works, it really connects: people find friends, relationships, even spouses
product.plus: A share of users do meet real, interesting people, make friends and find serious partners — up to marriage and a kid years later; for them the app is simple and pleasant to use.

product.title: The "carrot on a stick" algorithm: the app is engineered to frustrate you into paying
product.minus: Users describe the app as a deliberately built trap: an algorithm tuned to maximize spending, engineered hopelessness, and a swipe simulator with no real connections.

product.title: Likes and matches are hidden behind a subscription — useless without paying
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the free tier feels deliberately crippled — you can't see who liked you, can't really message, key filters cost extra. Users read it not as monetization but as a trap: it shows you '100+ likes' but you can only open them by paying.

product.title: You pay and matches still don't come — the algorithm feels rigged
product.minus: Even after buying premium, people report zero real matches or replies. Many notice a telltale pattern: likes suddenly pour in right as the subscription is about to expire — read as a deliberate nudge to renew.

product.title: The same profiles on a loop — swipes aren't being saved
product.minus: A persistent bug: after swiping left/right the same person reappears immediately, and the deck cycles through the same 30-40 faces. Users worry their own swipes aren't registering and doubt anyone is even seeing them.

product.title: Flooded with fakes and bots — there's basically no profile moderation
product.minus: People constantly hit fake profiles, AI photos, pictures with no person in them, and Snapchat scams in the 'opening moves'. They complain that no one checks whether a profile is real, and the report system is either missing or answers with copy-paste.

product.title: The app simply won't open and loads forever
product.minus: Basic stability is broken: the Bumble symbol pulses and nothing happens; you have to force-close and reopen several times. Often it starts right after paying — which makes being unable to even reply to messages doubly galling.

product.title: The verification code never arrives — you can't even sign in or register
product.minus: A whole class of users gets stuck at the very threshold: they enter the correct number but the OTP never arrives for days, or validation rejects a valid number. The result is they can't create an account or get back into one they've already paid for.

product.title: There's no support — just a bot that closes the chat
product.minus: When something breaks (especially billing), there's no help: an AI bot asks for your email and vanishes, no live agents, replies take 72 hours and are copy-paste. For an app that takes your money, the absence of real support is its own sore point.

product.title: Accounts get blocked for no reason — sometimes right after paying
product.minus: People get banned after barely swiping a couple of times and messaging no one, citing 'guideline violations'. The automated system misfires, the 'manual review' replies with the same template, and lifetime subscriptions and payments aren't refunded.

product.title: Billing nightmare: charged after cancelling, refunds refused, hard to unsubscribe
product.minus: A money pain all its own: charges continue after cancellation, payments don't link to the account, refunds are refused 'at the user's fault'. Unsubscribing is deliberately hard, and the bot sends you in circles while money keeps leaving your card.

product.title: Matches expire in 24 hours — connections cut off on a timer
product.minus: The 24-hour reply window feels like it contradicts the whole point of dating: busy people lose a match simply for not logging in on time, and a reconnect is offered for money. Many call it a money trap.

product.title: Feels hostile to men: your profile feels hidden, odds are slim
product.minus: Men report en masse that their profile feels buried under a flood of others, a match comes once a month at best, and matches don't reply. The 'women first' model, in their view, ends with paying and getting almost nothing back.

product.title: When it works — it delivers partners and higher-quality dates than rivals
product.plus: Despite the wave of negativity, some users genuinely found partners and even spouses here, and praise the more thoughtful profiles and respectful vibe. Some explicitly note that Bumble dates turn out higher-quality than on other apps.

product.title: Flexible filters and rich profiles — but much is locked behind payment
product.plus: Those who like the interface point to deep profile customization, precise settings, and filters rivals lack. The strength is detailed profiles that let you match on interests and goals; the only sting is that key filters cost money.

product.title: Fewer bots and scam accounts than other dating apps
product.plus: Against the fake-profile complaints there's a counter-signal: some users feel there are fewer scam accounts and bots here than on rivals, which is exactly why they gave it a shot. For dating, that's a meaningful edge.

product.title: Banned with no reason given, appeals rejected within minutes
product.minus: The single most common pain: accounts are deleted suddenly, with no warning or explanation, often right after a subscription is paid. Appeals are declined in minutes — users are convinced no one reads them, and getting unbanned requires uploading a government ID.

product.title: Useful features locked behind paywalls, useless without paying
product.minus: You can't see who liked you, communicate, or use basic filters without a subscription. People describe it as "useless if you are not paying" — even fundamental functions are gated, and the prices are called extortionate.

product.title: Hard daily like limit to force you to pay
product.minus: Only a handful of likes a day for free — some report 2, some 5, some 8-10. After that the app cuts you off, and the only way out is a subscription. People say it makes the app pointless for meeting anyone.

product.title: Sudden match drought — "shadow ban" to squeeze out a subscription
product.minus: A familiar arc: likes and matches flow for the first days or weeks, then drop abruptly to zero. Many suspect visibility is deliberately throttled to push Premium — and that paying actually makes it worse.

product.title: Forced AI face scan and biometric data retention
product.minus: Mandatory selfie verification constantly fails, while the TOS allows retaining biometric data for up to two years and sharing it with third parties. Some people refuse to hand a dating app face scans on principle and just uninstall.

product.title: "Too many requests" error locks you out of login and signup
product.minus: A huge technical pain: entering your phone number triggers "too many verification requests," the SMS code never arrives, and people are locked out of their own still-active account for days — while emails about likes keep coming.

product.title: Support replaced by AI bots that reply with boilerplate
product.minus: Support requests hit AI with no humans behind it: every issue gets the same boilerplate reply, nothing gets escalated, and contact just stops. When you lose access or are unfairly banned, there's effectively no help.

product.title: Bots, fake and inactive profiles that never respond
product.minus: The feed feels stuffed with bots, AI-generated and fake profiles; matches stay silent or vanish. People suspect many "matches" are old inactive or fake accounts, and some get outright scammed for money.

product.title: Intrusive AI assistant in prompts that only annoys
product.minus: An AI was bolted into the answer fields that pops up on every typing pause with unsolicited "feedback" — and when tapped, often says it has none. It reads as useless bloat on an otherwise decent app.

product.title: The "Signals" feature punishes those without matches
product.minus: The new "Signals" show an activity and "thoughtful messages" badge, but it needs 4 of 6 conditions, half of which depend on already having matches. Those without matches are caught in a vicious circle, and for many the feature simply doesn't work.

product.title: When it works, it genuinely leads to serious relationships
product.plus: The core strength and reason for the high ratings: people genuinely meet partners, spouses, "the one" here — sometimes in days, sometimes over years — and delete it for real. Many stress they did it on the free version.

product.title: Thoughtful profiles and higher-quality people than rivals
product.plus: Even critics call Hinge "the best of a bad bunch": prompt-driven profiles surface personality, the audience leans toward serious relationships over hookups, and people are more likely to actually respond. For many that's what keeps them despite the rest.

product.title: The free version is viable: you can message matches without paying
product.plus: Despite the paywall complaints, a notable group praises the free tier: you can message matches without paying, likes are effectively enough, there's a free weekly rose, and you can view your top liker for free. They meet people without spending a cent.

product.title: Filters ignored: shows wrong gender, age, and location
product.minus: The app routinely ignores your set parameters: it shows people outside your geographic and age dealbreakers, surfaces the wrong gender or orientation, and matches you with 18-year-olds. Some are angry that height/location filters exist while substantive ones are selectively missing.

product.title: Paywalled "undo" and stripping free features for $MTCH
product.minus: The undo button for an accidentally skipped profile — the thing that set Hinge apart — moved behind an expensive paywall. People explicitly tie the steady stripping of free features to pumping Match Group's market cap rather than caring about dates.

product.title: "Signals" deletes likes after 14 days and breeds toxic behavior
product.minus: An update started deleting received likes if you don't respond within 14 days — nominally "to make you talk more," but in practice people now frantically delete chats within a day of silence. A mechanic meant as an incentive bred exactly the toxic behavior it claimed to fight.

product.title: Safety of women and queer users isn't seriously protected
product.minus: Serious safety complaints: facing verbal abuse and threats, the company refuses to share data even with the user's national police; cis men set a female gender to proposition queer women, with no tool to stop it.

product.title: Likes are padded with overseas profiles to bait you into paying for premium
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people get dozens of "likes," but almost all are from Africa, Asia or the Philippines, while the few local matches sit behind a paywall. Many pay, discover the likes are fake or from the other side of the planet, and realize the whole feed was bait to sell a subscription.

product.title: Can't log in or create an account: number rejected, SMS code never arrives
product.minus: A huge slice of users simply can't get into the app. They're suddenly logged out, password resets fail (the email never comes), and trying to sign back in throws "invalid" or "already in use" errors on the phone number while the SMS verification code never arrives. Some note the problem has dragged on for years.

product.title: Accounts banned without explanation for "suspicious activity," appeals denied
product.minus: People get banned within minutes of signing up or after years of loyalty — often mid-conversation. Asked why, they get a boilerplate "suspicious activity," their appeal is rejected as "final," and they also lose hundreds of answered compatibility questions in the process.

product.title: Distance filter is broken — feed flooded with overseas profiles via Passport mode
product.minus: Even for free the app becomes useless: you set a small radius and get shown people on another continent who manually fake their location via Passport mode. Distance settings and preferences are simply ignored, making it impossible to find anyone local.

product.title: You pay for premium, then the app "forgets" you subscribed
product.minus: The payment goes through and money is taken, but the app says "not paid" and won't unlock the features you bought. Premium flickers on and off, forcing constant restarts and refreshes, and refunds are nearly impossible — support replies with autoresponders or stays silent.

product.title: Buggy interface: same profiles on loop, freezes, navigation hidden behind phone buttons
product.minus: The app loops the same already-swiped people, freezes on white screens, and the bottom bar slides under Android's system buttons so you can't tap "next" or open messages. Nagging notification pop-ups won't close no matter how often you hit the X.

product.title: Basic features locked behind a paywall — even messaging and likes
product.minus: OkCupid used to let you meet and message for free; now nearly everything costs money — seeing who liked you, liking back, or messaging all require an overpriced subscription ($30–40/month). Many refuse on principle, calling the model greedy and predatory.

product.title: Crawling with scammers and bots that funnel you into fraud
product.minus: Users run into fake profiles that beg for money, fish for contact info, or pull them into sextortion and romance scams. AI bots funnel people into sales pitches, and reports on profiles go unanswered — leaving the impression fakes are tolerated to pad the numbers.

product.title: Deep profiles and compatibility questions — the reason people loved it
product.plus: OkCupid's core value is its detailed profiles, question series and compatibility percentage that show how well you fit someone before you even message. Longtime users recall finding genuinely like-minded people here and building serious relationships.

product.title: When it works, people genuinely find love here
product.plus: Despite the avalanche of negativity, a share of users say OkCupid is where they met their spouse or partner, sometimes years ago. Many praise being able to message for free and try the app before paying, and note there are real people mixed in among the fakes.

product.title: "It used to be great" — features stripped away until it feels like a Tinder clone
product.minus: A recurring theme is nostalgia for what OkCupid once was. Over time they removed search, text answers to questions, cut thousands of questions down to hundreds, and dropped the "enemy percentage." Now it's just a Tinder-style swipe app, and longtime fans no longer see the point.

product.title: Customer support is effectively nonexistent: autoreplies, silence and being ignored
product.minus: When something breaks — a ban, a failed payment, lost access — reaching support means hitting boilerplate autoreplies like "someone will get back to you, be patient" or total silence. People send ten emails with no reply, and even paying customers can't get help.

product.title: The paywall has grown absurd: you pay for premium and still pay extra for likes and messages
product.minus: Premium stopped unlocking anything: to see likes, message first, or send more than one message a day, you must buy each feature separately. Users feel conned by a "misleading" subscription.

product.title: Overrun with fakes, bots and scammers — almost no real people left
product.minus: Female profiles are mostly fake, conversations die after a couple of messages, and fake-account moderation is essentially nonexistent. Many are convinced likes and matches are bot-generated to extract payment.

product.title: A cap of one first message per day makes the free version pointless
product.minus: Without paying you can message one new person every 24 hours — and if the app "deletes" that one message "for your safety", you're left with zero contact for the day. Swiping is useless because matches almost never happen.

product.title: Selfie verification is broken — real people can't pass, yet scammers get through
product.minus: A clear photo gets rejected 10-15 times in a row, selfies come out "blurred" even on a good camera, and you can't create a profile without passing it. Meanwhile scammers sail right through.

product.title: Bans with no explanation — often right after you pay, and appeals are ignored
product.minus: Accounts get banned for no reason, frequently days after a premium purchase, and requests for a reason or an appeal go unanswered. Money is not refunded when you're banned.

product.title: Billing as a trap: charges after cancellation, double/triple charges, a yearly bill instead of monthly
product.minus: The subscription is nearly impossible to cancel — the "Cancel Premium" button is hidden, it doesn't show up in Google Play, and the card keeps getting charged after the account is deleted, pushing people into overdrafts and bank penalties.

product.title: Location and filters are ignored: it shows people thousands of miles away and outside your age range
product.minus: Set a 5-mile radius and it shows profiles from another country; set an age range and people twice your age message you. The app keeps resetting your location to the wrong place and respects none of your search settings.

product.title: Phantom notifications: "you got a message/like", but the inbox is empty
product.minus: The app fires notifications about new messages and likes that don't exist: you open them and get an error or nothing. People read it as a desperate trick to make you open the app and pay.

product.title: Login and password reset are broken: verification tied to an old number and reset emails that never arrive
product.minus: Password reset is dead — the code email never arrives, and login demands a code on a phone the user hasn't had for years. Support points you to a dead page that just tells you to make a new account.

product.title: Customer service is effectively absent: copy-paste replies and tickets with no answer
product.minus: Inquiries get the same copy-pasted "go through Google Play" reply, and tickets go unanswered. No one will look up your account or help with a refund — you're left on your own.

product.title: A ghost town: it surfaces profiles inactive for months, and nobody matches
product.minus: The feed is full of accounts that haven't logged in for 3-10 months yet are labeled "recently active". You message everyone in range for months and get zero replies: people are sure the app is dead.

product.title: Veterans remember the free POF and resent the "complicated" Match Group redesign
product.minus: Long-timers remember a simple, free app for years; after the Match Group merge it became confusing, paywalled and, in their words, a "flaming pile of garbage". Nostalgia for the old POF is a constant theme.

product.title: Despite everything, some people genuinely meet someone — and the search plus message-before-matching is valued
product.plus: A share of users praise being able to message before matching and the handy search, see plenty of active people and quick connections. There are real stories of meeting, relationships and even marriages through POF.

product.title: A paywall on the conversation itself: premium doesn't unlock chat
product.minus: Users are furious at the double monetization: even after paying for premium or a subscription, they still hit a wall — messaging a specific person requires separate credits, often 250 per message. The core function of a dating app turns out to be paywalled on top of what they already paid for.

product.title: Spoofed-location profiles: "locals" turn out to be thousands of km away
product.minus: The most frequent complaint after the paywall: the "nearby" filter doesn't work. Users are shown profiles from other countries — Philippines, Nigeria, Cuba, Kenya — posing as locals with faked locations. Reports go ignored, and finding anyone nearby becomes impossible.

product.title: Sudden bans with no reason and no refund
product.minus: Many users report being blocked out of nowhere, often right after paying for a subscription, with no explanation and no refund. It stings most when the ban lands just after verifying or paying for a full year.

product.title: Backwards moderation: the reporter gets banned, the offender stays
product.minus: The report system works in reverse: a single complaint can get you blocked instead of the offender. People describe being banned after they themselves reported scammers or fake locations, while the actual fraudsters and bots stay on the platform for years.

product.title: Paywalled likes — and the suspicion they're faked to create FOMO
product.minus: Seeing who liked you costs money — and many suspect the like counter is inflated to manufacture FOMO: you pay, and the promised likes vanish or only appear as your subscription runs out. Without paying, thousands of likes are useless: the match never happens.

product.title: Unskippable ads jammed into the swipe loop
product.minus: Every few swipes an ad pops up that can't be closed: a tiny X, fake timers, redirects to Temu or Google Play. Sometimes a "semi-playable" ad game takes over the whole screen, forcing you to restart the app entirely.

product.title: Overrun by scammers, bots and green-card hunters
product.minus: Users describe the platform as flooded with fake profiles, bots, prostitutes and foreigners hunting for a green card or a way to extract money. Many call it a "mail-order bride system" and warn it can be outright dangerous for women.

product.title: Onboarding glitches: photos won't upload, verification loops
product.minus: Technical failures hit at the very start: the built-in uploader won't show photos, verification loops endlessly, a mistyped birth date can't be fixed, and the app freezes and crashes. Some people can't even create or open an account.

product.title: Whole regions cut off without warning (Iran, Korea and more)
product.minus: Users from entire countries are suddenly cut off with no notice, and requests for temporary access just to delete their own data go unanswered. It's especially acute for Iran: people can neither log in nor retrieve their personal information.

product.title: Regional price gouging: credits cost several times more in the UK
product.minus: Users notice huge price gaps between countries: the same credits cost 5x+ more in the UK than, say, the Philippines. Many call the subscriptions overpriced, and one reward — a single like for watching a 30-second ad — outright insulting.

product.title: Rare but real success stories — some people do find a partner
product.plus: Amid the flood of complaints, there are genuine reviews from people who found a spouse or partner here. They admit the pool quality is "a trial," but urge others not to give up — for some, Badoo led to marriage and real connections.

product.title: Veteran users: with habits and reverse image checks it's livable
product.plus: Some long-time users take the downsides in stride: fakes are everywhere, but screenshots, reverse image search, report and block keep them safe. A few find the interface simple, the audience mature, and the swiping itself relaxing and welcoming to anyone.

product.title: An empty feed: no crossings, no one nearby
product.minus: happn's core mechanic — surfacing people you crossed paths with — simply doesn't fire for many users. People go months, even a full year, without a single new profile, and the map and "vibes" stay empty.

product.title: The app is overrun with bots and fake profiles
product.minus: The single most common complaint: real people are scarce and the feed is packed with bots, fakes and OnlyFans spam. People go months without one genuine match, and the same photos show up across different profiles.

product.title: An organized restaurant-bill scam
product.minus: A separate and disturbingly systematic con: a "woman" insists on meeting at one specific bar or restaurant, and the bill arrives at 10–15 thousand, of which she takes a commission. Users describe the exact same script, especially in Bangalore.

product.title: Scammers pull you off-app and extort you
product.minus: The people who do message are often scammers on a VPN: they push you to WhatsApp or Telegram, send ChatGPT images as fake "proof," extort personal info and money, then delete the account.

product.title: You pay, and it gets worse
product.minus: The core grievance of paying users: after buying premium the profiles around you don't grow — they vanish. Several people made a second free account and saw more profiles than on the paid one, leaving the sense the subscription deliberately throttles the feed.

product.title: Free users can't do anything at all
product.minus: Basic actions — liking, messaging, seeing who liked you — are all locked behind a paywall. Without a subscription the app shrinks to staring at other people's profiles, with likes rationed to three at a time and a 24-hour wait.

product.title: Likes are hidden to sell you CrushTime
product.minus: Users spot a pattern: the people who liked you are deliberately pulled out of the swipe feed to force you to pay or play the "CrushTime" guessing game. The mechanic itself is buggy and burns your super-likes for nothing.

product.title: Accounts get banned right after signup with no explanation
product.minus: People get banned or frozen within an hour of creating a profile — before sending a single message — citing a "terms violation." Support replies with canned templates and refuses to explain what actually happened.

product.title: Removing the verified filter is a safety issue
product.minus: You used to be able to filter for verified profiles and see who was online and real — the latest update removed that. Against a backdrop of rampant scammers, users read it as a deliberate trade of their safety for money.

product.title: No video call or photo sharing — you can't tell who you're talking to
product.minus: There's no in-app video call and no way to send a photo inside the chat. With so many fakes around, that means you can't verify who you're talking to within happn — and users are effectively pushed to meet unverified people in person.

product.title: Location is ignored: matches from other cities and countries
product.minus: Despite the "crossed paths via GPS" premise, people are shown profiles hundreds of kilometers away — other states and countries — when the whole concept is local. And often you can't adjust the distance at all.

product.title: Pricing is opaque and steep
product.minus: The subscription cost feels both high and dishonestly framed: they advertise "$15," but that's weekly, so it's over $27 a month. And the "50% off" offers often just fail to load.

product.title: Buggy at every step: freezes, crashes, broken verification
product.minus: The app freezes during onboarding and when changing photos, crashes, and won't let you sign in even after paying. The video-selfie verification endlessly fails with "verification failed" for many, blocking them out of the product entirely.

product.title: Intrusive biometrics and data-selling feel alarming
product.minus: To use it you must keep location on at all times, and users are convinced that data gets sold. Separately, the demand for a detailed face scan including the iris from multiple angles unsettles people — they compare it to creating a government ID.

product.title: Notification spam and ads right on launch
product.minus: The app buries you in push notifications about new features and subscriptions, with pop-ups you can't dismiss that force you to "send a message" without credits. And some users are greeted by an ad the moment they open it.

product.title: You can't delete your account, chats or even photos
product.minus: Leaving happn turns out harder than joining: the account won't delete or deactivate, you can't remove a photo without replacing it with at least two, and dead "crush not available" chats can't be cleared from the list.

product.title: For some, the concept and the map do land
product.plus: Despite everything, some people praise the core "show who you crossed paths with" idea and the map, call the app easy to use — and a few find real dates. One user went on 4 dates with a guy without paying for premium.

product.title: You can't see who likes you without paying — the app is pointless free
product.minus: The number-one complaint: you get nonstop notifications that someone liked you, but you can't see or message them until you pay for premium. Users describe it as a trap — you pay, and the person who "liked" you suddenly vanishes from the Likes section.

product.title: White screen after install — it runs once, then won't open again
product.minus: A mass technical failure: after install the app works once, then shows a blank white screen on every later open. The only "fix" is to uninstall and reinstall over and over — some people did it six times.

product.title: Dead population: 1–5 profiles a day, then a 24-hour timer
product.minus: The "one batch at noon" mechanic turns into emptiness: people get 1–5 profiles a day (sometimes zero), then hit a 24-hour countdown. Outside big cities you see only a handful of profiles over weeks — the pool is simply empty.

product.title: $40–60 a month with no day or week option
product.minus: The subscription starts at $40–60 a month with no day or week plan to just test it. People call the "$3.99/wk" ads false advertising — in reality only the pricey monthly tier exists, and on top of that you still have to buy "beans" and "flowers" separately.

product.title: Filters and "dealbreakers" ignored — wrong people, far away
product.minus: People set distance, age and ethnicity and mark them as "dealbreakers," yet the app still serves up people from other states and far outside their preferences. Many are angry that some filters (like education) are also locked behind a paywall.

product.title: Suspicion the subscription throttles likes: you pay, likes drop
product.minus: A recurring accusation: as a free user you get dozens of likes, but the moment you subscribe the number suddenly drops by half or more. People read this as deliberately withholding likes to extract money, and call the app a "money grab."

product.title: Can't finish signup: stuck on "ethnicity" and GPS location
product.minus: A chunk of users never even reach the app: the "Next" button on the "optional" ethnicity field does nothing no matter what they type, and GPS location detection fails even with permissions on. Signup dies on the very first screen.

product.title: Fake and foreign profiles: "too many Asians" and green-card schemes
product.minus: Users complain that a big share of profiles look fake: matches live somewhere other than stated, photos fail reverse image search, and the pool feels packed with foreign nationals chasing immigration/green-card matches. Real accounts get banned while fakes stay.

product.title: Nagging popups and "hurry, they're popular" pressure even paying users
product.minus: Even after paying, the app buries you in popups like "this person is popular, spend flowers to stand out" and subscription sales. You can't turn them off without muting all notifications, and the buttons often only work after several taps.

product.title: Glitchy chat: messages get lost, arrive late, or fail to send
product.minus: Messaging itself is unreliable: texts hang, fail to send, arrive badly delayed, or get lost entirely. That hurts most because the app gives you a narrow window to connect, and the chat breaks the conversation exactly when it matters.

product.title: Curation for intentionality: one batch a day, focus on serious relationships
product.plus: Those the format fits genuinely value the philosophy: not endless swiping but a curated noon drop, a push to read profiles, and intentional matching. For people seeking serious relationships it feels like "quality over quantity" with built-in intentionality.

product.title: Real couples and weddings: for some people it genuinely worked
product.plus: Despite all the negativity, there's a steady stream of success stories: people met a partner, started dating, found "their person," and are even planning a wedding. For them the smaller-but-higher-quality pool and real verified people made the app worth it.

product.title: Fewer bots and scammers than rivals — "higher quality" men
product.plus: Some users directly compare CMB to Hinge, Tinder and Match and rate it better: fewer bots and scammers, verified profiles, an audience oriented toward serious relationships. For them that's the key upside in an otherwise "predatory" dating market.

product.title: Useful profile metrics and "dealbreakers" help you aim better
product.plus: Detail-oriented users love the stats: the app shows a person's response time, how often they break the ice first, whether they ever talk to matches at all, plus deep profiles and "dealbreaker" filters. To them it's smart design that helps screen and save time.

product.title: You can't even read incoming messages without paying
product.minus: The core function — talking — sits behind a paywall: matches arrive blurred and messages are readable only to paying members. People pay and still can't open a single message.

product.title: Almost no matches until you pay — your profile just isn't shown
product.minus: Users go months with one match or none, feeling their profile simply isn't shown to anyone without payment. Even after buying premium, many get no matches at all.

product.title: Swiping «no» burns your daily limit the same as «yes»
product.minus: The daily like cap is spent even on people you reject, so you can never reach the person who liked you — and it pushes everyone toward mass right-swiping.

product.title: The app loads forever and crashes constantly
product.minus: Multi-minute loads, crashes on every other launch, a glitchy chat that forces constant re-logins — and sometimes a reinstall locks you out of your account entirely.

product.title: Photo verification gets stuck — and locks you out of a paid account
product.minus: Face checks fall into «manual verification» that never finishes for hours; after paying, uploading a new photo demands re-verification again, leaving the app completely unusable.

product.title: Accounts get banned right after payment — with no explanation
product.minus: Users report being banned within seconds of paying, or simply kicked out and unable to get back in despite months of paid subscription.

product.title: A nagging «rate this app» popup on every single launch
product.minus: The app begs for a rating literally every time you open it — even before you have a single match; many people drop it to one star purely over this spam.

product.title: Bots, fakes and scammers begging for money
product.minus: Despite verification, the feed is full of fake foreign accounts and scammers who openly ask whether you have enough funds to keep them comfortable.

product.title: Personality over photos — the app's real strength
product.plus: Fans praise the focus on MBTI and compatibility rather than looks: conversations go deeper, people feel more genuine, and there's less ghosting than on other apps.

product.title: Verified photos and a thoughtful sign-up build trust
product.plus: Mandatory photo verification plus a deep sign-up with a personality test and audio/video intros make it feel safe and weed out people pretending to be who they aren't.

product.title: A social-feed hybrid: you can talk, not just wait for a match
product.plus: Unlike apps where you can't say a word before matching, Boo has a built-in social feed and lets you chat about posts with many people — a relief for those tired of pure swiping.

product.title: Too few people in your city or age range
product.minus: Older users and those in smaller cities hit an empty feed: one or two people a week in their age or radius, with almost no local singles.

product.title: An ad on every tap makes the app barely usable
product.minus: An ad pops up on every action — open the app, tap a profile, reply to a message. Clips drag on for 15-30 seconds and eat up half the user's time.

product.title: Predatory ads: a tiny close button redirects you to other apps and sites
product.minus: The ad's close button is made tiny and hard to see, so a tap "accidentally" opens the app store or browser. Sometimes the app downloads junk onto the phone by itself.

product.title: Once-free features moved behind a paywall, prices jacked up
product.minus: With each update what used to be free gets hidden behind a subscription, and the plans are sliced into expensive tiers. Pay for one and you still have to buy the next just to actually message people.

product.title: Bots, fakes and scammers flood the grid — even after you pay
product.minus: Half the profiles are bots, catfish and OnlyFans/Snap ads. Paying doesn't stop the spam, and users suspect the bots benefit Grindr itself by driving ad views.

product.title: Opaque bans hit real accounts, appeals stall for months
product.minus: Accounts get banned by automation with no reason given, sometimes right after paying or cancelling. Appeals don't work, and people wait 34 days or more for any support reply.

product.title: The app crashes, freezes and won't load profiles
product.minus: Every update breaks something new: the main grid loads zero profiles, the app hangs for 10-15 minutes, crashes on launch, and loses messages mid-typing.

product.title: Dirty subscription tricks: silent plan swaps and charges after cancelling
product.minus: An annual plan quietly gets swapped for a pricey weekly one, a weekly trial auto-renews, and charges keep coming after you cancel. Cancelling through the app itself is nearly impossible.

product.title: Paid Xtra cheats: the "hot" profiles vanish after you upgrade
product.minus: The Xtra section dangles attractive people nearby, but after you pay they disappear or turn out to be hundreds of miles away. Free unlocks and search deliberately hide the real distance too.

product.title: GPS lies, and the "online" status shows people long gone
product.minus: The distance map is wrong: random profiles 25+ miles away show as closest. And "online" lights up for people offline 10+ minutes, or even for the user who hasn't logged in.

product.title: Forced age verification feels like an invasion of privacy
product.minus: To lift a ban or confirm age, the app demands a selfie with a handwritten ID or a passport scan. Users find this humiliating and unsafe, especially given how sensitive the audience is.

product.title: The brand loses its core: women, fakes and pop-star Madonna marketing
product.minus: Long-time users feel the app has stopped being a space for gay men: women and fakes creep in, and the intrusive Madonna promo takeover of the screen only annoys.

product.title: For the loyal "despite everything" crowd, Grindr still finds partners
product.plus: Despite the flood of complaints, some users have found matches, friends and even marriages here over the years — especially while travelling and looking for locals. Those who can filter still have fun.

product.title: The app freezes at the exact moment you trade
product.minus: Users describe the same scenario over and over: the moment they try to buy, sell, or open a futures position, the app stalls, spins, and crashes — and while it's frozen the price moves, taking money with it. Some even bought a new phone thinking it was the hardware, but the lag stayed.

product.title: Getting your money out turns into a siege
product.minus: The most painful theme: money goes in easily, but trying to withdraw it gets held, transfers blocked for a week to a month with no clear reason, and sometimes released only at a loss. The feeling of funds being held hostage comes up again and again.

product.title: Verification is a maze with no exit
product.minus: KYC rejects every document, demands a passport and then another paper, and the ID screen rotates on its own. People spend days and hours trying to verify and never pass — especially those whose ID isn't in English or whose phone number changed.

product.title: Support replies with canned templates, then ghosts you
product.minus: When something breaks, there's no help: they tell you to reinstall and clear cache, make you keep a chat alive for hours, then stop replying. People complain of being "escalated" into nowhere with the problem never resolved.

product.title: Fees and spread eat your money before you even invest
product.minus: Users tally exact losses: sold $25 of bitcoin and got $19, deposited $200 and saw $180, around 4% gone to fees and slippage before investing at all. Many name the fees directly as their reason for leaving for other exchanges.

product.title: Sudden account lockout with no explanation
product.minus: Long-time loyal customers suddenly lose access: the account gets closed for a "terms of service breach" no one will show them, or recovery sends a code to an old phone number. The money stays inside while login is impossible.

product.title: The prediction market feels like a rigged casino
product.minus: A distinct pain is the predictions feature: people win by the facts (temperature, coin price) but are scored as losing, and payouts never arrive. They complain of "slip" that turns a 98% gain into 28%, and call it gambling.

product.title: Intrusive pop-ups and ads for new features
product.minus: Veterans dislike how bloated the app got: the screen is full of "new feature!" pop-ups, Coinbase One ads, games and predictions, while you have to scroll to find your own portfolio. They feel pushed toward gambling instead of simply buying crypto.

product.title: An easy start for first-timers in crypto
product.plus: This is the most common praise: for beginners Coinbase genuinely makes sense — a clean interface, simple buy-sell, clear steps, and the app teaches crypto by explaining coins. Many admit they'd never have figured it out without it.

product.title: An all-in-one platform: crypto, stocks, card, staking
product.plus: Experienced users like the breadth: one app for crypto trading, stocks, derivatives, staking and lending, the Coinbase debit and credit card, and an Advanced mode with detailed charts and lower fees. For many it's "the only app you need."

product.title: Long-running reliability and trust among some veterans
