product.plus: Despite the wave of criticism, a noticeable group of long-time users find Coinbase reliable and proven: years without issues, fast transactions, easy withdrawals, and a feeling of safety from identity confirmation before transfers. Some rate it above their traditional bank.

product.title: Money flows in easily, getting it out is near-impossible
product.minus: Deposits go through fine, but withdrawal triggers holds, a missing payout method, or a feature that's suddenly "coming soon." People wait months for their own money and feel robbed.

product.title: Support is a bot that talks in circles
product.minus: There's no live human: tickets sit open for weeks, the "live chat" repeats the same scripts, and the promised escalation to the "internal team" loops you right back to tier 1. The issue is never fixed.

product.title: Identity verification is an endless loop with no exit
product.minus: KYC breaks for no reason: an ID flagged as the "wrong state," a license over 90 days old, biometrics you're forced to redo. People sit in "reviewing your information" for two weeks or more and never get in.

product.title: Regional bans cut off access to assets you already own
product.minus: The app works in your state one year and not the next — Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, Florida. Worst of all, when a state's status changes they hand your assets to the state, or force you to sell everything, with no warning.

product.title: A seven-day hold on new funds defeats the point of crypto
product.minus: New deposits get frozen for 7 days (or 48 hours) with no upfront warning. By the time the hold clears the price has moved and you can no longer buy what you came for — the instant settlement that makes crypto worthwhile is gone.

product.title: Predatory withdrawal fees eat a real chunk of your money
product.minus: Withdrawal fees feel wildly out of proportion: $53 to move $300 of BTC, $40 to send, up to 35% on a basic transaction. Next to competitors charging cents, it reads as a rip-off.

product.title: Logged out for no reason, then locked out for good
product.minus: The app logs you out every few days; after a terms change or update the password stops being accepted, and codes never arrive by phone or email. None of the auth methods work and you lose access to your money.

product.title: A widget-ad update broke the app's entry screen
product.minus: After an update a widget ad pops up on launch, and both the "Got it" button and the X close the whole app instead of the popup. Charts also went glitchy and collapse on their own after the update — they used to be a strength.

product.title: No average price or total P&L — do the math yourself
product.minus: There's no proper position tracking: average price isn't calculated, past losing trades skew your total profit, and to know your real gain or loss you have to recompute it by hand. A basic trading feature is just missing.

product.title: Refusing to list Pi Coin despite the vote enrages users
product.minus: A whole wave of one-star reviews comes from the Pi Network community: a vote came back a clear "yes," people were made to deposit money to vote, yet the coin was never listed while useless memecoins keep getting added. It reads as manipulation and a broken promise.

product.title: Low liquidity and a thin coin list versus the global version
product.minus: The US version is noticeably poorer: thin liquidity, none of the new hot coins the main Binance carries, and missing assets users actually want like Kaspa. It drives people off to Uphold, Kraken, and Coinbase.

product.title: When it works, it's the best, simplest exchange with low fees
product.plus: For users who got set up, it's the best and clearest trading experience around: a wide coin selection, reasonable fees, a handy Lite/Pro mode, and staking. Many prefer it over Coinbase precisely for its simplicity.

product.title: The developer actually reads reviews and fixes bugs — users raise their rating
product.plus: A chunk of users come back and bump their rating: the developer responds to criticism, fixes the ad-popup login bug, and restores account access. The return of US banking and Florida support are also welcomed.

product.title: Getting money out is nearly impossible — buying is easy, withdrawing is not
product.minus: Deposits and purchases go through instantly, but the moment you try to withdraw, it turns into a stream of errors, locks and "reviews". People go months and years unable to pull money out of their own account.

product.title: Support is an AI loop — you can never reach a human
product.minus: The chat answers with AI templates and won't connect you to a live agent, and tickets get closed without resolving anything. Users describe an endless run-around where real help simply doesn't exist.

product.title: Account lockouts and login-by-error — with money trapped inside
product.minus: After an update or a simple phone change the app freezes on the login screen, spins forever or shows "unauthorized". Accounts get locked for days and weeks, and there's almost no one to unlock them manually.

product.title: Spreads and fees eat your profit — you pay at every step
product.minus: There's a fee to deposit, buy, exchange and withdraw, plus a huge spread between buy and sell price. Just to break even your asset has to rise noticeably; rivals like Coinbase or Binance are cheaper.

product.title: "Scam" and stolen funds — a frequent accusation against the platform
product.minus: Many flatly call the service a scam: money supposedly vanishes from the account, balances melt away, and accounts with assets get closed without explanation. For this group, trust in the platform is completely gone.

product.title: The passkey-verification glitch blocks crypto sends for years
product.minus: Trying to send funds throws "Passkey Verification failed" over and over. Clearing cache, reinstalling and resetting keys does nothing; you can buy, but you can't send.

product.title: The app is slow, freezes and crashes on launch
product.minus: Black screens, endless loading, lag and crashes — especially when trying to make a transaction. Users say every update makes it worse, not better.

product.title: Constant updates and intrusive push ads
product.minus: The app demands an update almost every time you open it, then buries you in pop-ups and notifications about sports, missions and airdrops — even with those notifications turned off. It gets in the way and slows the service itself.

product.title: New-address holds and sky-high withdrawal minimums
product.minus: A new send address gets frozen for a day, and the minimum withdrawal is so high that small balances are simply stuck. To leave the service some users have to forfeit their leftover funds.

product.title: CRO/ETH staking and unstaking work erratically
product.minus: You can't unstake CRO in the app — you need a browser — and ETH staking "activates" for weeks instead of the promised day. The CRO token itself has crashed and yields are far below what they used to be.

product.title: For beginners — a simple, approachable way into crypto
product.plus: Happy users praise the clean interface and how easy it is to buy and sell: a good starting point for beginners to learn crypto and get comfortable with it.

product.title: The card, rewards and long track record keep the loyal
product.plus: Some users stick with the service for years for the CRO cashback, the physical card and a reputation as an exchange that survived the 2022–2024 collapse. For them it's the "best crypto app" with a rich feature set.

product.title: Beginner-friendly entry is the main reason people love it
product.plus: Most happy users praise it for making investing accessible and understandable from zero: prompts guide you, you can start with tiny amounts, and buy fractional shares.

product.title: Money held hostage: getting funds out is nearly impossible
product.minus: Dozens complain the app holds their money — suddenly demands re-verification, restricts the account, or simply won't let you withdraw funds you deposited yourself.

product.title: Support is effectively nonexistent — just bots and automated menus
product.minus: The most recurring pain: when something breaks, you can't reach a human. Chatbots are useless, queues run 2-2.5 hours, and phone support is either unavailable or leads nowhere.

product.title: Signup and login break — locked out of your own account
product.minus: Many get stuck at the door: the signup form glitches, the system says your account «already exists» or conversely «doesn't exist», codes go to an old phone, the camera won't open for the ID photo.

product.title: Pushy Gold ads flood the app with pop-ups
product.minus: Users get bombarded with Robinhood Gold ads: every launch you have to dismiss pop-ups, and no matter how many times you hit «X» they come back — driving away even people who used to love the app.

product.title: Prediction markets on the home page — gambling instead of investing
product.minus: A growing complaint: the home screen forces a «prediction market» (bets on weather, elections) you can't hide without contacting support. Users see it as encouraging gambling, not investing.

product.title: Deposit «pending»: money debited but you can't trade
product.minus: A frequent mechanism: money is instantly pulled from your bank but sits «pending» 5-7 days, while the instant balance triggers an account restriction for «unpaid purchases». People miss trades and lose money because of it.

product.title: Accounts frozen without explanation for «suspicious activity»
product.minus: Several users describe accounts suddenly locked over a «security trigger» or «suspicious activity», with support refusing to even explain why — and the money inaccessible meanwhile.

product.title: Lag and crashes, especially on charts and during volatility
product.minus: After recent updates the app freezes and crashes; advanced charts update slowly or are broken, and during volatility prices load slowly — causing traders to miss trades and lose money.

product.title: Forced Plaid and data leaks raise privacy alarms
product.minus: Users are unnerved that to trade you must log into your online bank via Plaid, granting access to all your accounts — and some received a crypto scam right after signup and suspected a data leak.

product.title: Hidden monthly fee that's hard to cancel
product.minus: Some users discover they're quietly charged 5-10 dollars a month, even after they stopped using the app, and closing the account or cancelling is made deliberately difficult.

product.title: IPO access is advertised, but regular investors don't get shares
product.minus: There's heavy frustration around IPOs (especially SpaceX): pre-orders don't execute without notice, orders get cut to a single share, and priority allegedly goes to Gold members — leaving the regular investor with nothing.

product.title: Free trading and low fees are a genuine plus
product.plus: Many value the lack of trade commissions and the overall low cost; for the small investor it removes the entry barrier, though crypto fees are called high.

product.title: Gamification: a pretty facade that feels like a casino
product.minus: Even well-disposed users note the pretty interface is a «casino dressed up as investing»: the app nudges you toward trades and «rewards» and profits by holding your money, which keeps them from fully trusting it.

product.title: Easy to deposit, almost impossible to withdraw
product.minus: The classic trap: deposits go through instantly, but the moment you try to pull money out the nightmare begins — cancellations, endless «pending», partial payouts and held fees. People spend weeks unable to retrieve their own money.

product.title: Accounts get frozen with no reason given
product.minus: The scariest story for an exchange: the account is frozen or closed without warning or explanation, while the money stays inside. People beg for access to their own funds for months and get neither a reply nor their cash.

product.title: There's no support — just a useless AI bot
product.minus: Reaching a live human is impossible: every problem gets only an AI bot or canned emails, and real answers take days or never come. When your money is stuck, this becomes a disaster.

product.title: A hidden spread eats your money on top of the stated fees
product.minus: Even with a paid «fee-free» subscription, the buy price runs above market and the sell price below it by 1–5%. This spread is never shown upfront, and users feel cheated: technically there's no fee, yet money vanishes.

product.title: The app won't launch and freezes, especially after updates
product.minus: A recurring plague: the app hangs on the login screen, won't load or crashes — often right after yet another update, while the browser site still works. Trades fail at the exact moment you need them.

product.title: A 72-hour (or even 6-day) hold on funds, even on pennies
product.minus: After a deposit, your cash or freshly bought crypto is frozen for 72 hours and longer — whether it's $15 or $3000. People miss market moves and can't see why such a hold applies to trivial amounts.

product.title: Orders don't execute at the target price
product.minus: Limit and custom orders just sit there: the price hits the target but the trade doesn't fire, or slippage moves the price in the exchange's favor. Users suspect it's deliberate and lose money on it.

product.title: Verification and login — an endless loop
product.minus: Device registration on every update, broken two-factor, emails that never arrive, face verification stuck for days and KYC loops — people get locked out of their own accounts before they ever make a trade.

product.title: Genuinely simple for crypto beginners
product.plus: The number-one praise: the interface is clear and doesn't bury a newcomer in data, you can start with $5, and the first crypto purchase takes seconds. For people who never invested before, Kraken is an easy way in.

product.title: Cheap trades and a subscription that waives fees
product.plus: Those who avoid the hidden problems praise the low fees, fast trades and the Kraken Plus subscription that waives trading, conversion and withdrawal fees — for them it's an obvious win.

product.title: A sense of security and trust in the platform
product.plus: Despite the pile-on of complaints, a loyal core keeps their crypto here for years and trusts Kraken — citing account protection, being regulated and a reputation as one of the most trustworthy exchanges.

product.title: Staking, rewards and crypto-plus-stocks in one place
product.plus: Beyond basic buying, users value the passive income from staking, automatic buys, bonus reward wheels and holding crypto and stocks together — fans like the breadth of tools.

product.title: Funds vanish with no explanation
product.minus: The most frequent and devastating complaint: the balance was there, then dropped to zero on its own — coins «sent» to an address the user never authorized, with nobody able to explain where they went.

product.title: Support is effectively absent
product.minus: When money goes missing, there's no human to reach: the chatbot answers with junk, there's no live agent or phone line, and emails get brush-offs or silence.

product.title: A magnet for scammers
product.minus: It's riddled with fake token addresses, counterfeit USDT and dust attacks, while scammers swarm the Telegram channel — a newcomer who doesn't know better is almost certain to get played.

product.title: Swaps and transfers fail with errors
product.minus: Coin swaps constantly come back «failed», a simple USDT transfer won't go through for days, and transactions hang on errors — the wallet's core operations just don't work.

product.title: Updates break access to the wallet
product.minus: After yet another update people can't get in: passwords stop working, biometrics break, and part of the holdings simply disappear from the screen.

product.title: Balance doesn't update in real time
product.minus: Coins arrive but the balance stays unchanged — you wait 5–10 minutes after sending, receiving or swapping, and the lag is scary enough to feel like the money's gone.

product.title: Lose the seed phrase, lose everything
product.minus: The self-custody model is merciless: forget the 12 words, switch phones, or botch the Google Drive backup, and the money is simply gone with no one able to recover it.

product.title: Money charged, crypto never arrived
product.minus: On a bank/UPI purchase the money leaves the account but the coins never show up in the wallet — and it can drag on for weeks with no refund.

product.title: High fees and painful withdrawals
product.minus: Network fees bite, getting money out to a bank account is hard, and some users hit demands to pay or upload documents just to reach their own funds.

product.title: Cluttered, noisy interface
product.minus: Too many ads, blinking elements and «fireworks» — the wallet feels like a casino and loses any air of a serious financial tool; users wish for the cleanliness of Exodus.

product.title: Simple and friendly for everyday crypto
product.plus: For those who've found their footing, the wallet clicks: a clear interface, easy buys and transfers, fast swaps — many keep it for years as their main wallet.

product.title: A sense of safety and trust
product.plus: Despite the flood of complaints, a share of users come away feeling the wallet is a safe, dependable place to keep crypto — and that's what they recommend it for.

product.title: Wishlist for missing features
product.plus: Loyal users actively ask for additions — stop-loss and take-profit, a search across wallets, selling crypto in local currency — meaning they want to stay and see it grow.

product.title: Every update makes the app slower, not better
product.minus: The single most common complaint: after updates the wallet becomes painfully slow and laggy. Components reload on every transaction, switching accounts stutters, the app freezes — even copying an address becomes a chore. Users leave for Rabby, Zerion, OKX, which are "10 times better."

product.title: It used to be lean and simple — now it's bloated and reeks of "corporate"
product.minus: Veterans of 4-5 years remember how convenient the wallet used to be. New screens (trends, MetaMask card, ads and promos) and a pile of extra UI clutter have turned a self-custody wallet into something resembling a centralized exchange. Familiar features vanished and everything got harder.

product.title: Funds disappear or get stuck, and there's no support
product.minus: The heaviest reviews: people describe balances vanishing overnight, funds stuck in bridges and swaps, tokens that never arrive. Support is effectively absent, and the reply is "you did something." Some cases are phishing and drainers, but users blame the wallet for being helpless.

product.title: Balances show wrong figures or disappear entirely
product.minus: A distinct pain: the wallet shows inaccurate balance info — numbers jump, change, or disappear on their own. Users literally don't know how much they hold, and lose trust in the very point of a wallet.

product.title: Network switching is broken — you're stuck on Ethereum alone
product.minus: An update removed the network dropdown, so users can't switch to BNB, CoreDAO and other chains. Only Ethereum is active, balances on other networks are invisible — and MetaMask's own help still points to the old menu that no longer exists.

product.title: Crashes, closes, and won't open after updates
product.minus: The wallet crashes within a minute of opening, hangs on the loading screen, and won't let you enter your password to log in. On some phones (Redmi, Pixel) the app simply stops responding. Each update brings more crashes.

product.title: Importing a seed phrase doesn't restore old accounts
product.minus: A scary scenario: you enter your seed phrase but your old accounts don't appear — a fresh empty one opens instead. People seriously ask whether the version is fake. On top of that, accidentally created extra accounts can't be deleted, even after a reinstall.

product.title: False "no connection" errors with working internet
product.minus: A frequent bug: the app reports "no internet" or "unstable connection" while Wi-Fi is fine and every other app works. This leaves tokens and dApp connections hanging and transactions simply failing.

product.title: Won't connect to dApps, games and airdrops
product.minus: The wallet's core value is Web3 connectivity — and that's exactly what breaks: it won't connect to projects, airdrop games, third-party wallets like Safepal, or let you log into dApps via browsers. After the update, requests from web games are simply ignored.

product.title: Despite everything — the most stable and compatible wallet
product.plus: A loyal core sticks around for years: for many, MetaMask is the "gold standard" of non-custodial hot wallets, integrating with nearly every dApp and supporting all major chains. Even critics admit it works where others sometimes fail.

product.title: Simple and clear for managing crypto and Web3
product.plus: Those for whom the app works praise the clear interface, easy navigation and solid security options. For everyday holding of coins, tokens and dApp access they call it simple, beginner-friendly and one of the best in its class.

product.title: Funds get stuck in withdrawal for weeks and months
product.minus: The most common pain: withdrawals and transfers hang in "pending/confirming" for days, weeks, even years, leaving funds effectively locked inside the app with no explanation.

product.title: KYC verification fails and locks you out of your own money
product.minus: The app repeatedly rejects valid documents with no explanation and no way to re-upload, while already-verified accounts are suddenly asked to verify again — and access to funds is lost.

product.title: Support replies with templates or stays silent
product.minus: No phone, no human — just tickets and bots that reply with the same email on loop or vanish for weeks, leaving urgent money problems unresolved.

product.title: An app update breaks login into an endless loop
product.minus: After an update, login loops endlessly: the app keeps asking for the PIN or email confirmation, won't reach the wallet after 2FA, and reinstalling doesn't help.

product.title: Deposit goes through but the crypto never reaches the wallet
product.minus: The bank is debited, the Bitcoin purchase is "successful," yet the coins never appear in the wallet — they hang or show "failed," leaving the user with neither money nor crypto.

product.title: Users flat-out call the platform a scam
product.minus: The mix of stuck money, silent support, and locked accounts breeds a mass sense of fraud — people are convinced their funds were simply stolen, and they warn others off.

product.title: Swaps and in-wallet transfers are painfully slow
product.minus: Swaps, sends, and token exchanges drag on for hours, ERC20/Solana withdrawals hang, while rivals do the same near-instantly — assets get stuck mid-process.

product.title: High, opaque fees eat into your money
product.minus: Conversion, transfer, and swap fees feel predatory: inflated gas fees, percentages on USDC/USDT, high withdrawal minimums — the final amount often comes out at the "wrong price."

product.title: Losing the 12-word seed phrase = irreversible loss of funds
product.minus: There's no email-based recovery: forget the password and fail to save the 12 words (often without realizing how critical they are), and the wallet — and the money — is gone for good.

product.title: Accounts get disabled and locked with no reason and no email
product.minus: Years-old accounts are suddenly disabled "for compliance reasons" with no notice, wallet access disappears, and even creating a new account doesn't help — the money stays trapped inside.

product.title: Veterans praise the simple interface and no-account wallet
product.plus: For long-time users it's a beloved wallet that's simple even for newbies: everything works immediately with no sign-up, it's handy for holding Bitcoin, Solana and USDT, with a clean ad-free UI.

product.title: Fast local deposits and fiat conversion — where it works
product.plus: When it works smoothly, local deposits and fiat conversion are impressively fast: naira lands in the bank within seconds of withdrawal, deposits are "lightning fast," and failed transfers occasionally auto-refund.

product.title: Depositing takes a minute, withdrawing takes weeks
product.minus: Deposits clear instantly, but withdrawals leave people stuck for days and weeks: tickets sit unanswered, money "doesn't reflect," and some users never get their funds back at all.

product.title: There's no support, just an AI bot that solves nothing
product.minus: Reaching a human is nearly impossible: an AI bot answers with canned FAQ replies once every 10–25 minutes, tickets auto-close, and account managers are unreachable even for paying clients.

product.title: Fees at every step, despite the "commission-free" advertising
product.minus: You pay for everything: $1 to open and close a trade, $5 to withdraw, currency conversions, wide spreads, and overnight charges — users say fees eat all the profit, and the advertised "no commission" turns out to be untrue.

product.title: Copy trading is the headline feature people stay for
product.plus: The ability to copy experienced traders' moves and portfolios is exactly what people praise eToro for: beginners learn from others' decisions and get into the market without a strategy of their own.

product.title: Simple and clear — the best starting point for a beginner
product.plus: A clean interface and a low barrier to entry: people call eToro the simplest broker, an ideal first step into investing where you can start with small amounts and figure it out with no training.

product.title: Accounts get frozen with no explanation — and your money is inside
product.minus: Accounts get restricted and closed without a clear reason, sometimes right when trades are profitable: they suddenly demand a bank statement within 24 hours, lock access to the money, and threaten closure, leaving the user without their funds.

product.title: Positions close themselves, stop-losses fail to trigger
product.minus: People report trades closing randomly without their command, stop-losses failing or firing at the wrong price, and take-profit producing a loss instead of a gain — critical bugs for a trading app.

product.title: An update wiped watchlists and broke login
product.minus: After a recent update, watchlists and chart annotations vanished for many people, biometric login stopped working, and the app hangs on a white screen — years of work and familiar features gone with no warning.

product.title: Just a website in a wrapper: slow, glitchy, crashing
product.minus: The app is slow to start, lags, crashes on loading, and feels like a repackaged website rather than a native app — for real-time trading that's critical, and many compare it unfavorably to Trading 212.

product.title: Verification is an endless loop of rejected documents
product.minus: Uploading documents becomes torture: address and ID proof get rejected again and again even when files match the requirements, and the same requests repeat, leaving you unable to either trade or withdraw.

product.title: Feels like a scam: you sense your money will just be taken
product.minus: The accumulated stories — frozen funds, vanished coins, withheld "withdrawal fees" — leave many feeling it's outright fraud; reviews mention lawsuits and the word "scam" over and over.

product.title: The ISA account for UK users is a confusing trap with a third party
product.minus: UK users coming for a Cash ISA hit a mess: the account is dollar-based and run through third-party Moneyfarm, you can't fund the ISA from the main account, and getting back money you deposited by mistake costs a £5 fee — many leave for T212.

product.title: YouTube and email ads breed hatred before you even install
product.minus: Intrusive YouTube ads and a flood of emails (8 in 18 hours, none on topic) irritate people so much they download the app just to leave an angry review — pure anti-marketing.

product.title: Pushes CFDs instead of real stocks and ETFs
product.minus: Users notice the platform steering them toward CFDs instead of real stocks and ETFs, where fees and conversions eat all profit; on top of that the toolset is limited — no API, missing ETFs, and no crypto for small accounts.

product.title: Pulling out of markets leaves users locked out of their funds
product.minus: When the exchange stops serving a country (e.g. the USA), people complain that access to funds and accrued perks simply vanishes and emails go unanswered.

product.title: Support moves the goalposts instead of actually helping
product.minus: In disputes users follow every step and submit documents, only to be asked for more papers without being told which ones, and the issue drags on unresolved for years.

product.title: Token delistings turn into a rip-off on withdrawal fees
product.minus: The exchange delists a coin and forces you to withdraw or forfeit it, but the withdrawal fee eats a huge chunk of the investment — e.g. 300 ATEM tokens just to withdraw ATEM.

product.title: High, unexpected fees for holding and transacting
product.minus: Users complain the exchange is "stingy": they get hit with lots of fees, including just for storing crypto on the platform.

product.title: Frozen accounts and murky deductions destroy trust
product.minus: After years of using the card and app, people hit suspicious deductions and end up leaving for other services for peace of mind.

product.title: Fake KuCoin clones confuse newcomers
product.minus: People download the app thinking it's the real KuCoin (e.g. for Hamster) and find a fake that's useless for their purpose.

product.title: Futures leverage seems to work against the trader
product.minus: A trader describes leverage automatically rising when the position moves against them and falling when it goes their way, which feels like rigged mechanics.

product.title: This app duplicates the main one and feels redundant
product.minus: Some users see no point in this app: everything it does is already in the main KuCoin app and other crypto services.

product.title: Missing a proper portfolio view and findable settings
product.minus: Users ask for a portfolio like Kraken's and Trade Republic's and get lost in the new version, unable to find settings and their UID.

product.title: Loyal traders praise it as the best exchange they've tried
product.plus: Some users call KuCoin one of the best crypto apps they've used so far and give it top marks.

product.title: The free tier strips away the basics: you can't pick a specific song
product.minus: Without premium you have no control: you can't choose a track, can't turn off shuffle, skips are capped — the app decides what plays. Users say it stops being a music app at all.

product.title: Ads come in walls: several spots per couple of songs
product.minus: The top free-tier complaint is ad frequency: "5 ads per 2 songs," minute-long spots, ads before the app even opens. Killing the "30 minutes ad-free" perk pushes people over the edge.

product.title: Crashes and black screens after updates — even for paying users
product.minus: After a recent update (6/16/26) the app crashes on launch, hangs on a black screen, or closes mid-song. Reinstalling and clearing cache don't help, and it's premium subscribers who get hit.

product.title: The new widget broke what used to work
product.minus: Forcibly swapping the compact widget for a big 4×2 one is a widespread pain: the new one constantly buffers, shows no artwork, won't open the app, and eats a third of the home screen. People beg for the old one back.

product.title: Ads leak through even to those paying to avoid them
product.minus: Some premium users still get ads and banners they specifically pay to avoid — especially "Advertisement 1 of 1" inserts between podcasts. It reads as a breach of the deal, not a glitch.

product.title: Pushy auto-connect and ignored playback settings
product.minus: Music starts itself on other devices, plays where it wasn't launched, kicks in at night with the app closed, and shuffle keeps running even when it's off. You lose control over your own playback.

product.title: Price hikes and a sense of greed push people to rivals
product.minus: Price increases, features yanked from the student plan, and a general "money hungry" feel are driving long-time subscribers to Apple Music and YouTube Music. Years of loyalty don't offset feeling milked.

product.title: Login breaks: endless loading and "Something went wrong"
product.minus: Users can't log in even with the right password: endless loading, network errors, getting signed out after one album. Search also fails with "Something went wrong," and there's barely any in-app help.

product.title: Charged money — premium never unlocked, support is silent
product.minus: The payment goes through but premium doesn't activate; some are charged multiple times. There's no live support, replies are canned, and people resort to PayPal refunds.

product.title: Recommendations and auto-playlists nail your taste
product.plus: Users' biggest love is the algorithm: Discover Weekly, Daily Mixes, and "cruise control" off your liked songs match taste so well that people discover new artists and never want it to stop.

product.title: A huge library: almost everything is there
product.plus: A strength even critics admit: "100 million songs at your fingertips." People find childhood tracks, obscure recordings, and music from any country — over years of searching it rarely lets them down.

product.title: Podcasts, audiobooks, and cross-platform reach in one app
product.plus: Beyond music, people value that Spotify carries podcasts and audiobooks, hooks seamlessly into Alexa and Wi-Fi speakers, plays in the background across apps, and ties the account to concerts and ticketing.

product.title: Premium with lossless and yearly Wrapped feels worth it
product.plus: Long-time subscribers and family/Duo plans call premium the one subscription worth paying for: crystal-clear sound, lossless, no ads, and the beloved year-end Wrapped recaps.

product.title: The deepest catalog is the main, often only, reason people stay
product.plus: The fans almost always land on one thing: it has everything. Live versions, rare covers, remixes, user uploads and music videos you can't find elsewhere. For serious listeners this outweighs every other gripe.

product.title: Every update breaks something that used to work
product.minus: The single most common complaint: an update lands and something dies — casting, search, queue, downloads. People literally describe a "worked fine, then they changed it, now it's broken" loop. For some, uninstalling the update is the only way to get the feature back.

product.title: Removed features: Explore, Related, Up Next, start-radio
product.minus: Redesigns keep stripping out beloved features. The loudest losses are the Explore, Related and Up Next buttons, plus the ability to manually start a radio by artists and mood. People name exactly what they want back.

product.title: Moving the search bar is a mass irritant
product.minus: Relocating the search bar from the familiar top of the screen sparked its own wave of anger — even five-star reviewers beg for it to go back. On top of that, the search button sometimes just disappears.

product.title: Playback stops on its own — even on premium and offline
product.minus: The most painful technical complaint: playback randomly stops. Songs cut off mid-track, the queue empties, offline tracks go silent without internet, and the app has to be force-stopped. Premium payers are especially furious about what they're paying for.

product.title: Downloads and offline are unreliable
product.minus: Offline is a sore spot. Downloads never finish or auto-delete, a downloaded playlist loads slowly or can't be found in search, and when Wi-Fi drops the app tries to stream an already-downloaded track and stalls. Premium doesn't save you here.

product.title: The algorithm has slid into AI slop and no-name covers
product.minus: Recommendations, once a strength, have degraded. Mix and autoplay push AI-generated tracks and no-name covers — users are convinced it's a royalty-dodge. Shuffle replays the same 50 songs out of a 600-track playlist.

product.title: Playlist and library management is clumsy
product.minus: The library is cluttered with subscriptions and auto-playlists you can't remove, while your own playlists sit at the very bottom. Songs won't delete from private playlists, won't save to Liked, and there's no manual sorting or reordering of tracks.

product.title: Background play is locked behind premium
product.minus: Not being able to listen with the screen off without premium feels like a slap — especially since Spotify gives it for free. For many it's the deciding reason to switch to a competitor.

product.title: An ad after every single song on free
product.minus: The free tier is buried in ads — literally one after every song, plus constant premium-upsell pop-ups. The non-skippable foreign-language ads and aggressive online-gambling spots that can't be turned off are the worst offenders.

product.title: Billing and subscription: charged without consent, can't cancel
product.minus: Serious money complaints: double charges with no refund, payment goes through but premium never activates, you can't cancel a trial or subscription, and a forced "free" trial that then bills you. This isn't bugs — it's lost trust.

product.title: Podcasts are broken: feeds don't update
product.minus: After Google Podcasts shut down, people moved here and deeply regret it. Podcast feeds don't fetch new episodes for weeks, playback jumps around the episode, the queue falls apart, and podcast search is helpless. Many end up hunting for another app.

product.title: Doesn't remember where you left off
product.minus: The app loses your listening context: instead of resuming where you stopped, it launches a random song or jumps back to a search from a week ago. History doesn't even show the tracks you actually played.

product.title: The bundle with YouTube Premium is genuinely convenient
product.plus: People who already have YouTube Premium love that music comes bundled in — one subscription kills ads in both video and music. For many that's the very reason they left Spotify: the savings are real.

product.title: Casting to speakers and TVs constantly breaks
product.minus: The Google-flagship paradox: the app can't see its own Google Home, Nest and Chromecast devices. Casting breaks especially after updates, while other services and YouTube TV cast fine. For home-speaker users this is a dealbreaker.

product.title: No light theme, equalizer, or volume normalization
product.minus: Basics that competitors have had for years are simply missing: a light theme (dark-only), an equalizer, volume normalization, crossfade, mono/stereo choice. The sudden volume jumps between tracks are a pain of their own.

product.title: AI features feel forced and irritating
product.minus: Users didn't ask for AI and want it gone. The AI DJ with its gushing generated monologues is grating enough that decade-long subscribers threaten to quit, and there's no way to leave the beta. The vibe: AI gets shoved in instead of fixing what's broken.

product.title: Endless crashes and freezing
product.minus: Stability is shaky: a black screen instead of the UI, crashes when switching between apps, freezes when changing playlists, complaints about excessive CPU use. Even on new Pixels people regularly clear cache and force-stop just to keep it usable.

product.title: A second paywall on top of Prime: "paying twice for the same thing"
product.minus: What was bundled with Prime for years has been carved out into a separate paid Music Unlimited tier. Users see it as paying twice and a broken promise: "I already pay for Prime, why pay for music too?" For many it's the trigger to leave for Spotify or YouTube Music.

product.title: Ads that weren't there before: sudden interruptions even for Prime users
product.minus: The new policy injected ads even for paying Prime members, with no warning, mid-year. Reviewers keep drawing the parallel with how Prime Video "slyly" introduced ads and an extra fee to remove them — people feel cheated.

product.title: Music simply won't play: the track "loads" but no sound comes out
product.minus: The single most common technical complaint: pick a track and it spins forever or plays for a minute and cuts out — even on a stable connection, even on downloaded files. Reinstalling and clearing cache only helps for a while.

product.title: Constant crashes: opens and instantly shuts down
product.minus: The app crashes multiple times a day, sometimes right after launch, and the back button exits the whole app. Updates make it worse; the only fix is reinstalling or restarting the phone.

product.title: Downloads don't stay downloaded: offline mode breaks
product.minus: Downloaded tracks "expire" after a week, demand re-downloading every day, and still try to stream instead of playing from the device. For anyone who pays specifically for offline (car, no-signal commute), it kills the whole point.

product.title: You can't play music you bought: "I own it but can't access it"
product.minus: A distinct wound for long-time buyers of Amazon MP3s: purchased tracks don't show in the library, won't download to the device, and now even demand a subscription to access. People spent hundreds "to own" the music — and lost access.

product.title: Shuffle and playlists go rogue: the same loop over and over
product.minus: Shuffle replays the same cluster of songs, ignores autoplay being switched off, jumps to unrelated artists, and resets the playlist to the start after a pause. Controlling your own queue is nearly impossible.

product.title: Pushy upsell popups with an accidental-subscribe trap
product.minus: Every launch greets you with a full-screen Music Unlimited banner, and the buttons are laid out so you subscribe by accident before you can hit the tiny "no thanks." It's especially nasty in driving mode — people genuinely lost money on a subscription they never wanted.

product.title: Cluttered, unintuitive UI and a sluggish search
product.minus: The interface is called busy and stressful (compared to "what killed iTunes"), basics like the sleep timer and sorting are buried, and there's no A-Z jump for large libraries. Search got slower after AI was added — minutes instead of seconds.

product.title: A huge, deep catalog — the main reason to stay
product.plus: Even angry users admit the catalog is vast — rare, niche, and old albums turn up that others don't have. For many it's the sheer breadth of the library that outweighs all the technical sins.

product.title: High-fidelity audio: Ultra HD, Atmos, 360 — for audiophiles
product.plus: Audio-quality buffs praise HD/Ultra HD, Dolby Atmos, and 360 Reality Audio — for some listeners the sound alone is what keeps them subscribed. The built-in equalizer also gets called out as a plus.

product.title: Alexa and all-in-one: music, podcasts and audiobooks together
product.plus: Alexa and multi-room integration, plus having music, podcasts and audiobooks in one app, make it a convenient "one-stop shop" for happy users and a natural fit inside the Prime ecosystem.

product.title: A long free trial — a welcoming on-ramp for newcomers
product.plus: The 3-4 month trial is longer than rivals' and is repeatedly called the best offer anywhere — it pulls in people tired of Spotify and lets them try the service without pressure.

product.title: Podcasts treated as a stepchild: loses your place, mangles order, jumps to the newest episode
product.minus: For podcasts the app is nearly unusable: it forgets the last episode, plays out of order regardless of settings, and during music randomly jumps to your latest podcast. Subscriptions vanish and have to be re-followed.

product.title: Dolby Atmos and features quietly vanish: "degrades with every update"
product.minus: Long-time users report regression: Dolby Atmos support was pulled (support reportedly blamed Android), presets disappear, and perks like a free audiobook are gone. It feels like every update removes rather than adds.

product.title: Playback stops on its own and crashes mid-song
product.minus: The single most common pain: music randomly stops, throws an error or the app crashes outright — even for paying subscribers, on full signal, in the background. Force-stop and reinstall don't help, and it has dragged on for years.

product.title: An ethical Spotify alternative: pays artists and blocks AI music
product.plus: A large share of users came on principle — to get away from Spotify (politics, ICE ads, AI tracks). What keeps them is the sense that Deezer pays musicians more and filters out AI "slop."

product.title: HiFi sound quality is the main reason to switch and stay
product.plus: Listeners praise genuine lossless/CD-quality sound that is noticeably louder and cleaner than rivals — for many it outweighs every bug and justifies the price.

product.title: No free version in your country — but you find out after signing up
product.minus: Users create an account, hand over their email and age, pick 10 artists — and only then see "Deezer Free isn't available in your region, pay for Premium." Many read it as a dark pattern and delete the app on the spot.

product.title: Paywalls where rivals are free: 30-second clips, offline, lyrics
product.minus: Without a subscription a song plays for ~30 seconds, offline and lyrics moved behind Premium, and you can barely browse the catalog. The store listing promises free listening, and users call the gap deceptive — a "scam."

product.title: Flow and recommendations: magic for some, a 40-song loop for others
product.minus: The recommendation engine polarises: some worship Flow, but many complain the playlist loops the same ~40 tracks, drifts into a random genre, and the "don't play this" button changes nothing.

product.title: Casting to speakers, Alexa and Android Auto keeps breaking
product.minus: The link to Google Cast, Alexa, Bluetooth and Android Auto keeps dropping: music plays on both phone and speaker at once, controls vanish, and rebooting the phone is the only fix. In the car, ads lock the controls, which is outright unsafe.

product.title: Queue and "play next" are broken, especially offline
product.minus: Tracks added to the queue never play, "play next" disappears offline, and you can't queue favourites without a connection. The basic playback-control mechanic that rivals nail simply fails here.

product.title: Support replies with canned AI while year-old bugs go unfixed
product.minus: Users describe support as an AI bot repeating one answer and not reading the ticket; the promised escalation to a human never happens, and known bugs stay unfixed for months or years. Canned developer replies under reviews only add insult.

product.title: Library transfer from Spotify is easy and nearly lossless
product.plus: A key retention moment: thousands of tracks and playlists move over in minutes with only a handful lost. For many, the painless switch is exactly what made them stay.

product.title: Cancellation and account deletion are hidden, and charges keep coming
product.minus: The free trial turns into an instant full charge, cancellation and account deletion are buried (changing your password is easy — unsubscribing isn't), and refunds after cancelling are denied. Many call it theft.

product.title: AI music is flooding the catalog — against the core promise
product.minus: The main reason to switch — "no AI" — collapses: artist profiles are clogged with AI tracks and same-name imposters, and squatted songs slip into your likes via the converter. People who came precisely for a clean catalog leave disappointed.

product.title: Sound quality is the one reason people put up with Tidal
product.plus: Almost everyone praises the sound: Hi-Res, FLAC and Dolby Atmos clearly beat Spotify and the rest, and people forgive the app a lot for it.

product.title: Music cuts out mid-song with a "network error", even on solid Wi-Fi
product.minus: The single most common complaint: every other track the app throws a connection error and freezes, and only a force stop fixes it — even though Wi-Fi and 5G are perfectly fine.

product.title: Every UI update strips features and makes the app worse
product.minus: Redesigns keep coming: the progress bar and quality label are gone, lyrics got shoved to the top, and a floating player covers everything — users unanimously beg for the old look back.

product.title: Artist pages stop showing their albums and tracks
product.minus: A very common bug: open an artist and the albums, EPs and top tracks simply aren't there — just playlists and a bio. The only fix is leaving and re-entering, sometimes several times.

product.title: Downloaded tracks won't play offline — the core feature is broken
product.minus: Offline mode doesn't deliver: downloaded songs show up greyed out or "not available", playlists delete themselves and force you to re-download gigabytes, and the moment you lose signal the music is just gone.

product.title: Artists with the same name get lumped into one profile
product.minus: A long-standing, unfixed bug: different performers who share a name are merged into a single profile, so half the "new release" alerts are wrong and your feed fills with songs from the wrong artist.

product.title: Artist profiles are flooded with unlabelled AI "music"
product.minus: Feeds and real artists' pages are clogged with AI-generated slop anyone can upload under someone else's name; users demand an AI label and a block toggle, or they leave for Qobuz.

product.title: The app crashes and freezes, sometimes won't even open
product.minus: Crashes have become "part of the Tidal experience": it dies when adding to a playlist, when opening an album, hangs on the splash screen — and reinstalling or clearing cache doesn't help.

product.title: Android Auto and Tidal Connect are the weakest link
product.minus: In the car and on external gear everything falls apart: Tidal Connect drops from streamers, Android Auto never remembers your place in a playlist, Waze and Google Maps integration is gone, and Sonos/HEOS links keep breaking.

product.title: Search can't find tracks that are clearly in the catalog
product.minus: Search routinely returns "no match found" even with both title and artist typed in, and you can't search inside your own playlist — you scroll by hand. Everyone agrees Spotify is clearly better here.

product.title: The ethical choice: fair artist payouts and no ICE ads
product.plus: Many switched from Spotify on principle — Tidal pays artists 3-4x more and runs no ICE ads — and they'll endure the clunky app for that reason alone.

product.title: Playback doesn't resume where you left off
product.minus: A basic thing every rival has: if the app sits in the background even an hour, the queue empties and you must start the session over — especially maddening in the car via Android Auto.

product.title: You pay for a subscription but only get 30-second previews
product.minus: A harsh billing-and-access bug: people pay for premium or renew, yet the app still serves only 15-30 second previews — and support refuses refunds.

product.title: Shuffle replays the same 30-50 songs on a loop
product.minus: "Shuffle" really just loops a narrow handful of recently added tracks and ignores the rest of a library of hundreds; in Android Auto it only cycles the oldest ~100 songs.

product.title: When a redesign finally lands, users notice
product.plus: It's not all grim: some recent updates get praise — the new now-playing is handier, offline lyrics arrived, you can finally filter playlists when adding a track, and the app feels more stable.

product.title: A unique library: remixes and underground tracks found nowhere else
product.plus: The main reason people stay for years — remixes, leaks, independent artists and rare versions of songs you won't find on Spotify or YouTube Music. For music lovers it's irreplaceable crate-digging.

product.title: Ads have become unbearable: two or three in a row after every song
product.minus: Ads used to come every 5-10 songs; now it's 30-90 seconds after every 1-3 tracks, sometimes three in a row. Long-time users say outright: you won't annoy me into paying.

product.title: Constant crashes and music stopping for no reason
product.minus: The app crashes several times a day, songs cut off after 30 seconds, playlists hang. Even paying subscribers complain the track just stops mid-listen.

product.title: Favourite songs blocked by country geo-restrictions
product.minus: Globally known artists and favourite tracks are marked "not available in your country" — songs that play easily on other apps. It hits listeners in India, Brazil and poorer countries hardest.

product.title: The free tier is being gutted: downloads and popular tracks behind a paywall
product.minus: What used to be free now needs a subscription: offline downloads removed from the free tier, and popular or iconic songs locked behind Go+. Users feel they're being milked.

product.title: Free background play even with the screen locked
product.plus: A big draw is background play with the screen off while gaming or using other apps — all on the free tier, unlike the "greedy" Spotify.

product.title: Liked songs and playlists vanishing on their own
product.minus: Users lose hundreds of likes at once, playlists disappear, and past 1000 playlists the old ones start getting deleted. Like a song and it vanishes a second later.

product.title: Music auto-plays and hijacks audio from other apps
product.minus: A SoundCloud-specific bug: the app starts playing on its own even after being closed — in the car, or over Instagram/YouTube audio. No other media player behaves this way.

product.title: Better than Spotify: discovery without recycling the same tracks
product.plus: A constant comparison in SoundCloud's favour: it doesn't loop your same liked songs over and over but genuinely surfaces new artists in the vibe you picked. Many left Spotify for exactly this.

product.title: Can't create an account or log in, and support stays silent
product.minus: Some people can't even get started: sign-up fails after 10-20 tries and support requests go unanswered. After reinstalling, the app won't log back into the account.

product.title: An ethical platform for indie artists, yet its subscription squeezes them too
product.plus: Many are won over by the mission: SoundCloud uplifts the underground, gives a stage to little-known artists and is seen as the most "ethical" platform. Yet artists complain they pay more in subscriptions than they earn back.

product.title: Sound quality and streaming stability falter, especially over Bluetooth
product.minus: Complaints about no 320 kbps option, choppy audio over Bluetooth, lag and delays when switching tracks. Music lags and pauses unless you pay for Go+.

product.title: The redesign copies Spotify and is worse than the old one
product.minus: Long-time users dislike the redesign: the playlist "last modified" section is gone, getting to an artist's profile is harder, and the iconic cloud logo went from white to black — "it just looks like a copy of Spotify now".

product.title: Crashes and freezes mid-listen
product.minus: The top complaint: the app drops after a song or two, freezes, force-closes itself and dumps you on the home screen — even for paying subscribers, and whether it's open or backgrounded.

product.title: Too many ads — two spots between songs
product.minus: The free tier has effectively vanished: ads land after every one or two songs, the same spots repeat and got louder, and some users get intrusive, off-topic ads on top of it.

product.title: Stations repeat themselves and bleed in wrong genres
product.minus: The algorithm loops the same songs and blends in artists from completely different genres — rock mixes with rap, and stations barely play the very artist you picked.

product.title: Suddenly walls off what used to be free
product.minus: Longtime free users suddenly hit a paywall: skip limits, can't play a station without paying, and an upgrade prompt after every song — it reads as plain greed.

product.title: Drains battery and hogs the background
product.minus: The app keeps running in the background and burns through battery; the phone itself suggests putting it in deep sleep, and users have to force-stop it after every use.

product.title: Self-launches and opens from other apps' ads
product.minus: The app launches on its own — from ads inside other games, on Bluetooth or Android Auto connect, even with autoplay off; one user got woken up by music at 6:30 in the morning.

product.title: Ignores thumbs-down and won't let you block an artist
product.minus: The system ignores dislikes: thumbs-downed artists return almost every other song, you can't block a whole artist, and 'licensing requirements' force unwanted tracks to play out.

product.title: Music keeps stopping and won't play in the background
product.minus: Playback goes silent mid-song, the queue stalls, and music cuts out when the screen turns off or you switch apps — hitting paying users too.

product.title: Constant 'session timed out' and won't load
product.minus: The app sticks on 'session timed out' or wrongly claims you're outside the US, refuses to load even on Wi-Fi, and reinstalling doesn't help — locking out longtime subscribers.

product.title: Impossible to cancel, and they bill after you cancel
product.minus: Cancelling becomes a fight: no clear button on the site, charges continue after you cancel, refunds get denied, and the support bot gives the runaround — some cancel their card just to escape.

product.title: Clunky interface — editing stations takes too many steps
product.minus: Navigation is awkward: cleaning up a station, deleting a song from a playlist, or making a station from a playlist takes endless back-and-forth, and some actions only work on the desktop site.

product.title: Thumbprint station: easy to build your own mix for any mood
product.plus: Fans love the personalized radio specifically: within a couple of days it learns your taste, builds a thumbprint station from your likes, and surfaces new artists — the very reason people stay.

product.title: Solid free radio with short ads
product.plus: A chunk of users praise the free tier specifically: a wide music selection without paying, ads shorter and less frequent than Spotify's, plus one of the cheapest ad-free plans around.

product.title: Broad genre range — from jazz to K-pop
product.plus: Those who stay value the variety: jazz, blues, rock, country, soul, oldies, K-pop — Pandora offers wider choice and better variety than many rivals.

product.title: Offline downloads are the whole reason people stay
product.plus: Users value not just streaming but downloading to listen offline — in the car, on a hilly ride, with no wifi. It comes up again and again as the core use case.

product.title: Ads before downloads: three clips per single song
product.minus: Downloading one song now means watching three ads, and the close X first throws you into Play Store or shopping apps 2-3 times. Accidentally swipe the app away and you reopen it to watch three ads all over again.

product.title: The folk verdict: "better than Spotify"
product.plus: Over and over the app gets compared to Spotify and ranked above it — for free downloads and far less ad-choking while actually listening.

product.title: Downloading is dead simple — that IS the product
product.plus: Ease of downloading is the most-praised thing: "so easy to download," "very easy downloading, wow." For many it's the first app where they ever got their favorite music at all.

product.title: Some tracks won't download — or just aren't there
product.minus: Some can't download to their phone at all, others find the songs they want missing from the catalog. "The best but I can't download all the songs" is a typical caveat even in five-star reviews.

product.title: A vast catalog of every kind of music
product.plus: People feel they can find anything here: "whatever you want at any given time," "every phonk possible," music from everywhere — one user even downloads the Qur'an.

product.title: A premium wall on some favorite tracks
product.minus: Not everything is free: some favorite songs require premium. One user explicitly asks for a lifetime purchase — that would make it a five-star app, "almost there."

product.title: Flexible playback: slowed, sped up
product.plus: You can play a track the way you like it — slowed, sped up — and then download it that way too. For fans that's a feature in itself.

product.title: Music pauses on its own
product.minus: A bug slips through that breaks the core listening flow: the app keeps pausing the music for no clear reason.

product.title: Lyrics are missing from many songs
product.minus: A recurring request: add lyrics to every song. Right now some tracks have none, and it's the one thing keeping otherwise delighted users from full satisfaction.

product.title: Fast search — but gated by your data
product.plus: Search is praised for speed, with a key caveat: "very fast in searching songs when you have enough data." Without data the speed disappears.

product.title: You pick a song and it plays a «recommendation» instead
product.minus: The single most common complaint: pick a specific track and the app diverts you to «similar» or «cool» recommended songs, refusing to let you hear the one you actually chose. Many quit over exactly this.

product.title: Playback stops on its own and the app crashes
product.minus: After recent updates the music cuts out when switching to other apps, opening the lock screen, or getting a notification, and the app crashes constantly — for some this has dragged on for years.

product.title: The library is shrinking: songs vanish from likes and playlists
product.minus: It reads like losing licences from major labels: whole albums disappear (The Weeknd, Taylor Swift, Drake) and hundreds of saved tracks vanish straight from playlists and likes. People cancel their subscription specifically over this.

product.title: Too many ads, even in basic scenarios
product.minus: On the free tier ads run after every song, and basics like lyrics, repeat, rewind and playing in order are locked behind a subscription. For many it builds up until they uninstall.

product.title: Search is weak: it misses even an exact title
product.minus: The search engine is outdated and has no smart ranking: it surfaces unofficial covers instead of the original even when you type the exact title, and sometimes returns no results at all for a favourite artist.

product.title: Opaque charges and unwanted billing
product.minus: Money gets deducted for a subscription the user never signed up for, renewals happen with no warning, and support doesn't respond. It escalates to threats of legal action over unauthorized charges.

product.title: Regional blocks cut access to the catalog
product.minus: A paid subscription doesn't guarantee access: songs play for only 30 seconds as if «not Arabic», new Amr Diab albums are unavailable outside MENA, and users in Syria and elsewhere lose half their library entirely.

product.title: Lyrics view «swipes» you to the next track
product.minus: Trying to scroll the lyrics, the slightest deviation from a straight line is read as a swipe to the next song — making it impossible to calmly read along or skip between lyric sections.

product.title: The huge Arabic-music library is what users love most
product.plus: What the app is genuinely loved for: nearly all your favourite music is there, especially Arabic artists like Amr Diab, plus solid sound quality. For Middle Eastern music lovers it's the top choice.

product.title: Cheaper than rivals with a generous free tier
product.plus: Fans see it as a better-value alternative to Spotify: the subscription is cheaper, there's a free trial month, and you can listen for free even without premium. Via Vodafone Flex/Red, premium comes free.

product.title: Spot-on personalization and long-standing loyalty
product.plus: Those the algorithm works for praise how precisely it reads their taste, and stay for years — since 2012, whole families, no glitches and great sound. This is the loyal core.

product.title: Podcasts and religious content are a distinct draw
product.plus: Part of the audience comes for the full Quran with every reciter and for educational, including religious, podcasts — something rivals lack, and it keeps niche users around.

product.title: Playlists built over decades vanished overnight with no warning
product.minus: The core pain: users open the app to find playlists they spent years building are empty or cut down to a couple of songs. No notice, no chance to export first — just gone. For many these were sentimental collections (anniversaries, kids' songs), and the loss feels deeply personal.

product.title: Turning a music service into an AI song generator nobody asked for
product.minus: Users are furious that real-artist streaming was swapped for AI-generated music. It reads as a slap in the face to human musicians and a bait-and-switch: people pay for a catalog and get a "slop machine" with credits. The AI songs themselves are described as generic garbage that doesn't even do what you ask.

product.title: The real-artist catalog got gutted — whole labels and older music gone
product.minus: Huge chunks of the library disappeared: 200+ track playlists collapse to 17-32, well-known artists no longer come up in search. Users tie it to unpaid royalties and a Sony lawsuit, with mostly music from the last 5-6 years left. They describe it as "a music app with no music."

product.title: Downloaded offline tracks that were paid for got wiped too
product.minus: Even music downloaded for offline listening vanished — the thing people relied on while traveling or on the road. Some had bought individual tracks and "lifetime access" back in the Rhapsody days, and those purchases are gone too. It feels like paid-for content was simply taken away.

product.title: Still billing for a service that effectively no longer exists
product.minus: The subscription keeps charging for months even though there's been no music since September 2025. People who paid a year up front are left with no catalog. The company replies with a canned apology about a "temporary inconvenience" but gives no end date — users feel they're paying for a lie.

product.title: Cancelling the subscription is nearly impossible — the option was removed
product.minus: Cancelling is turned into a maze: in-app account management was removed, the website won't load, password reset fails. Some can't get out for ages and consider just having their bank block the charges. The subscription feels like a trap.

product.title: No real support — requests get the same recycled paragraph
product.minus: There's no way to reach a human: the phone doesn't work, emails don't reach the right team, and every request gets the same generated reply. Refund demands are ignored. It deepens the sense of abandonment for customers of 15-20 years.

product.title: Refunds are refused, and "class action" keeps coming up
product.minus: People who bought annual plans are denied refunds on a "14-day window" technicality while getting no service at all. The outrage is so widespread that reviewers openly rally each other toward a class action and threaten Better Business Bureau complaints.

product.title: Broken login: "signed in on another device," password reset fails
product.minus: After the update many simply can't log in: the app says you're signed in on another device, the saved password is rejected, and reset emails don't arrive. Some can't even register with email and are forced to use Google. Account and music access is lost out of nowhere.

product.title: The app crashes and won't play music after the update
product.minus: Beyond the catalog loss, the app itself runs badly: it crashes, won't load playlists, and either plays tracks partway or not at all. Some have to restart their phone after a few songs to keep listening. The basic playback function is broken.

product.title: Deep 15-25 year loyalty, burned by a single update
product.plus: Beneath the bitterness is rare devotion: people stayed since the Rhapsody era, 15-26 years, discovered countless 60s-70s artists through it, and never left for competitors because "I had Rhapsody." That loyalty is the measure of what the company torched.

product.title: Zero warning about the format change — found out only by the wreckage
product.minus: The procedural grievance: the company changed the entire platform without notice. Worse, some got emails saying "nothing is changing," then logged in to find everything empty. Had there been a warning, they could have exported playlists to another service in time.

product.title: A mass exodus to Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music
product.minus: The reviews have effectively become an exit guide: people describe using TuneMyMusic and export tools to move playlists to Spotify or YouTube Music and cancel. Competitors even throw in a free first month. This is no longer scattered churn but a coordinated exodus of the whole base.

product.title: "Netflix Household" locks the paying user out of their own account
product.minus: The household check punishes the most loyal: people get logged out on their own phone, the "I'm Traveling" button never appears, and a family member — or the payer themselves — can't sign in, after years of paying.

product.title: Ads crept into the paid plans people bought specifically to avoid them
product.minus: Viewers pay a subscription and still get 5-6 ad breaks per episode, ads louder than the show itself, and a sense of betrayal — escaping ads was the whole reason they left cable.

product.title: Favorite shows vanish from the catalog and get cancelled mid-story
product.minus: The catalog — the whole point — undercuts itself: series get pulled, good shows get axed after one season leaving viewers without an ending, and there's less and less reason to keep paying.

product.title: Video just won't play: endless loading, black or green screen
product.minus: A widespread playback failure: hit play and the screen goes black or green, content spins on loading forever, and reinstalling or clearing cache doesn't fix it.

product.title: Forcing an email onto every profile feels like data-harvesting
product.minus: The new requirement to attach a separate email to each profile reads as invasive data collection and selling, the popup blocks profile access, and people threaten to cancel over exactly this.

product.title: Charges continue after cancellation, payments don't reach the account
product.minus: A painful money knot: people get charged after cancelling, plans get upgraded without consent, and a paid subscription doesn't register in the app — account on hold, money gone.

product.title: Prices climb while value shrinks — a growing sense of greed
product.minus: Steady price hikes alongside show cancellations, ads and capped 1080p (4K only on premium) build a consistent narrative: the company gets pricier and greedier every year.

product.title: Missing regional dubs and subtitles users already paid for
product.minus: Viewers in India and other regions pay full price but get no Hindi/Tamil dub or subtitles — and language availability isn't shown before payment, which feels like a bait-and-switch.

product.title: Signing in and creating an account is a nightmare of email verification
product.minus: Email-link sign-in breaks down: a link-less email, a loop back to "create account" in the Android app, a demand to verify the device with someone else's phone — kicking people out of their own subscription.

product.title: Casting to TV got cut, pushing you to buy an extra device
product.minus: Screen casting was deliberately disabled on ad plans, unlike rival services — so to watch on the big screen you now have to buy a separate device.

product.title: DRM silently drops HD to SD — Widevine L1 falls back to L3
product.minus: On L1-capable devices the quality suddenly drops to L3/SD, and the only workaround is reinstalling the app before every viewing; DRM only inconveniences paying customers.

product.title: When it works, it's the benchmark: catalog, smoothness and offline downloads
product.plus: For a huge share of viewers Netflix stays the gold standard: a massive library of films, series and originals, smooth buffer-free streaming, spot-on recommendations and offline downloads for travel.

product.title: Recommendations and a slick interface that "know you better than yourself"
product.plus: A clean, fast, intuitive interface with the "My Netflix" tab makes it easy to resume on any device, and personalized recommendations reliably hit the viewer's taste.

product.title: Some viewers still believe the paid plan is genuinely ad-free
product.plus: For those on the ad-free plan, the absence of ads remains the killer argument for Netflix over rivals that still run ads even on paid tiers.

product.title: "Error code 9" — mass login lockout after an update
product.minus: After yet another update the app stops letting people into their account and dead-ends on "error code 9": login fails on the phone, the TV and the console alike. Reinstalling, clearing cache and updating the system change nothing, and the error code itself is documented nowhere.

product.title: Black screen after the ad — finishing an episode is impossible
product.minus: The defining pain for paying subscribers: after an ad break the screen goes black and playback never resumes. You have to quit, restart the episode, and hit the same ad again, trapped in an endless loop.

product.title: Too many ads on a paid plan — and pay more to remove them
product.minus: Subscribers are furious that a 20-minute episode can carry six ad breaks, with ads that often aren't even relevant. What stings most is that the company changed the rules mid-season and now charges extra just to get the ads "mostly" off.

product.title: Won't launch at all — endless loading or an "update" that does nothing
product.minus: For some users the app never even reaches the login screen: it loads forever or sits on a black screen saying "update" when there's nothing to update. The uninstall-reinstall cycle repeats over and over with no result.

product.title: Downloaded offline movies demand internet — the point of downloading is lost
product.minus: Episodes downloaded "for offline" refuse to play without a connection: the app randomly signs you out offline and demands you go online. On a flight or on the road this kills the entire point of downloading content ahead of time.

product.title: Constant buffering and mid-movie drops blamed on "no internet"
product.minus: Playback breaks for no reason: endless buffering, the movie freezes and claims "no connection" while other services stream in HD on the same network. Restarting doesn't help — sometimes you can only resume a couple of days later.

product.title: Broken on TVs and consoles — Google TV, Bravia, Android TV
product.minus: The app is especially unstable off the phone: on Google TV it won't get past the logo, on Bravia it won't resume after ads, on Android TV it keeps crashing. Users feel the big screen has simply been forgotten.

product.title: Broken navigation controls — Skip Intro, Next Episode, fast-forward
product.minus: Basic player controls fail: the skip-intro button doesn't respond, "next episode" crashes the app, and autoplay won't queue the next one. Skip Intro sometimes jumps to a random future episode entirely.

product.title: Rising price against falling quality and a shrinking catalog
product.minus: The subscription has been hiked up to double, and users directly compare it to Netflix while questioning what they pay for: content gets removed, new movies hit Amazon first, and the app glitches all the while.

product.title: Cancellation and billing are made deliberately murky
product.minus: Users complain that canceling is hard: the subscription doesn't show up in Google Play, the website won't let you cancel, and charges keep coming with no notice. Many read it as a deliberate trap to squeeze out maximum money.

product.title: The franchise catalog — the main reason people stay despite everything
product.plus: When the app works, the content is genuinely loved: Marvel, Pixar, Star Wars, Bluey, Gravity Falls and old Disney classics bring the whole family together. Many keep the subscription for years precisely for this library and the nostalgia of childhood cartoons.

product.title: A simple, family-friendly interface — when the bugs stay out of the way
product.plus: Those whose app is stable praise it for being easy: clear navigation, handy profiles, good picture quality and a family-friendly format. For many it's their main everyday app and a way to spend the evening with the kids.

product.title: You pay for the subscription and still drown in ads
product.minus: The number-one complaint: ads run even for paying users, often two-minute breaks every few minutes of show. People literally time it and conclude a third of their paid viewing is spent on commercials.

product.title: The "ad-free" tier still shows ads
product.minus: A distinct fury comes from people who paid extra for the ad-free version or got it via a phone plan: ads appear anyway, sometimes through ESPN. Users call it a lie and outright fraud.

product.title: The player constantly loses your place in a show
product.minus: A years-old bug: on resuming a series the app either restarts the episode, jumps to its last two minutes, or skips ahead to the next one. People restart the app just to fix playback.

product.title: Freezing, buffering and crashes instead of watching
product.minus: A very common complaint: endless buffering, freezes every few minutes and crashes across phone, Fire TV, Xbox and smart TVs. Users stress that other streamers work fine on the same connection while Hulu doesn't.

product.title: The Disney merger turned login into a nightmare
product.minus: After logins were merged with Disney, users can't sign in, get kicked mid-show and forced to re-login — sometimes several times a day and weekly. Some can't even cancel because they can't get in.

product.title: Content is locked behind endless add-ons and "upgrades"
product.minus: Users are frustrated that movies and shows once included now require separate add-ons, and live TV is gated behind a pricier ESPN plan. They feel pushed into paying twice over.

product.title: Casting, activation and multi-device setup are broken
product.minus: Bought on the phone but can't watch on TV; trying to activate a device hits endless steps; casting breaks and cross-device sync glitches. Simple actions become a quest.

product.title: Audio description turns itself on, and the sound misbehaves
product.minus: A known, unfixed bug: the monotone AI audio-description voice turns on even when the setting is off. Plus ads blast far louder than the show, the first seconds after a break are muted, and voices don't match lips.

product.title: Billing is opaque: overcharges, a hidden payment page, no way to cancel
