product.title: The advertised price turns into something else at checkout
product.minus: The price in the ad, the email or the product card is one thing, but in the cart and at payment it jumps up or a completely different sum is charged — classic bait-and-switch.

product.title: The "3 items for 99 cents" deal works as bait, not an offer
product.minus: The penny welcome deals either get cancelled after payment, or the coupon is killed for "account security", or finished off with extortionate shipping.

product.title: Support is a bot that exhausts you but never helps
product.minus: Instead of a human there's an AI bot and templated replies; no phone, no real help center, and users say support is built to wear you down.

product.title: Parcels vanish, and a "delivered" stamp kills any chance of a refund
product.minus: Orders get lost by couriers, marked delivered when they weren't, or sent to the wrong address — and the platform hides behind that stamp to deny refunds.

product.title: To return a defect, you're forced to pay return shipping to China
product.minus: Even with proven defects or fakes, the buyer is made to pay for tracked return shipping themselves, often costing more than the item, and offered coupons instead of cash.

product.title: Ads forcibly launch the app from inside other programs
product.minus: AliExpress ads pop up inside other apps, and the slightest tap or swipe launches it on its own, knocking you out of a game or task — users call it spyware-level behavior.

product.title: The new age check demands a selfie and a scan of your ID
product.minus: A sudden mandatory age verification demands biometrics and both sides of an ID even from decade-long customers, seen as data harvesting and a leak risk.

product.title: Gamification and popups get in the way of simply buying what you need
product.minus: Endless games, coins, popups and notifications turn buying into chaos: people switch to the browser or accidentally order the wrong thing just to reach what they wanted.

product.title: Hidden taxes and duties only surface on delivery
product.minus: Tax, duties and extra shipping aren't shown at purchase and land on the buyer at delivery, making a cheap item end up far costlier than promised.

product.title: You really can find great things for pennies, and that pays off
product.plus: When it works out, the delight is huge: people praise unbelievable prices and a giant selection of cosplay, clothes, gadgets and cute little things you can't get cheaper anywhere else.

product.title: Buyer protection does work — but only for some
product.plus: Some long-term loyal customers praise free returns, money back when an order is late, and the platform holding payment until confirmation — for them protection genuinely works.

product.title: Endless delays and slow shipping draw complaints
product.minus: Delivery dates slip routinely: items run weeks past estimate, tracking is useless, and couriers fake failed delivery attempts.

product.title: What arrives isn't what was pictured: fakes and wrong items
product.minus: Sellers send brand fakes, the wrong item or a stripped-down version, photos and descriptions mislead, and reviews look faked.

product.title: "Scam" has become the platform's defining label
product.minus: Buyers en masse describe the platform as fraudulent: money taken, item never sent or an empty box shipped, then the case closed — trust in the brand is shattered.

product.title: Payment methods break: G Pay and PayPal often fail
product.minus: Google Pay and PayPal payments regularly fail — the button does nothing, forcing a switch to PC or another method; many also miss local mobile-money options.

product.title: Unique, hard-to-find items are why people love Etsy
product.plus: Over and over, buyers say the same thing: Etsy has literally everything you can't get in a regular store — custom gifts, niche patterns, quirky finds. People compare browsing it to a great farmer's market.

product.title: Orders vanish and Etsy washes its hands of it
product.minus: The most painful theme: the item never arrives, the delivery date is endlessly pushed back, and once the cancel window closes Etsy declares it the buyer's problem. People lose tens to hundreds of dollars on packages that were never shipped.

product.title: AI slop and Temu resellers are crowding out real makers
product.minus: Loyal pattern and art buyers are furious: the feed is flooded with AI "creations" and stolen designs with no way to filter them out. Many say half the sellers just resell junk from Temu and AliExpress, and Etsy does nothing about it.

product.title: The makers and sellers are warm and responsive
product.plus: When a transaction goes well, it's the sellers who carry it: people praise quick replies, willingness to change a color or tweak an order, instant replacement of a defective item. Buyers return to the same makers for years and call them by name.

product.title: Support is effectively unreachable; accounts get hacked and suspended
product.minus: When something breaks, there's no help: requests go unanswered, the only contact channel is useless, and a hacked account drags on for months. Sellers have it worse — they pay to open a shop and it gets suspended immediately with no clear reason.

product.title: Refunds are swapped for Etsy credit — your money doesn't come back
product.minus: A distinct grievance: instead of a real refund, the system auto-issues Etsy credit. You're forced to spend it on the same platform and run into trouble again — people describe it as a loop of losing money over and over.

product.title: Shipping often costs more than the item itself
product.minus: Buyers complain shipping eats half the total, and the "free shipping" badge turns out to be a lie — the shop charges for it anyway. It's pushing several of them back to Amazon.

product.title: The app lags, freezes, and forgets your login
product.minus: Technically the app is rough: every cart click is a 20-second wait, checkout is nearly impossible, the sign-in screen hangs blank. After a break it forgets your credentials and you have to dig up and paste your password again.

product.title: You can't pay for multiple items in one checkout
product.minus: An annoying mechanic limit: items from different shops can't be paid for in one go — especially via Google Pay, where you pay per item. Buying three patterns means three separate checkouts.

product.title: Spammy notifications and autoplay videos in the feed
product.minus: The app bombards you with notifications day and night to nudge more purchases, and recently started greeting users with five simultaneously-playing "Behind the scenes" videos that can't be turned off and drain the battery.

product.title: Screenshots and access blocked "for security" — hurting gifting and downloads
product.minus: New restrictions infuriate long-time users: you can no longer screenshot an item to show family as a gift idea, can't print your own receipt, and digital patterns must be downloaded through a browser that keeps bouncing you back into the app.

product.title: The price jumps at checkout with no explanation
product.minus: It enrages buyers that the real total only surfaces on the last screen: the price doubles because of hidden shipping, and for one user a repeating address error kept inflating the charge from $202 up to $266.

product.title: The joy of supporting small makers and custom gifts
product.plus: For many, Etsy is first and foremost about supporting small businesses and handmade work, not cheap mass goods. Buyers are moved by the craftsmanship, the packaging, and the ability to order a personalized gift for the "impossible-to-buy-for" person.

product.title: "Not the Wish it used to be": veterans mourn the cheap glory days
product.minus: The single most common theme is nostalgia laced with disappointment: long-time users say it used to have the cheapest items and free shipping, but now the stock is just as generic at mid-range prices. Every comparison is against a better past.

product.title: "Ordered — never arrived": parcels vanish and the money with them
product.minus: A huge cluster of complaints is simply that items never arrive. People wait months, sometimes years, orders show as "delivered" but never land, and it almost always ends in a fight for a refund that never comes.

product.title: Support replies with copy-paste and AI boilerplate instead of solutions
product.minus: When something goes wrong, support sends the same template over and over or offers a token 20% refund. Users explicitly call it a runaround and blame fake AI responses that ignore the actual problem.

product.title: Prices caught up to and passed Amazon, Temu, Walmart — no reason to stay
product.minus: The core practical reason people leave: the same item is cheaper and faster on Temu, Shein, Amazon or Walmart. They cite hard numbers — a £189 flash drive, $80-205 pet fountains — and defect to the rivals they name by hand.

product.title: Login is broken: "oops, something went wrong" on a loop
product.minus: A whole wave of recent reviews is about being locked out. The app throws "oops something went wrong," won't accept old accounts, won't let users reset a password or create a new one. Reinstalling does nothing and people are stuck outside their own profiles.

product.title: What shows up is defective, fake, or the wrong item entirely
product.minus: Even when a parcel arrives, what's inside is often defective, a knock-off, or an entirely different item: the wrong knife, a cartridge for the wrong console. And returning it is nearly impossible, hence the recurring word "scam".

product.title: Getting a refund is a near-impossible quest
product.minus: Refunds are their own ordeal: a refund is "issued" but never hits the card; only 20% is offered for a defect; returns are refused over sizing; users are told to ship items back to China at their own cost. People lose tens to hundreds of dollars.

product.title: Slow shipping is the known price of paying so little
product.minus: Even happy buyers almost always add one caveat: deliveries take 2-3 weeks, sometimes months. Many tolerate it for the price but forget what they even ordered; for others it's the final straw.

product.title: For its loyal army this is still the favorite shop of the decade
product.plus: For all the negativity, Wish has a devoted core: people who've shopped here 10-15 years, call it their favorite app, and recommend it to everyone. To them it's a reliable, familiar ritual they stay loyal to.

product.title: Cheap prices and the thrill of the find are what people love
product.plus: The core value for happy users is low prices plus the treasure-hunt feel: you stumble on things you can't find in regular stores, cheaply. Many describe shopping here as a thrill and a pleasure, not just a purchase.

product.title: Quality is a "you get what you pay for" lottery
product.minus: Even loyal buyers admit quality swings seller to seller. A lot is outright cheap junk, fabric turns out to be polyester instead of cotton, things break fast. Buyers accept it as the cost of low prices, but it's a gamble.

product.title: Listings are vague: no materials, no video, no reliable sizing
product.minus: A concrete product gripe: listings don't tell you what you're buying. No fabric content or care info, no video inside bags and wallets, descriptions not in English, and sizing lies — order an L, get something that doesn't fit.

product.title: In any buyer-versus-seller dispute, Mercari almost always sides with the buyer
product.minus: Sellers report over and over that a buyer returns trash instead of the item or claims an empty box, submits fake "proof," and Mercari approves the refund while the scammer keeps the goods. Even unboxing videos and weight discrepancies don't help — the platform defaults to the buyer's side.

product.title: Support replies with scripts and AI templates but never actually resolves anything
product.minus: The single loudest complaint: support bounces you to a broken help center, sends the same AI reply on loop, reads from a script, and spends weeks promising to "notify another department" with no result. Reaching a real human is nearly impossible — you wait on hold and get hung up on.

product.title: High fees and pricey shipping eat almost the entire seller's profit
product.minus: Sellers call the 10% cut plus shipping markups extortion: you sell an item for $10 and pocket about $5, while the buyer pays $20 with shipping and tax. Many migrate to Depop, Vinted, and eBay, where fees are lower or nonexistent.

product.title: Huge selection and genuinely cheap finds are the main reason people come back
product.plus: Buyers love the breadth: they find things long gone from stores, vintage, collectibles, and rare items, often cheaper than on eBay. For many, browsing Mercari for a deal is the favorite part of their day.

product.title: The platform is overrun with scammers and counterfeits Mercari won't remove
product.minus: Replica sneakers, fake TCG cards, inauthentic perfume, counterfeit Pandora — buyers routinely receive fakes, and they say Mercari shields scammers for the cut and won't ban known offenders. One user lost $2000 on fake cards even with video proof.

product.title: ID verification with selfie and biometrics shuts out honest users
product.minus: The new requirement to upload a driver's license/ID and take a selfie through a third party (Jumio) locks out longtime users: the system "can't process" clear photos, and re-submitting is treated as "circumventing the ID check," triggering instant account closure. Many object to handing biometrics to a foreign company.

product.title: Seller payouts are frozen for ages, gated behind the buyer's rating
product.minus: The seller pays to ship, sends the item, and still waits days for the buyer to rate or for the 3-day window to lapse. Often the payout comes out to $0 over a "shipping issue" even when FedEx/USPS tracking and receipts prove otherwise.

product.title: Paid and never received it — "buyer protection" is charged but doesn't deliver
product.minus: Buyers pay a protection fee on every purchase, but when a package is lost or never arrives, Mercari refuses refunds citing a "delivered" status, and the money is simply gone. When a seller cancels a paid order, the refund also drags on for weeks.

product.title: A race to the bottom: staying visible means endlessly slashing your price
product.minus: Sellers complain the app forces a race to the lowest price: run a promotion and you're pushed to keep dropping it or your listing disappears. It goes as far as automatic "auto offers" and intrusive "promote this listing" banners no one asked for.

product.title: The app lags, freezes, and won't load item descriptions
product.minus: Technical glitches are constant: jerky scrolling freezes the screen, the app crashes after 5-10 minutes, and tapping an item often loads only the photo and price — the text and description never appear. The broken search fails to find even an exact listing title.

product.title: A real seller upside: effortless listing and decluttering in a couple of taps
product.plus: Despite the pain points, many praise how easy it is to list and sell: snap a photo, create a listing, and clear out clutter while making money. For some sellers it's their number-one app, ahead of eBay on usability.

product.title: The review system is one-sided: auto 5★ after 3 days with no way to contest
product.minus: If you don't rate within 3 days, the system auto-posts 5★ and strips your right to leave an honest review — users call it dishonest. Sellers can't see the buyer's rating before their own and can't defend themselves, and low stars are allowed even just for declining a discount.

product.title: When a deal goes smoothly, fast shipping and careful packaging delight
product.plus: The bulk of 5★ reviews are about specific successful purchases: item exactly as pictured, fast shipping, careful packaging, sometimes a nice extra from the seller. For happy buyers, Mercari is a reliable way to find exactly what they wanted.

product.title: Drive-up and pickup are the number-one reason people love the app
product.plus: The same theme repeats over and over: orders are ready in a couple of hours, you can tap «I'm on my way», and staff bring purchases to the car fast and cheerfully. For busy parents and people caring for elderly relatives it's a lifesaver.

product.title: Search returns junk and doesn't show real in-store stock
product.minus: Users call search useless: it pulls up tons of unrelated items, doesn't show what's actually in stock, and fails to surface pre-orders. By the time you grab a direct link from another website, the item is sold out.

product.title: Constantly logs you out and forces password/PIN resets
product.minus: Sign-in is a sore spot: the app spins, logs you out every couple of minutes and demands you re-login just to check a price. Many are infuriated at having to reset their card password or PIN every single time.

product.title: The Circle/Red Card 5% discount is a beloved perk — when it works
product.plus: The automatic 5% off with the Circle/Red Card plus Circle coupons are what users name as the main reason to save at Target, especially on bigger purchases. The loyalty program is a favorite for many.

product.title: Third-party sellers and scalpers are turning the catalog into Temu/Amazon
product.minus: The arrival of third-party sellers is seen as a hit to the brand: cheap drop-shipping and resellers flipping the same goods at inflated prices. A distinct sore point is bots buying up Pokémon cards on drops while real people get nothing.

product.title: Easy online ordering: no minimum, a 2-hour window, cart always visible
product.plus: Ordering from home is easy and pleasant: people call the interface friendly, love the no-minimum-order rule, the two-hour ready window, and that the cart stays visible — handy for the forgetful.

product.title: Inaccurate stock: «in stock» turns out to be out, substitutions needed
product.minus: Stock data lets people down: items flagged as available turn out to be gone, pickups fall through, and substitutions have to be accepted blind. For some nothing shows as available for curbside at all; for others the app won't let them pick a different version of the same item.

product.title: Delivery windows and prices don't match what was promised
product.minus: Paid delivery windows get pushed back without explanation, the 360 membership's «free delivery» is eaten by a «regional fee» buried in fine print, and the cart price suddenly comes out higher than on the listing. Trust in the promises erodes.

product.title: Support is trapped in an AI chat and phone tree with no path to a human
product.minus: The «report issue with order» feature errors out, the chat is now fully AI with no way to escalate to a human, and calling leads into an automated menu and hold. Reporting the error just ends the conversation — a closed loop.

product.title: App glitches: crashes, emptied cart, vanishing coupons
product.minus: The app randomly jumps back to the home screen, freezes when saving items for later, and mid-checkout the cart empties itself and drops Circle coupons and discounts that then won't reapply.

product.title: Pushy recommendations, ads and spam notifications annoy users
product.minus: Search and the feed push things you never asked for — flavored toothpaste instead of unflavored, ads in results like Amazon. The app forces you to rate and tip the driver with no opt-out, and marketing notifications pour in as spam.

product.title: Chaos around the Circle/Red/Debit card: lockouts, hidden limits, lost discount
product.minus: The Circle card is its own pain source: the app locks you out of the card right at checkout, the promised 5% suddenly becomes unavailable for no reason, the debit-card limit is opaque, and paying your bill in-app simply doesn't work (a blank black page).

product.title: The price you book at is not the price you pay
product.minus: The app shows one amount at booking, then the final fare climbs at drop-off with no route change or extra stops. Users call it misleading and outright fraud.

product.title: Drivers demand cash on top of the in-app fare
product.minus: A recurring complaint, especially in India: the driver drops you off and demands cash, often double the in-app amount, then argues or fights, and there's no one to complain to.

product.title: Drivers cancel at the last second, and the rider pays for it
product.minus: A driver accepts, sometimes calls to ask the location, then cancels seconds later; the rules aren't symmetric — riders get charged for cancelling while drivers face nothing.

product.title: Long waits to match a driver, or no driver at all
product.minus: Matching drags on for tens of minutes, especially when you're in a rush or it's raining; people wait an hour, abandon the trip, and end up late for work.

product.title: Discounted rides nobody will accept
product.minus: When the app offers a promo discount, drivers see the low fare and won't accept; coupons and deals turn into endless waiting in practice.

product.title: The app lies about pickup time
product.minus: It says 8 minutes, then jumps to 15+ once you select the ride; people use these estimates to time when to leave, and the lie even gets them charged for being "late".

product.title: Customer support is impossible to reach
product.minus: Tickets don't work, only a bot replies, there's no phone line; after a wrong charge or a lost item, users are left alone with an app designed to keep them away from a real agent.

product.title: Uber One and charges you never signed up for
product.minus: Users get enrolled in Uber One without consent, keep getting billed for months after cancelling with no refund, and some see random charges years later.

product.title: Booking ahead doesn't help — you get ditched at the last minute
product.minus: Pre-booking an hour or even a day ahead guarantees nothing: no driver is found and people get dropped at the last minute before flights, trains, and critical connections.

product.title: Forced reviews and tips before you can book
product.minus: The app blocks a new booking until you rate the last driver or leave a tip; it frustrates busy people who then click through random ratings just to get a ride.

product.title: When it works, drivers are kind and cars are clean
product.plus: The best reviews are about specific drivers — polite, on time, helpful with bags, clean cars, safe driving. One even returned a phone left behind.

product.title: A travel lifeline that helps you feel safe
product.plus: Loyal users value that Uber comes through in unfamiliar cities and abroad: you can see the driver beforehand and even track a delivery from another country, which feels safe — especially for older riders and people with disabilities.

product.title: Wildly inconsistent pricing for the same route
product.minus: The same route at the same time swings from 9 to 22 dollars; surge and fuel surcharges make the cost unpredictable, pushing people back to their own cars.

product.title: Price jumps within minutes and is almost always higher than Uber
product.minus: The defining pain: the same trip is quoted at $20 then $100, the price changes the instant you hit accept, and users immediately compare with Uber, where the same miles cost half as much.

product.title: Warm, caring drivers are the reason people keep coming back
product.plus: Despite everything, drivers get near-glowing praise: polite, careful, clean cars, helpful to elderly and wheelchair riders, safe driving, and often remembered by name.

product.title: Wait times are lied about, driver swapped right before pickup
product.minus: Promised "3 minutes," the driver doesn't move or gets swapped for a farther one — sometimes repeatedly — and you wait 15–25 minutes instead of what was quoted.

product.title: Support effectively doesn't exist — just a bot and empty apologies
product.minus: You can't reach a human, the chat replies "so sorry to hear that" then stops answering; in real crises — lost item, a crash, a safety threat — Lyft washes its hands.

product.title: Double charges and money held after the ride
product.minus: Charged twice for one ride, authorization holds kept for 5–7 days, surprise fees and a wrong car class added — and getting the money back is nearly impossible.

product.title: GPS and address lookup miss the door
product.minus: The map feeds drivers outdated routes and a wrong pin, the car almost never stops at the right house, and you can't move the pickup point in the app.

product.title: Scheduled rides get cancelled — and you're left late
product.minus: A pre-booked ride to the doctor, airport, or work falls through: no driver found or it gets cancelled, forcing a scramble over to Uber.

product.title: Cancellation and "late" fees where the service is at fault
product.minus: They charge a cancellation fee even when no driver was ever assigned, and fine you for being "late" though the app stopped notifying when the car arrived.

product.title: Ads in a paid app hide the driver's details
product.minus: Intrusive ads appeared in a paid service — they block the map, hide driver info, and, per reviews, drain the battery.

product.title: Stuck in a verification and confirmation loop
product.minus: The app suddenly demands ID re-verification from an already-verified rider and loops on the confirm screen — leaving people stranded at work or the airport for hours.

product.title: When you catch a low price — cheap, fast, and reliable
product.plus: A chunk of users call Lyft their daily car-free transport: fast pickups, sometimes cheaper than Uber, and Lyft Pink plus price lock genuinely save money.

product.title: Language barrier with drivers complicates problem situations
product.minus: Some riders complain drivers don't speak English — which muddles pickups, returning lost items, and sorting out accidents.

product.title: Driver accepts, then cancels — over and over
product.minus: The single most common complaint: drivers accept, stall, then cancel — sometimes two minutes away from you. Riders miss meetings, trains and clinic appointments.

product.title: Scheduled rides silently collapse at the last minute
product.minus: A ride booked hours ahead gets confirmed, sometimes even shows 'driver found' — then cancels at the scheduled moment with no warning, leaving people stranded.

product.title: Wait-time fees turn into a money grab
product.minus: Drivers game the wait-time clock: they mark 'arrived' before reaching you and rack up minutes. Fines kick in after 5 minutes — and the app won't even let you call the driver.

product.title: Support is a bot that resolves nothing
product.minus: When something goes wrong, all you get is an AI bot: cold hallucinated replies instead of help, refunds refused even with photo evidence, and no human anywhere.

product.title: Drivers extort extra cash beyond the app price
product.minus: Once you're in the car, the driver declares the app price too low and demands extra cash — or threatens to drop you off. Cash off-app, no record.

product.title: Charged upfront, refunds are a quest
product.minus: Payment is taken before the trip and often above the quote; the promised '3-day reversal' becomes a double charge refunded two weeks later — if at all.

product.title: Driver goes to the wrong place — or the wrong pickup
product.minus: The car shows up at a spot you didn't choose and the wait fee starts; flaky GPS scrambles destinations, and you can be dropped off far from home, luggage and all.

product.title: Rude drivers and dirty cars
product.minus: Rudeness, reckless driving, running red lights, and being thrown out for the mildest complaint. Cabins can be filthy, and support won't help swap the car.

product.title: Scooters: surprise restricted zones and parking fines
product.minus: A scooter unlocks normally, then a zone restriction pops up — trapping you with a fine. Parking spots and a ride-style score only add frustration.

product.title: Can't sign up: the verification code never arrives
product.minus: New users get stuck at the door: the SMS and call codes never come through and there's no help — the app fails before the first ride.

product.title: When it works — cheap, fast and pleasant
product.plus: Riders who get lucky praise the low price, fast pickup, clean comfortable cars and friendly drivers — rating Bolt above Uber on price and ease.

product.title: Precise pickup location — the bit drivers actually value
product.plus: For some users the pickup precision is the standout: Bolt hands the driver an accurate pick-up point better than rival apps.

product.title: One super-app for rides, food and payments is the core reason people love it
product.plus: The most frequent praise is that rides, food delivery, groceries and payment all live in one app: people call it a lifesaver and use it daily.

product.title: There is no real support — just a bot going in circles
product.minus: The deepest pain point: there's no way to reach a human, the chatbot loops and repeats itself, and issues like refunds, wrong orders or overcharges simply can't be resolved.

product.title: Money gets taken with no service; refunds drag on for days
product.minus: A recurring complaint: the card gets charged in advance or twice, the promised "30-minute" refund never arrives for days, and sometimes money is taken with no booking at all.

product.title: Wallet top-up hangs: the bank deducts but the money never lands
product.minus: GrabPay top-ups often get stuck in "processing": the bank already deducts the money but it doesn't appear in the wallet for an hour, leaving you unable to even buy dinner.

product.title: A forced passkey setup locks you out of the app entirely
product.minus: A whole wave of complaints: the "set up passkey" screen can't be dismissed, the setup itself fails with "Oops, something went wrong", reinstalling doesn't help, and the app becomes completely unusable.

product.title: Drivers cancel after a long wait, or push you to cancel yourself
product.minus: A painful pattern: you wait 15-38 minutes and the driver cancels anyway, or he stays put, goes unresponsive in chat and forces the customer to cancel the order.

product.title: Delivery is chronically late — food arrives cold
product.minus: A constant GrabFood complaint: orders run one to two hours late, the ETA silently slips several times, you can't cancel, the food goes cold, and sometimes the order is cancelled on you in the end.

product.title: A brutal cancellation window: just seconds to change your mind
product.minus: The rigidity of cancellation grates: a five-second window is useless, even a single Mart item can't be cancelled before a driver is found, and you get charged for cancelling on top of that.

product.title: The app is drowning in ads you can't swipe away
product.minus: A sharp complaint: full-screen ads cover even your ride tracking, take ages to load and make the app unusable, while push ads keep coming even with notifications turned off.

product.title: Prices surge and bite, and the vouchers are a bait-and-switch
product.minus: A frequent money complaint: fares swing wildly and can cost far more than rivals, while promo codes come back as "already redeemed", "invalid" or over the daily limit, so the promised savings never materialize.

product.title: A locked-in fare shown before the ride is what wins trust
product.plus: Despite the surges, many praise that the fare is shown and locked in before you confirm, which helps people plan their spending and avoid surprises.

product.title: Polite drivers and accurate tracking are the ride's real strength
product.plus: When it works, the rides earn genuine praise: polite and punctual drivers, clean cars, accurate map tracking and fast pickups.

product.title: Location drifts and drivers won't come to the actual pin
product.minus: A recurring problem: the pin shifts on its own and bumps up the fee, address notes don't get through, and drivers are too lazy to reach the exact spot — "door to door" turns into "meet me at the gate".

product.title: A flood of notifications you can't switch off
product.minus: Notification spam grates: the same alert fires over and over with no status change, ad pushes arrive even with notifications off, and they spill onto your watch too.

product.title: Sign-up and login choke on OTP codes and captcha
product.minus: A barrier at the door: verification codes arrive far too late or never, OTP never completes, and a captcha of blurry images finishes the job — you simply can't create an account.

product.title: The final charge is almost always higher than the quoted estimate
product.minus: People are charged above the top of the range over and over: a 19-24€ estimate becomes 27€, a max-19€ estimate becomes 44€, and a second trip quoted at max 20€ becomes 60€. Excuses about "fee variations" don't convince anyone.

product.title: The in-car meter shows one figure, but a larger sum leaves your card
product.minus: The sharpest grievance: the driver or app puts through more than the taximeter reading. Meter 28€ — charged 47.80€; meter 17.40 — 29.20; meter 11.90 — but the locked-in 17.50 was taken anyway.

product.title: A pre-booking only starts hunting for a driver at pickup time — and often finds none
product.minus: Booking a day ahead reserves nothing: the algorithm only starts searching minutes before pickup, and at 4am there are no drivers. People miss flights, ferries and trains, told of the cancellation exactly when the taxi was due.

product.title: Drivers accept then cancel, and the passenger pays the penalty
product.minus: A driver takes the trip, stalls a few minutes and cancels — yet the passenger is hit with a 3.99-6€ "waiting" fee. The rules, people say, protect only the driver, and there's no way to rate or report them.

product.title: No car appears until you pay extra for "priority"
product.minus: The standard search stalls for hours and shows zero cars, but pay the 4-5€ priority surcharge and a driver appears in seconds. Users read this as deliberate extortion, not a real shortage.

product.title: Support is a bot that promises a reply and then vanishes
product.minus: When a charge is disputed, users meet an AI bot promising a reply within 24 hours — then silence for weeks. There's no human to reach, tickets close with an auto-reply, and refunds are nearly impossible.

product.title: Random extra charges trickle in after the ride
product.minus: The charge doesn't come as one figure: half an hour to an hour after the ride, extra 50-cent, 3-7€ amounts land on the card with no explanation. A single ride shows up split into five separate charges.

product.title: Sign-up requires an SMS code — travellers abroad are locked out
product.minus: An app meant for trips abroad demands phone-number verification, yet the SMS or call code never arrives on a foreign number or without roaming. Email sign-up is either missing or the fields simply won't activate.

product.title: The map moves your pickup point and won't let you zoom in
product.minus: The app shifts the pickup point hundreds of metres and makes you walk to it, while the map can't be zoomed — it rubber-bands back out. The address locks in wrong, the driver gets the wrong spot, and there's not even a car colour.

product.title: When a car does come, the drivers and service genuinely delight
product.plus: The standout positive is people: drivers are polite, help with luggage and the elderly, arrive on time, cars are clean. Many call FREE NOW more reliable than Uber in Athens and Dublin and praise the transparent locked-in price before you confirm.

product.title: The core function breaks: the app won't load and freezes
product.minus: Sometimes the foundation itself breaks: a map opens where nothing is clickable, there's no keyboard, the app freezes and needs restarting. With a perfect connection you still can't order — the most basic thing fails.

product.title: Double billing: the driver takes cash and the card is charged too
product.minus: A distinct kind of fraud — the driver insists on being paid directly or hits "complete" early, and the app charges the same ride again. Sometimes one trip goes through as two payments with no refund.

product.title: Fares don't keep up with fuel prices — drivers work at a loss
product.minus: The single most common complaint: petrol gets pricier, inflation climbs, yet fares stay flat or even drop. Drivers say that after fuel and car maintenance there's almost nothing left.

product.title: Riders can lowball the fare to absurdity — so drivers just don't accept
product.minus: The haggling mechanic backfires on everyone: a rider can cut the fare below the minimum, and the request hangs for hours unanswered. Drivers ignore cheap trips, riders get stranded.

product.title: Setting your own fare is the standout loved feature
product.plus: Fans love exactly the negotiation model: rider and driver agree on a price that feels fair to both, and trips come out cheaper than the competition.

product.title: Riders cancel after the driver has already arrived — no refund for fuel or time
product.minus: A sharp driver pain: you burn fuel and time driving to the pickup, then the passenger cancels with no reason and no penalty. Worse, the driver's balance gets frozen for hours.

product.title: Support is effectively absent — and accounts get blocked on a single complaint
product.minus: Customer support either goes silent or humiliates you, users say. Meanwhile a single passenger complaint can permanently block a driver — even by phone IP — with no investigation.

product.title: Drivers demand extra cash after accepting the ride
product.minus: A common rider complaint: the driver agrees to a price, then mid-trip or on the highway demands more — or threatens to drop you, or asks you to cancel the ride yourself.

product.title: The cut taken from drivers feels too high against starvation fares
product.minus: Drivers are convinced the company cares only about its own commission (often cited at ~11-13%), while the partners the service can't exist without are treated as disposable.

product.title: Polite drivers and clean cars — when you get lucky
product.plus: Plenty of five-star reviews praise specific drivers: punctual, friendly, tidy, helpful to seniors, returning forgotten items. A lot rides on getting a good driver.

product.title: Cheap where other apps gouge you — a lifesaver for travellers
product.plus: Riders and tourists value inDrive as the affordable option: in Morocco, Nepal, Phuket — no getting ripped off, cheaper than Grab/Gojek/Uber/Careem.

product.title: Updates break the app and it's incompatible with many phones
product.minus: Technical breakage recurs: after updates the app won't load, won't accept orders, won't install on Pixel/Realme/Motorola, demands a photo each ride, throws an "incompatible" error.

product.title: The notification jingle turns into spam
product.minus: A handful of users are driven up the wall by inDrive's branded jingle: it plays even when you're not using the app and feels like intrusive spam.

product.title: Inaccurate pickup points and a flaky map
product.minus: The map won't let you enter an exact address — you must drop a pin manually or pick the nearest spot; pickup points are often wrong, confusing both driver and rider.

product.title: The driver never shows — especially on airport bookings
product.minus: A pre-booked airport ride collapses five minutes before pickup: the assigned driver cancels, the next ones too, and people barely make their flight by flagging down a street taxi.

product.title: Sign-up dies without a local number — tourists locked out
product.minus: The app refuses foreign numbers and never delivers the verification code, so a visitor without a Spanish or Latin American SIM simply cannot create an account.

product.title: Final bill exceeds the quoted price via hidden fees
product.minus: A price is agreed before the trip, then "high demand", processing and safety fees get tacked on, with the charge surfacing only after drop-off, unexplained and non-refundable.

product.title: Waiting fee for time that never happened — drivers stall
product.minus: Drivers mark themselves "arrived" before they get there or circle around to rack up waiting minutes, and support insists the bogus idle fee is "correct".

product.title: Support replies like a bot and resolves nothing
product.minus: Complaints about double charges, lost items and disputed fees get canned brush-offs, the chat is closed unresolved, there's no phone line, and the developer's store reply is the same "contact support" loop.

product.title: Long waits for a car that never materialises
product.minus: The app promises a car "in 2 minutes", keeps you on "searching for a driver" for 20–30 minutes and finds no one, while Uber pulls up in a minute — even in a major city centre.

product.title: The quoted ETA constantly lies
product.minus: It first shows a driver 5–9 minutes out, then he jumps to 15–20, turns away a block before you, or just freezes on the map — nobody signed up for that wait.

product.title: Double and phantom charges, holds eat your balance
product.minus: A single trip gets charged two or three times, holds stack on holds, and a 2021 ride can suddenly be billed — money is frozen for days and refunds have to be fought for.

product.title: Pricier than Uber and Bolt for the same service
product.minus: Fares run consistently 1.5–2x above rivals and sometimes above a regular street taxi, while the promised discounts and coupons simply don't apply.

product.title: Safety and vetted drivers are the standout strength
product.plus: When the ride does happen, many value the sense of safety above all: drivers are strictly vetted, and solo passengers trust whoever is driving them.

product.title: Clean cars and polite, premium-feel drivers
product.plus: Happy users single out impeccably clean, comfortable cars and courteous drivers — sometimes even with water on board, like a limousine service.

product.title: Pre-booking an airport car — a lifesaver when it works
product.plus: A share of users praise exactly the ability to reserve a morning airport car: the driver texts ahead, arrives on time and takes the stress out of travelling in a foreign city.

product.title: Drivers reroute and drop you at the wrong place
product.minus: Drivers lengthen the route to double the fare or leave you a couple of kilometres from the booked address — sometimes somewhere unsafe — and the app itself can switch the destination mid-trip.

product.title: Paid cancellations even when the service is at fault
product.minus: When a driver won't come and the rider must cancel to catch another taxi, they're charged a penalty anyway — while drivers cancel freely with no consequences.

product.title: Support replies with scripts and never actually resolves anything
product.minus: The single most common complaint: every issue gets a canned "sorry for the inconvenience", tickets are closed unresolved, and agents repeat copy-paste replies without engaging.

product.title: Money is taken, refunds never come back
product.minus: Charges for services never rendered, withheld deposits, partial instead of full refunds — money is stuck for weeks and customers have to chase it themselves.

product.title: Drivers accept then cancel — but the rider pays the penalty
product.minus: Captains accept, stall, then hit "the rider told me to cancel", dumping the cancellation fee on the customer; the algorithm penalizes drivers who then offload it onto riders.

product.title: Food arrives cold and hours late
product.minus: Orders sit in "preparing" for 1.5-2 hours, group delivery silently adds time, and captains carry multiple orders at once — food turns up cold, ice cream melted.

product.title: Orders get cancelled after a long wait
product.minus: Orders are accepted and paid for, then cancelled an hour or two later ("no captain", "restaurant closed") — with the refund pushed to the wallet and a request to reorder.

product.title: The final price beats the quote — "extra fees"
product.minus: The app shows the driver one price and the rider another, more is deducted than agreed, and the answer is "road tolls and checkpoints" — even for Plus subscribers.

product.title: Missing items in the order — no refund given
product.minus: Part of the order never arrives, and the reply is either a token refund, a denial citing the 24-hour rule, or a demand to reorder and pay delivery again.

product.title: You have a wallet, but you can't pay with it
product.minus: The wallet is topped up, yet the app defaults to cash and captains rudely refuse card/wallet payment, insisting on cash.

product.title: Careem Plus is impossible to cancel
product.minus: The cancel option is hidden or absent, charges renew automatically even when unused, and Plus members get none of the promised perks anyway.

product.title: Bike/scooter rental: 20-minute relocks and held deposits
product.minus: The "day pass" forces a relock every 20 minutes, the lock takes minutes to turn green, and post-ride deposits aren't returned but re-charged for the next ride.

product.title: Careem Pay transfers stall despite the promised timing
product.minus: The service advertises a 2-hour transfer, but funds don't arrive for days, the beneficiary sees nothing, and requests for an MT103 document or explanation go unanswered.

product.title: When it works — rides are smooth and drivers are polite
product.plus: Some users praise the clean, easy interface, accurate fares, punctuality and welcoming drivers; for some, CareemPay transfers are genuinely fast and cheap.

product.title: "Used to be great" — decline that drives loyal users away
product.minus: Long-time customers tell the same story: service, deals and support have sharply declined, and rivals (Talabat, Bolt, Deliveroo) now beat Careem on price and reliability.

product.title: Fare changes after the ride: you agree to one price, get charged another
product.minus: The single biggest complaint: the price shown at booking turns out noticeably higher when the trip ends — no traffic, no waiting, no route change, no explanation. Support replies with a canned «fare could increase due to reasons» and never clarifies the actual case, so riders read it as outright fraud.

product.title: Drivers accept then cancel — finding a car becomes an ordeal
product.minus: A relentless pain point: a driver grabs the trip, shows up «1 minute away» and cancels, or simply doesn't move and makes you wait until they cancel — often to squeeze a higher fare or chase a better trip. Riders wait 15–30 minutes for a car when rivals take 7.

product.title: Money is charged upfront, but refunds drag on for days and weeks
product.minus: Pay by card and the full fare is debited before anyone even accepts the trip. If the ride is cancelled or falls through, the money is held and the refund takes 10–30 days — while Uber returns it in seconds. For many riders this alone pushes them back to cash.

product.title: There is no real support — a bot replies with templates, or no one does
product.minus: When something goes wrong — a double charge, a cancellation, a rude driver — there's no one to reach. The chat closes instantly, complaints and emails go unanswered for weeks, there's no phone line, and a bot fires the same canned replies and closes the case unresolved.

product.title: Cancellation fees are charged even when the driver is at fault
product.minus: If the driver no-shows, cancels himself or never arrives, the rider still gets hit with a «late» or cancellation fee and no refund. It feels deliberate — you're pushed into cancelling so they can collect the fee.

product.title: Rude drivers, beat-up cars and a feeling of being unsafe
product.minus: Complaints about rude, unprofessional drivers, old and dirty cars with no quality control, swapped vehicles and plates, and a driver getting the rider's phone number after a cancellation. Women describe unpleasant incidents, and the company does nothing about the reports.

product.title: Ads cover the info you need and spill into other apps
product.minus: After an update ads cover the vehicle details until the car arrives, promo notifications flood in all day with no way to turn them off in settings, and DiDi ads even pop up inside unrelated apps and games.

product.title: Cheaper than Uber — the number one reason people stay
product.plus: The most frequent praise: when the pricing behaves, DiDi is consistently cheaper than Uber and regular taxis, sometimes by half. Riders compare prices before every trip and keep saving, which is why they stick with the app despite its flaws.

product.title: Drivers get paid more — and riders notice it
product.plus: A notable share of users value that DiDi pays drivers meaningfully more than Uber and see it as fair. Drivers themselves say they prefer DiDi, and riders connect the friendlier, more courteous service to the better pay.

product.title: Simple app, fast pickups and generous newcomer discounts
product.plus: For those whose trips go smoothly, the appeal is simplicity: ordering is easy, pickups are quick, and first rides come with big discounts and coupons. For many it's the effortless «download the app and you're in a car within minutes» experience.

product.title: Maps and routing fail: drivers get lost, routes wander
product.minus: The in-app map isn't kept current, so drivers get lost and end up in the wrong place. Routes often zig-zag through back streets, adding 5–10 minutes, and users suspect the longer paths are picked on purpose to inflate the fare.

product.title: Air conditioning only for an off-the-meter «negotiated» fee
product.minus: In hot-climate markets riders complain that nearly every driver refuses to turn on the AC until you haggle an extra fee on top of the fare. The advertised «comfort» AC option doesn't actually work in the latest app version.

product.title: Drivers accept the booking, then cancel at the last second
product.minus: The defining pain: a driver accepts, makes you wait, then cancels when a cash fare or a better offer comes in — leaving you to wait for the next one who may also cancel.

product.title: No price shown before booking, so you pay whatever they decide
product.minus: The app shows no fare estimate up front — no fixed price, not even a ballpark — so at the end the driver or the system can charge you whatever they like.

product.title: Support is a bot with no way to reach a human
product.minus: Any problem dumps you into a bot with a canned menu: no phone, no email, no live agent, and the chat just sends template replies or a link back into the app.

product.title: Drivers turn off the meter and name a price out of thin air
product.minus: Drivers refuse to switch on the meter and demand an inflated flat price judged by your accent; refuse and they simply won't take you.

product.title: Charged a cancellation fee even when the driver cancels
product.minus: The system bills a cancellation fee no matter what — even when the driver cancels or stalls in place to make you cancel — and clawing the money back is a long fight.

product.title: Can't find a car even when taxis are everywhere
product.minus: Finding a driver drags on 15–20 minutes or more in the city centre at peak time even though the map shows plenty of cars nearby — you can't rely on it for a quick ride.

product.title: Charged more than the meter, with hidden surcharges piled on
product.minus: The final charge routinely beats the meter and the estimate — a "busy fee", "boundary charges", or mystery card debits you were never warned about.

product.title: Registration and login break for no reason
product.minus: The confirmation code never arrives on foreign numbers, the app claims an account already exists, or it demands the last 4 digits of an old card — and with no support reachable you're stuck in a loop.

product.title: Driver leaves with someone else and there's no way to report it
product.minus: The car pulls up, picks someone else and drives off in front of you — or the driver fakes the pickup — and the app has no button to even report it.

product.title: Location and maps are wrong, forcing you to walk to the driver
product.minus: Outdated maps drop the pickup pin away from where you actually stand: the app sends the car a couple of streets off or to your last location, and you have to walk to the driver.

product.title: Won't accept short journeys
product.minus: After all the setup the app refuses to book a short trip: 2–3 miles to the station isn't worth its while, and you only find out at the very end.

product.title: Airport pre-booking only confirms 15 minutes before
product.minus: You book the airport ride hours or days ahead, yet confirmation only lands 15 minutes before — and if no driver is free, you're left stranded with no fallback.

product.title: When it works, it's the best way to get a London black cab
product.plus: It delivers properly-trained black-cab service with no haggling: quick to order, drivers polite and punctual, tracked on the map along the route — for many it beats Uber.

product.title: An honest meter with no arguing with the driver
product.plus: The big win in Israel — you get in without arguing about the meter: the price is transparent, you know what you're paying for, and it's fairer for everyone.

product.title: Friendly drivers make the ride a pleasure
product.plus: When you get a good driver — courteous, punctual, helping with luggage and a wheelchair, chatting warmly — the ride becomes a small pleasure, especially for tourists and those with limited mobility.

product.title: Pre-booking actually delivers a car on time
product.plus: When the ride is pre-booked it often works flawlessly: the car arrives on time, the route keeps to the minute, and you reach the airport exactly when you need to.

product.title: Fraud disputes are closed within days — almost always denied
product.minus: The defining pain: when money is stolen the dispute is rejected in 2 days as "no error occurred," users are asked for work schedules and personal documents, and money that was returned often gets clawed back after a fresh denial.

product.title: Check deposits stall: the availability date slides day after day, with no way to cancel
product.minus: The promised check-availability date is pushed back a couple of days, then again, and you only learn it once cancellation is already locked; funds sit "hostage" for a week while support says there's nothing it can do.

product.title: Accounts get closed suddenly with no reason given
product.minus: After years of good standing the account can be shut down following an "AI review" with no reason given on chat or by phone — and your money becomes inaccessible in the process.

product.title: Endless login loop: the app throws you back to sign-up even though the account already exists
product.minus: Entering a code or password runs you in circles: after verification you land back on sign-up, password reset "refuses to work," and a live agent makes you redo it all — sometimes for months with no access to your money.

product.title: Support hangs up and "can't do anything"
product.minus: Support runs on autopilot: when the bot fails, agents end the chat and hang up, say "I can't help you," are hard to hear and understand — leaving people feeling utterly powerless.

product.title: The card gets locked as "suspicious" at the worst possible moment
product.minus: A routine purchase at a gas station or in another state is suddenly flagged as suspicious, the card is locked for days, and support can't say when it'll work again — hitting truckers and frequent travelers hardest.

product.title: MyPay/SpotMe limits get cut without warning or reason
product.minus: The overdraft limit is given then yanked away: you budget groceries around it, then wake up to a slashed balance; MyPay drops from $500 to $200 with no change in income and resets even if unused.

product.title: Ads promise $200, reality is a referral quest with strings attached
product.minus: The loud "$200 for opening an account" turns out to be something else: the money only comes from referring friends, and the promised cashback plan is changed after you've already moved your deposit in.

product.title: Getting paid two days early is the number-one reason to stay
product.plus: Direct-deposit pay lands two days early (for some 5-6 days), reliably and "like clockwork" — for many the decisive perk they tolerate everything else for.

product.title: The Credit Builder card genuinely raises credit scores
product.plus: The Credit Builder card and bureau reporting deliver a real score jump — people cite concrete numbers like +111 points in a year — and it's the top thing credit-rebuilders love about Chime.

product.title: No fees and SpotMe overdraft with no penalties — a lifesaver when short
product.plus: No bank fees and a free SpotMe overdraft up to $200 with no penalties genuinely help: people say it decided whether they could get to work or eat, and the limit grows over time.

product.title: Not a "real" bank: no wire transfers, cashier's checks or personal-check deposits
product.minus: The moment a serious banking task comes up, the ceiling shows: no wire transfers or cashier's checks (it surfaced when buying a home), personal checks aren't accepted, and loading funds can cost a fee — "basically a credit card with your own money."

product.title: The "Add money" button now covers the balance — you can't quickly check your money
product.minus: Recent UI updates placed the "add money" button exactly where the account total should be; on top of that the app locks you out monthly and forces you to sign up for things before it'll show your balance.

product.title: Forced updates: don't update and you're signed out, can't even see a statement
product.minus: The app ultimatum-style demands you update or it signs you out and blocks even viewing a balance or statement; yet after updating it just crashes for some with a bug error.

product.title: Accounts closed with no explanation given
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the account is deactivated citing a "terms violation," but no one — not chat, not the appeal — will say which rule was broken. People who moved money from family for years suddenly find themselves locked out and cut off from their own funds.

product.title: Money vanishes and they won't help get it back
product.minus: Users describe money simply disappearing: a received payment shows in the history but never hits the balance, or funds vanish off the card. When asked to investigate, support points to its own "documentation" instead of the real balance, and people never get reimbursed.

product.title: Support runs in circles and resolves nothing
product.minus: Support is described as useless: the bot chat repeats itself, live agents recite scripted lines and miss the actual question. People burn 45 minutes or weeks on an issue and walk away with nothing.

product.title: An "update the app" loop with no way out
product.minus: The app demands an update, but the update either never shows in the store or, once installed, asks to update again — blocking transfers all the while. People reinstall five times and stay stuck in the loop, unable to send even $50.

product.title: Weak protection: accounts get hacked, claims get denied
product.minus: Strangers charge a locked card, fraudsters fail five attempts and still pull over a thousand dollars, and when a user disputes obvious fraud with full evidence, the claim is denied anyway.

product.title: Payments arbitrarily declined with no reason
product.minus: The fraud-detection algorithm kills legitimate payments: $3 transfers from customers get flagged as "payment failed" with no notice, an in-store purchase is declined with money in the account, and support can't manually override the block.

product.title: Pushy loan ads and spam notifications
product.minus: The app spams emails and push notifications about "hundreds of dollars" and constantly pushes Borrow loan and new-card ads. The Borrow service itself is called predatory: on a missed payment they pull money straight from your bank card, even overdrawing it.

product.title: Identity verification stalls and demands your SSN
product.minus: Identity verification jams: with correct data straight off a license the system still "can't verify," for two weeks, locking you out of your money. And a simple transfer to a friend suddenly demands a Social Security number — pushing people to Venmo.

product.title: Family and child accounts are clumsy by design
product.minus: A family account managed by an adult doesn't actually let them manage it: money sits stranded on a child's old account for months. And to move a child to a teen account at 13, you have to close it and create a brand-new one.

product.title: Locking the card is users' favourite feature
product.plus: The ability to instantly lock and unlock the card is something users genuinely love: it's handy to keep the card locked and open it only at the moment of purchase, shielding the balance from accidental and fraudulent charges.

product.title: Fast, fee-free transfers to family and friends
product.plus: The core reason people keep the app: instantly and fee-free (with green status) sending and receiving money from loved ones. It's a lifesaver when a grandchild or friend urgently needs help, and doubles as a simple payment tool for business.

product.title: Overdraft and Borrow bail you out till payday
product.plus: Despite the predatory complaints, for many the overdraft and Borrow micro-loan genuinely help bridge to payday: the limit grows from $50 to $200+ with use, and it's valued by people with no access to ordinary credit.

product.title: An accessible mini-bank for the unbanked
product.plus: For people without a regular bank account, the app is a simple on-ramp to cashless payments: easy to get a card, pay online without exposing your main card, file taxes free, and usable even by teens. Many call it the best of the prepaid banking apps.

product.title: Rates and instant currency exchange are the main reason people love Revolut
product.plus: For travel it's almost a benchmark: currencies convert instantly at near-interbank rates, the card pays everywhere, and cross-border transfers arrive in seconds with virtually no fee.

product.title: Accounts get closed suddenly with no explanation — even after 6-7 years
product.minus: Long-time customers receive an email announcing all accounts are permanently closed and cards blocked with no valid justification; the decision is declared final and impossible to appeal.

product.title: Funds get frozen and held while you prove the money is yours
product.minus: Even receiving a transfer from a friend, or moving your own money between your own accounts, can get funds locked while they demand to know who, when and why for hours before letting you reach your own cash.

product.title: Customer support is effectively absent — even on paid Metal and Premium plans
product.minus: When a real problem arises users hit a bot and canned replies; there's no human to reach, and disputes drag on for months with the whole burden of proof dumped on the customer.

product.title: Endless ID and login verification loops lock you out of your own account
product.minus: Document scans fail, NFC hunts endlessly for the passport chip, and password reset spins through verify-ID-then-email-then-re-enter-password loops; many get stuck for days or weeks.

product.title: Scam victims are left with nothing, with the theft labelled "normal activity"
product.minus: When money goes to fraudsters the bank refuses to refund and disclaims responsibility — even when a burst of withdrawals within five minutes is obviously suspicious; users feel there's no real protection.

product.title: A hidden exchange spread and fees larger than the transfer itself
product.minus: Behind "0% fees" sits an internal rate worse than the mid-market, and on specific operations absurd charges surface — like a $33 fee on a $25 transfer.

product.title: Investments and metals get force-sold, and trading is shut down at their discretion
product.minus: Revolut unilaterally closes commodities trading or force-sells your shares — even when the position is down — making you exit at a loss with no clear reason.

product.title: Recent updates break the app: crashes, hanging on the splash screen, phone incompatibility
product.minus: After updates the app slows down, crashes in the background or freezes on the Revolut logo entirely; a forced update can leave you with an incompatible version, pushing you to buy a new phone or close the account.

product.title: Won't run on "non-standard" phones: rooting, unlocked bootloader, degoogling, no screen lock
product.minus: The app refuses to launch on rooted or unlocked devices, demands a permanent screen lock and Google Pay, and after degoogling loses Samsung Pay support — paranoid checks hit ordinary users.

product.title: Sign-up stalls on an SMS code that never arrives
product.minus: Some newcomers can't even create an account: the SMS verification code never arrives, the request-a-call function doesn't work, and people leave for competitors without ever opening one.

product.title: Nagging "discover more features" popups and spam to order a card
product.minus: Every time you open it the app pushes "set a budget / open a savings account" popups and reminders to order a physical card — annoying gamification you can't turn off.

product.title: Pockets, instant notifications and virtual cards make everyday finances easy
product.plus: Salary pockets for bills, instant spending notifications, disposable and virtual cards, and built-in expense tracking help keep budgets under control — people love that it's "banking as it should be".

product.title: Accounts closed out of the blue with no reason given
product.minus: The single most frequent and most frightening complaint: the bank freezes or closes the account with no warning, refuses to give a reason and holds the customer's money — sometimes their only account — for days or weeks.

product.title: Payments frozen at the worst possible moment
product.minus: The anti-fraud system blocks transfers and payments without clear explanation — the card suddenly stops working abroad, an urgent transfer to a loved one is frozen, and the customer is locked out of their own money in an emergency.

product.title: "24/7" support that resolves nothing
product.minus: The chat replies fast but fobs you off with "we'll get back to you" — and never does; agents contradict each other, don't read the actual issue and have no power to resolve anything.

product.title: Face/video verification you simply can't pass
product.minus: Onboarding dies at the video/audio verification: the system keeps demanding "clearer" attempts, people re-record 7-18 times and still can't open an account — while rivals like Revolut and Wise do it in five minutes.

product.title: Sign-up declined with no reason at all
product.minus: Many never even get an account: applications are declined with no explanation, the anti-fraud AI flags them as a "threat", addresses won't be accepted — and people leave to open accounts at friendlier banks.

product.title: A forced update that locked people out of their money
product.minus: The app abruptly demanded an update that hangs on "Updating..." or won't fit for lack of storage — and without it you can't log in; with no web version, in an emergency the user is simply cut off from their money.

product.title: Savings pots where money gets stuck or vanishes
product.minus: Pots logic is unintuitive: money in the main account earns nothing until you move it into a pot; a rent pot demands the whole month at once even if you pay weekly; and sometimes an entire pot with £100 just disappears with no way to get the money back.

product.title: Pushy ads and upsells layered over the bank
product.minus: Open the app to check your balance and you're hit with pension ads and upsell spam on the home screen; users feel the app is built more for upselling than for usability, and your data is sold to advertisers if the toggle is on.

product.title: Getting paid a day early — the feature people stay for
product.plus: Fans' favourite feature: salary and regular income land a day early with no fees — reviewers call it a game changer and the reason they stick with Monzo for years.

product.title: The most intuitive, easy-to-use banking interface
product.plus: The most-praised thing is the interface itself: clean, intuitive, "the best banking app I've ever used" — easy face-and-voice login, instant notifications, everything at your fingertips.

product.title: Pots and categories that rescue people who struggle with money
product.plus: For people with ADHD and anyone drowning in their spending, splitting money into pots and seeing it all clearly is literally how they take control; separate pots, goals and bill-splitting are praised as the best part of the bank.

product.title: Fee-free abroad and the Max plan perks
product.plus: The card works abroad fee-free at a good exchange rate, and the paid plan adds cashback, interest, phone and travel insurance, lounge access and trip bill-splitting — users find the perks bundle genuinely generous.

product.title: Pulling out of the US left loyal customers stranded
product.minus: Monzo is closing US accounts — customers for whom it was their favourite bank after Simple shut down get notice of closure by May 15 and are upset: the app was easy, the buckets handy, and now they have to find a replacement.

product.title: Face login turns into an endless loop
product.minus: The app demands a selfie at login, throws "something went wrong", offers "another way" — then asks for a selfie again; people go months unable to get into their account, and the only "fix" is reinstalling for the tenth time.

product.title: Accounts get frozen with no warning and money held for weeks
product.minus: The promised "72-hour check" stretches to one or two weeks; the account is frozen and unfrozen with zero notification, and you only learn about the freeze when you try to pay for food or rent.

product.title: Support replies with robotic boilerplate and closes the chat
product.minus: Agents don't read your message, reply with copy-paste, bounce you from "specialist" to "specialist" and end the chat without listening; phone support exists only for paying customers, and even the "priority line" just routes you back to a broken chat.

product.title: The banking app has become an ad platform
product.minus: Every launch brings a pop-up about premium, cashback or "play a game and win"; ad push notifications keep coming even after you turn them off both in Android and in the app, and there's no unsubscribe button.

product.title: The app blocks hardened OSes like GrapheneOS
product.minus: On GrapheneOS and LineageOS the app refuses to start "for security reasons", blindly trusting Play Integrity — yet runs fine on an eight-year-old phone with a leaky system; users are forced to switch banks.

product.title: Accounts get closed and applications rejected with no explanation
product.minus: After ID verification you get "we can't offer you an account for legal reasons" with no detail, and long-time customers are closed off with a pointer to the T&C — while your data stays with the bank and can't be deleted.

product.title: Investing and stocks: you can buy, but can't sell
product.minus: The sell button for a stock simply doesn't appear, crypto can't be offloaded ("error" for weeks), the numbers in the portfolio and on the security's page disagree, and migrating a portfolio via third-party Upvest breaks and leaves you unable to trade.

product.title: Hidden subscriptions and promised perks that never arrive
product.minus: People are quietly put on a paid plan, the "free" card is disabled once you cancel, and an unused account triggers €81–162 demands up to debt collection; cashback and "up to 3×" referral bonuses turn out to be zero.

product.title: Device pairing and "update the app" gates block access
product.minus: The app gets stuck on the pairing screen even though the device is already paired (confirmed by email), and on a freshly installed version it demands an "update" right at the verification step; you can't use it on two devices at once.

product.title: A clean, minimalist interface people genuinely love
product.plus: When it works, this is one of the most pleasant banking interfaces around: clear, modern, clutter-free, with an instant overview of your finances and handy money organisation via Spaces.

product.title: Fast account opening and a real EU IBAN
product.plus: An account opens in a couple of hours with just an ID and no mountain of paperwork, giving you a German EU IBAN — something especially valued by students, expats and frequent travellers who avoid hidden fees abroad.

product.title: Free transfers and instant push on every spend
product.plus: Free instant transfers, a notification on every transaction before you even leave the till, and automatic splitting of income into Spaces make spending tangible and even nudge people into ETF investing.

product.title: The redesign was met with revulsion
product.minus: The new rounded-edge interface gets called ugly "like a bad PowerPoint", the balance and 3-month overview are buried behind extra taps, and the interface is changed every six months without asking — people beg for the old version back.

product.title: Weak savings rates and country gaps
product.minus: The savings rate is uncompetitive, many advertised features are unavailable in certain countries (Italy, Switzerland, Greece), and the promised "instant savings account" never shipped — against Revolut the bank loses out beyond Germany.

product.title: The advance is advertised as easy, but is effectively unreachable
product.minus: Users are lured by ads promising a day-one advance and amounts up to $250–$2000, but the moment they apply they hit a wall of hidden conditions: a separate account linked for 60+ days, a constant $100 balance, direct deposit routed specifically to Varo. The advance amount swings randomly, and those who repay on time get cut instead of raised.

product.title: Accounts get closed with no warning, money frozen for weeks
product.minus: The most common nightmare: loyal multi-year customers suddenly get their account closed or frozen "for no reason," citing the right to close "at any time for any reason." Access to paycheck and savings vanishes, money is mailed back by check 2–3 weeks later — meaning missed rent, no food, late fees.

product.title: The app crashes on launch — and locks you out of your money
product.minus: A huge chunk of reviews: the app crashes immediately on open or at the login screen, sometimes for weeks. Reinstalling, clearing cache and updating don't help — and since Varo has no branches and no phone line, an app crash means total loss of access to your paycheck.

product.title: There is no human support — just a chatbot running in circles
product.minus: Reaching a live human is impossible: the phone sends you to chat, chat sends you to the app, and the bot loops through canned answers without solving anything. Many suspect the "live agents" are bots too. It's especially brutal when you're already locked out of the account.

product.title: Disputes and fraud go unresolved — money just disappears
product.minus: On unauthorized charges, marketplace fraud or undelivered goods, Varo repeatedly refuses disputes without review, even with proof. Money "magically" disappears, and the answer is "name the transaction" or "it's not a covered purchase." People lose anywhere from $40 to $2,500.

product.title: Changing your phone number = permanent lockout
product.minus: Login is tied to your phone number, and if you change or lose it, getting back in is nearly impossible. The system keeps sending codes to the old number, you can't switch it via email, and there's no human to verify your identity — while your paycheck keeps landing in an account you can't reach.

product.title: You can't even get past sign-up and verification
product.minus: Many stumble before they even start: the address is flagged "not residential," the verification code is rejected, the application is declined without explanation after being approved. New users often hit an absurd "your account is closed" while still trying to create one.

product.title: Hidden limits and fees on every path to your own money
product.minus: Getting your own money out is a quest: hard limits on v2v/v2a transfers and ATMs, check deposits capped at $500, external transfers taking 1–2 days, cash only via CVS/Walgreens with crazy fees. The advance fee is $8 per $50 (effectively up to 192% APR), and it climbs with every repayment.

product.title: Referral bonuses are promised but never paid
product.minus: The $150-per-referral program systematically fails: people watch a friend use their link, yet neither side gets paid. Support replies with a rote "you didn't use a referral code."

product.title: For loyal customers, it's the best bank they've had
product.plus: For a large share of users it just works for years, and they genuinely love Varo: early payday, no fees, instant internal transfers, a leg up for low-income and bad-credit folks. Many call it better than Chime/Cash App and recommend it to everyone.

product.title: Early payday and perks — the real reason people stay
product.plus: When it works, the core perks genuinely land: pay arrives 2–3 days early with a heads-up email, a 5% savings account, credit building via Believe, cashback, and handy fee-free cash deposits. For some, fraud disputes are resolved in 24 hours with provisional credit.

product.title: Money lands but vanishes — deposits and balances that won't show
product.minus: A distinct pain: money that gets "stuck" — direct deposits rejected by a botched auto-setup, balance showing zero when linked, transfers hanging, and a misrouted deposit met with "we can't locate it." Notifications stopped showing the updated balance after a transaction.

product.title: Users want Zelle, dark mode and sane navigation
product.minus: Even broadly happy customers cite concrete gaps: Zelle was removed (and the "pay anyone" replacement isn't equivalent), there's no dark mode, account limits and info are hard to find, and navigation is confusing. Not catastrophic, but exactly what holds back a 5-star.

product.title: The "up to $750" advance actually starts at $50 and shrinks over time instead of growing
product.minus: The defining grievance: ads promise up to $750, but people with steady pay get $50–150, and the limit gets cut month after month with no explanation — even when they repay on time and earn more.

product.title: Disputes are almost always lost: the AI and support side with the merchant
product.minus: Users bring evidence, emails, screenshots — and Current still denies the dispute, with no provisional credit, support that "can't help", and the app sometimes kicking them out mid-filing.

product.title: Accounts get frozen or closed with no explanation — and money is stuck for weeks
product.minus: After a "fraud review" or a sudden closure, people go weeks or months unable to reach their own money — payroll still gets accepted, access doesn't, and no reason is ever given.

product.title: To get an advance you must first route your payroll here and put in a deposit
