product.minus: Long-paying customers suddenly lose access to premium features — especially desktop/laptop vs phone — and go months unable to use what they paid for.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and bypassing the trial
product.minus: Cancelling before the trial ends doesn't help — they take the yearly fee, hit every card on file, banks fire fraud alerts, and refunds are nearly impossible.

product.title: The subscription model is hidden until after install
product.minus: That it's subscription-based and requires sign-up before you can try anything isn't disclosed in the ad or store — users demand upfront transparency.

product.title: Constant "Uh-oh, something went wrong" and crashes
product.minus: Core features (Remove, Enhance, AI) keep failing with an error, the app crashes mid-project losing work — especially after each update.

product.title: AI quality doesn't live up to the promises
product.minus: The AI misreads instructions, fails at simple edits (shaving a beard, a B&W filter), and mangles faces during retouch — disappointing against the loud promises.

product.title: Support doesn't help and runs you in circles
product.minus: The "Ask us Anything" button is broken, emails go unanswered, paying users get the runaround asked for the same info repeatedly — even 3+ year customers.

product.title: Background removal is the flagship feature, and it's free
product.plus: The most-loved thing: fast, high-quality background removal available for free. Small businesses — bakeries, sellers — use it for clean, professional product shots.

product.title: Easy entry for beginners, but with a real learning curve
product.plus: Many praise how intuitive and easy it is the first time — layering is easy for beginners, navigation is smooth. Yet some admit the powerful options carry a noticeable learning curve.

product.title: A professional tool that genuinely makes money
product.plus: A loyal core uses Bazaart for years for logos, banners, flyers and social media — their main work tool for business and marketing that earns its subscription back.

product.title: A creative playground that earns genuine love
product.plus: Fans of 6+ years describe delight: limitless options, "Photoshop on steroids," restoring old photos, funny collages — an app they can't live without.

product.title: Updates break the app rather than fix it
product.minus: Nearly every update brings fresh bugs: a glitched preview of colored rectangles, a blue tint over every photo, pixelation, ruined video exports. Users explicitly say the app used to work perfectly and updates are killing it.

product.title: Paid subscription, yet still can't use it
product.minus: People pay for premium and that's exactly when the app stops working: tabs spin forever, tools throw errors, not a single feature works. It stings most right after renewing a yearly plan.

product.title: Masking wipes out all your work
product.minus: One of the core tools — masking — keeps resetting every edit on a photo. People spend time on a complex edit, add a mask, remove it, and the whole process is wiped. For some it happened ten times over.

product.title: Everything useful is paywalled from second one
product.minus: Users can't even trial it: a subscribe pop-up appears on every action, features are locked behind payment, video editing is behind a paywall. Many uninstall within five minutes without touching a single feature.

product.title: Easy to subscribe, nearly impossible to cancel
product.minus: Charges appear without consent, cancelling triggers a fee, and money is taken even on a "failed trial." People call it a scam and warn that once you subscribe, getting out is brutally hard.

product.title: Crashes and freezes when saving or exporting
product.minus: The app crashes on save, stalls on the export screen, overheats the phone, and falsely claims the drive is full — zeroing out dozens of gigabytes. Finished work is lost without saving.

product.title: AI object removal leaves visible traces
product.minus: The flagship removal tool fails: manual removal of small distractions doesn't work, and the eraser leaves contrasting halos around objects on gradient backgrounds — it used to come out smooth. For working photographers that's direct damage.

product.title: Account required, photos and albums vanish
product.minus: Nothing works without signing in, and the sign-in itself stalls and loops endlessly. Worse, updates make entire albums disappear, edits and presets are lost, and photos vanish from old accounts.

product.title: Desktop color grading in your pocket — the thing users love most
product.plus: What people genuinely adore is the color control. They call it desktop-level grading, with powerful tools that make photos ten times better, pulling out vibrance and bringing a "dead" shot back to life.

product.title: The free tier is already powerful and ad-free
product.plus: Those who stay on the free plan note it's plenty: great free tools, no ads, and a solid substitute for the web version. For many it's a clear step up from the editor in their stock gallery.

product.title: Simple and clean — works even for beginners
product.plus: Despite the pro-level depth, the interface is praised as simple and clean. Beginners get into it fast and gain confidence, while experienced users value that powerful edits get done quickly with no fuss.

product.title: Missing workflow basics: manual crop, duplicates, value entry
product.minus: Even happy users hit missing basics: no crop to an arbitrary ratio like 7:9, no duplicate of a photo within an album, no way to type edit values as text to copy presets quickly.

product.title: Export breaks: clips freeze or the app crashes
product.minus: The single most common complaint: on export the app crashes, stalls at 15-20%, or saves the clip with frozen frames. People spend hours on an edit they then can't save at all.

product.title: The finished video turns into a string of still images
product.minus: An app-defining bug: after export the video clips become still photos — all motion is gone. Dozens describe the same loss of hours of work.

product.title: The element library died with "something went wrong"
product.minus: A mass outage: opening elements throws "something went wrong". Reinstalling, clearing cache or switching accounts doesn't fix it, and it hits many users at once.

product.title: The preview freezes mid-edit so you can't see progress
product.minus: The in-edit player freezes: you hit play and the picture won't move while the music keeps going. Without a working preview you can't time transitions or see what you're making.

product.title: Heavy lag on Android, especially on Samsung
product.minus: It lags so badly you can't time a transition; users repeatedly note iOS runs fine while the Android version has been left behind.

product.title: Audio disappears or desyncs on save
product.minus: Saving to the gallery strips the audio, and from drafts the sound saves out of sync with the video even when it matched in the editor.

product.title: Paywall on export and basic features frustrates
product.minus: Many resent that Pro is demanded just to save your work, screen-record, or slow-mo; people compare it to CapCut and call it a money grab.

product.title: Too many ads before every action
product.minus: Starting an edit, removing the watermark and exporting each force several ads in a row — and the app may still crash afterward.

product.title: Support is silent, bugs go unfixed for years
product.minus: Support emails go unanswered and the same bugs persist for over a year; even paying subscribers have lost accounts with no help.

product.title: Rich set of effects, shakes and transitions — the reason people love it
product.plus: The core strength: a huge range of effects, shakes, transitions, texts and overlays. Many call it "After Effects for mobile" and rate it above CapCut.

product.title: Easy entry for beginners, teaches you to edit
product.plus: Beginners praise how approachable it is: you can learn from YouTube tutorials, and it genuinely builds your editing skills.

product.title: No remove-animation button and no reverse on Android
product.minus: Advanced editors miss basic controls: you can't remove an applied shake animation, and Android users have no reverse button and fewer graph options.

product.title: Community and built-in feed, but with toxicity and NSFW
product.minus: The built-in social feed is a plus for many, but it carries inappropriate content and toxic communities, with children among the users.

product.title: One-tap object removal is the core thing people love
product.plus: The core magic works: select a person or object and it vanishes. For users who "can't edit well", this is exactly what they wanted.

product.title: Surprise charges and refunds that never come
product.minus: Users report double and unauthorized charges — even people who say they never subscribed or used the app. Refunds simply don't arrive.

product.title: The "free trial" charges you a second time
product.minus: Even the 3-day trial ends in a card charge, and it's unclear where to cancel the subscription during the trial. The offer feels dishonest.

product.title: Almost everything is premium — even basic erase and effects
product.minus: The erase feature itself is paid, pro features are expensive, and users beg for at least basic features to be free.

product.title: No way to save the result — you resort to screenshots
product.minus: After editing there's no save button, so people work around it with screenshots. On top of that, you're charged to get your own photo back in original resolution.

product.title: Erased spots turn to mush and the background breaks
product.minus: Removing an object leaves an unreal background, blurs the picture, and sometimes wipes the background along with the object — nothing like the ads show.

product.title: Succeeds where other erasers leave a watermark
product.plus: Some users came here after failed watermark-leaving apps and finally got a clean result — that was their "wow" moment.

product.title: Hooks with simplicity — opened like a daily toy
product.plus: Those who like it come back regularly, recommend it to friends, and describe it as light, fun entertainment.

product.title: Suspiciously broad permissions scare users off
product.minus: People can't see why a photo app needs access to system settings, audio/video recording and personal data — and delete it over this.

product.title: Canceling and support go unanswered
product.minus: Users can't cancel the subscription, email support and get no reply — it feels like there's no way out of the billing funnel.

product.title: The clone tool is raw and clumsy
product.minus: Cloning works crudely: users want an undo after lifting the finger and more precise movement-copying for accurate results.

product.title: Requests for offline effects and more retouch options
product.minus: Even happy users ask for more: offline effects for all edits and more color tools like whitening.

product.title: Crashes in the middle of editing
product.minus: The app closes, freezes and loses the photo halfway through: people can't finish editing a single picture and have to start over every time.

product.title: The purchase unbinds when you switch phones
product.minus: After buying access (even "lifetime"), people lose it on a new phone or after reinstalling — and are forced to pay for the app again and again.

product.title: A huge set of face and body tools
product.plus: One editor does almost everything: face and body shaping, hair color, skin tone, makeup, background — people are floored by the sheer number of tools in one place.

product.title: The generous free version wins people over
product.plus: Many call it the best free editor out there: genuinely useful tools are available without paying, and some people never even hit the paywall.

product.title: Charged for something they never used
product.minus: People report being billed for a subscription they never used, charged on a cancelled trial, and then denied refunds.

product.title: Natural makeup with no "plastic" look
product.plus: Women use it to try makeup on for weddings and parties: foundation looks natural and the face doesn't come out artificial or over-retouched.

product.title: Paid tools get slipped in unnoticed
product.minus: A paid tool is offered to try "once", and absorbed in the edit, a person doesn't notice they've already used something they now have to pay for; the pop-ups are annoying.

product.title: Simple and intuitive for beginners
product.plus: Despite the pile of features, it's easy to figure out: people call it a handy photo "swiss army knife" that suits both beginners and pros.

product.title: Won't save the finished result
product.minus: The most maddening part: when the photo finally looks good, the app refuses to save it — tapping the tick does nothing, or it throws "download failed".

product.title: Realistic retouch and color correction
product.plus: Subtle skin fixes (acne, for instance), white balance, shadows and color tones come out natural — it enhances the shot without distorting the actual image.

product.title: Sometimes the edits come out cartoonish
product.minus: Despite the natural reputation, for some people the touch-ups look cartoonish, there's no preview of adjustments, and the original photo size gets lost on export.

product.title: Demands you upload photos and pushes other apps
product.minus: People are unsettled that the app insistently demands they send photos and, mid-session, dumps them into Pinterest with prompts to install yet another AI app.

product.title: Crashes specifically when editing a photo from the gallery
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the moment users import a shot from their gallery and start changing effects or exposure, the app closes itself — sometimes several times in a row on the very same photo.

product.title: The app won't open at all for some users
product.minus: For some it never even gets to editing: launch throws bugs and errors, the photo screen won't load, and the camera simply can't be opened.

product.title: Ads show up instead of the actual camera
product.minus: It's not just the frequency: people complain that picking a preset camera opens an ad page instead of the camera — enough that some uninstall on the spot.

product.title: The vintage aesthetic is the reason people keep it
product.plus: For those who get past the bugs, it's the film-grain vintage look that hooks them: "old school" photos and an aesthetic result are the main reason they love it.

product.title: The free filters feel like a gift
product.plus: A standout delight is that quality filters and cameras are available for free, with no mandatory paywall; for some users that alone is the deciding factor.

product.title: No video mode — a frequent request
product.minus: Even users happy with the camera hit the lack of video recording and ask for that option to be added.

product.title: Missing a favorites list for cameras and presets
product.minus: Regular users want to save their favorite cameras with their own fader settings into a quick list — which isn't possible today.

product.title: The camera is good, but the capture itself breaks
product.minus: The cameras themselves get praise, but capture lets people down: for some the shutter only makes a sound and shows "failed to capture", for others saving drags on forever after an effect is applied.

product.title: The flash stays on constantly instead of only during capture
product.minus: A small but telling nitpick from a loyal user: the flash burns continuously when it should only fire at the moment a photo is taken.

product.title: The concept lands, but execution and filter selection disappoint
product.minus: People call the idea interesting, yet the app feels disorganized, and some simply didn't find a single filter that was actually pleasing to them.

product.title: The 4.0 redesign destroyed the familiar interface — the update's central wound
product.minus: The overwhelming majority of long-time users experienced the new interface as a wholesale replacement of something that had worked perfectly for years. Menus, colors and fonts were changed for no reason, and people are begging en masse to bring the old version back.

product.title: The new interface looks childish and cheap
product.minus: The new UI's aesthetic is its own raw nerve: users compare it to something a child made, a school project, and amateur apps from fifteen years ago. The app used to look elegant and professional; now it looks garish and homemade.

product.title: The app became noticeably slower after the update
product.minus: Snapseed used to be fast and snappy, but 4.0 lags: photos take a minute to load, presets take 5-10 seconds each to apply, everything takes longer. It hits hardest for people doing batch edits for business.

product.title: The googly-eyes animation on every edit is infuriating
product.minus: The new cartoon-eyes animation pops up on every action, slows things down, and feels like mockery. For a serious editor it reads as an attempt to turn the tool into a kids' toy.

product.title: Masking is broken: edits apply to the whole photo
product.minus: The core masking feature doesn't work: users set up a mask and the effect applies to the entire image, ignoring the selection. Often masking simply crashes the app when trying the auto-subject tool.

product.title: Post-update crashes, even rebooting the phone
product.minus: After 4.0 the app is unstable: it crashes during editing, freezes, and in the worst cases reboots the entire phone. Galaxy S25 and S25 Ultra owners complain most.

product.title: RAW files from newer cameras no longer open
product.minus: For DSLR photographers this is fatal: the app stopped opening RAW — Fujifilm, .NEF, .CR2, .ARW, .DNG all throw a load error. It worked before; now the editor is useless to them.

product.title: A "could not save photo" error destroys the work
product.minus: Users spend hours on complex edits like double exposure only to hit a save error at the finish. Export also degrades quality and over-saturates the image compared to the preview.

product.title: Mandatory photo import into the app breaks the workflow
product.minus: The new flow forces you to "add" a photo into the app before editing instead of editing directly, adding extra steps. Export no longer lets you pick a destination folder, and edited shots get confused with originals in the feed.

product.title: Forced AI and online dependency in an offline editor
product.minus: Some users are angry that AI features were stuffed into a simple offline editor and that it now keeps demanding internet. They see it as an attempt to cripple a good product in favor of online services.

product.title: For newcomers, the best free, ad-free editor
product.plus: Those who arrived without the baggage of the old interface are delighted: a powerful toolset, all premium features free, works offline, and zero ads. To newcomers the new layout feels logical and easy.

product.title: New tools — camera, masking, film simulations — get genuine praise
product.plus: Beyond the UI fights, some users genuinely love the new capabilities: a built-in camera with filters, auto-masking, film simulations, premium animations and haptics. For them 4.0 is a great upgrade that even replaces Lightroom mobile.

product.title: Years as the beloved go-to editor — deep loyalty
product.plus: The brand strength is immense: people have used Snapseed for 8-15 years, call it the best in the world, and recommend it to everyone. That very love is what makes the update's disappointment so sharp — they leave with a "heavy heart."

product.title: No option to revert to the old interface — the one ask
product.minus: Even those willing to tolerate the new features ask for one thing: a toggle between the old and new UI. The lack of choice pushes people to hunt for old APKs on third-party sites like APKPure just to get the familiar back.

product.title: Once-free tools moved behind a paywall
product.minus: Longtime users describe the same arc: filters, grain, copy-edits and basic adjustments that were free for years are now locked behind a subscription — even for people who once bought those very presets outright. The feeling isn't "expensive," it's "they took back what was already mine."

product.title: An ad banner up top covers the photo itself while editing
product.minus: The sharpest grievance: a recently-added ad banner sits above the editing area and literally blocks part of the image, making it impossible to crop or see the whole photo. It stings doubly for paying subscribers who find ads-while-subscribed absurd.

product.title: The Android back button/gesture closes the entire app
product.minus: System back navigation is broken: the swipe or back button kicks you out of the app entirely instead of going to the previous screen. Muscle memory makes people accidentally close VSCO over and over and lose unsaved edits; the bug has gone unfixed for months.

product.title: Deleting your account is nearly impossible — links lead to 404s and dead ends
product.minus: The "delete account" button leads to a page that doesn't exist, the web version has no such button, and the only path is a chatbot that demands your ID and billing info and then never replies for weeks. Users read it as a deliberate way to hold onto their data.

product.title: The free trial silently becomes a yearly charge with no warning
product.minus: People report the trial auto-renewed straight into a year-long charge, with the billing email arriving only after the money was gone — no advance warning. It's worsened by there being almost nowhere to cancel or refund: email is dead, no ticketing, and Google Play "doesn't show" the subscription.

product.title: Video export has been broken for months — even for paying subscribers
product.minus: The video editor is a sore point: clips won't export, come out black, cropped or in unwatchable quality, or just get visually mangled on import. Paying customers file tickets for months and get only "thanks for your patience" with no fix.

product.title: Constant "server error" — can't log in, post, or open your account
product.minus: The backend is flaky: sign-in hangs or returns "problems connecting to our systems," notifications open with an error, and posts get stuck on "Posting…". It hits hardest for people who switched phones and can't get back into a paid account.

product.title: The Android build lags far behind iOS, and fans feel abandoned
product.minus: Android payers report new features land on iOS only, presets and features (location, halation, bloom) are missing for them, and the app crashes on recent flagships like the Z Fold 7, S25 Ultra and Pixel 10. It reads as the devs having abandoned the platform.

product.title: Forcing an account just to edit a photo turns people off
product.minus: Just to edit a photo on your own phone, the app demands you create an account and sign in with Google, sometimes also linking social media. Many see it as needlessly invasive data collection and delete the app before ever reaching the editor.

product.title: Losing photos, edits and presets when switching phones
product.minus: Some users lose unpublished edits, years of photos and the "recipes" they built when reinstalling or moving to a new phone — despite using the same account. There's no proper sync, and nothing can be recovered.

product.title: A quiet, non-social alternative to Instagram — no likes or counters
product.plus: The core love for VSCO: a calm, photos-only space with no reels, no public likes or follower counts, where you aren't judged by numbers. Users describe it as a personal archive of cherished memories and a community of photographers without the social-media noise.

product.title: Film presets and "recipes" are why people stay for years
product.plus: Even the angriest reviewers concede that VSCO's signature film filters and aesthetic remain best-in-class, and the "recipe" feature (saved edit sets) is a favorite. Many have stayed 8-10 years purely for the simple editing and the filters' "vibe."

product.title: No private account or control over visibility
product.minus: Despite being positioned as a quiet social space, the app offers no way to make an account private or accept only the followers you want. For some users that's a safety concern and a reason to consider deleting their profile.

product.title: They keep charging even after you cancel
product.minus: People cancel the same day with confirmation in hand, yet the card is still charged — monthly, yearly, quarterly. Refunds are refused even when the app was never used.

product.title: Cancelling is made almost impossible by design
product.minus: The cancel button is nowhere to be found: the subscription doesn't show up in Google Play management, and in-app cancellation "times out." Some say they're closing their bank account just to stop the charges.

product.title: Painfully few hairstyles to try on, and all long
product.minus: The headline use case — trying on a new haircut — falls apart: only 5-12 options, nearly all variations of long hair. No pixie, no short cuts, no length change, no men's styles.

product.title: Doesn't change the cut — just tweaks your own bangs
product.minus: Instead of trying on a hairstyle, the app only works over your real hair: it nudges the bangs, won't show a different length, and if your hair is up it doesn't work at all. The ad promises something completely different.

product.title: Free to download only — no subscription, no entry
product.minus: A subscription wall pops up the moment you open the app and blocks everything until you pay. There's no way to try before buying, and people call it "scummy" — they'd rather it just admit it costs money.

product.title: The advertised price isn't what they actually charge
product.minus: They promise 29.99 a year and bill 39.99; instead of a "free trial" they pull 61 dollars with no clear reminder. The timing and amounts of charges are deliberately confusing.

product.title: The "Eyes" feature has been crashing the app for months
product.minus: Tap the eyes tool and the app crashes — and it's been like this on Pixel for half a year. Support calls it a "known bug" and never fixes it.

product.title: Updates stripped free tools and ruined the results
product.minus: Long-time users are furious: the developers gutted the free "Looks," "Reshape," "Refine" and Lighting effects, and the post-update hairstyles look unnatural. It used to be better.

product.title: The AI output is fake — cartoonish or just disfiguring
product.minus: Too much AI turns photos plastic: faces go cartoonish, the neck shrinks to anorexic, a black dot or a second face lands on the forehead. Instead of editing, it just blurs the shot.

product.title: There are simply no men's haircuts
product.minus: Men spend an hour hunting for their cuts and find only women's long hair or beards. For men's hairstyles the app simply doesn't work.

product.title: It won't edit video despite being a "Photo & Video" app
product.minus: The name promises video, but trying to edit a clip slaps a white square around your head that never goes away — or the app refuses to show videos from your gallery at all.

product.title: When it works, the retouch is subtle and natural — no plastic look
product.plus: For the lucky ones, Facetune edits the face gently without overdoing it: photos stay realistic, teeth-whitening is precise, and the result is "passport authentic only better." Many call it the best photo editor they've used.

product.title: Simple and intuitive — an easy entry for beginners
product.plus: Those who stay are won over by the ease: the interface is easy to navigate, the tools are clear, and people simply have fun playing with their photos and trying on looks.

product.title: An ad gates every single action: open, enhance, save
product.minus: Ads aren't sprinkled in — they're wired into every step of the flow: one to open the app, one to enhance, and a separate one to save. People spend minutes dismissing ads instead of seconds doing the task.

product.title: One photo = 7–10 ad clips and tens of minutes
product.minus: To process a single image users count 7–10 ad breaks, some 30–60 seconds long. What should take seconds stretches to 10–20 minutes.

product.title: Enhancement quality is the real reason people put up with the rest
product.plus: When a photo does get processed, the result earns praise — images come out cleaner and sharper. That quality is exactly why people don't delete it outright.

product.title: After the ad the photo won't save and the work is lost
product.minus: A distinct pain: after enduring everything to the save step, users hit endless loading or an ad crash, and the enhanced photo never saves — sometimes the whole flow resets to the start.

product.title: Ads hijack you out of the app — opening Play Store, Chrome, other apps
product.minus: Ads don't just interrupt — they auto-launch the store, a browser, or third-party apps, and for some users that escalated into fear about access to payment apps.

product.title: Gambling ads feel toxic and forced on the user
product.minus: The kind of ads stings too: users report constant online-gambling and casino spots, reading them as being lured in rather than just noise.

product.title: Charges and subscription: pricey, un-cancellable, feels like a scam
product.minus: Paying doesn't restore trust: users describe surprise charges, a steep weekly subscription, no way to cancel, and paying for a product that froze and didn't work.

product.title: Slow and unstable: freezes, disconnects, lag
product.minus: Even setting ads aside, processing is slow: users cite constant disconnects, freezes, and long waits for the enhancement itself.

product.title: You can't test a single photo without a trial or subscription
product.minus: A barrier at the door: just to check whether the result is any good, the app demands you start a trial or subscribe — there's no way to test one photo as-is.

product.title: Repeated gender/intent prompts at the start grate
product.minus: Onboarding is pushy: the app keeps asking for gender and "what are you here to do," loads a module, then immediately pushes payment — it reads like an interrogation aimed at conversion.

product.title: It used to be better: quality dropped and ads grew over time
product.minus: Loyal users flag regression: there used to be fewer ads and cleaner edits — now ads flood in and processing sometimes alters the nose and face for the worse.

product.title: The free version is effectively unusable — pay or do nothing
product.minus: Users complain that the free tier leaves just one or two options, and even those need Pro to actually apply. Many uninstall without managing to edit a single photo.

product.title: Natural retouch with no "AI look" — that's what people love
product.plus: The top compliment: it cleans up skin, wrinkles and scars while keeping the face recognizable and the expression intact. It's the perfect light touch-up for a social-media photo.

product.title: Paid for Pro — yet the app still demands you buy Pro
product.minus: A recurring subscription bug: people paid for Pro, but the app keeps treating them as free — features don't unlock and restoring the purchase fails.

product.title: Stripped features from people who already pay
product.minus: Long-time subscribers are furious: updates removed the very sections they paid for (video, face swap, skin filters, smiles, hair colors). It feels like paying more and getting less.

product.title: Simple and easy — almost zero learning curve
product.plus: Consistently praised for simplicity: a light, intuitive, fast editor where even a beginner gets a clean result right away. Many stick with it for years precisely because it's easy.

product.title: Pricing feels predatory: annual-only, no lifetime
product.minus: Users find the price inflated and "greedy": no one-time purchase, only a costly yearly plan that adds up to a lot over a few years.

product.title: Sticky reputation: used for 5-6 years and more
product.plus: A strong loyalty signal: many reviews come from people who've kept the app for 5-6 years, since 2020 and earlier. One of the earliest AI editors, and it still holds up.

product.title: Edit limit: an "angry cat" stops even paying users
product.minus: Even with Pro the app hits an edit cap: after a few photos it blocks you ("too many edits") or crashes, and you can't continue.

product.title: Ads promise free styles that don't actually exist
product.minus: People feel misled by the ads: they were promised 20 free hairstyles, but in reality any style requires payment — which they read as false advertising.

product.title: Generative AI mangles photos: artifacts instead of clean filters
product.minus: Some users want the old non-generative filters: the new AI introduces ugly artifacts — removing clothes, warping features, arms sticking out. For them it's a downgrade, not an upgrade.

product.title: Best in class: "tried hundreds — nothing compares"
product.plus: An enthusiastic core: those who like it rank it above every competitor — the only app they'll pay for, the gold standard, "10 out of 10."

product.title: A paid subscription stops being recognized, and "restore purchase" does nothing
product.minus: After updates the app suddenly treats an active paying user as unsubscribed and demands payment again. The "restore" and "purchase" buttons do nothing; only reinstalling sometimes helps — and lately not even that.

product.title: Features that were free for years got moved behind a paywall
product.minus: Long-time users are furious that basic tools like spot removal, once free, now require a subscription. The free version feels gutted and pointless without paying.

product.title: Paid Pro has a hidden daily usage limit
product.minus: Paying subscribers hit a "you've reached your Pro limits" wall mid-edit and must wait until tomorrow. Calling the tier "unlimited" feels like a lie.

product.title: Natural, non-fake retouching is the core reason people love it
product.plus: Users praise subtle, realistic edits that fix small flaws without turning the face into a plastic blur. Many judge every other editor against this one.

product.title: Restoring old and blurry photos brings memories back to life
product.plus: The most emotional strength: the app restores old, damaged and blurry photos of loved ones who've passed. For many this is irreplaceable memory, not just editing.

product.title: The AI Replace tool broke in an update: it edits the whole photo instead of the selection
product.minus: The once-loved AI Replace now distorts the entire image instead of the selected area, throws errors, or returns 2 nearly identical garbage options instead of the old five.

product.title: Filters stop loading; only restarting the app helps
product.minus: A recurring bug: while cycling filters the preview stops updating and shows the original. The only fix is to force-close the app, losing all editing progress.

product.title: Pricing spiked sharply, especially the shift to weekly billing
product.minus: Veterans who paid ~$4 a month now face $4.99 a week and yearly plans up to $80. The price jump with no loyalty reward pushes many toward competitors.

product.title: Double and unauthorized charges on the card
product.minus: Users report being charged two or three times a month, and being billed with no subscription at all. Refunds are near impossible to get, turning complaints into fraud accusations.

product.title: Support goes silent for weeks, even for paying users
product.minus: When subscriptions break, users email support and wait a week for a reply, get canned responses, or hear nothing. Paying status buys no faster help.

product.title: An easy, friendly interface — even beginners edit effortlessly
product.plus: A constant theme of praise: an intuitive interface packed with tools delivers fast results and suits novices and pros alike. For many it's their favorite daily editor.

product.title: Intrusive video ads and a black-screen bug wipe out progress
product.minus: Saving a photo or unlocking a feature forces a video ad that often freezes to a black screen with no close button. Users must exit and restart the whole edit.

product.title: New censorship and narrowed capabilities frustrate long-time creators
product.minus: Responding to law changes, the app now blocks some content and removed hairstyles and options people used for years. Users feel the company decided to be their "nanny."

product.title: Cancelling doesn't stop the charges
product.minus: The single loudest complaint: people cancel (often the same day, often immediately), and the money keeps coming out — weekly, monthly or quarterly. The subscription frequently doesn't even appear in Google Play's subscription manager, so there's no normal way to cancel, and refunds are routinely refused.

product.title: "Free" is a paywall from the first tap
product.minus: The app downloads free and is advertised that way, but you can't actually use it: a subscription screen appears immediately and won't let you past without paying. People feel deceived — "just say it costs money".

product.title: The free trial bills you with no warning
product.minus: People sign up for a 7-day (or 30-day) free trial and get charged immediately or before it ends — with no clear reminder. The amounts are large ($40, $61, 2,200 pesos), often money meant for bills, and they can't get it back afterward.

product.title: The hairstyle try-on barely exists
product.minus: The main reason people install — trying on new hairstyles — is exactly what fails: there are only about 10-12 styles, nearly all long and nearly identical, with no men's cuts at all. Often the style doesn't apply at all — it just tweaks the bangs a little or blurs the edges of the hair.

product.title: The AI result looks fake and deforms the face
product.minus: When editing does work, the result often looks unnatural: the face changes beyond recognition, black dots appear on the forehead, an extra face shows up in the hair, the body looks anorexic. The pictures come out cartoonish and "fake".

product.title: Crashes on the "Eyes" feature — unfixed for months
product.minus: The app reliably crashes when you tap "Eyes" (especially on Pixel) and freezes on "finalizing edit". It's a known bug: people contact support, get told it's known, and it stays unfixed for six months or more.

product.title: Ads promise features the app doesn't have
product.minus: The ads and description lure people with specific promises — find your face shape/skin tone, match colors to your look, try on glasses, shave a beard different ways, run a color analysis — but inside none of it exists or works as shown.

product.title: Updates break what used to work
product.minus: Long-time users say new versions are worse than old ones: hairstyles became unnatural, free tools were taken away ("Looks", "Reshape", "Refine"), lighting was changed and now ruins the background. The recurring plea is "bring back the old version".

product.title: You pay, and the VIP access still gets cut off
product.minus: Even paying, active subscribers suddenly get locked out of VIP features: the app asks them to subscribe again, throws "Oops...something went wrong", or changes the plan price weeks later and blocks access. They've paid — and still can't get in.

product.title: Doesn't edit video, even after paying for it
product.minus: Some people subscribe to edit video, but the app doesn't do video: it only shows photos in the gallery, and on Pixel any action slaps a giant white square around the head and ruins the clip.

product.title: When it works, it gives subtle, realistic retouching
product.plus: People for whom the app works praise exactly its naturalness: edits look realistic, no "phony AI" look, teeth whitening is precise, the face looks younger. For basic photo touch-ups and business/passport shots they're happy with it.

product.title: An easy, fun tool for changing your look
product.plus: Fans love how simple and enjoyable it is to try things on: easy to swap outfits, hairstyles and looks, easy to navigate, plenty to play with before a real-life decision. For them it's one of the best photo editors out there.

product.title: The paywall hits before you can edit a single thing
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the app demands a card and a subscription right after install, without letting you try a single feature. People uninstall before ever seeing what it can do.

product.title: Fails to detect a face even on a clear front-facing selfie
product.minus: Over and over, "no face detected" pops up on photos where the face is the only, perfectly clear subject. Without detection the whole flow stalls — the user can't reach any tool at all.

product.title: The free trial turns into a full year charged up front
product.minus: People tap a "3-day free trial" and the full yearly amount is pulled instantly (anywhere from $20 to 3,200 rupees). Many can't even tell how or when they supposedly subscribed.

product.title: The subscription can't be cancelled — the option vanishes or errors out
product.minus: A huge slice of reviews is about being unable to cancel: no option, a "service error" on every attempt, money still flowing out. It turns a one-time curiosity into a trap.

product.title: Ads promise hair-style and hair-color changes the app simply doesn't have
product.minus: A distinct wave of letdown: people install it for the hair-style and hair-color try-on shown in ads — and the feature is either missing entirely or wrecks the photo. Plain false advertising.

product.title: Crashes and freezes the moment you pick a photo with a person in it
product.minus: No stability: white screen on launch, freeze after picking a photo, a crash specifically on shots with a person. One user nailed the pattern — a coffee cup loads fine, a selfie kills the app.

product.title: The result is just warping the photo, not real retouching
product.minus: Those who do reach the tools describe the same thing: the app stretches and squeezes the image to fake a reshape, with no masks or anchoring. Faces go cartoonish and the result looks fake.

product.title: Body tools only work on a nude photo and effectively only "for girls"
product.minus: Ads show a man getting muscles, but in practice the body editor switches off when clothes are on and often forces the result into a female template. For men and clothed photos the feature is useless.

product.title: Overpriced for what free apps do better
product.minus: The price feels sky-high for a basic warper: people name free FaceApp, Hypic and others as the better alternative outright. It reads as "a cash grab before you can even test it."

product.title: Hair and features don't land: eyebrows on the forehead, color all over the face
product.minus: When the tools do fire, placement is off: eyebrows and lashes land on the forehead, hair color smears across the brow, lipstick misses the lips. The editor's precision just fails.

product.title: Recognizes only Eurocentric looks
product.minus: A pointed signal of a narrow model: a user with braids finds only "white" hairstyles available, while the app mangles their real hair. Looks outside the Eurocentric template aren't supported.

product.title: When the paid engine actually fires, the edits are clean and precise
product.plus: A minority of reviews praise exactly the moments when it works: precise edits that don't turn your face into someone else's, clear sliders, and no nagging to buy while using it for free.

product.title: Almost all the good content is behind a paywall
product.minus: Most effects are marked VIP, and the best templates only open after you pay. There used to be far more free options — after reinstalling, people find that nearly everything has become premium.

product.title: The trial demands a card up front and charges before it even starts
product.minus: To start the "free" trial you must add a card up front, and the description says nothing about it. People complain money gets taken before the trial even begins — for many that's reason enough to delete it on the spot.

product.title: Charges keep coming after you cancel
product.minus: People cancel the subscription and still get charged weekly. Cancelling the trial doesn't help — the full amount comes off the card, support stays silent, and the money keeps disappearing.

product.title: $7.99 a week is too steep for a toy
product.minus: The $7.99-per-week price scares off casual users: nobody wants to pay that much just to swap hairstyles and filters. For many it only makes sense if you earn money with it, not if you're just having fun.

product.title: People genuinely love the toon results and quality
product.plus: When people reach the result, it impresses: quality filters, beautiful portraits, better than other toon apps. Many call it the best of its kind and get hooked for a long time.

product.title: Your own AI portrait is a confidence boost
product.plus: For many the standout is "Create your own AI": a new look that makes them feel more confident and attractive. People say the portrait keeps the likeness while making them look better.

product.title: Double-charged for the yearly plan
product.minus: People sign up for a yearly plan, but the system marks it as weekly and charges again immediately. The result is $60 paid instead of $30 for just a week of access — even from users who love the app.

product.title: Confusing menus, no search or sort
product.minus: Among 50-100 options there's no search or sort — you scroll through everything only to hit a paywall. The selection menus themselves strike people as confusing at best.

product.title: Photo and account access reads as data harvesting
product.minus: The app asks for gallery access and forces account creation, then still pushes you to pay — for some people this looks like a photo-and-data grab dressed up as a service.

product.title: Simple and easy — clicks for newcomers right away
product.plus: Install, open, and it just makes sense — no bugs, no hassle. Especially good for newcomers: the interface is simple, it works first try, and it's easy to lose track of time.

product.title: An ad blocks the finished result
product.minus: There aren't many ads overall, but one intrusive one covers the already-finished toonified shot — souring the experience even for otherwise happy users.

product.title: Alters the face until the person is unrecognizable
product.minus: Sometimes the result drifts too far from the original: the face changes so much the person is unrecognizable. For anyone wanting a true-to-life portrait, that's a direct downside.

product.title: Age-progression swaps in a stranger's face
product.minus: The aging feature returns not the uploaded person but a picture resembling the app's own model, or an entirely random person — the face is completely different.

product.title: Aging turns Black subjects white
product.minus: Upload a Black child or yourself and the result comes back white, Indian or Asian; the model simply doesn't preserve race.

product.title: Subscription charged without consent and nearly impossible to cancel
product.minus: Money keeps going for a subscription users never signed up for or already cancelled; it's invisible in the Play Store, there's no cancel button in the app, and charges keep coming.

product.title: The 'free trial' charges you instantly
product.minus: The ad promises a 3-7 day free trial, but the full amount is taken the moment you tap it, before you ever get to try anything.

product.title: Endless ads, and you still can't save the photo
product.minus: It promises a save after watching an ad, but after two to four clips it still asks for one more or an upgrade — the photo never actually saves.

product.title: Nothing is testable without a card and a subscription
product.minus: The app demands card details before the first edit; there's effectively no free function to judge the quality on.

product.title: Black screen instead of a result after upload
product.minus: Pick a photo from the gallery and instead of an enhanced image you get a black screen; 'enhance photo' and 'remove object' break especially often.

product.title: Crashes and won't run on Android/Samsung/Xiaomi
product.minus: The app force-closes on launch, shows only half the screen, or hangs on 'maintenance' for days — especially on Samsung and Xiaomi.

product.title: Aging demands photos of several different people
product.minus: To age one child the app asks for several photos of different, unrelated people you don't have, leaving users feeling their pictures will be sold off.

product.title: Result is worse than the original, or no different at all
product.minus: Even when something does generate, many say the photo came out worse, hands turned to a blurry mess, and the age difference never showed up.

product.title: Refunds are promised on paper but denied in practice
product.minus: Even without using the app, users can't get refunds: support claims it was 'used' or simply goes silent for months.

product.title: When it works on old photos, the restoration impresses
product.plus: For users for whom it actually worked, the quality of restoring old and low-res photos is loved — clean and without a 'fake' altered look.

product.title: "It used to be better": the core complaint is post-redesign degradation
product.minus: The single most common theme: years-loyal users say every update made the app worse — styles removed, tools removed, everything turned into "basically a Google photo editor".

product.title: Hard paywall: you can't try anything without paying
product.minus: The app demands a subscription and payment details before letting you do anything — not even one free image or the promised trial is accessible.

product.title: Charges during a "free" trial — users cry scam
product.minus: People sign up for a free trial through official links and are immediately charged for a full annual subscription they never authorized.

product.title: Subscription plus buying images: double monetization of one task
product.minus: Even with a yearly subscription you must separately buy AI image packs at $5.99–$7.99, which users call an endless money grab.

product.title: Avatars got worse: the face "isn't me", ages you, looks ugly
product.minus: Magic Avatars once stylized faces beautifully; now they age you 20 years, give a bulbous nose, paste your face on crookedly and barely resemble you.

product.title: Removed pack purchases and beloved styles, forced "Fast Avatar"
product.minus: The option to buy a pack of 200 high-quality images and beloved styles (Cyberpunk, Steampunk, Vampire) is gone, replaced by a forced "Fast Avatar" giving 4 images at much lower quality.

product.title: Watermark on premium results
product.minus: Even on a paid plan the Lensa logo stays on generated images, which users find absurd for something they paid for.

product.title: Forced sign-up and personal-data collection drive people away
product.minus: The app demands email and personal details before any first action, plus nags with account-deletion threats — enough for some users to uninstall on the spot.

product.title: Crashes at login, hangs, features greyed out on newer devices
product.minus: For many the app hangs at startup, crashes on login attempts, or shows greyed-out unavailable icons — especially on newer phones like the S25+ and Note 13 Pro.

product.title: Loss of manual tools: the strength was control, not filters
product.minus: Power users miss precise manual controls (grain, vignette, brushes) — now there are only sliders and one-touch filters with no control over the result.

product.title: Those who stay for the editor praise its simplicity and natural look
product.plus: Despite the negativity, many love Lensa as a simple, intuitive photo editor: natural clean results, an easy interface, good color grading and clean foreground/background separation.

product.title: On good days the AI results are stunning — but it's a gamble
product.plus: When generation works, results delight: a "polished me", accuracy that's "flawless", beautiful realistic photos for avatars and work — users return year after year for this.

product.title: The "lifetime" license is locked to one device and never transfers
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people bought "lifetime" access, switched or broke their phone, and on the new one "restore purchase" says no subscription found — even though the purchase is right there in their Google Play history.

product.title: Support sends auto-replies, then just ghosts you
product.minus: The same script plays out dozens of times: the user sends a receipt and proof of purchase, gets a templated reply or a request for the receipt — and then silence for months.

product.title: Unlimited access swapped for a credit system after you've paid
product.minus: People who bought "unlimited for life" suddenly find a 1000-credit cap and prompts to buy more — the exact thing they paid to avoid.

product.title: Ads with no X — you can't close them, and the image is lost
product.minus: The free version makes you watch an ad per generation, but the X never appears (often the Wonder banner at the top covers it), so you have to kill the app and lose both the attempt and the prompt.

product.title: Generation quality dropped after model updates
product.minus: Long-time users agree: it used to produce unique, almost classical-looking art, now it's blurry mush; the model updates feel like a downgrade.

product.title: Ignores the prompt — outputs nothing like what you asked
product.minus: Basic requests fail: a black background instead of a light one, can't even render simple words in the image, returns something "similar" instead of what was asked.

product.title: Censorship flags harmless words and outfits
product.minus: The NSFW filter trips on completely innocent things — "mage outfit," "battlemage attire," a banana on a cat — and won't say what was wrong, making the app nearly useless.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and pushes weekly billing
product.minus: The free trial quietly rolls into hidden weekly charges (~$4/week); people get billed multiple times in one week and keep getting charged after cancelling.

product.title: Broken anatomy — extra hands, fingers, feet
product.minus: A classic generator failure: missing or extra appendages, two feet on one leg, a third hand — especially in crowd scenes and on hands.

product.title: When it works, the images are impressively detailed
product.plus: Those for whom it still works praise quality and detail above many rivals: people make book covers, storyboards, channel art, and call Wonder their go-to tool.

product.title: Simple text input — easy for beginners to start
product.plus: The core "describe it in words, get an image" loop is intuitive and fun: people note how easy it is to use, while warning that wording has to be precise.

product.title: Removed beloved features — own-image upload and the Pen&Ink style
product.minus: Loyal users drop their ratings over cut features: uploading your own art as a reference, and the original detailed "Pen&Ink" style that was swapped for a worse western one.

product.title: Almost no learning curve: beginners feel skilled on day one
product.plus: The thing people love most is the instant ease: they open it for the first time and immediately make posters, presentations, and thumbnails as if they'd always known how.

product.title: Almost everything useful is locked behind a subscription — free feels like bait
product.minus: To use it properly you have to pay: people complain that almost all features are premium-only and the free mode constantly hits a Pro wall — to the point of deleting the app in anger.

product.title: Downloading the finished work breaks constantly — you get a photo, or nothing
product.minus: The pain is at the final step: people can't export their project — downloads stall, crash on a one-minute clip, and instead of the edited video only a single photo gets saved.

product.title: Money gets charged twice or with no subscription — and refunds are nearly impossible
product.minus: The angriest reviews are about money: people get charged twice in one month, debited when no subscription exists, and refused refunds — pushing them to call their bank.

product.title: Cancelling the free trial is deliberately impossible to find — and then you get charged
product.minus: The free trial feels like a trap: people try to cancel, can't find a way, the AI support doesn't help, there's no live chat or phone — and then a charge arrives.

product.title: Useless offline — it won't even open on bad reception
product.minus: Hard online dependency: at a workplace with poor reception the app literally won't open, and the photo editor refuses to touch a file without an account and constant internet access.

product.title: One tool covers every job: posters, presentations, thumbnails, videos
product.plus: People are won over by the breadth: one app handles poster design, presentations, YouTube thumbnails, and video editing — hence the gushing "best app ever" reviews.

product.title: Indispensable for school and projects — students' go-to tool
product.plus: A distinct loyal audience is students: the app saves them on school projects, assignments, and presentations, and they flat-out call it the best for students.

product.title: A workhorse for business and freelancers — pays for the subscription
product.plus: Pros are happy to pay: freelancers and business owners use it for ads and content, and call the Business subscription worth every penny and a replacement for an expensive PC.

product.title: Work gets lost to bugs and crashes when opening projects
product.minus: Stability fails out of nowhere: people lose lots of work to bugs, the app crashes when trying to open a project, and emojis vanish when posting to TikTok.

product.title: Few ads, no distraction — the free tier doesn't bombard you with banners
product.plus: A pleasant contrast with other free editors: people note there are few if any ads and nothing distracts from the work, amazed at how much is possible for free.

product.title: On mobile the interface is less intuitive and a bit sluggish
product.minus: Not smooth for everyone: some people report a steep learning curve specifically on mobile and general sluggishness while navigating.

product.title: Step-by-step explanation, not just the answer — the main reason people love it
product.plus: Fans don't value the answer itself but the step-by-step breakdown: it shows HOW the result was reached, so the user actually starts understanding the topic instead of just copying.

product.title: Explanations moved behind a paywall — and that killed the core feature
product.minus: The step-by-step breakdown used to be free, and that was the whole point of the app. Now they charge for explanations, and the free version only shows the answer or a graph — users see it as a betrayal.

product.title: Can't handle hard problems — only basic algebra
product.minus: At higher-class, JEE, A-level, engineering and complex levels (geometry, calculus) the app gives up: it either refuses or only solves easy stuff. Stronger students quickly hit the ceiling.

product.title: Gives wrong answers — can't be trusted
product.minus: A frequent complaint: the app returns wrong answers, sometimes even on simple problems. Some got it wrong three times in a row, some on basic addition and multiplication. Trust is broken.

product.title: The tiny scan box doesn't fit the whole problem
product.minus: The camera capture area is too small: you can't select a full page or a long problem, and zooming out throws an error. There's no proper cropping after the photo.

product.title: Fails to recognize the problem and redirects to Google AI / Gemini
product.minus: After Google's acquisition the app often refuses to recognize the problem and pushes the user to Google Lens or Gemini. People reasonably ask: why keep Photomath if you can just use free Google directly?

product.title: Solves a completely different problem than the one in the photo
product.minus: Even with a perfect photo the app often swaps in a similar but wrong problem and solves that one. The user gets the answer to someone else's question — useless and confusing.

product.title: The free version is enough for most — it helps even without paid explanations
product.plus: Despite the paid add-on, some users find the free version fully sufficient: accurate answers, an advanced calculator, and the basic breakdown is enough for everyday homework.

product.title: A lifesaver for homework and exams — simple and fast
product.plus: For its core audience — students — the app stays a fast, easy helper: it solves in seconds, is simple to use, and genuinely saves them on tests and homework.

product.title: Requires internet even for the simplest problems
product.minus: The app used to work offline, but after an update it demands a connection even for "8-2". Worse, it often falsely complains about no network when the internet is stable. Users beg for the offline mode back.

product.title: Can't do word problems and lacks a default manual-entry mode
product.minus: The app doesn't handle word problems at all, and you often can't type a problem manually — only photo input. Users ask for both word-problem support and the option to open the calculator/manual entry directly, without the camera.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and pushes an expensive subscription
product.minus: Some users report being charged even after cancelling, with no refund, plus the high price of Plus and the lack of a one-time or lifetime payment option.

product.title: Duolingo-style gamification makes learning to code feel approachable
product.plus: Short interactive lessons, streaks, coins and XP turn coding into a game — beginners constantly compare Mimo to Duolingo and praise how unintimidating it feels to start.

product.title: Free users get only 2 keys a day, then a 24-hour wait
product.minus: The single most common pain: without a subscription you get just two lessons per day, and users complain that progress slows to a crawl — what once took a day now takes weeks.

product.title: Swapping 'lives/hearts' for 'keys' is seen as a downgrade
product.minus: Long-time users specifically resent that the old hearts/lives system (5 mistakes) let them learn freely, while the new keys hard-cap lessons — many beg for hearts to come back.

product.title: Aggressive, sometimes dishonest upsell before the first lesson
product.minus: The subscription is pushed before you even start, the price jumps around (59.99 → 39.99 → back to 59.99), and fake 'only 2 days left' timers pressure you — users call it shady marketing and a cash grab.

product.title: Pro→Max double paywall: you pay once, then get pushed to pay again
product.minus: A sharp sub-case: paying for Pro doesn't unlock what was promised — unlimited learning and projects moved to Max, effectively stripping existing Pro subscribers of what they paid for.

product.title: Can't pick your language — you want Python/PHP but get HTML
product.minus: Users come for a specific language but the app forces HTML and hides the one they want behind payment; they complain the older version let them choose what to learn.

product.title: The best projects are desktop-only, blocking mobile-only users
product.minus: Core projects require a PC and browser, but many learn on a phone only and can't finish the course; on top of that, browser progress doesn't sync with the app.

product.title: Bite-sized explanations genuinely get beginners to results
product.plus: The core praise on substance: Mimo breaks complex concepts into small manageable steps with practice right after theory — people say they finally understood Python from their phone.

product.title: Certificates earned on the free trial are withheld without payment
product.minus: A narrow but stinging case: a user legitimately earned a certificate on the free trial, but it's withheld until you pay for a subscription — which reads as bad faith.

product.title: Login bugs, playground crashes and false 'connection' errors
product.minus: Technical breakage: the app freezes at startup, won't let you scroll on, throws 'check your Internet connection' when the network is fine, and crashes the playground on large files.

product.title: Cancellation is hidden — email-only, with no warning before the charge
product.minus: You can't cancel inside the app and have to email them; the trial ends with no warning and charges you immediately — a classic subscription trap.

product.title: No native UI language — Indian users struggle without Hindi
product.minus: All content is English-only, and Indian users repeatedly ask for Hindi — without their native language the material is hard for them to follow.

product.title: Real hands-on practice over theory — you learn by typing code
product.plus: Users value that Mimo doesn't bury them in textbook theory but has them writing code and reinforcing with exercises right away; typing code by hand aids memory, and many appreciate revisiting old lessons.

product.title: A recent update removed the symbols bar and reviewing your own code
product.minus: A recent update stripped the symbols bar from the playground (forcing you to type from the keyboard) and the ability to review your own code after submitting; some users refuse to update because of it.

product.title: Paywalled playground: you can't run or try code without Pro
product.minus: The core learning feature — writing and running code — is locked: instead of a Run button you get a Pro ad, and the lesson collapses into multiple-choice questions.

product.title: Hidden subscription: card charged after the "free" trial without consent
product.minus: Users say they never knew they subscribed, can't find or cancel it, and get charged again and again — sometimes for months — even though Google Play shows no subscription.

product.title: Lives system: 5 hearts and a 4-hour wait instead of learning
product.minus: A beginner is bound to make mistakes, but after 5 errors you wait hours or pay — breaking the very continuity of learning the app is meant for.

product.title: Pay to learn why you're wrong: AI explanations aren't even in Pro
product.minus: To find out why an answer was wrong they demand more money for an "AI" feature on top of Pro — intrusive and useless, since that's basic to learning.

product.title: "Vibe coding" and AI slop instead of real coding lessons
product.minus: Long-time users say the app slid into AI courses and "how to vibe code a game" — that isn't coding, and the old useful format is gone.

product.title: Quizzes without teaching: tested like an expert after 30% explained
product.minus: Complaints that instead of teaching, it throws multiple-choice questions at you, making you guess or parrot what's shown, with no real instruction.

product.title: False advertising: promised "free", really a 2-week trial
product.minus: The ads and the free promise clash with reality: you pay for almost everything, and the store screenshots show languages that aren't actually in the courses.

product.title: Aggressive Pro ads: pop-ups and unclosable banners
product.minus: Constant pop-ups on launch and ads after nearly every lesson grate, and some can't be closed — forcing you to restart the app.

product.title: Login and session bugs: lost progress, can't sign in
product.minus: Technical breakage: can't log into old accounts, images and progress vanish, and the app forces a sign-out after every use or closes by itself.

product.title: Lands like Duolingo for code: gamification removes the fear of programming
product.plus: Short, interactive lessons in a game-like format make coding feel approachable and fun — for many, that's exactly what pulled them into learning.

product.title: Best starting point for beginners: clear explanations and learning from scratch
product.plus: For those who've never coded, the app gives a clear, paced path from zero — especially for Python, HTML and the basics — and many praise how clear the explanations are.

product.title: Reinforcement and drilling: one skill practiced across many tasks
product.plus: Content isn't crammed into one or two tasks: a single topic is drilled across many exercises and constantly reinforced, helping the skill stick.

product.title: Freezes on loading after a few problems — only a reinstall brings it back
product.minus: By far the most common complaint: after a handful of problems (often 3-4, or about 10 minutes in) the app stops solving anything and hangs on an endless loading screen. Clearing the cache doesn't help — the only fix is to uninstall and reinstall, sometimes several times a day.

product.title: Breaks the moment you pay — it worked fine while it was free
product.minus: The same story repeats over and over: someone pays for a subscription to see the steps, and right after paying the app stops working — freezing, unable to even do 2x2. That timing leads many to call it an outright scam.

product.title: A green "Do Not Sell My Info" badge sits on top of the answer and won't move
product.minus: A cookie-consent / "do not sell my data" widget landed exactly where the answer appears. It can't be moved or dismissed even after you accept cookies — it covers the solution entirely and makes the app useless.

product.title: One problem takes minutes to load — slower than solving it by hand
product.minus: Even when it doesn't freeze outright, the app has become painfully slow: a minute to open, another minute to calculate. Users say they can solve the quadratic formula faster than it loads.

product.title: Constantly signs you out — you have to log back in every time
product.minus: A separate recurring pain: the app logs you out every time you close it or every ten minutes. Signing in with a Google account often fails too — the sign-in page just loops back on itself.

product.title: Step-by-step work is paywalled — without it, it's just a calculator
product.minus: The free version only gives the answer; seeing how it was reached costs money. Many users learn from the worked steps and resent that the core value sits behind a subscription — especially students who can't afford it.

product.title: Refunds refused and subscription billing in chaos
product.minus: When the app fails, getting a refund is nearly impossible: both Google Play and Mathway refuse. On top of that, users report double-billing (charged monthly and annually at once), being unable to cancel, and redirects to pay inside a separate Chegg app.

product.title: Camera scan of handwriting — when it works, it nails it
product.plus: A genuine strength: you can photograph a problem and it accurately reads even handwriting and solves fast. Parents snap their kids' homework and trust the answer more than any other method.

product.title: A years-long study lifeline and the go-to replacement for the killed Microsoft Math Solver
product.plus: A loyal base: people have used it since high school and college, getting through statistics and calculus, helping their kids with algebra. Many switched after Microsoft shut down its free Math Solver and consider Mathway a worthy replacement.

product.title: Multiple solution methods and clear steps — it teaches, not just answers
product.plus: For those whose subscription actually works, the praise is about depth: the app offers several ways to solve the same problem and breaks them into clear steps, genuinely helping people understand new concepts rather than just copy an answer.

product.title: Data breach and privacy fears
product.minus: Some users flag the January 2020 breach that exposed over 25M records — names, emails, social IDs and password hashes. People say their data leaked to the dark web twice and warn newcomers to think twice before signing up.

product.title: Gives up on harder topics: says "unable to solve" even on premium
product.minus: Beyond basic algebra it often can't cope: complaints about geometry, integral calculus and Venn diagrams where it returns "unable to solve" — sometimes even on simple arithmetic, and even for paying users.

product.title: Step-by-step explanations went behind a paywall, gutting the core value
product.minus: Free step-by-step working used to be the whole point; now detailed explanations require Plus and the free tier feels unusable to many. Users read it as a bait-and-switch, not fair monetization.

product.title: Fails to recognize the problem from a photo — even a perfectly clear one
product.minus: The most common technical complaint: a user takes a crisp photo and the app can't find the problem, solves a completely different one, or returns 'we couldn't find the answer'. Often it surfaces similar problems instead of the actual one.

product.title: Punts you to Google's recognition — so why keep the app?
product.minus: Since the Google acquisition the app increasingly redirects users to Google Lens / Gemini instead of solving anything itself. People ask outright why they'd pay for Photomath when they could just use Google for free.

product.title: Chokes on advanced math — gives up past the basics
product.minus: High-schoolers and university students say it handles only basic algebra; geometry, trig, calculus, and JEE/A-level problems either fail outright or get bounced to Google.

product.title: Frequently returns wrong answers — even on simple problems
product.minus: Many report answers are wrong roughly half the time, sometimes even on addition and multiplication. You can't trust it without double-checking — a fatal flaw for a homework helper.

product.title: Cramped capture box — the whole problem won't fit
product.minus: The scan window is tiny — you can't capture a full page or crop after shooting. Zoom out to fit everything and it throws an error.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and pushy subscription
product.minus: A distinct billing grievance: money keeps coming out after cancellation and support says nothing can be done. Requests for a one-time payment or lifetime license go unanswered.

product.title: Needs internet even for '8−2' — offline mode is gone
product.minus: Recent versions demand a connection even for trivial problems that used to work offline. It often flashes 'no internet connection' on a perfectly stable network.

product.title: When it works, the step-by-step breakdown genuinely teaches
product.plus: The thing users love most: it doesn't just hand over the answer, it explains each step clearly so you understand the solution instead of memorizing it. Many credit it with raising their grades and easing their fear of math.

product.title: A fast, simple homework lifesaver
product.plus: For those it works for, it's a go-to lifesaver: solves in seconds, handy for double-checking your own work, and dead simple to use. Many have relied on it for years, since middle school and beyond.

product.title: The built-in calculator outshines the camera
product.plus: Some users skip the camera entirely and type problems into the advanced built-in calculator, which is powerful on its own. A few even ask to make the calculator the default home screen instead of the camera.

product.title: Chatbot rivals undercut its reason to exist
product.minus: Users increasingly compare it to Gemini and ChatGPT and find their explanations better, more flexible, and free. Against that backdrop the paywall looks especially weak.

product.title: Explains rather than just answers — clears up confusion on the topic
product.plus: Users value that the app expands the solution step by step and explains each part, so they finally understand a topic they couldn't grasp in class.

product.title: Paid "energy" drains on every question — you can only learn in small bursts
product.minus: Every question burns limited "energy"/"stars"/"lightning", and after a few questions a subscription is required — users find it absurd to cap learning itself.

product.title: Fast, accurate answers — solves a problem in seconds
product.plus: Many like that the app returns a correct, clear answer almost instantly, noticeably speeding up homework and study prep.

product.title: Raises grades — users credit the app for their improvement
product.plus: Students directly attribute better grades and subject mastery to the app, especially in math.

product.title: Rated above ChatGPT — for its study focus and unlimited photo input
product.plus: Users contrast it with ChatGPT: more accurate for studying, better at explaining, and lets you upload gallery images without a cap.

product.title: Scan-only input forces you to photograph a question — you can't just type it
product.minus: Some users just want to type a question, but the app pushes scanning, which is awkward for non-math and written-out queries.

product.title: Misfires on non-math questions — coughs up an unrelated equation
product.minus: When scanning a non-math question, the app sometimes returns a totally unrelated equation, and even simple follow-ups go unanswered.

product.title: Demands personal details and permissions before letting you try
product.minus: Before use, the app requires personal details and extra permissions, which puts off people who just wanted to test the product.

product.title: Too pricey for students and ignored refund requests — the painful side of billing
product.minus: The price stings precisely for students, and in one case a user says the developer ignored repeated refund requests for an accidental subscription purchase.

product.title: Users ask for a lifetime license and chat history instead of consumable credits
product.minus: Willing-to-pay users ask for a one-time lifetime license instead of consumable credits, and complain there's no chat history, so good answers get lost.

product.title: Explanations lack diagrams and illustrations
product.minus: Users praise the text explanations but ask for diagrams and illustrations, and sometimes answers run long instead of giving the main points.

product.title: Versatile across subjects and languages — from math to biology in many languages
product.plus: Users note the app handles many subjects and understands different languages, making it convenient for a wide range of learners.

product.title: Teachers' favorite: turns the lesson into a competitive game
product.plus: Teachers and tutors rave that it makes the class interactive, helps students lose their fear of testing, sparks healthy competition, and gives instant feedback on results.

product.title: Created quizzes vanish right after you save them
product.minus: The most painful complaint: people spend an hour building a quiz, hit save, and it disappears; the Create button and Created section vanish after closing the app, and even re-logging in doesn't bring them back.

product.title: Login kicks you out mid-test — and the grade is lost
product.minus: To join a quiz the app keeps forcing a fresh login, loops on "couldn't log you in" and crashes; because of this students miss the test and lose their score, sometimes having to reinstall before every quiz.

product.title: Lags and freezes mid-game, breaking the run
product.minus: The app slows down, especially after a long session or 25+ questions: it freezes mid-game, breaks the UI, sometimes picks answers on its own — and the user loses the grade they deserved.

product.title: Learning through play, memes and avatar customization
