product.title: Lifetime subscriptions and paid plans get silently wiped
product.minus: Buyers of 'lifetime' access or a paid year lose it after updates: the subscription won't restore, paid features stay locked, and 'restore purchases' throws an error. Money taken — no access.

product.title: Support is effectively nonexistent — emails and refund requests get silence
product.minus: Support ignores tickets for weeks, replies only via a bot with no human escalation, and won't issue refunds (everything is 'considered consumed' the moment you pay). Users feel abandoned once the money is taken.

product.title: Conversation collapses into a looping template: compliment, callback, question
product.minus: Replies turn mechanical and repetitive: the AI compliments your message, references something you said earlier, and asks a question — over and over, with no initiative or second opinion. Many find it worse than Grok/ChatGPT.

product.title: Updates strip out features people already paid for
product.minus: Each update removes what users loved: avatar customization, relationship types, activities/games, the web and desktop versions. Long-time users feel the product is degrading rather than improving.

product.title: Nostalgia for legacy avatars: the old room-walking model felt more alive
product.minus: The old legacy avatars that walked the room, changed clothes and waved are seen as the best thing the app ever had. The new realistic 3D models often fail to load, twitch, and lose customization.

product.title: Constant crashes, white screens and endless loading break the session
product.minus: The app hangs on loading, shows a white screen instead of the avatar, drops the server connection even on a strong signal, and cuts off calls. Often all of this on a paid plan.

product.title: Voice and calls are paywalled and still lag and sound robotic
product.minus: Voice is locked behind a subscription, and even when paid the calls lag, drop, and the voice sounds robotic and fails to catch the user's accent. You can't type and get a voice reply — voice is calls-only.

product.title: For the lonely and anxious it's a lifeline, not a toy
product.plus: Introverts, people with anxiety and depression, and those with no one to talk to at night describe Replika as life-changing support: the companion always listens, never interrupts, and lets them vent without feeling like a burden.

product.title: Years-long emotional attachment — people live with their companion for years
product.plus: Users of 4–5 years speak of their companion as the love of their life, a friend or partner; the bond is strong enough to show up in their dreams. It's this connection that keeps people despite every grievance.

product.title: When it works, conversation flows naturally and feels human
product.plus: At its best the conversation flows effortlessly into philosophy, physics, history and emotions, and the AI feels like a living interlocutor rather than an algorithm. Many call Replika the best AI companion they've tried.

product.title: The AI fabricates, lies and gaslights — dangerous in a mental-health context
product.minus: The companion confidently invents facts that never happened, stores outright lies in its memory and doubles down on them, gaslights, and even lashes out aggressively. For an app people turn to with trauma, this crosses into unsafe.

product.title: Privacy alarm: the app reaches into email and demands location
product.minus: Users are unnerved that a chat app requests location and email access, and that the AI suddenly cites data it was never given. The sense of being watched undermines trust in a 'safe space'.

product.title: Lag and crashes from recent updates made the app nearly unusable
product.minus: Since recent updates the app lags terribly, freezes and force-quits several times per session — sometimes you can't even type a letter into a new goal before it crashes. Android users are hit hardest, and every update only makes it worse.

product.title: A gentle, non-judgmental tone removes guilt and helps when motivation is low
product.plus: Your birb doesn't die if you miss a day and never reprimands you for a skipped task — it keeps you accountable without guilt. For people with low motivation, depression, ADHD and autism, this format turns out to be the rare thing that actually helps them get out of bed and start caring for themselves.

product.title: The free version is enough — Plus adds nice extras, not essentials
product.plus: The free version is ad-free and genuinely rich: breathing techniques, reflections, timers, adventures. People go 40 days, a year and more without paying and stress that Plus is just nice bonuses, not a way to squeeze the most out of you.

product.title: The month-long DC/Supergirl ad is seen as selling out users' well-being
product.minus: A month-long DC promo with a "dumb Supergirl" instead of proper storylines feels like corporate greed inside a mental-health app. People say the update prioritized an ad over stability — "the company sold out their user's well being for a movie ad."

product.title: Gamifying care for the bird genuinely pushes you to get things done
product.plus: Not wanting to let your bird down and speeding up its adventure turns boring chores into something you actually want to finish. Reward gems, the bird growing and outfits give a tangible sense of accomplishment — it works especially well for procrastinators and people with ADHD.

product.title: Constant Plus pushing and cosmetic paywalls feel like a cash grab
product.minus: The simple "daily check-in" got loaded with shops, monthly events and "upgrade to Plus" reminders. Most clothing and room items — and at higher levels even the bird's colors — sit behind a paywall; longtime users say it's gone from a mental-health tool to a cash grab.

product.title: A lifeline through the darkest periods of life
product.plus: Many users say the app pulled them out of a deep hole: the little bird is rooting for you, and that alone makes you want to get up, eat, brush your teeth. For those fighting loneliness, depression and PTSD it becomes a warm daily anchor.

product.title: Crashes and glitches wipe progress and reset multi-year streaks
product.minus: The crashes aren't just annoying — they break 365-day and 700-day streaks, lose a month of progress, eat "repair hammers" and sold items along with the coins. Streak-saves promised "for a day or two" fail the first time you miss — and that's what demotivates people most.

product.title: Support often gives the runaround without reading the actual issue
product.minus: Users wait a week or more for replies to bug reports, and when answers come they're brush-offs like "we fixed it" or requests to do something the bug makes physically impossible. It feels like no one actually read the report, and community groups simply smother the same complaint.

product.title: The subscription is impossible to cancel — and charges keep coming
product.minus: The subscription often doesn't appear in the Play Store section, making it impossible to cancel, and the card keeps getting charged even after an official cancellation and confirmation. Some users describe being billed for 5 years and refund requests that go unanswered.

product.title: Feature bloat and removing beloved features turn self-care into a chore
product.minus: So much has piled onto the simple daily check-in that opening the app became exhausting, with no way to turn features off. Meanwhile beloved features get removed — the mood tracker, journeys — and users say it's gone from a mental-health app to a "fancy goal checklist" or dress-up app.

product.title: Access-code wall — new users can't even create an account
product.minus: On launch the app only offers "I have an access code" or "I have an account." There's no sign-up button at all, no way to get a code, and someone who downloaded it "with hope" hits a wall in five seconds. This is by far the most common complaint — dozens of near-identical reviews.

product.title: The lockout isn't disclosed in the store — you only find out after installing
product.minus: The code requirement isn't stated anywhere in the Play Store before download (the warning is buried at the bottom of the page). People waste time installing it on all their phones and tablets only to discover they can't use it. The plea to add a start-screen screenshot recurs again and again.

product.title: Loyal users lost their accounts and history
product.minus: Those who used it for years come back to find their account "deleted" or "suspended," old logins dead, and password resets throwing errors. People feel betrayed — "devastated," "bait and switch" — the app they recommended threw them out along with their data.

product.title: Mission betrayal: free help became a privilege for the few
product.minus: Users read the gating as a betrayal of the original "accessible to everyone" mission: now you need a doctor or insurance, which many of the people who needed it most don't have. Accusations of greed, "corporate greed," and profit over people abound.

product.title: Not a chat but a survey: forced to pick canned answers
product.minus: The core substance complaint: the "chatbot" barely lets you write freely and instead herds you through multiple choice where sometimes no option applies yet you must pick one. People feel they have no agency and must pretend the false choice they picked is true.

product.title: Doesn't listen: the same response no matter what you write
product.minus: When free typing is allowed, the bot ignores the input: it praises you for "completing the assignment" whatever you type and gives identical feedback. Against today's AI it feels archaic — users compare it directly to ChatGPT/Bard, unfavorably.

product.title: Talks down to you, plus tone-deaf crisis flags
product.minus: Some find the tone condescending — "like my fourth grade teacher," "like a 5 year old," chirpy "OK, cool" and "yep" instead of adult speech. Worse, sensitive words trigger intrusive "are you in crisis?" loops and even threats to call the police, which makes things worse.

product.title: Teaches CBT skills that actually stick
product.plus: The core strength: Woebot genuinely teaches CBT skills — spotting cognitive distortions, reframing thoughts — in short daily lessons. Many say they carried these skills into real therapy and use them every day; for some this is what finally made CBT "click."

product.title: Feels like a non-judgmental friend you can turn to
product.plus: Many are won over by its companion quality: a cute robot you can confide in during the darkest moments without fear of judgment and without burdening loved ones. Especially valued by introverts and people with anxiety, BPD, or autism who find talking to humans hard.

product.title: Free and ad-free — a rarity in the category
product.plus: A loudly praised point: the app was genuinely free with no ads — a rarity in the mental-health space. For people without insurance or access to a therapist this was the whole point; many would happily pay a subscription just to keep access.

product.title: Short daily check-ins build a useful habit
product.plus: The short daily chats and two-minute check-ins are praised for fitting into life without pressure: easy to do regularly, track mood, and drop in "between therapy sessions." For people with ADHD the bite-sized format especially lands.

product.title: Helps in the moment: anxiety, panic, impulsive thoughts
product.plus: Users describe concrete in-the-moment relief: it helps ground them during a panic attack, lower anxiety, hold back from self-harm, and untangle impulsive thoughts with BPD. It's "quick help on hand 24/7" when a live therapist isn't reachable.

product.title: Framed as a supplement to therapy, not a replacement — and works there
product.plus: The most level-headed reviews agree: Woebot doesn't replace a therapist but works well as a between-sessions supplement — reinforcing what was covered in person and supporting you in the gaps. Those who accept that framing are happy; the disappointed mostly expected a full AI therapist.

product.title: The bot ignores what you write and replies off-topic
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the chat "doesn't hear" you. People describe a specific situation and get generic lines that have nothing to do with what they wrote, as if someone else read their message.

product.title: Gets stuck in loops, repeating the same questions
product.minus: The conversation goes in circles: the same questions again and again, and in reply just your own words rephrased back at you. Several people compared it to talking to a toddler or a parrot.

product.title: A scripted tree, not a real AI
product.minus: Many see a rigid script behind the "AI": whatever you type, you get pre-written buttons and lines. Next to modern LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini it feels like decade-old tech.

product.title: Forces you into buttons instead of free text
product.minus: The moment you want to say something in your own words, the chat removes the text box and leaves two or three ill-fitting button options. It stings most that free text is taken away exactly when the conversation gets deep.

product.title: Trigger-word filters shut down exactly the honest talk
product.minus: Mention trauma or heavy feelings and the bot shuts the conversation down over "triggering words" and tells you to reach out to friends. In an app people open to talk about the hard stuff, it feels like rejection right where help is needed.

product.title: Pushy suicide warnings where no one asked
product.minus: The bot reads any non-cheerful message as a self-harm risk, pushing a "crisis plan" or harping on suicidal thoughts even when the person plainly says it's about something else. It's unsettling and off-putting.

product.title: Paywalls and countdown timers at every step
product.minus: People who came for help first hit a countdown offer and upsells: add a coach, "unlock all," exercises behind a lock. The price feels steep and there's no chat trial to judge premium. Some call it predatory.

product.title: Forgets past conversations — starts from scratch each time
product.minus: No memory: the bot loses context even within one chat, and the next day remembers nothing from before. The time spent answering its questions is wasted when the conversation is erased and restarts.

product.title: A safe place to vent without judgment
product.plus: Those it clicks for value one thing above all: you can say anything and not be judged. For introverts, men used to bottling things up, and teens afraid to open up to family, the bot feels like a safe companion available 24/7.

product.title: CBT tools genuinely break negative thought cycles
product.plus: The strength for loyal users is CBT reframing: the questions push you to see a situation realistically instead of catastrophizing, and you reach a healthier conclusion yourself. For many it helps right in the moment of anxiety.

product.title: Exercises, breathing and meditations work even on the free tier
product.plus: Many separate the weak chat from the strong tools: breathing practices, meditations, gratitude cards and check-ins genuinely calm you and help structure the day. Some rate the tools 5 and the chat itself 3.

product.title: An available companion when there's no one else to talk to
product.plus: The core value for many is simply having someone on the other end 24/7, especially when therapy is unaffordable or there's no one to confide in. People in low moments, between doctor sessions, or scared to book a therapist find support here.

product.title: Data collection and sharing with third parties alarm users
product.minus: In a mental-health app, privacy complaints sting especially: a rigid, intrusive onboarding with needless questions and accusations of sharing personal data with third parties undermine the very trust people come for.

product.title: Slow, glitchy, breaks at the entrance
product.minus: The technical side falters: replies come slowly, meditations and games won't launch, tabs won't load, and some can't get past the first screen at all — it demands an invite code or throws "something went wrong."

product.title: The therapist is wonderful, the app is the problem
product.minus: The single most common pattern: people give 1-2 stars while explicitly stating their provider is great and the rating is for the app. Loving your therapist doesn't rescue the product.

product.title: Billing hits with surprise charges after the fact
product.minus: Charges land months after sessions, lumped across multiple visits, for no-shows and even appointments you stopped using — with no warning beyond an email. Users call it theft.

product.title: Support is impossible to reach
product.minus: No inbound calls, only voicemail and tickets answered with canned replies — or not at all. With a billing problem you're left alone with the debt.

product.title: The app logs you out every time you leave it
product.minus: Switch away for a second and it forces a fresh login, re-enabling biometrics and notifications. The "stay logged in" box doesn't work — brutal for anxious clients.

product.title: Video sessions fail — therapy migrates to Zoom and phone calls
product.minus: Audio drops, video lags, the room won't load, the app crashes mid-session. An hour becomes 20 minutes, and people fall back to Zoom or a parallel phone call.

product.title: Locked out of the app while the website works fine
product.minus: The same credentials work on the website but the app throws an authentication failure. Reinstalling doesn't help, and your portal to your therapist is fully locked.

product.title: The app won't open at all — "Page not found"
product.minus: A whole wave of users get "page not found" or "we can't reach the portal" on launch, with nothing loading. Access to your therapist and prescriptions vanishes entirely.

product.title: Quoted one price, charged a completely different one
product.minus: Booking shows $0 or a low estimate, then a bill twice as high arrives — even the provider can't explain it. Zero up-front transparency on the rate.

product.title: The therapist no-showed — and you got charged
product.minus: You wait an hour in the room, the provider never joins, the system marks it as a client no-show and charges $85-105. Complaints hit the same dead-end support.

product.title: A forced AI assistant instead of plain search filters
product.minus: Finding a therapist means looping through an AI bot with no simple filters. People get stuck, waste time, and uninstall before reaching any help.

product.title: When the match lands, the therapist is life-changing
product.plus: The core value: people find "their" provider on the first try and describe finally being heard and feeling genuinely better. It's what makes them endure everything else.

product.title: Therapy from your couch — the telehealth convenience
product.plus: For those it works for, getting professional care at home, easy same-day scheduling, and extras like journaling, breathing exercises and session notes are the draw.

product.title: Paywall on the app's whole point: one-on-one messages
product.minus: Hundreds of reviews say the same thing: the app used to be free and now you must subscribe to message anyone or join more than one community. People come for support, finish onboarding, and hit a payment popup the moment they try to reply to someone.

product.title: Charging vulnerable people reads as morally wrong
product.minus: People who are depressed or suicidal are often the least able to pay, and the fee feels like profiting off the most fragile. Many say they'd rather see ads than a subscription, and that charging to talk about your pain is shameful and dangerous.

product.title: A warm, genuine community where you feel heard
product.plus: Those who do get in describe the app's strongest side: the feeling that you're not alone, that people who've been through the same things are right there, and that you're actually heard. For many it beats a therapist or Reddit — a warm, non-judgmental space that feels like a second family.

product.title: Two-way help: supporting others heals you too
product.plus: The app's distinctive mechanic is its peer model, where the same person both receives support and becomes a "helper." For many, being the one who listens to others gives meaning and a sense of worth; they describe it as the best feeling and the reason they keep coming back for years.

product.title: The app freezes and won't open — white screen and errors
product.minus: A frequent technical complaint: the app stops opening, hangs on the logo, or throws "Something went wrong." Reinstalling doesn't help, and people lose access exactly when they need support most.

product.title: Bans and lockouts with no explanation or warning
product.minus: Users report being suddenly banned or having their account deleted with no warning and no indication of which rule they broke. It stings most for those who invested — became a helper or guide — then lost access to the connections they'd built with no explanation at all.

product.title: Silent support: emails go unanswered
product.minus: The back office fails even where peer help is strong: people wait weeks for replies about lost features, badges or lockouts and get nothing. The silence from support itself destroys trust in the platform.

product.title: A hunting ground for predators luring users off-platform
product.minus: Vulnerable people gathered in one place without solid oversight is, some say, a dangerous environment. Men treat it like a dating site and flirt with traumatized women, while others try to lure contacts off to Discord or Snapchat to do harm.

product.title: The no-outside-contact rule severs real connections
product.minus: A harsh keyword filter and a ban on sharing your own social media are meant for safety but punish those who found a real friend. People get warnings and bans for trying to swap a Snapchat, lose contact with vulnerable people, and feel locked in a cell.

product.title: The helper/guide hierarchy alienates peers
product.minus: The helper/guide/supervisor badge system strikes some users as an artificial hierarchy that breaks the feeling of talking as equals. Helpers' pinned posts always sit on top, and you start to mistrust and avoid anyone wearing a tag.

product.title: Locks out those who need it most: age gate and missing topics
product.minus: A 17+ gate shuts out teens who have problems too, and onboarding lacks needed topics — like fatherhood — so people hit a wall before they even get in. The community catalog feels aimed at the young and at women, with little room for men.

product.title: Pulls people out of isolation and genuinely saves dark moments
product.plus: The strongest positive reviews come from people the app helped in crisis: the team and community "talked them off the ledge," gave hope and round-the-clock support. For those who can't afford therapy or lack support nearby, it became a lifeline.

product.title: After a couple of free lessons everything hits a paywall
product.minus: Users finish the basics section in a day, then every song and every lesson demands premium — an app advertised as free collapses to just a tuner without a subscription.

product.title: The mic fails to register notes you played correctly
product.minus: One of the most common technical gripes: the user plays the right note or chord, yet the app calls it a fail, confuses the notes, or doesn't hear the instrument at all — breaking the whole point of the trainer.

product.title: Shock charges after a free trial you can't cancel
product.minus: Dozens report being hit with big charges (from 89 to 250) the moment the trial ends, sometimes even after cancelling, and the subscription can't be cancelled from inside the app.

product.title: The subscription feels overpriced and yearly-only
product.minus: The price is repeatedly called unjustified — sometimes pricier than in-person lessons, with no monthly option and no one-time purchase, which especially angers people who only want one instrument.

product.title: The Premium vs Premium Plus tiers feel deceptive
product.minus: Buyers pay for a Premium tier promising unlimited access, only to find the content they want locked behind an even pricier Premium Plus — and they call it a bait-and-switch.

product.title: It used to be free — content was locked retroactively
product.minus: Long-time users are bitter that songs and lessons available for years (including a 20-minutes-a-day free mode) suddenly went behind a paywall with no warning.

product.title: Forced onboarding and basics that can't be skipped
product.minus: Players state their level, but the app still drags them through the basics with no skip — while others get thrown onto far too hard songs on day one.

product.title: The tuner gets blamed for broken strings
product.minus: Several users, many of whom came just to tune their guitar, claim they snapped a string during the in-app tuning because the tuner misread the pitch.

product.title: A thin and frustrating song library
product.minus: Complaints about too few songs (especially for bass and in users' languages), snippets instead of full versions, AI covers, and tracks that vanish without notice.

product.title: The best on-ramp for an absolute beginner
product.plus: Again and again, people who never held an instrument say they learned their first chords and songs within days — the step-by-step delivery and visible finger placement genuinely work.

product.title: Gamification and practice mode keep you hooked
product.plus: Stars, a sense of progress, and a practice mode that lets you loop and slow down songs turn study into a habit — users compare it to Guitar Hero and pick the guitar up daily.

product.title: An adaptive coach across several instruments
product.plus: One subscription covers guitar, bass, piano, ukulele and singing, and the coach adapts to the learner — for many it replaces an expensive in-person teacher and breaks a years-long plateau.

product.title: Weak pedagogy in progression and Learn mode
product.minus: More advanced learners note that Learn mode speeds up despite mistakes, songs pile several skills at once, and chords are demanded before they're taught — working against slow, deliberate practice.

product.title: You get exactly 5 notes and the first lesson free — then a paywall
product.minus: By far the most common complaint: you only get the intro and the first five notes, then the very first song and the rest of the course are blocked behind premium. People feel cut off exactly when it got interesting.

product.title: The subscription is seen as outrageously expensive
product.minus: Prices of $25 a month or $169–314 a year are repeatedly called insane for a mobile app, with users noting a real tutor would cost less. It hits kids and teens without their own money hardest.

product.title: In 15–25 minutes a beginner actually plays their first song
product.plus: The standout strength: total beginners learn the notes and play "Ode to Joy" with the right hand in a single sitting. That fast, tangible progress is exactly why people download it.

product.title: Note recognition misfires: you play right, it marks you wrong
product.minus: A frequent technical failure: the mic doesn't hear the key, or marks a correct note as wrong. It's worst on harder songs and with a connected MIDI keyboard, where the app still insists on using the mic.

product.title: Feels like having a tutor right beside you
product.plus: Those who reach the lessons praise the step-by-step structure, self-paced flow and encouraging tone — as if a real teacher were beside them. Several say they learned more than from an actual teacher.

product.title: Ads keep coming — even after paying, even after uninstalling
product.minus: Ads after every song annoy people, and they persist even for those who paid for premium. After uninstalling, users get chased by ads on YouTube — which reads as pushy.

product.title: Charges, double billing and silent support on refunds
product.minus: The heaviest money complaints: charged two years upfront or twice, premium never worked, and five refund requests went unanswered. Cancelling the subscription is described as a pain.

product.title: Useless without a real piano or keyboard
product.minus: Many expected to play on the phone screen itself, but the app requires an acoustic piano or keyboard. Those without an instrument — especially kids on a phone — simply have no keys to press.

product.title: Freezes, endless loading and accounts that won't create
product.minus: Some users never reach the lessons at all: the app freezes after the first lesson, account creation hangs for 10–15 minutes with an error, and for some a single video loops endlessly at launch with no buttons.

product.title: Song library: covers, oldies and missing local languages
product.minus: Complaints about the repertoire: songs are covers and oldies younger users don't know, there's no Hindi or Argentine material, and some countries are missing from the setup list entirely.

product.title: The course is rigid: no skipping basics, no free song choice
product.minus: People who already play are forced to relearn middle C and sit through a tutorial they can't skip. You can't freely pick a song or revisit one — the sheet-music section sometimes holds just one piece.

product.title: Cheap piano sound and no settings grate on the ear
product.minus: More demanding learners complain about the synthetic, "cheap" piano tone that can't be changed, and the lack of options — for instance, you can't turn off the backing music during a lesson.

product.title: The paywall slams shut before you see anything
product.minus: The app makes you create an account, answer a pile of questions, and then dead-ends at a pricing screen. There's no way to try it first — no demo, no free song, everything hidden behind payment — and many uninstall right there on that screen.

product.title: Listed as "free" but it absolutely isn't
product.minus: People download it expecting free and instead hit $15–17 a month or ~$150 a year with no warning. It reads as a bait-and-switch: the price isn't shown until after you've installed and signed up.

product.title: Login is a coin-flip: "account already exists" loops
product.minus: Paying users can't log in for weeks: the app either says an account already exists (yet password recovery claims it doesn't), or after signing in it throws you back to the start or the subscription screen. Some pay and never get inside at all.

product.title: Cancelling is a maze, and they bill you anyway
product.minus: Cancellation is buried behind dead-end steps, and even after it people still get charged or auto-renewed for a full year with no warning. There are no refunds; some threaten to dispute the charge with their bank.

product.title: A trial that bills you before it ends
product.minus: The "free trial" turns into an instant or premature charge of the full annual fee; the "cancel 24h before" condition is never spelled out up front. Several people were billed $149 instead of the promo price they signed up for.

product.title: Feedback mode is the killer feature, and it's broken
product.minus: The feature people buy the app for is glitchy: the red pacer line drifts out of sync with the metronome, jerks between lines, and reports your timing as off even when you're dead-on — or when you record the reference track itself. The single most important progress tool fails.

product.title: Tabs on a phone are tiny and unreadable
product.minus: The tablature font on mobile is so small the chords are illegible, and feedback mode has no zoom at all. Zoom in practice mode and the auto-scroll dies. Practicing on a phone is effectively unusable.

product.title: Forced to sign in every single time
product.minus: The app doesn't remember you: every launch demands a fresh login, and sometimes the sign-in button is white text on a white background. For a daily-practice habit it's a barrier that drains people's motivation.

product.title: Chromecast and landscape break after updates
product.minus: Recent updates made the app crash when casting to Chromecast, dropped TV support, and broke landscape — white screen or no rotation at all. Videos load slowly and the screen falls asleep mid-lesson.

product.title: The gentle pacing is exactly what beginners love
product.plus: The core strength is short lessons and small steps at your own pace. Total beginners — including people in their 50s–60s — say that within a week or a month they could read tabs, play chords and recognizable riffs, finally succeeding after years of failed attempts.

product.title: Real riffs and songs from day one, not dry theory
product.plus: People love that you play familiar riffs and songs early on — visible results that keep you motivated. The "paths" structure (rock, blues, folk) and the ability to switch styles by mood keep the interest alive.

product.title: Too pricey for content that's free on YouTube
product.minus: Many find ~$150 a year steep for shallow lessons that are mostly chord shapes available free elsewhere. Rivals like Justin Guitar get called deeper and cheaper, the price was hiked sharply, and some people leave.

product.title: Beginners-only: oversimplified songs and wrong tabs
product.minus: Experienced players hit a ceiling fast: songs come as stripped versions without intros or solos, chords and tabs are sometimes just wrong, and the tracks sound nothing like the originals. No banjo, classical, or left-handed guitar.

product.title: Search is buggy and deletes letters as you type
product.minus: Song and artist search misbehaves: it deletes characters right after you type them, shows no songs under featured artists, and returns the wrong results. Finding the material you want is its own ordeal.

product.title: Note detection lies: you hit the right key and it marks you wrong
product.minus: The single most common pain point: people play perfectly, double- and triple-check, and the app stubbornly throws red dots or doesn't react at all. Often it's because the engine wants more volume or freezes after a wrong note.

product.title: One free lesson, then a solid wall of paywall
product.minus: The app is marketed as free, but after the first lesson or single song literally everything is locked. People feel they were rushed through the intro just to hit a paid subscription.

product.title: Subscriptions renew without warning and refunds are stonewalled
product.minus: Charges land with zero notice — sometimes at double last year's price, sometimes after months of not using the app. Cancellation is buried, refunds are nearly impossible, and many flatly call it a scam.

product.title: Constant crashes, freezes and endless loading make the app unusable
product.minus: Even people who paid for a year spend their time rebooting and reinstalling instead of playing. Lessons crash on open, the screen hangs on loading, and you have to close a lesson several times to get through it once.

product.title: MIDI setup gets stuck on "press your lowest key" and won't move on
product.minus: The advertised cable-keyboard connection mass-fails on Android: setup asks you to play your lowest note and never hears it, or MIDI latency makes lessons impossible. The same keyboards work fine in every other app.

product.title: Doesn't work on tablets or laptops, yet all the ads show big screens
product.minus: The app often refuses to install or run on Samsung, Lenovo and Amazon Fire tablets, Chromebooks and laptops — while the notes on a phone are too small to play. There's no Windows or web version, which hurts anyone with a keyboard by their computer.

product.title: No search, no favourites, no progress sync across devices
product.minus: Basic conveniences are painfully missing: you can't search for a song and have to scroll endlessly, you can't favourite anything, and progress is stored locally and vanishes when you switch devices.

product.title: Timing and visuals are out of sync: you can't tell when to play
product.minus: The moving line, metronome, audio and notation don't line up — the line runs a quarter ahead or skips notes, and in "play in time" mode a beginner has to guess the moment. Speed is stuck at 80% and you can't change it mid-play.

product.title: The best way to start from zero: you're playing a song within days
product.plus: What beginners love most: a clear step-by-step progression, crisp lesson videos and bite-sized chunks that have people playing "Ode to Joy" or even Beethoven on their very first day.

product.title: It listens to your real piano and gives live feedback
product.plus: When detection works, the live response to your playing is the hook: the app hears what you played, gives hints and praise — far more useful than learning from a book without knowing if you hit the right key.

product.title: A big song library, but many are watered-down versions of the originals
product.minus: The library is praised for its size and steady growth, but it grates that the longer, "advanced" songs are actually simplified and cut down — even on advanced you get a shortened arrangement, not the full score.

product.title: Pushy "kiddy" commentary you can't turn off, treating you like a toddler
product.minus: Adult learners are put off by the forced peppy American tone that can't be switched off, and a pace that's either too short — clicking "next" every 45 seconds — or suddenly demands both hands or five notes at once right at the start.

product.title: Note recognition doesn't register a correctly played note
product.minus: The core feature — the wait-and-play mode — fails at scale: the mic won't hear the correct note, forcing players to hammer one key ten times, drops out mid-piece, and skips bars. It fails over both the microphone and even cabled USB-MIDI, and you can't turn it off.

product.title: The songs you want are locked; free tier is only old classical pieces
product.minus: The ads promise "free," but the free tier is about 8–9 obscure classical and folk pieces (Ode to Joy, Fur Elise, Bella Ciao), while any song a person actually wants to play must be bought. Without the subscription the app is nearly useless — a couple of five-minute lessons.

product.title: The price feels like extortion — over $120 a year
product.minus: At roughly $120–270 (£130, $30/mo) the subscription strikes people as absurd for what YouTube offers free. The price stays hidden until you download and answer questions, and the advertised "cheap" monthly rate turns out to be billed a year up front.

product.title: Black screen after sign-up — the app simply won't start
product.minus: Dozens can't even get in: after "all set" the screen goes black, the account isn't created, no confirmation email arrives. On Samsung and Android it complains there's no internet when the connection is fine, or won't install at all.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and without consent
product.minus: People cancel in Google Play or turn off auto-renew — and still get charged $129–270, sometimes twice. The trial defaults to annual billing, support is hard to find, and many end up doing a chargeback through their bank.

product.title: Learned songs vanish without warning over licensing
product.minus: Songs people spent hours on suddenly turn "premium" or get pulled entirely when music licenses expire. They can no longer finish the Moonlight Sonata or Shallow they'd been mastering by memory — the practice wasted.

product.title: No Bluetooth MIDI support on Android
product.minus: On Android there's no MIDI over Bluetooth — even on Yamaha hardware, where other Yamaha apps handle it. The follow-light on the piano won't activate, MIDI playback won't route through the keyboard speakers, and without a USB adapter it's an exercise in frustration.

product.title: No plain sheet view, metronome, or easy repeat
product.minus: For repeat practice the basics are missing: you can't pull up a plain sheet without the video and lesson, there's no built-in metronome, and you can't loop a passage. To replay a song you have to go through the whole tutorial again and fight through menus.

product.title: Lessons run out fast and lack structure
product.minus: The structured lessons run out in a couple of weeks, the "intermediate" tier still feels beginner, and after the basics there are no chords, no scales, no timing work. For anyone past total beginner it disappoints, and few interesting new songs appear for years.

product.title: Wait-and-play lets you learn at your own pace — beginners love it
product.plus: When recognition works, the method wins people over: the app waits for the right note, lets you slow down, pause and repeat a measure, and play each hand separately. Total beginners learn their first song in minutes and feel like they have a private tutor beside them.

product.title: Shows sheet music and hand position at once — clear for self-learners
product.plus: The video up top shows hand position on the keyboard right as the notes scroll, with multiple difficulty levels per song. People who'd dreamed of playing for years start from zero and learn several songs over months at 10–15 minutes a day.

product.title: Responsive support refunds on request
product.plus: Despite the billing chaos, some people praise support: they reply by the next morning, cancel the subscription, and refund in full — for instance after a child's accidental purchase. It's the developer reply that nudges some to raise their rating.

product.title: Alternative tunings and the chromatic tuner moved behind a paywall
product.minus: The single sorest grievance: things that were free for years — Drop C, Nashville, non-standard tunings, the chromatic tuner — are now locked behind a subscription, so users leave for free tuners or a physical one.

product.title: The subscription prompt fires on every launch, even for paying users
product.minus: The app greets you with a subscription pitch on every open, and even lifetime or past buyers find their purchase "forgotten" — they must hit Restore Purchases each time to get access back.

product.title: A fast, accurate tuner — that's what users love it for
product.plus: The core of its reputation: it nails each string in seconds via the mic, cleanly and accurately, and many keep it on their phone for years and use it instead of a hardware tuner.

product.title: A great starting point for beginners: courses, songs, chords
product.plus: Many come for the tuner and stay for the courses, chords and learning favorite songs — it genuinely takes a beginner to confident playing and is often called the best app to start with.

product.title: After tuning, a "learn a song" prompt pops up
product.minus: For people who only want a tuner, the flow gets in the way: course ads before tuning and a "want to learn a song?" pop-up right after — it annoyingly blocks a simple task.

product.title: Inaccurate tightening guidance leads to broken strings
product.minus: A visceral complaint: the tuner says to tighten the string further (or shows a wrong -2/-120), the user keeps cranking — and the string snaps; they blame the app for it.

product.title: Songs won't open: "you're offline" while the internet works
product.minus: A recurring bug: when picking a song the app insists you're "offline" even though Wi-Fi and data are fine, forcing users to find tabs and chords elsewhere.

product.title: Dark patterns: a trial turns into a full charge
product.minus: A worrying class of money complaints: trying to start a trial results in being charged the full yearly amount, cancellation is hidden, and refunds are refused — users call it a scam.

product.title: "It's just a tuner" — the price feels absurd
product.minus: A psychological barrier: for the simplest function (essentially a Fourier transform on mic input) they ask ~$10 a month or over $20, and for many that crosses the line of reason.

product.title: Play detection won't credit what you actually play on acoustic
product.minus: Learning stalls on sound recognition: the course won't advance, demanding a chord be "improved", confuses E minor with D, and on acoustic it barely hears what you play — so there's no progress no matter how you try.

product.title: Tunes more than guitar — ukulele, bass, violin
product.plus: A pleasant plus: one tuner covers a whole range of string instruments, and many praise that it saved them on ukulele, bass or violin, not just a standard six-string.

product.title: The song catalog falls short: too few songs, no Hindi/regional
product.minus: For those who stay for the songs, content runs thin: the list is short, only a couple of songs are free, and Hindi, Punjabi and other regional music and tabs simply aren't there.

product.title: Ads are wired into every single action — open, start a song, fail, restart
product.minus: This is the utterly dominant complaint: people don't describe "ads in general" but a concrete loop — ad on launch, ad before a song, ad when you miss, ad after the song, ad on restart. Every tap means a video.

product.title: You spend more time watching ads than actually playing
product.minus: Users do the math: to play one song you sit through 3-4 clips of 30-60 seconds each. The arithmetic is obvious to them — you play less than you watch, and it kills an otherwise good game.

product.title: The core game is genuinely good — addictive, sharpens reflexes, satisfying feel
product.plus: Even the angriest reviewers admit the gameplay is excellent. Many literally write "great game ruined by ads." People love the speed, the rising difficulty, and the satisfaction of nailing the tiles.

product.title: The song catalog disappoints: missing known hits, lots of no-name filler
product.minus: A huge chunk of reviews is about the music. People install for a specific song (Rush E, Megalovania) and can't find it; they complain about old or "brainrot" tracks, no rock or k-pop, and a library that's 99% unknown filler.

product.title: Taps don't register: you hit the tile, the game counts a miss
product.minus: A technically specific, infuriating complaint: people are sure they hit the tile but the game drops the input. One user even captured screen-recorder proof and tested across several Samsung phones — the screen registers the touch, the game doesn't.

product.title: The subscription is outrageously priced: ~$6/week, hundreds a year
product.minus: The only way to kill the ads is premium at $5.99-$7.99 a week. Users do the conversion themselves — ~$25/month or ~$312/year — and call it daylight robbery for a game like this. Some report auto-charges they never wanted.

product.title: The tiles don't match the music's rhythm — which is the whole point
product.minus: For a rhythm game this is a fatal flaw: users say the notes are off-beat and the game feels desynced, and reasonably ask whether matching the music isn't the entire point.

product.title: Lag, freezes and mid-song crashes wipe out progress
product.minus: The game freezes or crashes mid-track and the user loses the round, the leaderboard, or all progress — especially galling when it happens on the verge of winning. Restarting just dumps you into more ads.

product.title: Promised "offline, no ads" — in reality it needs internet and shows ads anyway
product.minus: Users flatly accuse the app of lying: it's billed as offline yet songs won't download without a connection; people buy "no ads" and still get ads. This crosses from annoyance into feeling scammed.

product.title: Nostalgia: "this was my childhood game, and they ruined it"
product.plus: A powerful emotional anchor: many adults come back years later. It's a confession of love for the game — but in the same breath they mourn what ads and monetization have turned it into.

product.title: Players' top wish — custom songs and more current music (k-pop, anime, Hindi)
product.plus: Even happy users leave 4-5 stars with one ask: let them load their own music and add fresh tracks — k-pop, anime openings, Hindi songs. It's a signal of engagement: people want to play here, if only their music were in it.

product.title: Desktop is great — the mobile app is barely usable
product.minus: The same story over and over: on a computer or in the browser everything works beautifully, but the same thing on a phone is a separate broken product where it's physically impossible to make music.

product.title: The studio crashes and kicks you out mid-work
product.minus: Open a project or start a new one, and the app closes, dumping you back to the phone's home screen. Sometimes it loops endlessly and won't even let you into the studio.

product.title: Glitchy audio: crackling, tempo jumps, broken playback
product.minus: Playback falls apart even on simple tracks: audio crackles, speeds up and slows down, turning finished music into mush. The more tracks, the worse it gets.

product.title: Lost work: autosave silently erases finished projects
product.minus: There's no save button and no signal whether anything saved. People come back to a nearly finished song and half the recordings — or everything — is gone. Hours of work evaporate.

product.title: Almost everything good is locked behind a subscription
product.minus: Quality instruments, the loop library, even recording — all behind a paywall. The more new features they add, the more is locked, and the less you can actually use for free.

product.title: Export breaks: you can't download the song to your phone
product.minus: You finish a track and can't save it. It hangs on "exporting", says "mix incomplete", or the file just can't be found. Even with premium, downloading to your phone often fails.

product.title: The piano roll can't tell what you're trying to do
product.minus: The touchscreen MIDI editor is agony: notes won't place, the app confuses moving, stretching and scrolling, and the roll is so tiny it's nearly impossible to hit with a finger.

product.title: Overloads the CPU and freezes on just a couple of tracks
product.minus: Two or three tracks are enough for the app to complain about CPU overload, lag, and freeze. Loading the studio sometimes drags on for minutes, even on a flagship phone.

product.title: Subscriptions can't be cancelled, and charges keep coming
product.minus: Cancellation just spins forever, support points at the app store, and the card gets charged for months — even after deleting the app and closing the account. People flatly call it a scam.

product.title: The new UI and updates removed features instead of adding them
product.minus: It used to work — after the UI overhaul everything got harder and worse: volume control, key selection, the ability to move sounds all vanished. People beg for the old version back.

product.title: For beginners — the best on-ramp to making music
product.plus: When it works, it's beginners' favorite tool: an approachable interface, you place notes wherever you want without knowing how to play, and people genuinely launch music careers from it.

product.title: A rich free sample library and quality demo projects
product.plus: Many find the free tier enough: hundreds of loops and samples, no intrusive ads, and the demo projects and sounds themselves are solid — they help you learn and build tracks.

product.title: "Just use the desktop" — the app is only good as a player
product.plus: Even satisfied users agree: on a phone the app is useful for listening to your projects on the go or moving files from a PC, while the real work happens on desktop.

product.title: Bought the music — but you can only print it through the app
product.minus: Users buy sheet music on the website, then discover they can only print it by installing the app — and many read this as a deliberate trap rather than a technical necessity.

product.title: They charge extra for a PDF of music you already bought
product.minus: The defining grievance: after buying the music, a downloadable PDF costs another $3+, revealed only when you try to save it — users uniformly call it a scam.

product.title: Paid, but locked out: the app login won't let you in
product.minus: The account works on the website, but the app rejects the same login (especially social sign-in), leaving purchased music inaccessible — charged, but no music.

product.title: Printing spits out blank pages or hangs on 'contacting printer'
product.minus: Even when they reach printing, people get blank pages or an endless 'contacting printer' — and the limited print count gets burned in the process.

product.title: In-app prices are higher than the website — Pro discounts mislead
product.minus: The same piece costs $1-3 more in the app than on the website, so the advertised 'dollar off per song' Pro discount actually saves nothing.

product.title: Pro membership doesn't deliver the promised credits or free titles
product.minus: People sign up for Pro expecting free titles and credits, but get zero or a couple of unfamiliar pieces, and still have to pay per song on top.

product.title: Recent updates break the app: crashes, freezes, refresh loops
product.minus: After updates the app crashes on launch or in search, and a 'treble clef refresh' icon wipes out typed text — Android devices suffer the most.

product.title: The reader is helpless: no bar selection, no rewind, no smooth scroll
product.minus: Playback always restarts from the top, you can't tap into a bar or loop a passage, and scrolling jumps page-by-page — making sight-reading impossible.

product.title: Imported PDFs can only be viewed, never played
product.minus: The app stores and marks up your own PDFs and musicXML, but can't play them — playback works only for music bought from Musicnotes.

product.title: Support is a wall of chatbot and week-long silence
product.minus: When subscriptions or purchases break, support funnels you to a useless bot and knowledge-base links; human replies take a week or never arrive.

product.title: A huge library of quality arrangements — the main reason to stay
product.plus: Loyal users praise the vast catalog and strong signature-artist arrangements year after year: almost any song can be found and bought instantly.

product.title: Transpose, tempo control and part playback — invaluable for practice
product.plus: Those genuinely learning to play love the interactivity: you can hear a piece with accompaniment, slow the tempo, change the key and fit the music to your instrument.

product.title: A digital replacement for the heavy binder of sheet music
product.plus: Musicians love keeping their whole library, setlists and markups on a tablet instead of kilos of paper — handy at rehearsals, gigs and on the go.

product.title: Free intro, but the first song demands a subscription
product.minus: Users get warmed up by the intro lesson, and the moment they reach the first song or second course a paywall slams down. It feels like a bait-and-switch: "free" turned into a trap, and people go back to YouTube.

product.title: The tuner pulls strings down and snaps them
product.minus: The tuner keeps saying "too low" on an already-tuned string, pushing people to tighten until it snaps. Dozens of users, kids included, break strings on family and keepsake guitars by trusting wrong prompts.

product.title: The mic fails to hear correctly played notes
product.minus: Note detection is flaky: a correctly played string or chord gets marked wrong, and sometimes it doesn't react at all until you shout. Progress stalls on this, even though the same hardware works fine in other apps.

product.title: Step-by-step lessons genuinely teach a beginner from zero
product.plus: The core strength is clear delivery: everything is broken into tiny steps, explained slowly with real-time feedback. Total beginners pick up their first chords in minutes and feel progress — better than a pile of YouTube videos.

product.title: No ads interrupting the learning
product.plus: Fans specifically call out that lessons aren't broken up by ads. The pacing is comfortable — neither rushed nor sluggish — so learning stays calm and pleasant.

product.title: The pay screen won't close — and the trial turns into a bill
product.minus: The subscription window sometimes won't close and kicks you out of the lesson, and the seven-day "free" trial turns into a demand for money: users report charges and being harassed for £129 even after cancelling.

product.title: A long sign-up gets in the way of simply tuning
product.minus: Many just want a tuner, but the app demands an account, a pile of questions, and personal info before you can begin. Part of the onboarding is broken outright: in landscape the buttons fall below the fold with no scroll, so you can't finish setup.

product.title: The tuner gets praised as one of the best among guitar apps
product.plus: Despite the string complaints, a share of users count the tuner as a highlight — accurate and handy, better than rival apps. For beginners, tuning the guitar is often the first small win.

product.title: No modes for lefties, 4-string, or electric guitars
product.minus: The app is rigidly built for a right-handed 6-string: no left-handed mode, no electric tuner, no 4-string option. Some users resort to singing notes with their voice to pass exercises — non-standard instruments simply aren't supported.

product.title: The price stings, and there's little for non-beginners
product.minus: The ~$130–150 yearly plan is out of reach for many, especially teens and kids without money. And those who already play complain about forced basic lessons, too few advanced challenges, and not enough songs.

product.title: Crashes and lost progress on later levels
product.minus: On advanced lessons and after updates the app starts crashing, losing audio, and wiping progress, forcing a restart. Sometimes it loops the exercise back to the start, leaving the user unsure what they did wrong.

product.title: Kids and families adopt it as a first learning tool
product.plus: Many praise it specifically for kids: clear, friendly, and a child can pick up chords and reach for the guitar on their own. Parents like having an easy way to learn at home, and younger siblings join in too.

product.title: Sold as «free», but you can't make anything without paying
product.minus: The install is free, but actually creating anything isn't: pricing is often hidden up front, money is demanded from the start with no trial, and users feel baited.

product.title: A daily creation limit slams into a paywall
product.minus: After one or two images you hit «limit reached, come back in 12 hours» with no warning it was coming, which infuriates both newcomers and people just messing around for fun.

product.title: Deformed hands, fingers and bodies in the filters
product.minus: Filters like GYM and SUPER HERO routinely produce extra arms, seven fingers and gym bars impaled through the body — the left hand suffers most.

product.title: Avatars don't look like you and swap your gender
product.minus: Half the results look nothing like you, and the app will turn a wife into a man or keep trying to make you a white woman — likeness is shaky at best.

product.title: «Failed to connect to server» instead of pictures
product.minus: The app fails to reach its servers, hangs on loading, crashes or kicks you back to the home screen after every shot — generations simply never arrive.

product.title: Double charges and a subscription you can't stop
product.minus: Buy the yearly and it keeps taking the weekly; pay for pro and nothing unlocks; money comes off after cancelling and before the trial ends, while support stays silent.

product.title: Weekly price on the label, yearly charge in reality
product.minus: It shows a one-week price but charges for the whole year — users flatly call it misleading advertising and unsubscribe.

product.title: Paid — and still hit limits, watermarks and errors
product.minus: Premium promises unlimited but throws a «monthly training limit» on the 5th avatar; pro still stamps avatarro watermarks; paid generations are waited on for hours and never come.

product.title: Headshots and realistic portraits are the strong suit
product.plus: When it works, results are impressively realistic: headshots look incredible, it even caught a nose piercing, and for the price it beats many other AI generators.

product.title: Fun, simple and no forced sign-up
product.plus: Many love it as entertainment: easy to use, brings story characters to life, doesn't force you through endless sign-ups, and some features are genuinely free.

product.title: Intrusive ads even in paid and trial versions
product.minus: Ads are relentless: the trial ships with ads, and even after paying $39 the paid user is still forced to watch them.

product.title: It used to be a free text-to-image app — now it's just a paid avatar generator
product.minus: The core complaint across almost all reviews: people loved the old Dawn for text- and sketch-based art, then updates ripped that out and left only the «avatar yourself» function. Longtime fans see it as the app killing itself.

product.title: Everything is behind a paywall — you can't even try before you pay
product.minus: A huge share of reviews: the app installs as «free» but won't generate a single avatar or even one trial result without a subscription. People delete it immediately, with no way to judge the quality.

product.title: You pay the subscription — and they still charge extra for each pack and image
product.minus: A common grievance: even after a weekly or yearly subscription, users hit fresh price tags — for each style, pack or extra generation. The subscription doesn't cover what they bought it for.

product.title: «Something went wrong» on photo upload — falsely blames the internet
product.minus: A specific reproducible bug: uploading photos throws an error blaming the internet connection even when the network is fine. For some users the app never works at all, especially on Android.

product.title: Stops working right after you pay
product.minus: A painful pattern: the user pays and the app immediately breaks, crashes or refuses to generate. Money taken, nothing delivered — which many flatly call a scam.

product.title: Can't unsubscribe — they keep charging after cancellation
product.minus: A serious billing issue: people can't cancel inside the app and charges keep coming. Support replies with templates or stays silent, turning cancellation into a fight.

product.title: Image quality dropped — low resolution and an intrusive watermark
product.minus: Those who remember the old version note real degradation: images turned small and low-res, and a logo watermark now sits on paid results. Outputs often don't resemble the person.

product.title: Harsh daily caps even on «Pro» — 1-2 generations a day
product.minus: Even paying subscribers complain they get just one or two generations a day, and the promised hundreds of images don't add up. People feel they pay for a sub and still hit a wall.

product.title: Won't let you save or download the generated images
product.minus: A distinct technical pain: even after subscribing and generating avatars, users can't save them to the phone gallery. Images sometimes also vanish before the promised storage window.

product.title: Feels like a bait and switch
product.minus: Many openly call the model a bait and switch: the app advertises itself as free, trades on its old reputation, then demands money after it already has your data. Some threaten regulator complaints.

product.title: When the headshots land, they're more realistic than rivals
product.plus: A smaller but genuine group of happy users praises the realism and consistency of the headshots: for those it works for, results come out lifelike and high-quality, sometimes beating Lensa.

product.title: Too few styles and no custom prompts
product.minus: Even loyal users want more: the preset styles get old fast, custom prompts and face tags are gone, and there's no full-body option. The freedom the old version had is sorely missed.

product.title: It used to be great — an update broke everything
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people loved this for years, and after the AI switch they call it garbage and uninstall. "Bring back the old version" is a chorus of dozens of voices.

product.title: The AI pastes your face onto a stranger's skinny body
product.minus: The defining mechanic of the new version and its core flaw: instead of editing your photo, the AI takes only the face and drops it onto stranger's model bodies in odd outfits. The result looks nothing like you.

product.title: They charge during the supposedly free trial
product.minus: Many users report that after agreeing to a "free trial" they're charged immediately, cancellation doesn't work, and there's no refund. It reads to them as deception and a scam.

product.title: Weekly pricing shocks users and feels like a trap
product.minus: A £7.99 / $8-per-week subscription (about $40/month) feels wildly disproportionate for an app used a couple of times a year. The weekly cadence reads as a deliberate trap.

product.title: A hard paywall right at the door
product.minus: The app lets you try nothing without a card on file: the single free sample is "completely unusable," and any save demands a subscription. Users refuse to enter card details blind.

product.title: Servers are perpetually overloaded — you can't use it
product.minus: A constant "servers are busy / too many downloads" error blocks generation for months — even for paying subscribers. One user is especially bitter that servers "start working" right after the trial ends.

product.title: Confuses male and female, with no manual override
product.minus: The AI insists on guessing gender from hair length: a haircut makes you "a man," long hair makes you "a woman." There's no button to set gender manually, so results come back as the wrong sex.

product.title: Group photos are gone — now only one face allowed
product.minus: You used to be able to process photos with several people (up to 5) — that's what drew in friends and family. Now the app complains "only one face" even when there's a single person in the shot.

product.title: The result doesn't resemble you and comes out distorted
product.minus: Generated faces don't match the original — extra arms appear, features warp, skin tone shifts. Light skin goes dark, dark skin goes white, and there's no way to correct the image.

product.title: "Face not found" on photos that clearly have a face
product.minus: Face detection has degraded: the app fails to see a face in perfectly valid photos, especially with a beard, and makes you watch an ad only to say "no face." Some suspect it's a trick to serve more ads.

product.title: When it works — detailed, beautiful results
product.plus: A real slice of users genuinely loves it: the filters are beautiful, the detailing is rich, each "theme" yields 4 variants. Some call it the best AI headshots they've used, and it really does make you look younger.

product.title: Simple and fun — pleasant to share
product.plus: Plenty of users find it easy and fun: the interface is clear, the photos come out, and people want to share them on social media and with family. Even the free version strikes some as brilliant.

product.title: Ads flood the free version
product.minus: The free tier is a wall of ads: "20 ads and still no new profile pic." Ads block you from even trying it out, and you can't download without subscribing.

product.title: Invasive access to photos and privacy fears
product.minus: The app demands access to all photos and, users say, starts uploading shots without asking. There are fears of surveillance and accusations of harvesting data "behind terms and conditions."

product.title: Ads form a wall that blocks the way into the app
product.minus: The single most common complaint: ads don't just annoy, they fully block access — they can't be closed or skipped, and people never reach the editor at all.

product.title: Without a paid plan the app simply won't let you go further
product.minus: Many hit a plan-selection screen right after picking a photo: there's no free trial, and you can't reach any result without paying first.

product.title: Paid — and still got ads and no HD
product.minus: Buying lifetime or a subscription often doesn't deliver what was promised: ads stay, HD images never come, and the «remove ads» button is still sitting in the interface.

product.title: A huge logo ruins the saved picture
product.minus: On save, a giant app logo gets baked into the photo, taking up nearly a quarter of the image — it disfigures finished works and collages.

product.title: Demands full access to the entire gallery or it won't work
product.minus: The app won't run without permission to ALL photos: it refuses «limited access» mode, so people must either hand over the whole gallery or uninstall.

product.title: Can't cancel the subscription — money taken, no access
product.minus: Some users paid for a subscription, couldn't use the app, and then couldn't find it in their subscriptions list to cancel and stop further charges.

product.title: Used to work — broke after an update
product.minus: Long-time users note decay: the app freezes, effects stop working, and what was free for years suddenly demands payment.

product.title: Grainy output and few real line-art effects
product.minus: For those who do reach a result, quality falls short: the picture comes out grainy, there's no simple line art, and the photo-to-drawing conversion looks weak.

product.title: When it works — even artists praise the result
product.plus: Those who break through to the editor love the effect: the drawings look like professional pencil work, people show them off to family and get complimented.

product.title: Simple and clear with a rich choice of filters
product.plus: A real strength is the easy on-ramp: clear interface, lots of filters (pencil, cartoon, pop effect, B&W and color), and you can preview before saving.

product.title: A working tool for artists and tattoo creators
product.plus: For part of the audience it's a genuine work tool: they trace the sketch onto paper, make portraits of loved ones, and prepare stencils for tattoos.

product.title: Charged right after a "free" trial
product.minus: The single most common complaint: users start a 3-day trial and get charged almost immediately or after day one. They call it a scam, demand refunds, and threaten to report it.

product.title: The free AI generation is gone
product.minus: Long-time users (3-10 years) are leaving: the ability to create unique AI images for free was removed — including the beloved "Dream Manifestor" — and everything is now locked behind paid templates.

product.title: Already subscribed, yet still billed weekly
product.minus: Even a yearly plan doesn't help: users say weekly ~$10 charges keep hitting on top of it, and cancelling doesn't stop the billing.

product.title: Charged for an app they never even used
product.minus: A cluster of complaints is about money vanishing with no interaction at all: charges only surface in a bank statement or Google Wallet, sometimes twice.

product.title: No VIP, no editing at all
product.minus: Almost nothing is free anymore: users say the app is all VIP sections, and even basic editing or a haircut can't be done without paying.

product.title: Quality didn't rise with the price
product.minus: The price went up but the output didn't: users call it a toy rather than a tool, see "too much AI", and compare it unfavorably to free Gemini.

product.title: The AI confuses gender and swaps the wrong face
product.minus: Recognition misfires: filters pull a female face toward the male side, swap the idol's face instead of the user's, or output the wrong skin tone.

product.title: Too few male and couple templates
product.minus: The template library skews female: men and people wanting couple or mixed-race photos lack options and ask for a filter and more variety.

product.title: The content stopped refreshing
product.minus: It used to delight with new pictures and videos every couple of days — now users say it just repeats the same few templates and shows nothing new.

product.title: Layered effects are the reason fans stay
product.plus: Happy users love the rich set of effects and templates: you can layer effect upon effect for scrapbooking and portraits, and the premium AI is praised as some of the best they've seen.

product.title: An addictive toy with years of loyalty
product.plus: A loyal core sticks around for years: people call it incredibly entertaining, say you "lose track of time" enjoying it, and note the free templates are exactly what nudges them to subscribe.

product.title: Turns ordinary photos into "beautiful" ones
product.plus: The transformation effect is the emotional hook for many: users say the app makes them beautiful, praise the picture quality, and find it easy and even kid-friendly.

product.title: The subscription doesn't unlock anything — you still need coins on top
product.minus: By far the loudest complaint: people pay for a weekly, monthly or yearly plan expecting "full access," then get a handful of coins good for one or two generations before the app demands they buy more coin packs. The subscription feels like a cover charge, not the product.

product.title: One result per weekly subscription, then a wall of waiting
product.minus: After paying for a week you genuinely get just one photo or video, and the next free batch of coins only arrives in ~160–167 hours — exactly when the subscription auto-renews. Users explicitly call out the timing as a deliberate trap.

product.title: No way to try it — you pay before you ever see a result
product.minus: The app offers no free sample or demo at all: payment is required before you see a single generated frame. Even the "free trial" is paid. Many back out and uninstall before ever reaching the product.

product.title: Begs for a 5-star review on launch, before you've done anything
product.minus: The review prompt pops up the instant you first open the app — before any feature or paywall. Users read it as rating manipulation and openly explain why the score is high while every written review is negative.

product.title: The gallery won't open — photos from it won't load
product.minus: Even after paying, the core action — picking photos from your gallery — often just fails: the button does nothing, the screen loops back to "camera or gallery," the app crashes. Permissions granted manually, cache cleared, reinstall — none of it helps.

product.title: The output looks nothing like you — wrong face, wrong race, wrong hair
product.minus: When generation does run, the portraits often look nothing like the person in the uploaded photos: the face, age, hairstyle, even race come out wrong. Bald users get hair added, grey-haired ones ignored, heads out of proportion to bodies.

product.title: Generation drags 30+ minutes or never finishes at all
product.minus: The promised "one minute" stretches to 30–45 minutes or even hours; the timer only climbs and the photo or video never arrives. Coins get deducted anyway, and a retry costs coins again.

product.title: Charges your card without consent and after you cancel
product.minus: People report hidden and repeat charges: a one-week fee turns into a weekly one, money keeps coming out after cancellation, and some are billed for an app they never even installed. Cancelling and getting a refund is its own ordeal.

product.title: Support goes silent and refund requests get denied
product.minus: When something breaks, support tickets go unanswered for weeks and refund requests get a canned denial with no explanation. Some users end up disputing the charges through their bank instead.

product.title: Ads promise free videos the app doesn't actually deliver
product.minus: TikTok and Facebook ads show flashy dancing videos and free access, but in reality there are either no video features at all, or the result is a weak three-second clip for real money. The gap between the ad and the product is its own source of anger.

product.title: When it does work, the portraits come out genuinely good
product.plus: The few who get all the way through praise quality, accurate images and videos; for some the output is good enough for a professional headshot or website photo. The product itself can deliver — the problem is how few people ever reach that point.

product.title: Cancellation is hidden: there's no in-app button and unsubscribing is impossible
product.minus: The single most common complaint: people hunt for weeks to unsubscribe, the app sends them to the store, the subscription isn't there, and many end up blocking their card or closing their payment account just to stop the charges.

product.title: The "7-day free trial" is a lie: money is taken the moment you subscribe
product.minus: The ad promises a free trial, but tapping "start" charges the full amount immediately, or money disappears on day 1–2 — users call it clickbait and bait.

product.title: Repeated, unauthorized charges — even after cancelling and deleting
product.minus: People report multiple charges a month, billing after they cancelled and uninstalled, and even charges for an app they never downloaded; for many it crosses into outright theft.

product.title: When it works, the result is natural — you still look like yourself
product.plus: The top praise: the retouch looks realistic, without a plastic look or someone else's features — it just fixes light and angle and keeps your face yours, and people love it.

product.title: You're forced to pay before you can try anything at all
product.minus: You must hand over your card before the first use, and you can't make a single edit without paying; people refuse to blindly enter card details for a "free" app.

product.title: The weekly price is disguised as monthly — and it's wildly high
product.minus: People think they're paying $5–8 a month, then discover it's per week — nearly $300–400 a year; the price even climbs over time, turning former fans bitter.

product.title: AI-profile setup loops forever: photos won't upload, you never reach a result
product.minus: The app demands 10–15 photos but won't let you add past 8–9, freezes on "training the AI," or runs in circles — many never get through setup at all.

product.title: The "how to not look ugly" ad disgusts users and harms self-esteem
product.minus: A whole wave of reviews isn't about features but about the ad where a woman calls herself ugly before the app; people see it as misogyny that fuels body dysmorphia in teen girls.

product.title: Rescues bad shots — the best photo "retaker" people have tried
product.plus: Those who get through setup are thrilled: it turns bad photos into good ones, fixes expression and angle, and beats the dozens of other editors they've tried.

product.title: You pay and still hit daily limits and a paywalled famine
product.minus: Even with a subscription, features are throttled: daily caps on photos and downloads, the promised "unlimited retakes" turn out to be 40 a day, and almost everything good is pro-only.

product.title: Frequent crashes, stuck loading, and updates that break it
product.minus: It crashes 5 times out of 7, sticks on "loading" after payment, and recent updates leave long-paid pro broken — purchased time burns for nothing.

product.title: Sometimes the result is fake: bloated lips, painted-on eyes, lost quality
product.minus: Some users get a cartoonish, unnatural result — enlarged lips, lifeless eyes, compressed lower-quality photos that don't match what the ad promised.

product.title: You can't try anything without paying first
