product.minus: It installs for free, but the very first launch slams a subscription wall in your face: you can't upload a photo, generate anything, or even change your username until you pay. People uninstall within minutes, having never seen a single result.

product.title: An ad after every single tap
product.minus: The ads aren't just frequent — they're wedged into every step: to view your own past creations you first have to sit through a clip, and afterward the feed scrolls away from them. Double back-to-back ads, no skip, traps you can only escape by force-closing the app.

product.title: Paid for a subscription — but everything inside runs on tokens
product.minus: The yearly sub is already paid, but the app has moved to tokens: once your coins run out, generation stops — even with months left on the subscription. Even basic photo editing now costs tokens, and video is a separate currency that no plan includes.

product.title: The result looks nothing like the face you uploaded
product.minus: The core promise — "this will be you" — keeps failing: the likeness slips, the face becomes a stranger, the gender flips, and in video the face vanishes the moment the subject moves, replaced by a generic model. And you pay for every generation, even the botched ones.

product.title: Every update makes the app worse
product.minus: Long-time subscribers describe years of decline: 10 free generations a day became 5, then 3, then zero; custom prompts were removed, the limit cut to 280 characters, model quality dropped. The old version is remembered as the golden one.

product.title: The app simply won't open
product.minus: A huge cluster of complaints — the app just stops launching: endless loading, "timed out", "unable to resolve host", "internal server error", certificate and Java-path errors. People with paid yearly subscriptions can't get in for months.

product.title: Generation fails with an error
product.minus: Even when the app opens, generation breaks: "error rejection", NSFW blocks on harmless prompts, "billing unavailable error 3", "PERMISSION_DENIED", "internal server error" right when you build a pack — and what you made vanishes the moment you return to the app.

product.title: Bodies are generated from a stereotype, not from reality
product.minus: Body types behave absurdly: "curvy" produces obesity, "skinny" produces anorexia, "muscular" makes you fat; there's no average "dad bod", no height control — everyone becomes a tall, long-armed supermodel. It lightens dark skin and makes Asians look non-Asian.

product.title: The price stings, especially the weekly plan
product.minus: A $13-15 weekly subscription feels like robbery — more than a gym membership. The tiers keep multiplying (premium → ultra → elite → supreme), each with a new token type, and users say it all adds up to over $100 a month.

product.title: Charges and subscriptions without consent, and no support you can reach
product.minus: People report charges after uninstalling, refused refunds, and no way to unsubscribe in-app or via Play. The support phone number doesn't exist, emails go unanswered, and Discord mods delete inconvenient posts.

product.title: When it works, the quality and likeness impress
product.plus: Those who push through the paywall and ads praise the realism and detail: a single frontal selfie is enough to see yourself at 20, 30, 40, like a professional shoot. Many tried 8+ rivals and call this the best.

product.title: An easy, fun, addictive way to try on any look
product.plus: Despite everything, a loyal core loves the app for its ease and playfulness: they make characters for D&D and novels, "put hair back on their head", and laugh at the results. For them it's the best face-swap and a source of styling inspiration.

product.title: You pay before seeing a single image
product.minus: A hard paywall right at launch: not one trial generation, not a single sample. People have no idea what they're paying for and reasonably leave a one-star before ever using it.

product.title: The subscription gets you just 2 generations a week
product.minus: After paying comes the real surprise: a cap of ~2 photos a week, disclosed nowhere up front. After that it's wait seven days or pay again.

product.title: Paid for a year, yet still nagged to pay more inside
product.minus: Even a yearly or "lifetime" plan doesn't unlock things: after a couple of generations the app demands you buy extra credits on top. People feel cheated.

product.title: Asks you to rate the app in the first seconds
product.minus: A "rate us" prompt pops up literally seconds after opening — before you've done anything. Users flat-out call it a red flag and rating manipulation.

product.title: Keeps charging even after you cancel
product.minus: The most alarming pattern: charges continue after cancellation, there's no in-app way to cancel, and some are billed without ever installing it. People end up disputing with their bank.

product.title: Results don't look like you, or just come out ugly
product.minus: Even for those who pay, the output often doesn't resemble the face: it ages you, adds wrinkles, extra arms and distortions. Some complaints aren't about money at all — they're about the AI quality itself.

product.title: "Free" in the ad turns into a paywall
product.minus: The ads and the "try now" wording promise a free trial, but everything runs into payment. The gap between the ad and reality is a recurring theme.

product.title: When you can't cancel, leaving is hard
product.minus: Cancellation is buried or unavailable, and trying to exit serves up a special offer and loops you back to the pay screen. Walking away cleanly is nearly impossible.

product.title: The app crashes and hangs even after you pay
product.minus: Technically shaky: crashes on open, an endless registration loop, an outdated build after purchase, "limit reached" right after logging in. You pay and can't even get in.

product.title: When it works, the headshots are genuinely good
product.plus: The minority who reach a result praise the realism and quality: natural selfies, professional headshots, the face stays recognizable without a "surgical makeover". The generation engine itself isn't the weak link.

product.title: Basic features get removed, and your data is taken forever
product.minus: Separate alarms: the key LinkedIn headshot for professionals vanished, you can't swap your uploaded photos, and the terms claim a perpetual right to all your images. None of it builds trust.

product.title: Cancelling is nearly impossible — the subscription isn't even in Google Play
product.minus: The single most common complaint: cancellation is hidden so well that the subscription can't be found in the app or in Google Play subscriptions, while charges keep coming. Users email support with no reply, cancel four times over, and end up reporting to their bank.

product.title: "Lifetime" access vanishes after a new phone or an update
product.minus: People bought lifetime back in 2022–2023, and now logging in returns "email not found" — even with a receipt in hand, support says there's no record of the purchase. For them "lifetime" turned into "until the developer gets bored."

product.title: Pay upfront — no trial, no way to see what it actually does
product.minus: The app walks you through the whole setup, takes your photo, then hits you with payment — you can't even try one video. People reasonably want to see what it can do first, and uninstall in droves before ever getting a result.

product.title: Videos hang in "generating" for hours and days — with no way to cancel
product.minus: A started video can spin for 2 hours, 3 days, with some waiting 10 hours or three weeks. Worst of all, the stuck render can't be cancelled, and the app blocks any new video until the old one "finishes."

product.title: Even Pro gives just 3 videos a week, then asks for more money
product.minus: Paying for Pro barely helps: an undisclosed cap of 3 AI videos a week, plus a prompt to pay more for extras. The purchase essentially just removes the ads.

product.title: Hidden pricing: a $7.99 entry turns into $19.99–20 charges every week
product.minus: The real cost is never shown upfront: you pay $7.99 to "try," then a week later $19.99 or $20 is quietly taken weekly. The pricing is deliberately confusing, and users feel tricked.

product.title: Animation quality is weak: lip-sync misses, the face is a "cutout" that melts
product.minus: The output is far from the ads: lips out of sync, the face moves like a flat cutout along a fixed boundary, with a new "melting" effect. Many compare it unfavorably to Grok, Manus, and D-ID.

product.title: Demands a rating and payment before you've done anything at all
product.minus: The app demands a rating right after the tutorial, before the first animation — and people leave a one-star for the nerve of it. Same with payment: money is asked for before any result.

product.title: Region blocks and "inappropriate photo" errors break the whole point of paying
product.minus: After payment the app declares it's unavailable in your region (USA, Florida, Illinois), or flags any clothed photo as "inappropriate" — even a dress or a swimsuit. The result: nothing and nowhere to animate.

product.title: Support stays silent or sends template apologies — refunds are unreachable
product.minus: Emails go unanswered for months, tickets sit open since last year, and the promised 30-day refund is out of reach: no phone, no working contact. Even answered tickets are just automated "sorry" replies.

product.title: When it works, it's genuinely fun and easy family-photo entertainment
product.plus: Those for whom it works genuinely have fun: animating photos of family and pets, making singing videos with grandkids, praising how simple it is even "for a dinosaur." Some monetize the clips, some say it reminds them of the old Wombo.

product.title: Templates force singing and music, while the effect you wanted (dance, kiss) is gone
product.minus: People want the photo to dance or do a specific scene, but the app stubbornly makes the character sing over random music. Features like "kissing" suddenly disappear a week after someone bought the app specifically for them.

product.title: Used to be free — now almost everything is behind a subscription
product.minus: The core grievance: people used a generous free version for years (some over a decade), then one update moved 90-99% of sounds behind a yearly subscription. It doesn't read as 'a bit pricey' — it reads as 'they took away what was mine'.

product.title: Locked the personal mixes I'd been using for years
product.minus: The sharpest pain isn't the catalogue in general — it's the personal mixes users built for themselves. Someone opens the app at bedtime and their go-to rain-and-thunder combo now demands a subscription. The very thing the account was for is gone.

product.title: I already paid for the old app — and they swapped it for a subscription
product.minus: Veterans paid a one-time fee for Relax Melodies / Relax Meditation to unlock everything 'for life'. The app got renamed BetterSleep, the old purchase was wiped, and they're asked to pay again. It reads as a straight betrayal of paying customers.

product.title: Can't even try it — paywall on the first screen
product.minus: New users never hear a single sound: after a batch of questions they're met with a demand to subscribe and add a card before anything works. Many uninstall before reaching the product at all.

product.title: The subscription is impossible to cancel — it loops you
product.minus: In-app cancellation works like a trap: it asks your reason, dangles a 'discount', and declining drops you back to the start — subscription still active. The website demands a password you never created if you signed up via Google.

product.title: Charged after the trial was supposedly cancelled
product.minus: The trial flips fast (sometimes in 3 days) into a full $40-70 annual charge. Users report being billed even after cancelling, charged on a backup card, and kept on the hook for years — with no working refund.

product.title: The sound cuts off mid-night and wakes you up
product.minus: Even paying users see the sound die or the app crash after an hour or two, despite an all-night timer. For people who need noise to STAY asleep, this kills the whole purpose — and clearing cache or reinstalling doesn't fix it.

product.title: Crackle and static in the voice when sleep tracking is on
product.minus: A specific reproducible bug: turn on sleep recording/tracking and the meditation and story voices start to crackle, hiss, 'sound like under a plastic bag'. Turn tracking off and the audio is clean. The two headline features fight each other.

product.title: Cluttered interface, buttons move without warning
product.minus: The home screen has bloated: it's unclear how to even start tracking, and endless 'buy premium' popups pile on. The 'Routine' button many people rely on keeps vanishing and reappearing across updates, breaking their nightly ritual.

product.title: Almost no fresh content — same things on repeat
product.minus: Loyal, paying subscribers complain that new stories and sounds barely get added for months, so they're stuck on repeat. Add growing irritation at 'AI music' they consider slop. It's the reason given for not renewing.

product.title: A rich sound mixer — you build your own soundscape
product.plus: The app's biggest source of love: a huge library and the ability to layer and blend sounds into a personal combination. People with tinnitus, misophonia, PTSD and ADHD say their custom mix is what cuts through their noise and sends them to sleep in minutes.

product.title: Asleep in minutes — for many it genuinely works
product.plus: Underneath all the money fights sits a real core: people fall asleep fast and deeply with this app for years and wake up rested. Some call it their 'sleeping pill' and say they can't fall asleep without it.

product.title: Sleep stories and meditations with beloved narrators
product.plus: Beyond sounds, people stay for the bedtime stories, meditations and hypnosis — especially specific narrators' voices (Aster J. Haile gets named repeatedly). For quieting anxiety, racing thoughts and post-stress nights it's a value of its own.

product.title: Sleep recording and tracking — you hear what happens at night
product.plus: For those it clicks with, the feature is genuinely loved: the app records the night and shows sleep cycles, letting you replay snoring, sleep-talking, even the cat. It helps people understand their patterns and pairs with the ResMed CPAP app.

product.title: The price is hidden until the end of a long survey
product.minus: Users go through onboarding, answer dozens of personal questions and link an account, and only then discover the app is paid at around $100-130/year — the «extract data first, reveal price last» flow reads as a bait-and-switch.

product.title: The «free trial» charges you immediately
product.minus: A very common complaint: users pick the 7-day trial and get charged the same day for a full year or quarter, and the promised pre-charge reminder never arrives.

product.title: Ads promise «free», but a card is mandatory
product.minus: YouTube/social ads frame the app as free, yet you can't even reach the trial without a credit card — and for the ADHD audience it targets, this feels like preying on vulnerable people.

product.title: The free version is capped at 10-minute sessions
product.minus: Free used to work fine, but an update cut playback to 10 minutes, forcing you to manually restart the timer — which breaks sleep and flow and makes the free tier pointless.

product.title: Too expensive for «background sound»
product.minus: The ~$120/year (and ~$20/month) price feels wildly out of proportion to what users see as background sound; many say they find the same on YouTube or Spotify for free, and students or low-income users simply can't afford it.

product.title: Cancelling and refunds are nearly impossible
product.minus: After being charged, users can't find where to cancel, Google Play doesn't show the subscription, and no refund is given; some keep getting billed even after cancelling, and again a year later without using it.

product.title: Relentless upsell — even for paying users
product.minus: The app constantly pushes purchases: discount pop-ups, a «shake the tree for a coupon» gimmick, self-ads on launch. It annoys even paying users who see «50% off lifetime» banners every single time they open it.

product.title: The ad sound doesn't match what's in the app
product.minus: Many came for a specific ad track that isn't in the app, or the sound turns out completely different — harsh, crackly, «pings and chimes». Some say the tones physically hurt their ears and even amplify tinnitus.

product.title: Confusing UI: you can't tell what's playing
product.minus: The UI is overloaded with animations and layers: you tap and can't tell what's actually active or which section it's from. Slow audio transitions and unlabeled buttons especially hurt the ADHD audience it targets.

product.title: Genuinely helps with focus and ADHD
product.plus: For a large share of users the core just works: the adaptive soundscapes noticeably quiet «brain chatter», cut intrusive thoughts and drop them into flow — ADHD users especially praise it, describing the effect as close to magic.

product.title: Puts you to sleep fast — and for real
product.plus: As a sleep aid it works almost instantly for many: people drop off in 5-10 minutes instead of their usual 20, wake less at night, and describe sleeping «like a baby».

product.title: Crashes, battery drain and broken integrations
product.minus: Loyal users complain about stability: the app crashes in the background, won't resume after a call, drains battery and data abnormally, and the reworked Google Fit / Health Connect integration loops on permission requests and breaks the smart alarm.

product.title: The music genuinely gets you into focus within minutes
product.plus: The most common praise: a track pulls you into "flow" in 5–7 minutes, people lose track of time and get the task done — especially for work, study, and coding.

product.title: An essential tool for people with ADHD
product.plus: Users with ADHD describe it as a lifesaver: the ADHD mode and background stimulation help them start a task, stay on track, and even calm down when anxious.

product.title: Playback randomly stops in the middle of a session
product.minus: The biggest single complaint: the music just stops after 10–60 minutes (or mid-sleep at night), breaking the very focus it was turned on for; sometimes the track repeats or switches on its own.

product.title: You can't even try it without a card — instant paywall
product.minus: Right after install the app demands an account and card details with no free version and no sample to listen to; many uninstall before they can tell whether it even works.

product.title: The price feels absurd next to Spotify and YouTube
product.minus: $70–100 a year for music users feel they could find free on YouTube or Spotify reads as overpriced — especially to students and teens for whom the subscription is out of reach.

product.title: Subscription auto-charges after trial; cancelling is a nightmare
product.minus: Money gets taken after the "free" trial even when cancelled or barely used; support goes silent and cancellation is made nearly impossible — users call it a "scam" and "predatory."

product.title: The music is too repetitive and grates over time
product.minus: Over an hour the same looping tracks get boring, and the "wobbles" and high-pitched tones leave some users anxious, with a headache, or feeling it's artificial noise rather than music.

product.title: Frequent crashes and false "you're offline" errors on working wifi
product.minus: The app crashes, freezes, and stubbornly shows "offline" on a perfectly good connection; for long-time subscribers who slept to it for years, it turned a working tool into a broken one.

product.title: Responsive support and caring devs — for some users
product.plus: Some users praise fast, human support: the developer reaches out personally, replies early Monday morning, and resolves issues — which builds trust in the product.

product.title: Genuinely helps people fall asleep and sleep better
product.plus: The sleep category works for many: people fall asleep faster and sleep more soundly, some using it daily for years and reporting their best sleep in ages.

product.title: Skeptics feel none of the promised effect
product.minus: A share of users feel none of the advertised effect on focus or relaxation, dismiss the "neuroscience" as pseudoscience or marketing, and prefer their own playlist, lofi, or classical music.

product.title: Missing playlists, casting, and volume control
product.minus: Users can't build a queue or playlists of the tracks that work for them, there's no casting to speakers/TV for sleep, and the base volume is sometimes too loud even at minimum.

product.title: Charging a subscription for looped white noise feels absurd to users
product.minus: People fundamentally don't get why a «basic mathematical function» — white noise — should cost a monthly or yearly fee. Many would happily pay once, but the subscription reads as greed and a reason to switch to YouTube or a box fan.

product.title: The sound silently shuts off mid-night and wakes you up
product.minus: The core functional failure: a sleep app that closes itself or cuts the audio in the middle of the night, sometimes after just 20 minutes, jolting people awake. It does the exact opposite of its one job.

product.title: Almost everything is locked behind a paywall, even a ceiling fan
product.minus: Users complain that 95% of sounds are premium — even the simplest ones like a ceiling fan are locked, the ~10 free ones are buried at the bottom of a 200-sound list, and without a sub you get just one mix of two sounds. A favorite sound can suddenly turn premium after an update.

product.title: Hidden pricing and surprise charges after a «free» trial
product.minus: Advertised as free, but people get hit with $40 a year after a forgotten trial — and the subscription doesn't even appear in their list until after the charge. Card is required before the «free» trial starts, and some are billed after cancelling, which reads as a scam.

product.title: Loud full-screen ads wake you up and won't close
product.minus: Ads in a sleep app are their own nightmare: restarting the cut-out sound at night forces an ad; ads now have sound and blast about mahjong or divorce, waking everyone; full-screen banners can't be closed without killing the app.

product.title: Auto-starts whenever Bluetooth connects, especially in the car
product.minus: After an update the app auto-plays the last sound the moment the phone pairs with any Bluetooth — earbuds or car — even with autoplay off and not running in the background. On every drive it just starts up by itself, which is maddening.

product.title: Constant crashes make a sleep app unusable
product.minus: Beyond silent shut-offs, the app outright crashes every night, often predictably — at 4:30am, at 4am, right after you've fallen asleep. Buying premium doesn't fix the crashing, which frustrates people the most.

product.title: Heats the phone and drains the battery overnight
product.minus: The app oddly taxes the phone: it drains the battery even while charging and overheats the device enough that wireless charging pauses itself. Other noise apps don't do this.

product.title: Sounds loop in short clips with audible skips and artefacts
product.minus: Some users hear the seams: sounds are cut into short loops and the jarring skip at the join keeps them awake. The free sounds get called loud, repetitive and poorly compressed, and the brown noise gets called static that isn't real brown noise.

product.title: A survey and sign-up before you're allowed to listen
product.minus: Before the first sound it forces a 20-question survey, asks your age and an account, then drops a payment screen right after. People come for a simple set of sounds and instead hit a wall of personal-data collection, then delete it.

product.title: It genuinely puts people to sleep — irreplaceable for years
product.plus: The core strength: people fall asleep in 5–10 minutes for years and can't sleep without it. It helps with insomnia, tinnitus, misophonia and anxiety, saves them while travelling, in hospital and on shift work, and calms babies. Many call it the best they've tried.

product.title: A huge sound library with custom mixes
product.plus: Those who stay praise the sheer choice: hundreds of sounds you can layer and volume-balance individually into your own soundscape. They rate the audio quality and authenticity above rivals, and prize rare ones like the aquarium or airplane cabin.

product.title: The free version is plenty for many users
product.plus: Against the paywall complaints, a large group insists the free sounds are enough: fan, airplane cabin and rain play all night in the background with the screen off, ads are rare or silent, and it works offline. They call the free version better than rivals' paid tiers.

product.title: Easy to use, plays all night, with a timer
product.plus: For the happy users it just works: easy to operate, holds the sound all night without crashing, keeps playing with the screen off and in the background, and the timer shuts it off at a set time. Many keep it for years with no issues at all.

product.title: The Avrora rebrand erased lifetime purchases
product.minus: Users who bought lifetime back in the Sleep Booster days were left with two sounds and two meditations after the Avrora switch — or the app asks them to pay again for access they already own forever.

product.title: The ritual won't auto-advance from story to sounds
product.minus: Breathing into story into sounds used to play through on its own; now the app freezes between steps, so you have to wake the screen and tap play again — staying awake at the exact moment you'd finally drifted off.

product.title: Playback dies the moment the screen locks
product.minus: After an update the app stopped playing in the background: lock the phone and the sound cuts out, and support's reply is to ask for a screenshot of music not playing while the screen is off.

product.title: The timer is ignored and sound runs all night
product.minus: A 15-30 minute timer gets ignored: users wake in the middle of the night to rain or white noise still playing, hours after it was supposed to shut off.

product.title: The breathing-story-sounds ritual knocks you out in minutes
product.plus: The chain of guided breathing, a calm story and ambient sound has rescued people with real insomnia, anxiety and PTSD for years: many fall asleep before the story ends and use it to replace sleeping pills.

product.title: A hard paywall: not a second to try before you pay
product.minus: After an update an app that was free for years locked the sleep ritual behind a subscription, and newcomers get one recording before being forced to enter a card — there's no way to judge it before buying.

product.title: The free trial bills you and traps the subscription
product.minus: The three-day trial charges immediately — often for six months upfront — and there's no cancel button in the app: people cancel before the trial ends and get billed anyway, then go in circles with unresponsive support.

product.title: The alarm fires on its own and won't turn off
product.minus: The alarm goes off even with the timer disabled, in do-not-disturb mode, and when the app wasn't even used — and there's no on-screen way to silence it, leaving only a phone restart or uninstall.

product.title: Snore and sleep-talk recording is what people stay for
product.plus: The overnight sound recording catches snoring, mumbling and sleep-talking — a source of morning laughs for some, and for others a real tip-off that they had sleep apnea.

product.title: Recording cuts the night short and can't tell a snore from a fan
product.minus: Recording either stops after an hour or two, saves nothing at all, or indiscriminately captures a fan, planes and passing cars — dozens of useless clips instead of the actual snoring.

product.title: No new content since 2021 — the stories are memorized
product.minus: Even loyal paying users complain that there have been no new stories, meditations or sounds for years, their favorites are memorized word-for-word and no longer work — and some loops are too short or audibly repeat.

product.title: A new device wipes everything you paid for
product.minus: On a new phone the premium account is recognized but the library of sounds, meditations and stories doesn't restore — you're left with the basic couple of options, while Facebook login and old emails fail to let you back in.

product.title: Post-update crashes on launch
product.minus: After an update the app many people relied on starts crashing the moment it opens: reinstalling, rebooting and a clean start don't help — until a later patch finally fixes it.

product.title: When support engages, the issues actually get fixed
product.plus: A share of users who reach a real person report quick replies and genuine fixes — restored access, recordings working again, bugs cleared — a notable exception amid the flood of complaints.

product.title: Sounds that were free for years vanished behind a paywall overnight
product.minus: The app's defining wound: people listened to their mixes free for years, even a decade, then an update locked nearly the whole catalogue. Only 3–9 sounds stay free; the other 95–99% need a yearly subscription.

product.title: Long-time users get locked out of their own saved mixes
product.minus: It stings hardest for those who built the perfect sleep mix: after the update their favourite combos (rain, thunderstorm, thunder) are locked, leaving them with one irritating sound instead of the routine they relied on.

product.title: The free trial turns into an instant year-long charge
product.minus: Users say the "7-day free" ends almost instantly and the card gets hit for a full year ($40–70) with no chance to cancel in time — and support refuses to refund the first charge.

product.title: Cancellation is trapped in a loop: a discount instead of an unsubscribe button
product.minus: Trying to cancel runs into a loop: it asks your reason, dangles a "discount", and any tap sends you back to the start. Cancelling in-app is physically impossible, and the website demands a password you never made if you signed up with Google.

product.title: Paid "lifetime" access was wiped after the rebrand
product.minus: People who once paid to fully unlock the old Relax Melodies / Relax Meditation found the app renamed BetterSleep, their lifetime purchase voided, and a subscription demanded all over again.

product.title: Audio cuts out mid-night and wakes you — even for paying users
product.minus: The core technical failure for a sleep app: playback dies after an hour or two, or after a few minutes, despite an 8-hour timer. It happens on different phones and to people who already paid for a year.

product.title: Turn on sleep tracking and the voice and music start crackling
product.minus: A consistent bug: the moment sleep recording starts, the meditation and story audio distorts with static and crackle "like under a plastic bag". Turn recording off and it's clean again — so you must choose between tracking and decent sound.

product.title: The "Routine" button keeps disappearing and reappearing without warning
product.minus: A favourite feature for regulars — the routine (a meditation followed by an all-night mix) — keeps vanishing or getting swapped for "Programs", and the layout is reshuffled so often that people can't even tell how to start tracking.

product.title: The sound mixer is what people still love it for
product.plus: A huge library and the ability to layer any sounds into your own custom soundscape is the main reason people come back for years and bring their friends and family aboard.

product.title: The bedtime stories and the narrator's voice genuinely put you to sleep
product.plus: Sleep tales, meditations and especially narrator Aster's voice are praised for quieting racing thoughts; for many this is the part they pay for and stay for.

product.title: People fall asleep in minutes — especially with tinnitus and misophonia
product.plus: For those it works on, the effect feels almost medical: asleep in 2–5 minutes, with a tuned sound that "cuts through" the ringing of tinnitus or masks triggers for misophonia and PTSD.

product.title: You pay — but new content has nearly dried up
product.minus: Loyal subscribers complain that story and sound updates, once weekly, are now rare: the same sleep tales and three "new" tracks recycled for months, leaving people debating whether to renew.

product.title: The one core job — actually ringing — fails after updates
product.minus: The most frequent and most damaging complaint: alarms simply don't ring in the morning, even with every permission granted. People showed up late to work, nearly got fired — for an app that exists to do exactly one thing, that's fatal.

product.title: Missions actually drag even the heaviest sleepers out of bed
product.plus: The core reason people love it: to kill the alarm you must solve a puzzle, scan an object, or take steps — snoozing isn't an option. For people who sleep "like a rock", it's the only thing that works.

product.title: Intrusive ads ambush you the second you wake up
product.minus: Ads pop up at the exact moment you're groggily trying to dismiss the alarm: people tap banners instead of snooze, get thrown into AliExpress and Shopee, and can't get back on the first try.

product.title: Used to love it, then an update broke everything — long-time fans walking away
product.minus: A recurring refrain: "used it for years, it was perfect, now it's a bloated machine of ads and subscriptions". People who recommended it to everyone are deleting it after years of loyalty.

product.title: The paywall pops up while dismissing the alarm — charging half-asleep users
product.minus: The ugliest grievance: the purchase prompt appears right as a half-asleep person tries to silence the alarm, and people end up buying a yearly plan without realizing it. Some threaten legal action.

product.title: Loud enough to break any sleep — but it wakes the whole house too
product.minus: The app's strength becomes a liability: it's so loud it wakes the entire family, neighbors and roommates. Especially when a mission won't let you silence it fast — household conflict is guaranteed.

product.title: Paywalling a second alarm feels like a shakedown
product.minus: What stings isn't paying per se, but that basic things — multiple alarms, ad removal — sit behind a subscription. "A subscription for an alarm clock?" reads as absurd to many, especially since it used to be free.

product.title: Works where the built-in Google and Samsung alarms gave up
product.plus: A strong retention hook: people come because their phone's stock alarm stopped ringing. For them Alarmy is the rescue — the one that actually goes off.

product.title: Powering off the phone is a loophole that kills the alarm
product.minus: Even devoted fans find the gap: half-asleep you can long-press power and shut the phone off, bypassing the mission. And those with a power-off password can't silence it at all without a full shutdown.

product.title: Heavy client: lag, gigabytes of storage, and other apps breaking
product.minus: The bloat isn't just cosmetic: the app lags the phone, eats over a gigabyte thanks to ads, and users say it stops other apps from opening. Some even thought their phone had been hacked.

product.title: A student favorite: early wake-ups for study, exams and prayer
product.plus: A clear picture of the core audience: schoolkids, JEE/NEET aspirants and students use it to rise at 4-5am for study or Fajr prayer. To them it's a discipline tool, not just an alarm.

product.title: No way to use your own music — not from the gallery, not Spotify/YouTube
product.minus: A common "almost five stars" snag: people want to wake to a favorite track from Spotify, YouTube Music or their own gallery, but the app won't allow it — they're stuck with the built-in sounds.

product.title: Already paid for everything in TaoMix 1 — now pay again
product.minus: The deepest grievance: people bought the full version of the original TaoMix (often "one payment for all sounds"), the developer pulled it from the store, then shipped TaoMix 2 where the same sounds cost money again. It reads not as a bug but as a deliberate betrayal of loyal users.

product.title: The paywall swallowed nearly all the sounds
product.minus: Only ~8-10 basic sounds stay free; everything else is split into paid packs. Many are annoyed that the listing never mentions this, and that the once-generous audio mixer turned stingy.

product.title: The unique "moving" sound mix is the killer feature
product.plus: The heart of the app is the rotating circle of dots where sounds shift their own volume and position, so the soundscape never gets monotonous. This dynamic, customizable approach is praised as unique on the market.

product.title: Build your own sound mix for any mood
product.plus: The top reason people love it — full customization: build your own set of sounds, set the volume, speed and frequency of each, and save profiles for sleep, study, meditation or focus.

product.title: An indispensable bedtime ritual for years
product.plus: The most devoted users listen every single night for years (some since TaoMix 1 in 2015) and say they can no longer fall asleep without it — especially with tinnitus, anxiety or jet lag.

product.title: Sound cuts out on its own in the middle of the night
product.minus: A sleep-killing bug: the app stops playback on its own after a few hours or pauses at night, even with a timer set or "infinite" mode on. For people who fall asleep to the sound, this wakes them up and defeats the purpose.

product.title: Starts up at random and wakes you
product.minus: An unnerving habit: the app launches itself in the background at random, plays over music in other apps, or wakes you at night. Users keep an "empty" soundscape loaded just so it won't suddenly start.

product.title: No account — switch phones and lose everything
product.minus: No account login or sync: switching phones or reinstalling loses your saved soundscapes and purchases, forcing you to pay again. You used to be able to send a mix to another device — now even that's gone.

product.title: Purchases fail, support goes silent
product.minus: A double blow: in-app sound purchases fail ("transaction declined" across multiple cards), while emails to support go unanswered or bounce as undeliverable. Against rumors of a change of ownership, it cements a feeling of abandonment.

product.title: No way to preview a sound before adding it
product.minus: Browsing sounds is painful: there's no preview, so each one must be added to the soundscape one at a time with a ton of clicks. On top of that, sounds are filed under "scenes" (wind hides in "sleeping in a tent") rather than by type, making them unintuitive to find.

product.title: No separate volume control or clear navigation
product.minus: Compared to the first version the interface lost ground: no home page, no separate in-app volume control, no settings, no exit button. People want the sounds as a backdrop to a podcast, but volume is tied to the system slider.

product.title: Sound quality and natural samples
product.plus: Even those unhappy with the paywall admit the sounds themselves are excellent and realistic, blend together beautifully, and usually loop without obvious seams. For many it's simply the best sound library among apps of its kind.

product.title: Short loops with clicks, too few sounds per pack
product.minus: The audio is praised, but the details draw complaints: loops are short and get repetitive fast, there's an audible click at the seam, and the paid banks feel thin (only one whale sound, for instance). Many simply ask for more sounds and variety.

product.title: Drains battery and crashes while running in background
product.minus: The app noticeably drains the battery by running in the background and crashes now and then — especially while building soundscapes and on newer Android versions where sound drops out with the screen off. Users end up keeping the phone on the charger all night.

product.title: Helps you sleep, focus and block out noise
product.plus: The concrete payoff that keeps people around: falling asleep in minutes, focus during work and study, and masking unwanted noise at the office or home. It calms anxiety, tinnitus and stress — people use it literally every day.

product.title: Users ask for custom-sound import and Chromecast
product.minus: The top requests from loyal users: the ability to import your own audio files (not just record through the weak mic, which yields quiet, short clips) and Chromecast/Google Cast support to send sound to a speaker.

product.title: Playback dies in the middle of the night and the sudden silence wakes you
product.minus: The defining pain: playback suddenly stops at night — the app still claims it's playing, but no sound comes out, and that silence is exactly what jolts people awake. Unrestricted battery mode, timer, and bedtime mode all fail to fix it. Often you have to Force Stop it just to get sound back.

product.title: Ads turned predatory: they fire on every tap and wake you up at night
product.minus: An app people loved for years got suddenly buried in ads: change a sound — ad, open a setting — ad, reopen it — ad. Full-screen unskippable spots appeared, sometimes minutes long, firing at night at full volume and waking people. Some users leave over this alone.

product.title: A huge sound library and mixing are the main reasons people love it
product.plus: What keeps people loyal: a massive selection of nature sounds and white/brown/pink noise, plus the ability to layer them and tune each one's volume into a perfect personal mix. Users call themselves "DJs for weather sounds" and stick around for years.

product.title: It genuinely helps people fall and stay asleep — it does its job
product.plus: The core outcome people install it for: those with insomnia, tinnitus, and anxiety fall asleep in 15 minutes and stay asleep through the night. The sounds mask noisy neighbors, crying kids, plane noise, and ringing ears. Many use it every single night.

product.title: Audible loop seam: the sound jumps or dips in volume every 20-30 seconds
product.minus: On some tracks the loop seam is audible: every 15-30 seconds there's a sharp skip, a pause, or a volume drop of nearly half. For continuous white noise this is especially jarring — the seam wakes people and breaks immersion. Users ask for seamless looping or smooth crossfades.

product.title: Drains the battery and heats the phone more than music streaming
product.minus: For an app that's "just playing an MP3", the battery drain is abnormal: the phone dies in a couple of hours or wakes up half-charged even on the charger. Users directly compare it — YouTube and music streaming use less. The phone also gets noticeably hot.

product.title: Crashes in the middle of the night — wakes you instead of soothing you
product.minus: Recurring crashes specifically at night: every night for a week straight, across different phones, even after recent updates. The effect is the opposite of the goal — the crash and silence wake you, and you can't fall back asleep.

product.title: Predatory tactics: ads under the Play button, fake-update buttons and trackers
product.minus: Some users see not just ads but deliberate deception: a banner placed exactly where the play/pause button is so you mis-tap; an X close-button that's part of the ad; a fake "update" button leading to who-knows-what install. Plus complaints of thousands of tracking attempts per day.

product.title: Simple, clean interface that remembers your choices
product.plus: People praise how little there is to figure out: a clean, easy interface, everything a couple of taps away, and it remembers your favorite sounds. You build your mix once and then just lie back and drift off.

product.title: Usable free with no account — a one-off ad instead of a subscription
product.plus: Many are won over by a model that's fair for a free app: everything you need is available for free, no account required, and you can watch one ad to unlock a specific sound rather than pay monthly. Set a timer and no ad interrupts you mid-sleep.

product.title: Sound quality degraded after an update
product.minus: Long-time users complain that after an update their favorite sounds got worse: rain now sounds "like it's hitting a trash bag", the plane turned into "rushing water", and the white noise became too loud and harsh even on the lowest setting. What soothed them for years now grates.

product.title: Shuts itself off mid-night and wakes you up — the exact thing it's meant to prevent
product.minus: The dominant pain: the sound just stops after a few hours (sometimes minutes), even with no timer set, and the sudden silence wakes light sleepers who then have to grab their phone and restart it mid-night. For insomniacs it's brutal.

product.title: Sounds exactly like a real fan — a lifesaver for those who can't fall asleep without one
product.plus: The loyalty core: people used to sleeping with a fan say the sound is indistinguishable from the real thing and replaces a box fan or sound machine. Perfect for when you forgot your own at home.

product.title: Indispensable when traveling or during power outages — when your own fan isn't there
product.plus: A crisp value scenario: hotels, someone else's house, camping, power outages, a broken fan. Your phone is always with you, your fan isn't, and the app fills exactly that gap.

product.title: Shady ads: pop-ups, fake virus warnings, and installing other apps without consent
product.minus: A segment describes aggressive, scary ads: a fake "Google Play" warning of viruses with no close button, demands to install or update other apps before it'll run, and apps installed without consent. It reads as spyware.

product.title: Buying Pro doesn't fix the core problem — and often gets lost when you switch phones
product.minus: Those who paid feel cheated: the paid version still shuts off at night, doesn't fully remove ads, and on a new phone the purchase shows as "already paid for" but won't download or restore.

product.title: Simplicity is the whole point: one screen, pick a fan, volume, timer — done
product.plus: People value that it's a "basic" app with nothing extra: a few fans, a volume slider, a timer, clear settings. The very absence of bloat is what keeps them for years.

product.title: Plays in the background with the screen off and without draining the battery — you can use the phone meanwhile
product.plus: A meaningful technical praise: the sound keeps going with the screen off and when you switch to other apps, doesn't drain the battery overnight, and works with no Wi-Fi or signal. You can play "before-bed games" while the noise runs in the background.

product.title: Embedded background noise — beeping, clicks, static — baked into the tracks ruins falling asleep
product.minus: Sound-sensitive users hear artifacts in the loops: background beeping, clicking, static. For an app sold as smooth white noise it's counterproductive — those very sounds are what keep them awake.

product.title: Masks tinnitus and racing thoughts — for many it's a medical relief, not just a comfort
product.plus: A distinct segment: people with tinnitus and racing thoughts use the noise to drown out the ringing and "chop up" pre-sleep thoughts. For them it's not a convenience but the thing that lets them sleep at all.

product.title: Doesn't just stop — it switches to another sound: a quieter fan, or a blasting podcast or ringtone
product.minus: A separate nightmare scenario: instead of silence the app turns on a ringtone, music or podcast at full blast, sometimes overriding silent mode. Being jolted awake by noise mid-night is worse than the silence.

product.title: Forced notifications and trackers you can't disable — and that get in the way of uninstalling
product.minus: A privacy red flag: the app demands notification access, won't let you turn it off, won't work without tracking permission, and users say that once granted it resists being uninstalled. It alarms people and reads as malicious behavior.

product.title: It used to work for years — the post-ads degradation is driving away long-time fans
product.minus: The most bitter pattern: people who loved it for 5-10 years and recommended it to everyone say that once ads arrived the audio went "off", crashes and dropouts began, and they're reluctantly moving to competitors.

product.title: After an update the app stops opening, and only a reinstall fixes it — wiping all progress
product.minus: The single most common pain: the app freezes on the loading screen and the only way to revive it is to uninstall and reinstall. Every time that wipes saved progress, sometimes recurring week after week. Users say the bug has gone unfixed for years.

product.title: Short 7-minute workouts make exercise actually happen even on a crazy schedule
product.plus: The core reason for the love: 4–10 minute sessions you can squeeze into a lunch break or any window of the day. People stay for years precisely because "only 7 minutes" removes the barrier and turns exercise into a habit.

product.title: Categories and tabs open empty — you have to hunt for a workout by hand in the "all" list
product.minus: Sections like Arms or Back come up empty, workouts won't load, grey screens appear. Search and favorites vanish, and the only way to find anything is to scroll the "all" tab. It turns a simple task into a tiresome fishing trip.

product.title: What was treated as free now hits a premium wall by day two
product.minus: Only day one is available, then every step demands a subscription. People arrive after googling "free" and feel cheated. Longtime users are angry that an app they used for free for years is now paywalled.

product.title: A huge library for every level and time slot — from 4 minutes to an hour
product.plus: Variety is the second pillar of the love: hundreds of workouts for beginners through advanced — yoga, HIIT, stretching — ranging from 4–5 minutes to an hour. Users value that they can match it to their mood, level and free time.

product.title: There is no support: emails and tickets go unanswered for months
product.minus: Reaching the developers is nearly impossible: people write 3–4 times over months and get silence. It hurts most around subscription and billing problems. The "contact us" links often don't even work.

product.title: Exercise instruction videos are broken: error 152-15 instead of a demo
product.minus: The tutorial clips are YouTube links that return error 152-15 or are simply unavailable. Without them it's unclear how to do a movement correctly, and even the paid version doesn't help. People relied on these videos to learn proper form.

product.title: Charges during the trial and after cancellation — money gone, no refund
product.minus: The free trial charges immediately, cancellation requests are ignored and the card is billed anyway, and there's no way to get a refund. The subscription price also climbs as users grow attached and afraid of losing access.

product.title: An update broke the voice guidance and forced full-screen ads
product.minus: After an update the voice stopped naming the next exercise, counting down and signalling the halfway point — forcing you to stare at the screen. On top of that, pop-up ads take over the whole screen with no way to close them, so you can't even start a session.

product.title: The onboarding survey fixates on weight loss — triggering those who came for health
product.minus: A reinstall is met by a long survey about how much weight you want to lose, asking whether you "want to be attractive" next to an obviously AI-generated image. Even picking the "strength" goal, users get a weight-loss focus. For anyone with a past eating disorder it's an outright trigger.

product.title: Real results: people lose weight and see their bodies change over years
product.plus: This isn't just "I like it" — users report concrete results: 45 lbs lost, 7 lbs in a week, muscle built and pandemic weight kept off for years. For many it replaced a trainer and a gym.

product.title: The Android version lags behind Apple: fewer programs and no account to save data
product.minus: On Android there are fewer programs than on iPhone and no proper account — a reinstall means starting over. Friends on different phones can't follow the same plan, and a yearly subscription won't transfer to a new device. Users feel shortchanged.

product.title: An update blocked playing your own music during a workout
product.minus: After an overnight update the app stopped letting your own Spotify or other background music play on the same device. For those who train to their own playlist it removed a key part of the experience. The developers later fixed it — and users explicitly thanked them.

product.title: 7 minutes is a low enough bar to actually defeat the «no time» excuse
product.plus: The number one reason people stick: 7 minutes a day is a «no excuses» commitment you can squeeze into any day, a work break, or life as a busy parent of five. That tiny commitment compounds into a real, consistent habit.

product.title: The free tier is exactly one workout forever; everything else is behind the paywall
product.minus: The most frequent pain point: after the first week only the single full-body workout stays free, so you grind the same exercises for months. Users feel baited and then asked for $80/year, and many leave for free alternatives like YouTube or Fiton.

product.title: Gamification — leagues, badges and unlockable «character» coaches — genuinely keeps people coming back
product.plus: The app feels like a game: events, rankings, challenges, three «lives». Unlocking different coaches (a mobster, a pirate, a yogi, an angry mom) turns the routine into something fun and is a standout motivator to keep going.

product.title: Audio cues plus animated exercise demos make workouts easy for a total beginner to follow
product.plus: A voice coach names each exercise, counts the time, announces rests and side changes, while the animation demonstrates the move along with you. There are many assistant «voices» to pick from, which especially helps people who have never worked out.

product.title: Android is a second-class citizen: the exercise modifications iOS has are missing
product.minus: A recurring complaint specific to Android users: iOS lets you modify exercises (e.g. exclude ones for an injury), but on Android you're stuck blindly skipping or hunting for workarounds. Several explicitly envy their iPhone-using partners.

product.title: Crashes, freezes and failed exercise downloads — especially on Pixel Watch
product.minus: Technically the app often fails: it crashes mid-workout, can't download exercises despite reinstalls and a VPN, and closes within seconds on Pixel Watch 2. For paying users this reads as «waste of money».

product.title: The watch is near-useless standalone: vibration dies when the screen turns off
product.minus: The wearable integration is half-baked: when the screen goes off the vibration stops, so you can't tell when to switch exercises or rest. You also can't add workouts to the watch without the phone — it keeps pushing you back to the phone.

product.title: Intensity doesn't adapt to beginners, injuries or chronic conditions
product.minus: The app throws beginners into workouts that are too hard, changing the difficulty doesn't change the exercises, and people with injuries or heart conditions have no way to exclude what's unsafe. Rests feel too short for some, and there's no cool-down phase.

product.title: Effective full-body workouts with no equipment — a real gym substitute
product.plus: Despite the short format the workouts genuinely deliver: people sweat, feel their muscles and see results within the first week. No equipment or gym needed — you can train anywhere, anytime, making it «the best alternative» when you can't get to the gym.

product.title: No sync with Health Connect / Google Fit / Garmin — a dealbreaker for some
product.minus: The lack of health-platform integration comes up as a reason to cancel: people want their workouts to flow into their main health app and Garmin data used to tailor load. Without it, the ecosystem doesn't come together for them.

product.title: The social side — leagues, friends, live sessions — creates a sense of community
product.plus: Shared events, rankings and the ability to work out «with others» give an unexpectedly strong sense of community and extra motivation. For a chunk of users this is what sets Seven apart from other fitness apps.

product.title: Progress and stats are fragile: miss a day and it resets, reinstall and you lose everything
product.minus: Progress tracking punishes breaks and glitches: skipping a day resets your progress, a couple weeks of inactivity locks you out, and a reinstall wipes your points and stats. One user suddenly lost a decade of achievement history.

product.title: Full-screen ads block you from even starting a workout
product.minus: Ads sit between every exercise and the «X» often doesn't dismiss them — after the latest update the app freezes on an ad and won't let you start at all.

product.title: A paywall and subscription where it used to be free
product.minus: Some users hit a $60-a-year subscription with no one-time-purchase option; one was charged for the whole year right after a «7-day free trial».

product.title: A free core that lasts for years is the loyalty driver
product.plus: Many stress that the main six-level programs are completely free, and they've stuck with the app for 5–10+ years precisely because of it.

product.title: Gradual difficulty ramp keeps people in the routine
product.plus: Six levels with a smooth intensity ramp and built-in rest days help both beginners and people who quit monotonous routines stay consistent for months.

product.title: Visible weight-loss results are the main motivator
product.plus: Users report real weight loss — from a few kilos to 45 kg and 100 lbs — and tie it directly to staying disciplined with the program.

product.title: Short 5-minute workouts fit easily into the day
product.plus: Sessions are short enough to squeeze into a busy day yet still leave you feeling thoroughly worked.

product.title: No gym, no equipment — workouts at home
product.plus: The bodyweight exercises can be done anywhere with no equipment, replacing the gym for people who won't go.

product.title: Animation and visual guides teach correct form
product.plus: Clear animations, videos and breathing cues show how to do each exercise correctly — beginners who don't know where to start especially value this.

product.title: Broken Google Fit sync over «sensitive data» access
product.minus: After OAuth, Google and Samsung Health block the app for requesting sensitive-data access, so fitness-tracking integration simply doesn't work.

product.title: Progress is lost when you switch phones
product.minus: There's no proper account sync: moving to a new phone doesn't carry your progress over, forcing you to start from scratch.

product.title: Too few hard levels — you hit a ceiling
product.minus: Experienced users run out of upper levels: the advanced exercises feel too easy and end too soon, leaving no room to progress.

product.title: No split-screen support on tablets
product.minus: Tablet users have asked for years to bring back split-screen and hover-window modes, but even the 2025 updates still lack them.

product.title: Used to be a one-time purchase, now the same thing wants a subscription
product.minus: Long-time users who once bought the full version for $5-6 found content locked behind a subscription after the update, and their old purchase no longer recognized.

product.title: Forced to log in and hand over personal data just to do a workout
product.minus: The top grievance of veterans: the app used to just work, but now demands account sign-up, personal details, and suspicious permissions — for many a reason to uninstall.

product.title: Simple workouts that genuinely deliver, year after year
product.plus: The loyalty core: people return after 5-15 years, see real results, drop tens of kilos, and call it the best home-workout app they've found.

product.title: Animated demos with voice cues make moves easy to follow
product.plus: Exercises are shown by trainers/animation, instructions are read aloud, and a chime marks the timer — no need to stare at the screen, ideal for beginners.

product.title: Short workouts that fit a busy life — and free
product.plus: 5-20 minute sessions with a choice of body area (abs, butt, cardio) and level — low barrier, free, and zero 'no time' excuses.

product.title: Ads and 'upgrade to paid' popups clutter the experience
product.minus: After the update ads turned intrusive, popping up on first launch and piling on with nags to buy premium — driving some users straight to YouTube.

product.title: Dated, sometimes confusing interface
product.minus: Even fans admit the UI looks a decade behind: confusing menus, no refresh, and many see it as the one real flaw of an otherwise solid product.

product.title: HealthConnect and TV pairing break the way in
product.minus: Setup stalls on a demand to connect a mysterious HealthConnect and on failed Android TV / Chromecast pairing via QR code — people simply can't get started.

product.title: The purchase has to be re-bought on every new device
product.minus: The paid version doesn't carry across devices or platforms: swapping a tablet or moving from iOS to Android forces a re-purchase, and support doesn't help.

product.title: Crashes and freezes since the recent update
product.minus: Since the update the app stopped opening at all for some, crashes or stutters mid-exercise, and emails to support go unanswered.

product.title: One-size-fits-all plan — risky for beginners and seniors
product.minus: No adaptation for age or limitations: the same workout for 23 and 73, a demo with knees hyper-extended past the toes, and no exercise modifications feel off-putting and at times unsafe.

product.title: Asking for more exercises, music, rest, and calorie data
product.minus: Fans rating 4-5 stars want it to grow: more variety and zones (chest/back), music or a voice, a rest pause between exercises, and accurate calorie counts.

product.title: Switch away mid-workout and the app restarts, wiping your progress
product.minus: Switch to your music, answer a text or let the screen go dark, and the app closes and restarts the workout from scratch, losing your logged sets and active minutes.

product.title: Android is the neglected build: the same bugs never hit iPhone, and the team 'doesn't test on Android'
product.minus: For the same price Android users get a years-old broken build; reviewers flatly say nobody on the dev team seems to own an Android, because none of this happens on iPhone.

product.title: 'You're not subscribed' — even though you paid, and the content locks you out
product.minus: The app keeps throwing up the paywall mid-workout and refuses access to programs the user has already paid a month or a year for.

product.title: Crashes on open and mid-workout, especially right after the latest update
product.minus: A very common complaint: the app crashes on launch or several times per workout, and users say every new update makes things worse than before.

product.title: Logs you out, then the password reset claims your email has no account
product.minus: The app suddenly logs you out, then insists your email isn't tied to any account and never sends the phone code, leaving a paid subscription unreachable for days.

product.title: An update killed the timer sounds, so you must stare at your phone the whole set
product.minus: The beeps between sets and the start countdown stop working after updates, making it impossible to train without constantly looking at the screen.

product.title: The 'Done' and 'Dismiss' buttons hide behind Android's system bars and can't be tapped
product.minus: After an update the UI bleeds past the screen edges: the finish, weight-log and photo buttons sit under the top and bottom system bars and literally can't be clicked.

product.title: An update deleted the app itself — and it won't let you reinstall
product.minus: After an Android update (often tied to Android 12) the app vanishes from the phone and refuses to reinstall, cutting people off from a subscription they paid a year for.

product.title: The 'free' trial charges you early, and cancelling or getting a refund is nearly impossible
product.minus: Users get charged on day two of the promised week or after cancelling; support points to Google, Google points back to the developer, and nobody manages to get a refund.

product.title: The workouts and programs are exactly why people put up with the rest
product.plus: Whitney's programs (and the other trainers') give real structure: warm-up, cool-down and rests are laid out for you, you don't have to think what to do next, and people see real results and stick to a routine for the first time.

product.title: The exercise video clips make the gym un-scary for beginners
product.plus: Short clips of each exercise plus the difficulty levels give beginners a visual guide to form — many got over their fear of the machines and of 'looking like they don't know what they're doing' for the first time.

product.title: Weight and rep tracking is weak: the numbers don't carry over between workouts
product.minus: Logged weights and reps don't pull through to the next session, history disappears and entry is clunky, so people end up tracking progress in a separate app or notes.

product.title: No Samsung watch, no Health Connect, no TV casting — the Android ecosystem is ignored
product.minus: The app won't pair with a Samsung watch, lacks Health Connect for syncing with Oura, and gives no proper TV casting, while the iPhone side has these integrations.

product.title: Without a subscription you can do almost nothing — not even journal or save a photo
product.minus: There isn't a single free workout, and journaling, progress photos and weight tracking all need the ~$15/mo or $120/yr subscription too — which grates because Whitney's content is free on YouTube.

product.title: When support replies and the bug gets fixed, people put the five stars back
product.plus: The team does close some issues: users rewrite their rating from 1 to 5, praise fast and kind support replies (sometimes within 12 hours) and follow-up emails explaining the bugs.

product.title: Swapping curated playlists for «pick your own music» killed the app's signature feature
product.minus: Trainers used to sync tracks to the workout: «when the beat drops, you sprint». After the update the original playlists are gone, so the trainer's cues hang in the void — the music doesn't match the tempo, there's no drop, the instructions are useless. Long-time subscribers are threatening to leave in droves.

product.title: Music drowns out the trainer's voice, with no separate volume control for it
product.minus: After the update the music plays at the same volume as the trainer. There's a slider for music but none for the voice, so the cues are unintelligible even with the voice maxed out. For an app whose entire point is listening to the trainer, that's fatal.

product.title: The app glitches and crashes right in the middle of a workout
product.minus: Crashes every couple of minutes, force-closes during streaming, freezes — and it's gone unfixed for years. People stand in the gym unable to load anything, the workout cuts off, and you can't finish it.

product.title: An «you're offline» error on a live connection blocks the workout
product.minus: The app insists the user is offline even on Wi-Fi and refuses to load even downloaded workouts. It hits outdoor runs especially hard: on a shaky connection the workout just stalls.

product.title: The exercise videos don't match the spoken cues
product.minus: The exercise images and videos are out of sync with the audio: the trainer says one thing, the screen shows another, and sometimes there's no demo at all. You have to swipe through the visuals by hand mid-workout. Especially rough for visual learners and non-native English speakers.

product.title: Workouts don't get logged — streaks and stats vanish
product.minus: Completed workouts don't save: minimize the app or take a call and the session isn't counted. For anyone keeping a streak or tracking progress it stings — the work is done but the stats stay empty.

product.title: A mandatory biometrics screen hard-locks you out
product.minus: The app demands birthday, weight and height and won't move on — and the data won't save, so it keeps asking again and again. People get stuck on this screen and can't reach the workouts they already paid for.

product.title: They charge after cancellation and bill instead of giving the free trial
product.minus: The 7-day trial charges immediately rather than after a week; sometimes a monthly sign-up turns into a $99-104 annual plan. The card keeps getting billed months after cancellation, and there's no support phone on the site — hence the «scam» accusations.

product.title: The trainers are what people love and stick with for years
product.plus: The live trainers' audio guidance is the core value: they motivate, hold the pace, and explain form as if they were right beside you. It's the trainers who keep subscribers for 5-10 years, even when everything else is buggy.

product.title: Screen-free audio format — work out anywhere without staring at your phone
product.plus: The workout runs by voice in your earbuds and the phone can stay in your pocket: handy on a run, outdoors, in the gym, at home. For people sick of screens after remote work, or who don't want to watch an instructor on video, it's the decisive edge.

product.title: A huge library for every level and format — from meditation to running
product.plus: Thousands of workouts filterable by duration, level, body part and trainer: running, strength, cycling, yoga, stretching, meditation and sleep. It fits both beginners and advanced users and slots into any schedule — all cheaper than a gym membership.

product.title: No metric units and no sync with watches or trackers
product.minus: Pounds, feet and miles only — Europeans are stuck with no kg or km and no way to switch. On top of that Garmin, Fitbit, Strava and Wear OS don't really connect and heart-rate monitors aren't found — odd for an app of this caliber.

product.title: Silently stops counting unless you open it every day
product.minus: The single most common complaint: to count anything, you have to manually open the app every morning, otherwise it sits at zero all day. People lose whole days of activity just because they forgot to wake the tracker.

product.title: Accurate and easy on the battery — that's why people love it
product.plus: The app has a loyal core: people praise it for accurate counting and for barely touching the battery. For many it's the best pedometer they've used in years.

product.title: Crashes on launch and just won't open
product.minus: For a chunk of users the app crashes right on opening — especially after an update or on certain phone models. Nothing helps: restart, reinstall, clearing cache — and the day's data is lost in the process.

product.title: Suddenly zeroes out and wipes your saved history
product.minus: The app loses data: it zeroes the counter mid-day, erases weeks and months of progress, sometimes after a phone restart or update. For anyone tracking long-term it's a dealbreaker.

product.title: Counts steps while you're driving
product.minus: The algorithm reacts to any motion, not real steps: a car ride — especially a truck or a bumpy road — racks up hundreds or thousands of phantom "steps". People keep asking for a simple pause button that isn't there.

product.title: Simple and clear — does what you need, nothing extra
product.plus: The minimalism wins people over: a clean clear interface, a bar right on the home screen, no GPS or account needed. "Does exactly what I want" is a recurring note from people who tried a pile of other pedometers.

product.title: Tracks at random no matter what permissions you grant
product.minus: Even with permissions granted and battery optimization off, tracking stays unpredictable: counts some days, not others, at random. The "Help: not recording steps" button only works a fraction of the time.

product.title: Worked for years, then broke after an update or new phone
product.minus: A very common arc: the app served faithfully for a year or two, then — after an update or a move to a new phone — started glitching or stopped working entirely. Former fans leave disappointed.

product.title: Motivates you to move and keeps you on track
product.plus: For its loyal audience it's not just a counter but a motivator: it nudges them to walk more, helps with weight loss, and gives a sense of achievement at day's end. Especially valued by people with desk jobs.

product.title: Pushy ads and fake close buttons
product.minus: Ads spoil the free version: the close X sometimes opens another ad, the banner sits right next to the day icons and triggers accidental crashes. Some feel they're being tricked toward a subscription.

product.title: No way to edit steps manually, no start/stop button
product.minus: Basic control is missing: when the app skips a day you can't manually enter the right step count, and there's no pause button to exclude car rides. Users explicitly ask for both.

product.title: Time and distance come out wrong
product.minus: Beyond steps, the time and distance metrics are wrong on their own: an hour's walk becomes "13 minutes active", 5 km shows as 2.3. Without accurate time you can't tell your walking pace.

product.title: A huge program library is the core reason people love it
product.plus: Users prize the enormous selection — P90X, Insanity, T25, 21 Day Fix, yoga, cardio, strength, meditation — all in one place and for every level, from beginner to advanced.

product.title: Workouts at home or anywhere — no gym needed
product.plus: Being able to train at home, while travelling, at the gym or straight from a phone is what keeps people for years; for many it fully replaces a gym membership.

product.title: Casting to TV (Chromecast/smart TV) is constantly broken
product.minus: The most frequent technical complaint: the app refuses to cast to TV, shows a spinning dumbbell, keeps dropping Chromecast, or simply doesn't support Android casting — a deal-breaker for many at $35 a month.

product.title: Predatory billing: silent auto-renewal and refusal to refund
product.minus: Many reviews describe one scenario: the annual plan silently auto-renews with no clear notice, the card is charged, and no refund is given even days later — while access is revoked immediately.

product.title: Nightmare support: third-party chat only, no human reachable
product.minus: Support runs through a third-party chat with no phone line; instead of fixing the issue agents try to upsell, and BODi and Google bounce the blame between each other.

product.title: After updates the app won't open or hangs on loading
product.minus: Recent updates break launch: the app either won't open at all or spins endlessly on phone, tablet, Fire TV — reinstalling and clearing cache don't help, and people are paying for a service they can't use.

product.title: Random logouts and threats to delete downloaded workouts
product.minus: The app logs people out on its own, claims "another account" is logged in, and threatens to wipe offline downloads — users had downloaded workouts deleted multiple times, and getting back in is a struggle.

product.title: Videos buffer and freeze mid-workout
product.minus: Playback is unstable: videos load slowly, buffer and freeze mid-workout on any device — users lose momentum and the time they could have spent exercising.

product.title: Expensive, with opaque pricing: ad says one thing, checkout says another
product.minus: The price stings and often doesn't match the ad ($19 in the ad → $30 at checkout); in Canada and on monthly billing it's steep, and some feel free YouTube is the better alternative.

product.title: No proper tracking: workouts don't log to a calendar
product.minus: Basic tracking is broken: a completed workout doesn't appear on the calendar and shows as not done, there's no interactive program calendar or place to log weights — users resort to printing PDFs and tracking on paper.

product.title: No family profiles: everything logs to a single person
product.minus: The app supports no multiple profiles per account the way Peloton or even BODi's own bike do — couples can't track progress and program completion separately, though users call it a simple, obvious add.

product.title: Users miss the groups and "coaching" — the social layer was cut
product.minus: Long-time users lose motivation as BOD groups and coach communities are wound down: those kept them consistent, and now old coaches are even made to pay — people miss the sense of a team.

product.title: Fast, visible results within the first days and weeks
product.plus: The single biggest driver of five-star reviews: people say they notice body changes within days or drop kilos within weeks, and that keeps them motivated.

product.title: Simple, clear exercises at home with no equipment
product.plus: People value that the workouts are short, clearly instructed, and need no equipment — you can do them anywhere, even in bed.

product.title: Lands perfectly with beginners
product.plus: For people just starting out, the app eases them in: the load is doable and the moves are clear, which lowers the fear of beginning.

product.title: Real effort: sweat and burn read as a sign of progress
product.plus: People read the sweat and muscle burn as proof the workout is working, and they like it — it feels like a real session.

product.title: You can schedule the next workout and adjust the exercises
product.plus: Users like being able to pick the time of the next session, swap exercises, and tailor the plan — it gives a sense of control.

product.title: A warm-up before every session
product.plus: People specifically call out the warm-up before each day — they see it as an important, caring detail other apps skip.

product.title: Most workouts sit behind a paywall, and "free" is misleading
product.minus: Many are angry that a supposedly "free" app actually locks most workouts behind a subscription, and several users have to ask outright whether it's even free.

product.title: Surprise charges with no warning
product.minus: The harshest reviews are about money taken without notice and no refund afterward; for one person it was all they had for the month.

product.title: Ads on nearly every tap
product.minus: Some users complain ads pop up after almost every action; meanwhile others say there are few and they only appear after the workout — the experience is clearly uneven.

product.title: Aggressive push notifications insult instead of motivate
