product.minus: After updates (the August one especially) the app won't open, hangs on a black screen, or crashes on launch — streaks lost, paid content unreachable. For some it's been broken for months.

product.title: Video buffers and freezes mid-stretch
product.minus: Sessions stutter and freeze every few seconds — even on downloaded videos and on connections that handle YouTube and Netflix fine. A 15-minute stretch balloons to 30 because of the freezing.

product.title: The mobility test is iPhone-only; Android pays the same
product.minus: The headline feature from the ads — measuring your mobility for a personalized plan — isn't on Android, and nobody warns you before you pay. Android users pay the same price for a stripped-down version.

product.title: Login loop: paid, but can't get in
product.minus: After signing up and paying, the app keeps bouncing you back to the "Join now" screen saying you're already subscribed — an endless sign-in / subscribe / already-subscribed loop with no way through.

product.title: Genuinely relieves pain and restores back and joint mobility
product.plus: Long-term users repeatedly say chronic back, knee and hip pain went away and their range of motion grew markedly — some avoided surgery and have held the result for years.

product.title: Removes the decision: open it, press play, stretch
product.plus: The core value for regulars is that it removes the planning: a ready 15-30 minute session every day, streaks for accountability, and the stretching habit finally sticks.

product.title: No instructions or modifications — figure it out yourself
product.minus: The voiceover barely explains what you're stretching or why, how to get in and out of a pose, or how to modify it for an injury or limited flexibility — instead it endlessly repeats breath counts. Hard for beginners and people with bad joints.

product.title: Pricier than Netflix or Spotify — for what's free on YouTube
product.minus: $15-25 a month strikes many as absurd for a set of stretching videos: people are embarrassed to admit what they pay and point to free alternatives like YouTube and Down Dog.

product.title: Music and voice got worse after the move from ROMWOD
product.minus: Old ROMWOD fans complain the music is no longer synced to the session, doesn't dip under the voice, and doesn't stop on pause or at the end; you can't lower or mute it — and you used to be able to.

product.title: A calm voice and pace turn recovery into meditation
product.plus: Those the format clicks with value not just the stretch but the breathing and mindfulness: a calm voice, long holds and a gentle pace bring relaxation, better sleep and mental clarity after training.

product.title: Sessions too intense for beginners and the inflexible
product.minus: Despite onboarding questions about your time and level, the app drops you straight into the deep end: 4-minute holds, kneeling poses, moves for the already-flexible — and the short beginner routines were removed. Not for people recovering from injury.

product.title: Casting to TV is broken — and it matters
product.minus: Chromecast works one week and not the next, and won't cast to older models or LG TVs at all. For anyone who needs a big screen while stretching this is critical, and support sits on these tickets for weeks.

product.title: When support does respond, it fixes fast and refunds
product.plus: A counterpoint to the complaints: some users describe fast, human support — cast and access bugs fixed by an update within 48 hours, and refunds eventually issued, bumping ratings from 1 to 3-5 stars.

product.title: The price and paywall only appear at the very end of onboarding
product.minus: People go through a long quiz, install the app, and only at the very end learn that nothing works without a subscription — it reads as a bait-and-switch and a waste of time before they've even tried a single class.

product.title: You pay for each stretching package separately
product.minus: A subscription unlocks only one type of class, not everything: splits, backbends and full body are each billed on their own — and people feel cheated stacking several subscriptions that add up to a gym membership.

product.title: The price feels absurd next to free YouTube content
product.minus: $20-34 a month or $160-270 a year for stretching videos strikes many as a rip-off, especially when similar clips are free elsewhere — even fans of the content hit this price wall.

product.title: Videos won't load, the app crashes and freezes
product.minus: Classes have to be downloaded and either crawl for minutes or hang entirely; videos cut out mid-session and dump you back to the home screen — people have paid but can't open a single class.

product.title: The pace is too fast — no time to get into or hold a pose
product.minus: The instructor moves to the next exercise while a beginner is still figuring out the last one: there's no time to fix posture or hold the stretch, so you rush through and the benefit is lost even on the beginner level.

product.title: A long chatbot questionnaire irritates before you even start
product.minus: To reach the app you must answer dozens of questions from a fake-human bot with no skip option — for many that alone is reason to uninstall before seeing a single stretch.

product.title: Cancelling is hard and the charges keep coming
product.minus: People report being unable to cancel, being charged after cancelling or after a supposedly free week, and support denying any subscription exists while a charge is pending — this erodes trust the most.

product.title: Progress is wiped out suddenly without warning
product.minus: Mid-challenge your progress can vanish, your account can get blocked for "suspicious activity", and you're thrown back to a day you finished long ago — with no warning and no explanation.

product.title: The "beginner" programs are actually too advanced
product.minus: Even after picking the beginner level, stiff or overweight users hit exercises beyond them, with no alternative poses, blocks or straps offered — the app really only works for the already fairly flexible.

product.title: The stretching genuinely works — flexibility and splits arrive
product.plus: The most common praise: after years of stiffness or injury people actually get their splits, gain hip and back mobility and feel a difference within days or weeks — the program delivers measurable results.

product.title: Clear instruction, plus variety of classes and levels
product.plus: People love that the cues are clear and chatter-free, the instructor is visible on video, and there are classes for every level and length from 5 to 45 minutes — which keeps motivation up and boredom away.

product.title: Responsive support saves the day even after failures
product.plus: Even among the frustrated, many single out support: mistaken charges refunded within a day, accounts unblocked, free trials granted — for some it's the only reason they stay.

product.title: A simple, clean, no-frills interface is the number-one reason people love it
product.plus: Over and over, users praise the minimalism: it shows which stretch to do, signals when to switch sides or move on, and distracts you with nothing else. No music, no clutter, straight to the point — exactly what they wanted.

product.title: The harsh "one workout per day" free-tier limit infuriates people
product.minus: The most frequent complaint by far: the free tier allows exactly one stretch routine per day. People want to warm up before and after a workout, or stretch morning and night, but they're forced to pick one or wait a full day. Many beg for a limit of at least 2-3 a day; many just uninstall.

product.title: It asks you to rate the app before you've even been able to use it
product.minus: An entire wave of one-star reviews comes from being forced to rate during the setup questionnaire, before the first session. Users rightly point out it creates massive confirmation bias and poisons the review honesty, and the tactic annoys them enough to deliberately mark it down.

product.title: The paywall funnel pressures you before you ever get to try the product
product.minus: On first open you get a "lifetime offer" that vanishes the moment you close the popup, a pile of questions, and the price revealed only at the very end. The bitter irony: several users say they were actually willing to pay until this FOMO tactic pushed them away. The price is hidden until the finish.

product.title: The streak and reminders genuinely turn stretching into a habit
product.plus: It works: people hold streaks of 25, 31, even 406 days and openly admit only the fear of breaking the counter keeps them coming back. The gentle reminders and home-screen widget achieve what they never managed before — a consistent daily habit.

product.title: A huge selection of routines by body area and by length
product.plus: A core strength: routines are split by body area (lower back, shoulders, posture) and by time — from 5 minutes up to 30. You can squeeze in a short session on a busy day or go long when you have time. For many, the variety lasts a long while without feeling repetitive.

product.title: Static cartoons instead of video: unclear how to do it or where it should stretch
product.minus: During an exercise you get the name and a static, often blurry cartoon, with no voiceover and no explanation of where you should feel the stretch. To see the video you have to leave for the instructions screen, which breaks the flow. For a true beginner there's no step-by-step guidance into the correct position.

product.title: It genuinely improves flexibility and relieves back pain
product.plus: Behind all the paywall talk, the core result holds up: it works. People with chronic back pain, desk jobs, and morning stiffness report concrete gains — more flexibility, less hip, hamstring, and lower-back pain, and easier mornings.

product.title: It asks about your "problem areas" but the routines ignore them
product.minus: The app interrogates you about health, conditions, and problem areas, then its "recommended" still suggests things you physically can't do. A woman 7 months pregnant gets stretches impossible with a big belly; someone flagging their knees gets kneeling moves. For true beginners and people with limitations, it misses.

product.title: Custom routines and AI generation — but customizing them is clunky
product.minus: The idea of custom routines and AI-built sets is liked, but the execution stumbles: you can't reorder exercises within a routine, so adding one means rebuilding from scratch; custom routines often can't be edited or even deleted; and the AI generation simply fails for some people.

product.title: Billing complaints: charges after cancellation and lost paid access
product.minus: A narrow but vicious cluster of money complaints: charges two months after cancelling in trial, no refunds, and worst of all, people who paid for a yearly or "lifetime" plan getting locked out and unable to restore access while support stays silent. For a paid product this is the heaviest reputational hit.

product.title: Glitches: history logs the wrong routine, widget and sound fail, streaks reset
product.minus: Technical rough edges spoil it even for fans: the history logs a random routine instead of the one you did and sometimes resets the streak "for no reason"; the widget won't update the counter until you re-add it; sound cues stop working or are too quiet; and the timer on the first exercise starts with zero delay.

product.title: Depth of customization is what users worship it for
product.plus: Every parameter of a practice is adjustable: yoga style, length, level, instructor voice, music, focus areas, and even the speed of transitions between poses. It fits any mood, time slot, and body.

product.title: The move behind a paywall killed the free version people loved for years
product.minus: Long-time users who started in 2017–2021 got basic yoga for free and recommended it to people without money. Now nothing starts without a subscription, and devoted fans feel betrayed and leave.

product.title: The price reads as greed, especially with no regional localization
product.minus: The annual plan runs around 99.99 € and is multiples of what the first year cost; pricing isn't localized by country, so after currency conversion it feels insane. People feel they're paying for piles of modes they never wanted.

product.title: The dashboard redesign buried the navigation people relied on
product.minus: After the new interface, features are buried in menus that make no sense, saved practices vanished, and it now takes longer to reach the settings for each practice. Former fans call it the product getting worse.

product.title: Freshly generated, well-built sequences feel like a live class
product.plus: Each practice is generated fresh so it never gets stale, the sequencing is balanced and gets smoother with every update. Many compare it to a studio class and reckon it often beats one.

product.title: The team's generosity: free subscriptions for those in need
product.plus: The developers gift trials and subscriptions to people who can't pay — after job loss, a diagnosis, depression. That humanity turns users into lifelong advocates for the brand.

product.title: Perfect for squeezing short practices into a busy schedule
product.plus: Being able to set a practice to exactly 10–25 minutes for whatever window you have makes sessions realistic in a busy life. Users say this is exactly what made them consistent.

product.title: Welcoming to beginners, yet some balance poses aren't beginner-friendly
product.minus: The app bills itself as beginner-friendly, yet the beginner level throws in poses like dancer's pose that demand balance beginners don't have, with no alternative offered.

product.title: Server unreachable — the app simply won't start
product.minus: Some users never get past the load screen: endless loading, a can't-reach-server error despite working internet, and in Russia it stopped working entirely.

product.title: Billing and support fail at the worst moment
product.minus: Reports of duplicate charges totaling hundreds of dollars with no active subscription, inability to cancel, and renewal for an extra year. Support replies with an off-topic canned AI answer or stays silent.

product.title: Gamification and pushy "challenges" clash with the spirit of yoga
product.minus: The new gamified approach with stats and "make it a challenge" takes up half the page, can't be dismissed, and keeps getting pushed — for many it runs against what yoga means to them.

product.title: Crashes on GrapheneOS and casts to TV unreliably
product.minus: On GrapheneOS the app crashes at the login screen despite a promised fix for paid users; casting to TV is unreliable, there's no Android TV app, and the video runs 5+ seconds ahead of the audio.

product.title: You still can't build your own practice by hand
product.minus: For all the customization, users can't assemble their own sequence of poses — the app always generates it, and many have long asked for a manual practice-builder option.

product.title: The content genuinely works — it's what keeps people for years
product.plus: The most frequent praise: clear step-by-step sessions, detailed voice guidance, good instructors, and a wide range from beginner to advanced. People keep coming back after 6, 8, 10 years.

product.title: A paywall that hits at the worst moment: you sign up, fill the questionnaire, then can't practice without paying
product.minus: Many users complain the app demands payment up front, won't even let them try a free guided session, and only after a pile of questions does it become clear nearly all content is locked behind a purchase.

product.title: Charged without consent: one purchase, billed for two or three
product.minus: A recurring and alarming pattern: people pay for one package or plan and get charged multiple times — for "separate subscriptions", ebooks and premium they never ordered.

product.title: Cancellation is a nightmare, and charges keep coming after you cancel
product.minus: Cancelling becomes a months-long fight: you get an unsubscribe confirmation yet the charges keep coming; support demands the exact transaction time down to the second and stalls on promised refunds.

product.title: Upsells even for paying members: every session is a gauntlet of pop-ups
product.minus: Paying doesn't stop the pressure: before and after each session you get hit with offers to buy more 3-5 times, and users spend minutes dismissing windows before they can practice.

product.title: Stacked tiers: what you already paid for gets moved into a new paywall
product.minus: Loyal users are furious: content their paid plan used to include gets carved into "Master", "Meditative", and a separate meditation subscription, forcing them to pay again for the same thing.

product.title: Bought for life, then locked out: lifetime access overwritten
product.minus: People who paid for lifetime membership or a yearly plan lose access — it gets "overwritten" by a new premium subscription, or the app simply won't let them into what they already paid for.

product.title: Ads disguised as your own content, with the close button hidden
product.minus: The interface deliberately confuses: ad blocks are made to look like content you own, flashing banners appear early in the morning, and the "X" to close is hidden to provoke an accidental tap.

product.title: The onboarding questionnaire repeats on every launch and breaks the app
product.minus: A usability regression: on every launch the app re-runs dozens of profile-building questions with no way to skip, which for some longtime users made it literally unusable.

product.title: Practice on your terms: choose level, length and intensity
product.plus: A big draw for busy people and different bodies: you pick level, length and intensity, there are personalized/AI plans, reminders and customization — practice whenever and however suits you, without judgment.

product.title: Real bodily results: flexibility, back pain, weight, stress
product.plus: Users describe concrete outcomes: weight dropped, flexibility and balance improved, easier on back pain, fibromyalgia and stress — for many it's an "anchor" for daily self-care.

product.title: Expansion beyond yoga: tai chi, meditation, ayurveda — a plus for some, dilution for others
product.plus: Many welcome the variety: tai chi, meditation, pilates and ayurveda were added, and for some it's the best tai chi program they've found and a reason to stay.

product.title: Technical glitches: crashes, sessions won't load, login and password-reset trouble
product.minus: A less frequent but real pain: pages load endlessly, sessions vanish, the "next" button replays the same class, login fails after switching phones, and password reset is a struggle.

product.title: Support is a lottery: sometimes a refund, more often promises that evaporate
product.minus: Support experience is polarized: some praise quick fixes and refunds, but many more were promised refunds by Emma/Stella that never came, or got no reply at all.

product.title: Review manipulation: premium in exchange for 5 stars
product.minus: A clear trust signal about the rating: several reviews openly admit they're giving 5 stars only to claim the promised free premium access.

product.title: The original Moves video app was abandoned on Android
product.minus: Users reinstalled the familiar alo MOVES to fix bugs, only to find the Android version hasn't been supported for two years and the original app can't be brought back — and the replacement is useless without a studio nearby.

product.title: Wanted video workouts, got a storefront instead
product.minus: People come for the video workout app but get only the website shop and a customer service that does nothing to help.

product.title: Useless without a studio nearby
product.minus: The whole value is tied to physical studios: no locations in Canada means there's simply no point in using the app.

product.title: The app won't finish downloading and just doesn't work on Android
product.minus: On Android the app never finishes downloading and looks broken: iOS works, but here all that's left is a non-functional shell.

product.title: Paid for a subscription before learning it was unusable
product.minus: Users sign back up and pay, then realize the app is completely unusable — leaving them feeling they wasted money and chasing a refund.

product.title: Yearly auto-renewal charges with zero reminder
product.minus: By far the most common complaint: the subscription auto-renews for a full year with no email or in-app reminder before the charge. People only learn about it from their bank statement — often a year later, long after they forgot the app existed.

product.title: Renewal price jumps 3-4x over the intro offer
product.minus: They lure you in with a cheap promo (≈$25-39 / £28 / 35€), then silently bill $119-200 / £103 / AU$198 in year two. The price jump itself is the shock: people would have paid the same again, but not triple or quadruple with no heads-up.

product.title: Refund requested same day — flat refusal
product.minus: Even when people contact support on the day of the charge (or minutes after), the answer is a canned "the annual subscription is non-refundable." Many only got their money back by disputing through PayPal or their bank — the company refunds only under payment-processor pressure.

product.title: Cancelling only works by email — not in-app, not in Google Play
product.minus: A subscription bought via the website/Facebook doesn't show up in Google Play, so the usual cancel doesn't work. The only route is emailing support — and those emails often go unanswered, so people cancel 2-4 times and still get charged.

product.title: Support replies with autoresponders, the "contact us" link goes nowhere
product.minus: The website "contact us here" button leads nowhere, the in-app contact form throws errors, and tickets get closed with "we haven't heard from you." At its worst, one user got CC'd on another customer's complaint, full name and email exposed.

product.title: Downloaded "offline" videos still need internet
product.minus: People pay specifically to train offline — at the gym, on trips, working offshore — but downloaded clips won't play without a connection: only the music runs, not the video. The "download" is cloud-based rather than stored on the device.

product.title: Content goes years without updates — you hit a ceiling
product.minus: Loyal users finish every workout and challenge several times over and complain nothing new gets added for years. Stale "New Year 2024" and out-of-season challenges still sit there — it feels like an abandoned app. There's no progression past the basics.

product.title: Workout pace is too fast for beginners to follow
product.minus: The flows are breath-led and move fast, with little explanation of the poses — you end up rewinding to see what to do. The voice-over often lags the demo: you haven't heard the cue yet and the instructor is already in the next pose.

product.title: Workout, weight and water trackers lose data
product.minus: What should motivate instead frustrates: the activity tracker logs workouts wrong or not at all, resets streaks, and wipes weight and water history. For one user the weigh-in keeps adding a phantom 200 lbs.

product.title: TV casting is blocked, and following along on a phone is awkward
product.minus: TV casting used to work — it was removed, and now every cast attempt is blocked, with no smart-TV app. Doing poses while peeking at a tiny phone on the floor is awkward: many beg for casting and a big-screen version back.

product.title: No search or filters — you can't find the workout you want
product.minus: For such a big library there's no real search or filters by level, duration, goal or body area — you scroll an endless list, and opening one video resets it to the top. Favourites and playlists are hard or impossible to find.

product.title: A big, varied library of short workouts to fit your mood and time
product.plus: The core reason fans stay: yoga, HIIT, strength, mobility, flexibility, meditation and recipes all in one, picked by duration (even 5 minutes) and intensity. Devoted users stick around 3-4 years and report real gains in strength, flexibility and posture.

product.title: Breath cues and instructor voice-overs make the practice feel premium
product.plus: For those who stay, the detailed verbal pose explanations synced to the breath stand out — for many it's the best instruction they've had online or in person. Specific coaches (Danni) and the morning quiz become a loved start-of-day ritual.

product.title: For followers it's not an app — it's Sadhguru's presence in your pocket
product.plus: The most common feeling here isn't "convenient" but "life-changing": people thank the app not for features but for letting them stay close to the guru and his practices every day.

product.title: Every update breaks something
product.minus: An app that used to be simple and just worked keeps regressing after each release: users say outright that every update breaks something that was fine before.

product.title: Practice-tracking breaks and wipes your progress — hearts broken
product.minus: The most painful failure: the app stops logging completed kriyas and meditations, loses stats and streaks, sometimes even erasing access to courses already completed — and support fails to fix it for months.

product.title: The only fix is reinstalling, several times a week
product.minus: For a chunk of users the app regularly freezes on a blank screen or won't open, and the only way to do their kriya is to uninstall and reinstall — for some it's become a daily ritual.

product.title: The music, mantras and chants are a reason to love it on their own
product.plus: Beyond meditations, users single out the rich library of chants, bhajans and Isha sounds — for many it's the music that helps them focus and sink into practice.

product.title: Free depth: a whole library of practice at no cost
product.plus: Users value that a huge body of meditations, yoga, quotes and material is available for free — the app reads as a generous gift rather than a paywalled subscription.

product.title: Inner Engineering and Shambhavi live right inside the app
product.plus: The core value for advanced users is access to initiated practices like Shambhavi Mahamudra and post-Inner-Engineering support — for them the app has become the home of daily sadhana.

product.title: Casting, video and Exclusive content buffer and fail to load
product.minus: Playback lets users down: casting to a TV has been broken for years, video and the Exclusive section buffer even on good internet, new episodes simply don't show up — and there's no offline download.

product.title: Support and volunteers draw as much anger as the bugs
product.minus: When something breaks, what finishes people off is the silence: emails go weeks unanswered, the promised "24 hours" never arrives, and some users report rude treatment from volunteers.

product.title: The new "checklist" UI alienated the people who loved the cosiness
product.minus: The redesign turned the app into a clinical to-do list: users who loved the warm, inviting interface now find it cold and unfriendly — enough to start hunting for an alternative.

product.title: The Exclusive subscription can't be cancelled from inside the app
product.minus: Billing turns into a trap: the FAQ promises an easy way to cancel the Sadhguru Exclusive subscription, but there's no button for it inside the app, and support emails go unanswered for weeks.

product.title: Won't install on SIM-less tablets and certain devices
product.minus: Installation isn't universal: on SIM-less tablets (Samsung Tab S9 Ultra, Moto Pad 60 Pro) and some devices the app either won't install at all or throws an install error.

product.title: The program is life-changing and genuinely relieves pain — and that earns it forgiveness for everything
product.plus: Over and over, people say DDPY brought them back to life: back, knee and neck pain gone, recovery after injuries and surgery, weight lost. It's the results that keep them, despite the clunky app.

product.title: The interface is stuck in 2016: years without updates, unintuitive and clunky
product.minus: Even fans of the program call the app itself "garbage" and "amateur hour": the design hasn't changed in years, navigation is painful, and you have to "fight" to do anything. The money, they feel, isn't reinvested in the product.

product.title: Constant crashes, especially on launch and mid-workout
product.minus: The app dies on launch, when opening a download, and deep into a custom workout — at which point it won't give credit for it. People reinstall it several times.

product.title: A huge library for every level — even bed-bound users
product.plus: There's so much content it lasts for years: programs for every age and physical ability, from bed yoga to extreme, with modifiers for injuries. Everyone finds what fits them.

product.title: Heart-rate monitor and watch won't connect — but Bluetooth finds the neighbours
product.minus: Heart-rate monitors stop syncing, while the app picks up a neighbour's car across the street or their Samsung oven. Samsung and Google watches aren't supported at all — only Apple Watch, otherwise wear a separate chest strap.

product.title: The app is locked to landscape and wastes a third of the phone screen
product.minus: On a phone the app only works in landscape, which is awkward, and after an update a gray box appeared at the bottom eating a third of the screen. Many find the website easier to use than the mobile app.

product.title: Casting to TV barely works — the Chromecast button is permanently greyed out
product.minus: The app isn't supported on smart TVs, Roku and many Android boxes, and the Chromecast button is "grayed out" most of the time. People end up working out staring at a phone instead of the TV.

product.title: Anti-consumer billing: the price doubles at checkout and discounts don't apply
product.minus: The advertised discounted price suddenly nearly doubles at checkout, Black Friday deals and the trial don't apply, and there's no way to reverse the purchase afterward. To get the free trial they demand a card upfront.

product.title: Cancelling the subscription is nearly impossible, and emails go unanswered
product.minus: People try to cancel many times and can't — the screen is stuck on the last workout, and emails asking to cancel get no reply. One says it cost them $300.

product.title: Dallas is the motivator who gets people off the couch; a sense of "family"
product.plus: DDP himself and the instructors keep saying "make it your own, at your own pace" — which removes the guilt of not keeping up and genuinely motivates. People feel part of a family and stick with it where other workouts made them quit.

product.title: Not just workouts: nutrition, recipes and a healthy-lifestyle mindset
product.plus: Beyond workouts the app has hundreds of simple recipes with videos, nutrition plans, and motivational and teaching clips on the three pillars — fitness, nutrition and mindset. People treat it as a template for living healthier, not a one-off workout.

product.title: Videos won't load after updates, and the app needs a connection even for downloads
product.minus: After yet another update the videos stop loading both in the app and on the website, leaving it useless. Even videos downloaded to the phone require a connection, and individual buttons like the menu simply break after updates.

product.title: Once-free features were mass-migrated behind a paywall
product.minus: People shot and edited for free for years, then updates locked almost everything behind a subscription — even the in-app camera and basic retouch. Long-time users from 2015-2020 read this as betrayal, not product progress.

product.title: Charges without consent and a free trial that isn't free
product.minus: The most toxic complaint: someone takes the 7-day free trial, cancels within minutes, yet a full yearly fee still hits their card or GCash. Many swear they never subscribed at all and the money vanished anyway.

product.title: 2,600-peso GCash charges nobody authorized
product.minus: A distinct cluster from Filipino users: 2,600 pesos for a yearly plan suddenly leaves their GCash with no one having signed up. Often the money was set aside for medical needs or a child, and no refund comes — hitting the most vulnerable.

product.title: Ads block even opening the app and taking a photo
product.minus: Full-screen ads now gate the launch and every shot: 2-3 minute Temu/AliExpress clips with no exit button, after which you still can't save the photo. Ads that once unlocked features now simply block you.

product.title: Prices feel outrageous and keep jumping up
product.minus: The subscription reads as a rip-off: €60 a year just to use it as a plain camera, a jump from 3.45 to 10.99 a month, a rise from 1,900 to 2,600 in two weeks. On top of a yearly plan you still buy credits — it feels like an endless money grab.

product.title: Cancelling doesn't stick, refunds denied, support silent
product.minus: Even after cancelling, users keep getting debited, and refund requests get "no refunds" or silence. There's no contact address and replies are canned, pushing people to file fraud claims with their bank.

product.title: Intrusive data collection as a condition of use
product.minus: To keep using it, the app demands consent to scan which apps are installed on your phone, with no clear explanation and no deny-all button. Add facial recognition and photo uploads for processing, and even paying customers walk away.

product.title: Won't save photos and crashes mid-edit
product.minus: The most basic action — saving the result — often breaks: after updates you can't save even a photo edited with free tools, video audio disappears, and the app crashes mid-edit or stops opening altogether.

product.title: Slow loading and freezes without perfect Wi-Fi
product.minus: Much of the work happens in the cloud: without strong Wi-Fi the app freezes on loading, and trying on outfits or swapping a photo takes minutes. A "Network error" pops up even on solid internet, also blocking ad-based unlocks.

product.title: AI results look fake and crude
product.minus: The paid AI often disappoints: faces come out cartoonish, results are obviously AI-generated, and even then they're capped by limits. Hairstyle and men's-style choices are thin — people with hair up or men have almost nothing usable.

product.title: Rich set of filters, effects and beauty tools
product.plus: Those who get past the paywall praise the product itself: the best radiant filters and effects, natural on-the-spot makeup, loads of styles and stickers. Many call it the best editor and have used it for years for selfies and photo work.

product.title: Simple, easy interface and years-long attachment
product.plus: A real strength is how easy it is: users praise it as very user-friendly and easy to navigate, giving exactly the result they want. Many have used it for 4-10 years and genuinely love it, which is why the recent changes sting.

product.title: Pleas to bring back ad-unlocks and the monthly plan
product.minus: A constructive but painful ask: students and users without a card beg for ad-based unlocks instead of payment, while those who paid monthly were forced onto a pricey weekly or yearly plan — and plead in reviews to bring the monthly option back.

product.title: VIP isn't final: a VIP+ tier appears for features you already paid for
product.minus: After paying for VIP (sometimes a full year upfront), people find previously available features moved behind VIP+ or extra credits, with no clear notice before payment. It reads as a bait-and-switch, not an upsell.

product.title: Ads don't disappear even for paying subscribers
product.minus: Users with an active (often yearly) subscription still get ads — intrusive ones with fake close buttons that dump you onto a website. Paying stops delivering the promised ad-free experience.

product.title: Updates rip out the features people built their workflow on
product.minus: Recent updates remove templates, presets, the layers tool, makeup templates and video body-editing — the very things people paid for and stayed years for. They're swapped for "weird AI stuff," making the app useless to long-time users.

product.title: Trial and auto-charges: money leaves without clear consent
product.minus: The 7-day trial turns into a yearly charge, cancelling during the trial is hard, and some see funds (GCash/GoPay) taken seemingly without installing or consenting at all. Many get a refund only by fighting through support.

product.title: Support actually issues refunds — and people remember it
product.plus: Despite the billing chaos, some praise support: the team is responsive and refunds for accidental or unauthorized subscriptions actually go through — sometimes even after Google Play declined.

product.title: Unsaved work vanishes for good
product.minus: There's no backup: leave the app or fail to save in time and the whole project is permanently deleted. Just switching to TikTok is enough to lose nearly everything.

product.title: Even basic edits demand an internet connection
product.minus: Brightness, contrast and other elementary edits don't work offline, and the app repeatedly asks you to re-download filters you already downloaded. On a poor or "undetected" connection the editor simply stalls.

product.title: Freezes, crashes and lag, especially on Android
product.minus: The app crashes on launch after updates, glitches and quits while editing video, and runs noticeably slow on Android. For some, video and photo editing don't work at all.

product.title: Paid options disguised among the free ones
product.minus: Paid options are hidden among the free ones, making tool selection a minefield: you spend time, reach the result, then hit "join now to continue." Things that used to be free (eye angle, HD) are now paywalled.

product.title: A rich free toolkit and ease of use are why people love it
product.plus: Despite the complaints, many praise the abundance of free features, the intuitive interface and the speed: ad-free collages, fast edits, easy to learn. For some it's their favorite editor for years.

product.title: AI beautification and photo upscaling impress with results
product.plus: The real strength is the AI quality itself: smoothing skin and eyes in seconds, turning blurry shots into HD, upscaling and beauty effects that save time. The results are what makes people willing to pay.

product.title: VIP pricing is high, with no local-currency option
product.minus: Even loyal users call the subscription too expensive and would subscribe monthly if it were cheaper. It's compounded by dollar-only pricing: users in Nigeria, Malaysia and elsewhere ask for local-currency options.

product.title: Free trial charges money without clear consent
product.minus: By far the most common complaint: people start a "free 3-day trial" without realizing it auto-charges when it ends — often immediately. Hundreds of near-identical refund pleas, with money pulled from GCash, e-wallets, and cards, sometimes belonging to others.

product.title: Ads became unbearable and trick you into taps
product.minus: Before every shot there's an unskippable 15–60 second ad. The close X is deliberately rigged so that instead of exiting you get thrown into Google Play or an ad download. Even paying for premium doesn't stop them.

product.title: Once-free features moved behind the paywall
product.minus: Long-time users remember the app as free and generous. Now almost every effect, filter, wardrobe item, or even basic editing demands VIP — people feel cheated out of what they used to have.

product.title: Paid for VIP — but get no access
product.minus: A huge cluster of complaints: the subscription is bought and paid, yet the app keeps demanding payment again. It especially breaks when switching to a new phone or tablet — VIP doesn't transfer, while Google Play says "you're already subscribed".

product.title: Photo quality and effects keep people loyal for years
product.plus: Beneath the complaints there's genuine love: users have made BeautyCam their first install on every new phone for a decade. They praise crisp HD photos, the "iPhone camera" effect, remastering old shots, and the wealth of free options.

product.title: Updates ripped out the old version's beloved features
product.minus: Updates wiped out whole chunks: "Hight", the vibe camera, "classic", photo stretching, instant filters. People beg for the old version because the new one shoots worse and slaps on preset makeup and stickers.

product.title: Meitu support does sometimes refund — and earns praise
product.plus: A counterpoint to the rage: those who reached the developer by email (not via Google Play) often got refunded the same day. Some furious 1-star reviews flip to grateful 5-star ones after a fast refund.

product.title: Support goes silent and Google denies refunds
product.minus: The flip side: many get only a bot, emails ignored for weeks, and Google Play rejects the refund. People beg repeatedly for their money and threaten to report to banks and regulators.

product.title: Subscription is pricey — and the price doubled
product.minus: $50 a year for a beauty camera strikes users as absurd, especially those who remember it free. The monthly plan was removed in favor of a costlier weekly one, and users openly call it greed.

product.title: Glitches, crashes and "no network" break shooting
product.minus: Plenty of technical breakage: crashes when ads play, filters and "Looks" failing on Samsung, blurry photos, broken video recording, and features showing "no network" on a perfect connection.

product.title: The free tier is generous — plenty to love without paying
product.plus: Despite the aggressive VIP push, some users stress that a lot is free — background removal, photo enhancement, filters. "Just use the free stuff" reads as a real tip from loyal fans.

product.title: The AI Wardrobe is loved, but locked behind VIP
product.minus: The AI Wardrobe sparks real excitement — but almost everything in it is paid. Users repeatedly beg for at least one free daily use and more men's clothing; the excitement curdles into frustration.

product.title: Live Photo on Android is the whole reason people install it
product.plus: A huge share of users come straight from TikTok specifically for the Live Photos their Samsung/Android can't do, and the app genuinely solves that pain.

product.title: Saved Live Photos turn back into a still picture
product.minus: The single most common failure: users shoot a Live Photo but in the gallery or in other apps it either won't move or doesn't save at all.

product.title: Lots of genuinely free cameras and filters
product.plus: The thing users single out versus rivals — most cameras and filters are free, and even the free set is enough for great-looking results.

product.title: Once-free filters keep disappearing behind a paywall on updates
product.minus: People install for a specific filter, then after an update it suddenly demands a subscription — and the free pool shrinks with each release.

product.title: Lag, freezes and the app closing by itself
product.minus: The app noticeably lags and sometimes closes on its own, especially in live mode and video, and users note other apps on the same phone run fine.

product.title: Feels like real film stock, not just a filter
product.plus: Users fall in love with the grain texture and how a shot looks like it was actually taken on a 90s camera rather than a filter slapped on a normal photo.

product.title: Too many ads — for a chunk of users
product.minus: Ads are the top irritant for people who'd otherwise rate 5 stars: some say they can barely do anything, while others say there are barely any and they're skippable — the experience is very uneven.

product.title: Photos just stop saving
product.minus: Beyond Live Photos, some users can't save ordinary shots either — sometimes after it used to work, which hurts most while travelling.

product.title: Needs internet where users don't expect it
product.minus: Downloading filters and effects requires a connection, sometimes slowly, and shooting offline runs into network errors — even though users expect a camera to work without internet.

product.title: Can't remove or swap an imposed filter
product.minus: Users want simple control over filters — turning off the "cool" one that tints everything blue, or getting a plain shot — but the option isn't there.

product.title: Diary and date-stamping turn a photo into a keepsake
product.plus: Being able to flip a shot over and write a diary entry or date makes the photo feel like a physical keepsake — users love the app specifically for this.

product.title: Rescues shots on weak phone cameras
product.plus: For people with cheap or weak phone cameras the app noticeably improves the image — a reason to install on its own, separate from the aesthetic.

product.title: Almost every camera is locked behind a paywall
product.minus: The app's defining pain: only 2-5 cameras are free, everything else is marked VIP. People feel it's «free in name, paid in practice» and ask the devs to either make the app honestly paid or unlock more filters.

product.title: Photo quality like a real digicam
product.plus: What the app is genuinely loved for: shots come out clear and «like from a physical camera». Many say it's indistinguishable from a real 2000s digicam and rate it 10/10 for quality alone.

product.title: A substitute for an expensive digital camera
product.plus: The strongest delight driver: people can't afford a trendy digicam, and the app delivers the same result for free. They literally call it «saved me from buying a digicam» and «will save you tons of money».

product.title: The Y2K and 2000s aesthetic is the main draw
product.plus: People come here for the nostalgia and vintage vibe: shots «like the early 2000s», their Instagram feed turns aesthetic. It's the product's emotional core, not just a filter.

product.title: Live Photo on Android — a feature people couldn't get before
product.plus: A distinct joy for Android owners: the app brings the «iPhone feature» — live photos — to any phone. For many that's the decisive reason they installed it and love it.

product.title: Lots of cameras, but they all look nearly identical
product.minus: A skeptical thread: with dozens of «cameras» it's mostly the frame and layout that change, while the image itself stays the same. Some see it as just an excuse to sell a pricey subscription.

product.title: Paid for VIP Forever — access never unlocked
product.minus: The most painful money story: people pay for lifetime VIP, but the app says «No Purchase Records Detected» and won't unlock the cameras. Support doesn't reply to emails — hence the demands for refunds.

product.title: Crashes and Live Photo glitches on some phones
product.minus: A minority's technical pain: the app crashes (especially on Samsung), and live photo sometimes goes black or «glitchy». People say they'd raise their rating if performance were optimized.

product.title: Free cameras give only a handful of trial shots
product.minus: A monetization nuance even happy users notice: you can try a premium camera, but only 3-10 times before it locks. It feels like a tease rather than real free access.

product.title: All-in-one: filters, collages, editor, frames
product.plus: People like that the app isn't just a camera: there's a carousel/templates for collages, a shadows-and-highlights editor, stickers and frames. The «all under one roof» feeling adds value beyond shooting.

product.title: Almost no ads — and people value it
product.plus: Despite the aggressive VIP monetization, there are barely any ads, and people single this out as a plus: «no ads», «very less ads». A clean shooting experience without banners.

product.title: A one-time lifetime buy as the fair alternative to subscription
product.plus: For some, the demand for honest monetization is met: you can pay «a couple euros» once and unlock everything forever without subscribing. Those who did call it completely worth it.

product.title: Basic features that were free for years moved behind the paywall
product.minus: Long-time users repeatedly say small edits — skin smoothing, eyelashes, eyeliner — are now premium, and the app quietly turned into a paid one.

product.title: A paid subscription won't activate — the app demands you buy it again
product.minus: Dozens show an active subscription in Google Play, yet the app says they have no purchase and asks for money again; 'restore purchase' doesn't help.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and after the free trial
product.minus: People cancel or take the 7-day trial and still get charged — sometimes for a whole year, sometimes repeatedly after cancelling.

product.title: Support is effectively unreachable — they reply only to reviews, not emails
product.minus: Users send emails with payment screenshots for weeks with no reply, yet notice the company answers a public review the very next day.

product.title: The free version is nearly empty — a few hairstyles and basic makeup
product.minus: Free mode gives you literally 2-3 hairstyles and a couple of makeup tools, with everything else locked, so you can't really try the product without subscribing.

product.title: Saving photos is locked, and sometimes the button just disappears
product.minus: Some users can't save an edited photo without paying; for others the save button vanishes after a hairstyle edit and they have to clear the cache.

product.title: Phantom charges — for an app they never used
product.minus: People find G-Cash or card charges for a subscription they never signed up for, sometimes years after a single install, with no one to contact.

product.title: AI hairstyles and edits distort the face and look unnatural
product.minus: Trying on hairstyles makes the AI reshape the face, brows, eyes and ears into an 'alien' result, and makeup lands in the wrong spot and can't be moved.

product.title: Ads now even for those who paid for an ad-free version
product.minus: Ads have become intrusive and often won't close; some complain they still see ads even after paying for the ad-free version.

product.title: When it works, it's a years-long favorite face editor
product.plus: Many have used it for 10+ years on every new phone — simple, intuitive, a comfortable go-to face editor.

product.title: Natural results — 'still me, just a little prettier'
product.plus: Fans love the subtlety: it enhances rather than rebuilds the face, smooths skin, removes shine, and keeps the photo realistic.

product.title: A safe try-on room for hairstyles and makeup with no real-world risk
product.plus: Users value trying on makeup, hairstyles, hair colors and outfits with no commitment — seeing a new version of themselves and restarting as often as they like.

product.title: Charges hit accounts with no warning, refunds are refused
product.minus: Users report yearly charges appearing out of nowhere — sometimes after they cancelled or uninstalled — and when they ask for a refund, support hides behind a 7-day policy or gives conflicting answers.

product.title: Nearly everything useful is now behind a paywall
product.minus: For years the basic retouch tools were free; now almost nothing works without a subscription — the free features are either useless or capped at a single edit a day.

product.title: You pay for premium and the features still don't unlock
product.minus: Paying subscribers keep hitting a "server is down" wall and an endless "restore purchase" loop that errors out — the app won't recognise their payment, especially with more than one Google account on the phone.

product.title: The "free trial" demands a card before you touch anything
product.minus: The app surfaces in search as "free" but forces you to enter card details and sign up for a trial before you can make a single edit — which many users flatly call a bait-and-switch.

product.title: Cancelling is a maze — there's no button inside the app
product.minus: People spend months or even years unable to cancel: there's no cancel option in the app, Google Play sends them in circles, and the charges keep coming.

product.title: The best interface among photo editors — tools are easy to find
product.plus: Even users annoyed by the pricing admit the navigation is intuitive, the tool you need is right there, and for sheer ease of use it beats the competition.

product.title: AI restoration of old and blurry photos genuinely wows
product.plus: The warmest reviews are about restoring old, moisture-damaged and blurry photos — the result beats every other app users had tried.

product.title: A loyal long-haul base — years of devotion to the app
product.plus: A huge share of the rave reviews come from people who've used it for 5, 9, even 10 years — making gifts for family, retouching for magazines, ranking it their number one.

product.title: Crashes when opening the camera or shooting
product.minus: For some users the app crashes every time the camera opens, takes other running apps down with it, and the face won't even show in the viewfinder until the shot is taken.

product.title: The AI slaps a "violation" label on ordinary photos
product.minus: The AI moderation blocks harmless shots — bikinis, plain portraits — flagging them as "insensitive" or rule-breaking, so the edit you paid for can't be done.

product.title: AI edits look unnatural and align poorly
product.minus: The automatic processing falters: hairstyles sit crookedly on the head, beauty filters don't carry into the final video, and double-chin reduction is weak — the result is far from realistic.

product.title: Ads and coin microtransactions even on top of a subscription
product.minus: Even after subscribing, users run into ads and have to buy extra "coins" for basic functions — a second layer of monetisation stacked on top of access they already paid for.

product.title: It used to be free — now everything sits behind a paywall
product.minus: The most common complaint: the app used to work for free (or had a set of free features), and after updates everything moved under subscription. Even things labeled "try" can't actually be used — applying or saving demands payment. Long-time loyal users are leaving precisely because of this.

product.title: They charge the subscription but don't grant access
product.minus: People pay for a year or subscribe — and after paying still can't use the app at all. The money is gone but features stay locked or ask for payment again. It turns the purchase into wasted money.

product.title: Charges without consent and no way to cancel
product.minus: A cluster of reviews describes outright billing abuse: the card charged monthly instead of the paid year, money taken after cancelling and uninstalling, or charges with no subscription at all. Users call it a scam and theft.

product.title: Support never responds
product.minus: When something breaks with billing or subscription, contacting support is futile: people send emails and reminders for weeks and months and get no reply at all. It deepens the sense that the app is abandoned and built only to take money.

product.title: Edited video won't save
product.minus: The core flow breaks: after editing (especially video) saving either hangs forever or "saves to nowhere" — only the original remains. For a paid app this turns the whole effort into wasted time.

product.title: The Art feature works on photos but not on video
product.minus: A very specific product gap: the "Art" button/effect appears for photos but is simply missing when you pick a video. Users see it on others' clips, expect it for video, and are upset it was either removed or withheld.

product.title: Slow, freezing and endless exports
product.minus: Performance disappoints: the app crashes while editing, freezes on features like resize, and video export can drag on for hours without finishing. Ironically, for some it got slower right after they paid.

product.title: Free only on iPhone — Android has to pay
product.minus: Users notice a platform unfairness: free editing options are available on iOS, while Android is charged for the same thing. It reads as discrimination and "just not fair".

product.title: The result looks natural and beautiful
product.plus: Those who do get it working praise the quality itself: retouch makes the face prettier yet natural, effects blend well and don't look artificial. For many it's the best beauty editor they've tried.

product.title: Easy, simple and versatile for photos and video
product.plus: Fans note it's easy to use, packed with fine-grained customization, and handles photos, video and selfies alike. It gave some the confidence to share their pictures, and others value that it doesn't push ads.

product.title: The price shuts out those who can't pay
product.minus: A distinct pain is affordability: people plainly say they can't afford to pay just to "look temporarily beautiful" and ask for a free mode even if it has ads. For part of the audience in poorer regions this puts the app out of reach.

product.title: The subscription is nearly impossible to cancel, and the charges keep coming
product.minus: People spend weeks hunting for a way to cancel: the support link is dead, the AI agent replies with templates, and the weekly charges keep hitting — many end up disputing through their bank or reporting to Google and the BBB.

product.title: Refunds are promised but never delivered
product.minus: Those who paid and could never use the app request a refund by the book — and get neither money nor a reply; support bounces them to Google Play, where getting it back is nearly impossible.

product.title: "Free" turns into a paywall right after you upload your photos
product.minus: It's advertised as free, but once you go through the whole flow — pick 10-12 photos, hit continue — you're hit with a demand to subscribe or buy coins before trying anything.

product.title: Coins get spent even when the result fails
product.minus: Generations often end in a red "cancelled" X, yet the coins are already gone and don't come back; the paid tier gives a couple of tries that deplete even when the image comes out botched.

product.title: After the update, the results stopped looking like you
product.minus: An update tanked the likeness: faces, body shape, sometimes even race get altered, the head balloons, and no amount of chat-editing restores the old quality — people beg to roll the version back.

product.title: The new AI chat replaced the simple template interface
product.minus: What used to be one tap on a template now has to be coaxed out of a subpar AI chat: it's slower, rejects even fully-clothed people on "safety" grounds, and users start shopping for a replacement.

product.title: Unauthorized charges and complaints of money being "stolen"
product.minus: Users report repeated $7.99 charges they never authorized, stolen credits and deleted profiles; mentions of class-action investigations and threats to dispute the payments as fraud surface in the reviews.

product.title: Crashes, errors and photos that never showed up
product.minus: Some paying users simply can't use the app: a perpetual "oops ran into a problem", errors on editing, the face captured wrong, and paid-for photos that never appear.

product.title: Training a Lora from your own selfies gives a genuine likeness
product.plus: The app's core magic is training a personal model (Lora) from your photos and then dropping you into any scene with convincing likeness; the closer the subject, the better the output, especially in makeup shots.

product.title: Keeps your real features where other apps distort them
product.plus: Fans value that the app enhances photos without rebuilding the face — your shape, eyes, nose and mouth stay yours; that's exactly what sets it apart from rivals in their eyes.

product.title: An easy on-ramp to video trends and social-media creativity
product.plus: When it works, it's just fun: photo-to-video, effects, trends (like the basketball stadium one), outfit swaps — a simple, intuitive tool that puts you in dream places and situations.

product.title: The free trial doesn't let you actually try the product
product.minus: The trial feels like bait: instead of access to features you just get ads pushing more coins, no way to judge if you like the output, and people end up paying $7.99 "for nothing".

product.title: Constant «upgrade to Premium» popups make the app almost unusable
product.minus: Every other tap opens an upsell screen — the nag lands on nearly every screen, the close button sometimes doesn't work, and the app's actual purpose gets buried under it.

product.title: Downloaded offline maps fail to open exactly where there's no signal
product.minus: The whole point — download a route in advance — regularly breaks: with no reception the map won't load, throws «sorry the trail is no longer available», or just shows blank white tiles.

product.title: The free version is bait: everything useful is behind a year-only subscription
product.minus: Marketing says «free», but really it's a 7-day trial then $35/month or ~$80/year; there's no monthly option, no risk-free trial, and basic functions are walled off.

product.title: The subscription is nearly impossible to cancel — it loops you around
product.minus: The cancel button bounces you between the website and the app, opens a discount instead of cancelling, and demands four taps across four screens — a textbook «Hotel California».

product.title: They charge you even after you cancel before the trial ends, and won't refund
product.minus: Several users report the trial is billed immediately, and cancelling days before the deadline still results in a full-year charge — with «no refunds».

product.title: Driving directions to the trailhead send you tens of miles off
product.minus: The «Get Directions» to the trailhead reliably routes you wrong — to the peak, to a random spot in the middle of nowhere, or 20-40 miles off; a recent bug that wasn't there before.

product.title: Drains battery and overheats the phone — dangerous out of coverage
product.minus: Even offline and in battery-saver mode it kills the battery in a couple of hours and heats the phone; on the same track Gaia used 4% while AllTrails used 41% — a real risk mid-hike with no signal.

product.title: Activity tracking breaks: phantom miles, random stops, wrong distance
product.minus: Tracking either stops itself (e.g. after taking a camera photo), or won't stop and logs the whole drive home as part of the hike, or reports 44km for a 4km walk; there's no easy way to end a hike at the car.

product.title: Forced to install the app and log in just to look at a map
product.minus: The website is deliberately broken and shoves you to the app store, and without an account you can't even open a map — users read it as data harvesting and surveillance.

product.title: The «you are here» dot vanishes or gets stuck in another country
product.minus: The core reason people install it — seeing yourself on the trail — fails: no blue dot, the phone keeps hunting for GPS, and one user's location was stuck in Ireland while he was in Alaska.

product.title: Keeps you from getting lost — saves you and gets you home even offline
product.plus: The thing users love most: the «wrong way» alert and GPS dot without signal have repeatedly rescued lost hikers and led them back — for many it's an indispensable tool in the mountains.

product.title: Huge trail database with community reviews — even obscure routes turn up
product.plus: The app's strength is a worldwide catalog of trails with reviews, ratings, filters (difficulty, dog-friendly, how busy) and a sense of what to expect; users say it's the community that makes it valuable.

product.title: Difficulty ratings and descriptions dangerously lie — «easy» turns out hard
product.minus: Routes marked «moderate» turn into 6-hour climbs, «easy» ones injure disabled users, and trails lead down restricted or non-existent paths — and you can't even warn others by rating the difficulty.

product.title: Support is bot-only, no humans reachable, emails go unanswered
product.minus: Even long-time paying subscribers complain: the bot is useless, no human is reachable, emails are ignored, and the only advice is «uninstall and reinstall» — impossible with no signal.

product.title: An indispensable companion for a day on the trail — simple and accurate
product.plus: For many it's the category standard and a must-have: accurate maps, a handy 3D route preview, easy onboarding; people won't hike without it for years and recommend it to beginners and pros alike.

product.title: Clunky UX: broken filter sliders, taps on trails do nothing, no name search
product.minus: The interface is called «clunky»: distance sliders and filters don't work, tapping a labeled trail opens nothing, trails vanish on zoom, there's no auto-rotate and trail-name search disappeared.

product.title: It used to be better: AI added, free features removed, veterans leaving
product.minus: Long-time users describe «enshittification»: free categories (camping, fishing), waypoints and photo-locations removed, a controversial AI trail generator added — and they're leaving for Komoot, Hiiker, Gaia, Organic Maps.

product.title: Unique private spots you won't find anywhere else
product.plus: The core reason people love it: users find spots on private land, farms and ranches away from the crowds — places that simply aren't on Google Maps or standard camping guides. That's the whole product.

product.title: The app glitches, flickers and won't open
product.minus: The single most common pain: the app freezes, flickers, jumps, and for many just hangs on the orange logo and never loads even after reinstalling. Version 4.11.1 crashed immediately on launch.

product.title: Search resets to the top of the list and restarts itself
product.minus: Browsing options is nearly impossible: the list scrolls back to the top after 6-7 results, the search refreshes itself every half-second, and it flings you back to your own location instead of where you searched.

product.title: Easy booking and direct contact with the host
product.plus: When the app behaves, the core flow gets praise: quickly find a spot, see photos and amenities, book it, and message the owner directly — "Airbnb for camping" in the best sense.

product.title: Warm hosts make the trip
product.plus: A huge share of the 5-star reviews are about the hosts themselves: welcoming, attentive, bringing coffee and firewood, leaving you alone when you want privacy. The people are what turn a plot into an experience.

product.title: Hidden service fees ambush you at checkout
product.minus: The listed price isn't the final one: large non-refundable service fees only appear at payment. Users were charged $123 and $150 in fees, and $60 on a fully host-refundable booking still a month away.

product.title: Hosts go unvetted — scams and dangerous situations happen
product.minus: No identity or background checks on hosts: people drove to a plot sold 22 months ago, to bookings that didn't exist, and in one case a host locked a guest in a shed and took her phone — yet stayed on the platform.

product.title: Affordable prices and a sense of adventure
product.plus: Many praise the value: cheap last-minute spots, overnight stops on road trips, spontaneous getaways. For bikepacking and van life it's the go-to app.

product.title: Android's "back" button closes the whole app
product.minus: The system "back" gesture/button on Android doesn't go to the previous screen — it exits the app entirely. It grates at every step and exposes a half-baked cross-platform wrapper.

product.title: Hosting only works on desktop, with bots instead of support
product.minus: Hosts are cramped in the app: you can't toggle between properties, multiple listings force you to desktop, and support is email-and-bots only — no phone or chat even in an emergency.

product.title: Login and password reset send you in circles
product.minus: Logging in is its own ordeal: password reset loops endlessly, the Facebook and Google login buttons don't work, and the app makes you sign in again every time you open a new campground.

product.title: Inaccurate listings: missing toilets, wrong access, wrong region
product.minus: Listings can't be trusted: spots are flagged as having toilets they don't, caravan-friendly sites are actually on steep slopes, filters barely work, and notifications push US deals to users in Australia.

product.title: Map and navigation show dollar signs instead of places
product.minus: The map is hard to read: dollar signs cover the area names instead of place labels, some listings can't be selected from the map at all, and figuring out where a camp is and how far it is from you is needlessly hard.

product.title: Can't book multiple consecutive nights
product.minus: A core flow breaks: you pick 4 nights but checkout shows 3; some people can only book a single night instead of two — and you're forced to start over from scratch.

product.title: Overpriced for what's on offer
product.minus: A segment feels a bare camping plot shouldn't cost as much as a hotel room; hosts allegedly price their chicken field like prime real estate, and good value for money is rare here.

product.title: Silently stops recording mid-day
product.minus: The defining pain: the app confirms it's recording, then logs nothing — it captures one run in three, loses entire days or stops with no warning, forcing you to babysit it all day.

product.title: Core functions locked behind the paywall
product.minus: On Android the free version won't even show trails on the map — only lifts — and individual-run stats moved behind premium, so users feel they can't even try the app out.

product.title: Finding friends on the mountain is the killer feature
product.plus: The number-one reason people love it: you can see where friends and family are on the mountain, plan meet-ups, compare stats at day's end and stop playing phone tag — it's why they keep it.

product.title: Logs nonsense when you're off the slope
product.minus: Forget to stop recording and it logs your drive home as a run, posting a 198 mph "top speed" from the I-70 highway, and you can't properly edit or delete these bogus runs — there's no auto-pause when you leave the resort.

product.title: Android is a cut-down port of iOS for the same price
product.minus: The Android build is visibly poorer (no offline maps, several versions behind) yet costs the same as friends pay on iPhone — and that gap stings almost more than anything else.

product.title: Inaccurate speed and altitude, especially on Android
product.minus: The GPS data drifts: elevation jumps by hundreds of feet, speed is overstated by around 10% (sometimes 93 or 198 mph), and the devs acknowledge the bug but blame the Google library and won't fix it.

product.title: Drains the battery in a single ski day
product.minus: Some users say the phone dies before the day ends, especially if you don't pause it — though others praise how light it is; it comes down to the battery-optimization settings on a given device.

product.title: Shady billing and charges after cancelling
product.minus: People cancel the trial and still get charged the annual fee — sometimes for years; the promised day-before reminder never arrives, and the broken support page makes refunds impossible.

product.title: No watch app and missing integrations
product.minus: For years users have begged for a Wear OS, Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch companion so they don't have to pull out the phone, while Garmin, Samsung Health and Health Connect integrations are missing or half-working (read-only, won't write back).

product.title: Map stuck at half-screen, resort info won't collapse
product.minus: After an update the trail map fills only half the screen and the resort-info card can't be minimised — too little to navigate an unfamiliar slope, and there's not even a compass to tell which way is north.

product.title: When it works, it's the best tracking app out there
product.plus: For those whose recordings hold up, the app wins them over: accurate vertical/speed/lift/run stats, a gorgeous 3D day playback, a clean interface — many call it the best ski app they've used, better than Epic.

product.title: The Call Ski Patrol button genuinely saves people
product.plus: A quiet but powerful feature: the Call Ski Patrol button proved invaluable when people got hurt on the slope — torn MCL and ACL, an injured knee — and help came right away.

product.title: Timeline editor and responsive support
product.plus: When recordings do glitch, two things save the day: the timeline editor that lets you trim the drive home and fix runs, and a support team that's responsive, ships fixes in hours and personally helps migrate data from old trackers.

product.title: A worthy replacement for Ski Tracks and resort apps
product.plus: Many came over after Ski Tracks went paid and stayed happy: a family plan for 5-6 people at $30/year feels like fair pricing, and one app replaces every resort's individual app.

product.title: Used to be free — now you can't do anything at all without a subscription
product.minus: The app's defining wound: returning users find that every basic function, even planning their own route, is locked behind a paywall that simply didn't exist when the app was free.

product.title: "Corporate greed" — the acquisition killed a beloved product
product.minus: Long-time fans repeat the same story: the app was wonderful until it got bought out, after which the focus shifted to squeezing money rather than being useful.

product.title: "There was a problem creating your trip" — it fails at the very first step
product.minus: Many users can't even begin: creating a trip throws an error that no amount of toggling Wi-Fi, reinstalling, or using exact addresses will fix.

product.title: Silent auto-renewal and refusal to refund
product.minus: Users get charged for renewals with no advance notice, and refund requests are met with refusal or a "7-day grace period" excuse, even after a year of not using the app.

product.title: Cancelling is nearly impossible — you must email and ask permission
product.minus: Because the subscription isn't billed through the Play Store, you can't cancel in settings — you have to email support, and cancel attempts hit "try again later."

product.title: Paid and still locked out: a pro account is told to pay again for premium
product.minus: Even paying subscribers report their trips locked, the app still demanding an upgrade, and "restore subscription" spinning forever without working.

product.title: The price is hidden until you've entered all your info
product.minus: The app makes you input a pile of details before revealing the price, and the purchase screen doesn't list tier costs at all, frustrating even users willing to pay.

product.title: The absorbed Campendium got worse — campers lost their favorite tool
product.minus: Roadtrippers absorbed Campendium and, users say, gutted its data and features: free overnight spots and amenities became hard to find, and the Android version was dropped entirely.

product.title: Constant freezing and crashing — you can only edit a route by restarting
product.minus: The app freezes and crashes when adding a stop or editing a route, forcing dozens of restarts within a single planning session.

product.title: Doesn't work outside the US — Canada, Europe and the UK unsupported
product.minus: Users in Canada, the UK and Europe can't even find their own cities or addresses; the app keeps pushing US locations and is useless abroad.

product.title: No on-road navigation: no Android Auto, no offline maps, no routing
product.minus: After planning, the app won't actually navigate: no Android Auto support, no working offline maps, and you must manually re-enter waypoints into Google Maps one at a time.

product.title: Clumsy editing: stops won't drag, dates wreck the whole route
product.minus: Rearranging stops is painful — dragging fails, adding a stop dumps it at the top, and entering dates auto-rewrites the dates on every other stop.

product.title: A forced AI autopilot that doesn't work and blocks your own planning
product.minus: The new version forces you through an AI autopilot instead of manual planning, and it freezes, errors out, and gives inaccurate suggestions far from your route.

product.title: Stale, incomplete place data — many spots closed, links broken
product.minus: Attraction and campsite data is often outdated: places are closed, links go nowhere, and in-app reviews don't match reality, so users cross-check with Google.

product.title: Not RV-friendly: no way to add your rig, no diesel, no RV routing
product.minus: For its core RV audience, the app lacks the right vehicle in its list, doesn't distinguish gas from diesel, and ignores rig size when routing.

product.title: For loyal fans — the best long-haul, multi-stop trip planner there is
product.plus: Users for whom it works plan multi-week cross-country trips with 150 waypoints, shareable family links, date breakdowns and budgets year after year, and won't travel without it.

product.title: Surfaces offbeat stops along the route you'd never have found yourself
product.plus: When the explore feature works, it reveals quirky roadside curiosities and off-the-beaten-track stops you'd never spot otherwise — the very reason people love it.

product.title: Upgrade pop-ups hit you on every screen
product.minus: Every other tap opens an ad for the paid plan. Users who loved the app for years say the relentless Plus/Peak pop-ups make it nearly unusable and are actively driving them to competitors.

product.title: Once free, now behind multiple paywalls
product.minus: Core features everyone relied on moved behind subscriptions — sometimes two paywalls deep. Building your own route, checking a simple A-to-B path, even seeing the trail map beforehand are all locked, even though the community contributed the data.

product.title: The trail guide is the gold standard for navigation
product.plus: Users' core love: the app keeps you on the trail, warns you of a wrong turn, and gets you out of the woods again and again. Many say they wouldn't hike without it and that it has literally saved them when lost.

product.title: Offline maps are a lifesaver where there's no signal
product.plus: After navigation, the most-loved feature: a pre-downloaded map runs off the phone's GPS with no signal out in the backcountry. Paired with a compass, many call it the reason worth paying for the upgrade.

product.title: Downloaded maps won't open offline — the exact thing you downloaded them for
product.minus: The cruelest bug: arriving at a trail with no coverage, users get "Sorry the trail is no longer available" or grey tiles that never load. The whole point of downloading is to work offline — and that's exactly what breaks, even for paying subscribers.

product.title: Drains battery so hard it's dangerous off-grid
product.minus: The app drains the battery and overheats the phone even in airplane mode with the map already downloaded. One user measured AllTrails eating 41% on the same track where Gaia used 4%. On a multi-hour route with no coverage that's a real safety risk.

product.title: Driving directions send you tens of miles from the trailhead
