product.minus: The "Get Directions" feature to the trailhead reliably dumps you at a random spot or the peak, sometimes 20-40 miles from the real trailhead. For paying users who trusted navigation for years, it's become a persistent bug.

product.title: Activity tracking lies: wrong distance, dropped recording, the drive home logged as the hike
product.minus: Logging is a weak spot: distance is off by half a mile or more, recording starts and stops on its own, there's no easy way to end a hike back at the car — and the whole 65 mph drive home gets logged as part of the hike.

product.title: Cancelling the subscription is a Hotel California maze
product.minus: Cancelling is nearly impossible: the app sends you to the website, the website back to the app, the Cancel button opens a discount offer, and you must click it four times across four screens. People get charged for a full year even after cancelling on time.

product.title: Forced to install the app and make an account just to see a map
product.minus: The website is deliberately crippled to push you into the app, and you can't view a map without signing up. Users call the "to save your bookmarks" excuse a pretext for data collection, and many leave for Organic Maps, Mapy or Hiiker where you can look without an account.

product.title: The community and curated reviews are the irreplaceable value
product.plus: Even angry reviewers concede the app's strength is fellow hikers' notes on trail conditions, elevation gain and technical details. It helps you pick a route to match your experience and mood and know what to expect before setting out.

product.title: Difficulty ratings are misleading — dangerous for the vulnerable
product.minus: Trails marked "easy" or "moderate" turn out brutal: 3 hours become 6 with serious climbing. One disabled user was hurt on an "easy" route and couldn't even warn others — the app won't let you rate a trail's difficulty.

product.title: The category benchmark for finding and planning hikes worldwide
product.plus: Despite the criticism, for many it's the go-to and the category benchmark: a huge trail database, accurate routes, filters by length and elevation, and a 3D route preview. People take it on holidays worldwide and won't head to the mountains without it.

product.title: Point it at the horizon and it names every peak around you
product.plus: When it works, it's magic: you stand on a summit, hold up your phone, and it labels the neighboring peaks. People re-summit mountains they've already climbed just to understand the surrounding topography better.

product.title: On Android it's a pale shadow of the iPhone version
product.minus: The defining pain: people fall in love with the app on a friend's iPhone, buy it on Android, and get a buggy, stripped-down version missing the promised features. The same line repeats over and over: "so much better on iOS".

product.title: Crashes on launch — half the users never even see the app
product.minus: For many, the app crashes on the start screen and never opens at all: the splash shows up and immediately disappears. People reinstall, even switch phones, and still never get to see what it looks like.

product.title: Paid once — and now they demand a subscription
product.minus: People bought the app, then an update locked it behind a subscription: free now means one location per day. Past buyers feel cheated and forced to pay a second time.

product.title: Labels the wrong mountains — and misses the ones right in front of you
product.minus: The core function is unreliable: it finds peaks hundreds of kilometers away that you can't even see, yet fails to name the closest summits in the foreground. The pointer lines are off and the distances are scrambled.

product.title: Photo import and AR overlay are the top crash triggers
product.minus: Two headline features — photo import and the teleport/panorama mode — are especially unstable: photo import crashes the app every time, teleport quits while building the panorama, and the screen just cycles until the battery dies.

product.title: The AR outline shakes and drifts — lining up the mountains is nearly impossible
product.minus: The live overlay has to be matched to the real mountain silhouette by hand, but the outline jitters at the slightest movement and never knows which way it's pointing. An uncalibrated compass and sensors are to blame — you're constantly fighting to keep it aligned.

product.title: The developers actually fix problems and respond
product.plus: When support kicks in, it's surprisingly good: people report fixed crashes, a requested feature added within a week, and thank the developers by name. It pulls their ratings sharply back up.

product.title: Advertised as "free" but priced steeply — it feels like bait
product.minus: The app is marketed as free, but the free version is nearly useless and the real app is locked behind a very expensive subscription. Some users immediately request refunds and call it a scam.

product.title: Constant nags to rate after every photo grate on people
product.minus: After every photo the app immediately begs for a review. The pushy rate-me reminders annoy people enough that they dock a star for it right in the review.

product.title: Claimed offline support is really only half-offline
product.minus: The app promises to work without a signal, but it won't launch in airplane mode and areas must be downloaded in advance — slowly. Exactly in the backcountry, where there's no signal, it lets you down the most.

product.title: Clumsy navigation: no pinch-zoom, fixed angle, blurry 3D
product.minus: Basic map controls are broken: no pinch-zoom, limited zoom-out, and hitting the limit makes the map jump and shift position. There's no tilt, the angle is fixed, and the "HD 3D" comes out blurry on Android.

product.title: The overlay doesn't match the mountains because of the compass — sometimes by 90°
product.minus: The single most common complaint: the peak silhouette is rotated away from what your eyes see, often by 20-30°, sometimes a full 90° or even 180°. Calibrating the compass doesn't fix it, people try three phones of different brands — yet other apps on the same devices have no heading problems.

product.title: When it does line up with reality, it's the magic the whole thing was built for
product.plus: When the heading is right, the reaction is euphoric: it nails distant peaks, helps people get to know the mountains around a new home, settles arguments in unfamiliar terrain. Users say it "just works" and finally answers the question they've been asking for decades — what hill is that?

product.title: One-time payment, no subscription, no ads — loved as a thing in itself
product.plus: The business model is its own reason for praise: pay once, no ads, no in-app purchases, no nagging. Buyers call it "the perfect smartphone app" and recommend it specifically for this.

product.title: Offline use with pre-downloaded data — a lifesaver where there's no signal
product.plus: A key strength for the mountains and the backcountry: download the data once and it works without internet. This is exactly what people who go beyond cell coverage value.

product.title: To figure out what you're looking at, you have to already know what you're looking at
product.minus: The misalignment creates a vicious circle: the only way to align the overlay is to manually anchor it to a peak whose name you already know. That destroys the entire point of the app in new places — exactly where you need it.

product.title: Demands a data download on every launch — and without signal it all stops
product.minus: Even after pre-downloading, the app asks to update on every launch, and without internet — which is precisely when you need it — it won't work. Sometimes the download itself fails after a few percent or hangs on a spinner, leaving the paid product unusable.

product.title: In landscape photo mode the peak labels pile up into an unreadable heap
product.minus: When users rotate the phone to landscape to take a picture, the peak names stack on top of each other and become illegible, and the controls for adjusting the outline get inverted. Reinstalling and switching orientation mode don't help.

product.title: Works worse outside the West: Peru, Nepal, India, Eastern Europe
product.minus: The data coverage is clearly skewed toward Western countries: in Peru, Nepal, India and smaller Eastern-European countries peaks aren't recognized or are labeled inaccurately. Even loyal users admit accuracy drops outside the West.

product.title: The peak silhouette is too smoothed-over and short on detail
product.minus: The horizon rendering draws criticism: clearly jagged peaks look rounded in the app, the silhouette lacks detail, and that makes peaks hard to identify. The thin lines and tiny font are also hard to read under bright sun at altitude.

product.title: Crashes or won't launch on Pixel and newer Samsungs
product.minus: Some users can't even open the app: it crashes on the splash screen on the Pixel 8 Pro or breaks on newer Samsungs. The upside — the developer ships fixes fast, and people later bump their rating back to 5 stars.

product.title: The developer replies fast and actually fixes things — rare-level support
product.plus: When support responds, the impression is strong: a reply within a couple of hours on a Sunday, a concrete fix, fast updates for new phones. It outweighs prior frustration and brings people back to five stars.

product.title: Shows distant giants while missing the peaks right in front of you
product.minus: The peak-selection logic frustrates: the app labels huge summits dozens or hundreds of kilometers away but won't show the lower mountain right in front of you. People want a setting to restrict the horizon distance.

product.title: An indispensable mountain companion — the app people take to every summit
product.plus: For its fans this isn't a toy but a must-have: taken on every summit, used daily on the Great Divide Trail, the first app installed when switching phones. A simple UI with no learning curve and one job done excellently.

product.title: Solid topo maps are the core strength
product.plus: Users single out the quality of the topographic maps themselves as good — it is the reason they keep the app.

product.title: GPS tracking drops out mid-route
product.minus: On the trail the tracking stops correcting GPS tracks without warning, so navigation fails exactly where it matters most.

product.title: Importing tracks from other apps fails
product.minus: Trying to fall back on importing data from a separate GPS logger app also fails — there is no backup path.

product.title: Coverage outside the USA is weak
product.minus: Abroad the maps stop being dependable: in Thailand a user struggles with what works fine inside the USA.

product.title: Sometimes maps don't load at all
product.minus: Some users get no maps at all — the app simply does not work for them, leading straight to an uninstall.

product.title: Price feels too high for what fails to work
product.minus: When the basics fail, the cost reads as clearly too high and becomes the final straw.

product.title: Records your track quietly and reliably, with zero fuss
product.plus: The core reason people love it: drop the phone in your pocket, hit start, and it logs your hike, bike ride or motorbike trip for years without dropping out. Many have used it for years and call it the best tracker they have tried.

product.title: They keep charging after you cancel, even during the free trial
product.minus: The most painful complaint: people cancel and the charges keep coming, sometimes for months. One cancelled during the two-week free trial and was still billed £16.90 for the year; another saw the app insist there was no subscription until an active one suddenly resurfaced.

product.title: The track itself is accurate, but the stats lie
product.minus: It plots the line accurately but the numbers do not match: speed reads nearly half the real value, a 5-minute walk clocks 31 mph, and cumulative ascent gets averaged so descending a hill makes you lose climb. Anyone relying on the figures cannot trust them.

product.title: Works offline and exports tracks even on the free version
product.plus: For the outdoors this is decisive: it records with no internet or signal, and you can export the finished track as GPX/KML without paying. Cyclists and searchers praise having offline maps on hand anywhere and are pleasantly surprised export is free.

product.title: Simple, clean interface with no ad noise
product.plus: Even non-techy users get it fast: a clean, clear screen with no pop-ups or ads. Many call out that it does not drain the battery or eat storage — it just does its job.

product.title: Basic features get locked behind a subscription you did not expect
product.minus: Its free reputation trips on a paywall: you cannot save daily track files or export off-phone without paying, there is no one-time purchase instead of a monthly fee, and you often cannot even try it without signing up for a trial. One user thought they were donating and ended up subscribed.

product.title: A favourite tracker for motorbike, bike and water trips
product.plus: A narrow but passionate crowd: motorbike tourers, motocross riders, cyclists, snowboarders and jet-ski users log every ride for years. They praise easy route sharing, daily stats, and tracking that does not drop out the way motorbike-specific rivals do.

product.title: Stripped-down navigation: no search, no route compare, no profiles
product.minus: Anyone expecting a Google Maps replacement hits gaps: no search bar, no way to compare two routes from A to B, no multiple profiles for different transport modes, no kilometre markers on the map. Users call the UX short-sighted — as if the devs never go into the field themselves.

product.title: Updates break things that used to work
product.minus: Regressions hit the core function: after updates recording turned inaccurate, track length is logged wrong, speed fragments into hundreds-of-metres chunks instead of fine segments, and some now meet "No signal" and "no coordinates" errors where it once recorded cleanly.

product.title: The map is unreadable in town and vanishes offline
product.minus: In town the basemap fails: creeks and roads are undecipherable and labels cover turns. Offline on the road the map disappears entirely, leaving a bare track — awkward for outdoor navigation.

product.title: Privacy fears and fake-review suspicion
product.minus: A chunk of users distrust it: they complain location data is shared with third parties whether you like it or not, call it spyware, and suspect many of the glowing reviews are fake — which undercuts trust in the high rating.

product.title: Used to be free — now everything is behind a paywall
product.minus: Long-time users are furious: features that were free for years (layers, parcel lines, owners) were taken away and locked behind paid tiers. Without paying you're left with "a plain old map", basically Google Maps.

product.title: You can't cleanly cancel — they charge you anyway
product.minus: People cancel inside the trial window or ahead of time — and still get charged. Cancellation is buried, accounts can't be deleted, and refunds don't happen.

product.title: Ownership and boundary data is years out of date
product.minus: The app's core value — who owns the land and where the lines are — only updates every 2-3 years. People go a year and a half without seeing their own parcel; satellite imagery is older than free Google's.

product.title: An update logs you out and demands you pay again
product.minus: After an update the app logs you out, "doesn't recognise" your paid subscription and tries to bill you again. Endless support emails don't fix it.

product.title: Hidden free trial with auto-billing on install
product.minus: Nothing tells you the app is paid until you install it. They demand a card immediately and enrol you in a trial with auto-billing — sometimes without the user even agreeing.

product.title: Nagging upsells to the next tier even after you've paid
product.minus: You pay for one state or Premium, and the app still endlessly teases and pushes you to upgrade to Elite. It annoys even paying users.

product.title: Tracking and waypoints break in the field, off-grid
product.minus: Right when you need it most — out of cell range, in the woods — tracks and waypoints vanish, the screen goes black, offline mode glitches. Trust in the tool collapses.

product.title: Locks you out — login and sign-up errors
product.minus: Many simply can't log in or register: login errors, email/Google/Facebook rejected, codes sent to an old email. Often after switching phones.

product.title: Real-human customer support — the app's biggest plus
product.plus: The most common praise: you reach a real US-based human, no AI bots, fast and patient. They restore lost waypoints, fix billing, explain features — people are won over by it.

product.title: Indispensable navigation: never get lost, always find your truck
product.plus: The loyal core uses it to not get lost in thick woods: drop a pin, track a blood trail, then find your exact way back to the truck or camp. A decade in the wilderness and nobody got lost.

product.title: Parcel boundaries keep hunters on legal land
product.plus: When the data is right, it precisely shows where you may hunt: public/private boundaries, distance from houses, who the owner is. It removes the fear of accidentally trespassing.

product.title: Useful far beyond hunting — all year round
product.plus: Many use it for work, mushrooming, fishing, hiking, scouting property and even finding forgotten cars — and they value the online classes plus the wealth of layers and tools.

product.title: Exporting your own video is locked behind a subscription
product.minus: People spend hours editing and only discover the paywall at the moment of saving — once the work is done and the export button just leads to a subscription screen. It feels like a trap rather than honest monetization.

product.title: Black screen when splitting clips or previewing
product.minus: The most destructive bug: when splitting a clip, adding media or previewing, the picture goes to a black screen while the audio keeps playing. Sometimes footage just disappears inside the project, and only a restart helps.

product.title: Adding music or your own audio requires Pro
product.minus: A basic thing for any video editor — laying a track or your own audio file over a clip — is locked behind a subscription. Users are outraged at paying to use their own files when the phone does it for free.

product.title: Used to be free — now almost everything costs money
product.minus: Long-time users describe a slow decline: features that worked free for years are stripped behind the paywall one by one. The feeling is that the app "became about money, not enjoyment".

product.title: Capped at 2 projects without a subscription
product.minus: The free version allows only a couple of projects/videos before a purchase is required. For anyone editing regularly, this hits a wall almost immediately.

product.title: Constant crashes and freezes while editing
product.minus: The app crashes every few minutes with "something went wrong", especially on longer projects and Chromebooks. It's not just annoying — it threatens hours of lost work.

product.title: Charges, double-billing and a subscription you can't cancel
product.minus: Serious billing complaints: charges after cancellation, double-billing, money taken despite declining the trial, and no way to reach support or cancel.

product.title: Colors wash out: video turns pale or black-and-white
product.minus: After recent updates the app wrecks color on import: clips come out washed out, white-blue or nearly black-and-white. It looks like a problem handling high-resolution video.

product.title: No keyframes, cropping or advanced effects
product.minus: Experienced creators miss tools essential for serious editing: keyframes, graphs, masking, chroma key (green screen), cropping, text animations. There are few effects and they're weak.

product.title: The Android version is noticeably cut down vs iOS
product.minus: Android users complain that features available on iPhone — like the "apply to all" button — are missing for them, yet they're still charged for the meager set that remains.

product.title: Intuitive interface and a gentle learning curve
product.plus: The thing people love most: editing is genuinely simple and pleasant, and you can learn it yourself in minutes. Even those angry at the paywall admit the editor itself is convenient and beginner-friendly.

product.title: Lightweight, fast and gentle on weaker devices
product.plus: Many are won over by how little storage it takes, how fast it runs, and that it handles even HD video on modest phones and tablets — where rivals like InShot buffer.

product.title: Great for montages, clip mashups and stop-motion
product.plus: For concrete jobs — stitching clips, building a photo slideshow to music, making stop-motion or a family video — the app delivers a clean result and is loved by niche creators (Gacha, gameplay, YouTube Shorts).

product.title: Asking for personal info scares people off at the start
product.minus: Users are put off that the app asks for personal information before they've even done anything, which makes them suspicious and ready to walk away.

product.title: Verification codes don't arrive for US phone numbers
product.minus: Sign-in hits an SMS verification step that, per a US user, doesn't work for American phone numbers, leaving them stuck before they can even start.

product.title: Freezes dead on the startup screen
product.minus: On a Samsung S10 the app suddenly stopped working and got stuck on the opening screen; clearing the cache and reinstalling didn't help, even though the phone itself works perfectly.

product.title: Some reviews aren't about this app at all
product.minus: Several reviews are clearly off-topic — about a driver/transfer service and a medical centre — pure noise that says nothing about the editor itself.

product.title: Constant crashes destroy the finished video
product.minus: The most common complaint: the app stops every few seconds, and it tends to crash right when the video is finally done — hours of work vanish and nothing can be exported.

product.title: You pay — and it still doesn't work
product.minus: Users upgrade to premium specifically to fix the problem, but the paid tier behaves identically: won't load photos, won't save, crashes. The sense of wasted money and demands for refunds recur over and over.

product.title: You can no longer add your own music
product.minus: You used to be able to drop in your own tracks — that was removed, leaving only the built-in library. For many it broke the core value: the videos "lost the magic."

product.title: The 60-second cap is infuriating without a subscription
product.minus: Free and even on some paid tiers the video is hard-capped at 60 seconds (and in places just 4 photos). Going longer requires paying — the single most common gripe about limits.

product.title: Opaque tiers and hidden charges
product.minus: The subscription ladder is confusing: Premium turns out to be "basic" and what you need sits in Professional — and you only learn this after paying. Trials charge on day one, and cancelling is made nearly impossible.

product.title: The price is out of line with what you get
product.minus: $20 a month or $120 a year for a phone auto-editor strikes many as absurd when free alternatives abound. The price has climbed over time, and loyal users leave specifically because of it.

product.title: Photo and video import just fails
product.minus: Importing works intermittently: "something went wrong," some files are rejected without explanation, sometimes only 3 of 17 photos load. It blocks the work before editing even begins.

product.title: Support bounces you in a Google ↔ Magisto loop
product.minus: When a billing or subscription issue arises, Magisto sends you to Google and Google sends you back to Magisto. Tickets fail, replies are canned, and loyal multi-year customers are left with nothing.

product.title: Auto-editing doesn't show what you want
product.minus: The headline feature — AI picking the moments — misfires: it chops clips into a chaotic remix and shows the rest instead of the key shots. You end up re-editing by hand anyway, so why pay.

product.title: Brilliantly simple: the AI does it all for you
product.plus: The core love: drop in photos and clips and a couple minutes later you get a polished movie with music and effects, no manual editing. This effortlessness is exactly why people stay for years.

product.title: Years-long loyalty and nostalgia
product.plus: Remarkably rare for an app: people have used it for 8–13 years, leave and come back, keep memories in its cloud. For divorced parents and memory-keepers it's an emotional anchor.

product.title: Polished output and a pleasant interface
product.plus: When it works, people love the result: professional-looking output, a pleasant interface unlike other editors, a good range of filters. Especially praised on the PRO tier.

product.title: Newbie-friendly ease is the core reason people love it
product.plus: Dozens praise figuring it out with zero experience — trimming, stitching, adding text and music without feeling you need to be a tech nerd.

product.title: Years-long loyalty: "my workhorse since 2020"
product.plus: A huge share of reviews come from people who've used it 5-10 years and stay put — it's their go-to for YouTube, Reels and TikTok.

product.title: The free version is genuinely useful — you barely need to pay
product.plus: Many get by on the free tier for years — all the basics are there, and some buy Pro out of gratitude rather than need.

product.title: After updates the app simply stopped working for a chunk of users
product.minus: Former fans report videos won't load after an update, IO errors pop up, even a 6-minute clip won't open — the app has gone "dead" for them.

product.title: The missing "impose"/overlay button enrages even Pro subscribers
product.minus: Android lacks the video-overlay (impose) button that the iPhone version has; people bought Pro for it — and without it the app is useless for reaction videos.

product.title: Constant crashes and freezes mid-edit
product.minus: It crashes, shows "not responding", the screen blacks out — users have to go in and out repeatedly, losing the editing session they already paid for.

product.title: "Lifetime" license vanished — they demand a subscription again
product.minus: People who bought Pro or lifetime access found the features taken away and a yearly subscription pushed instead — to them a flat betrayal of what "lifetime" means.

product.title: Pushy Pro pop-ups and a deceptive nudge for 5 stars
product.minus: Every launch throws up a subscription screen, and a floating menu leaves only a "yes I'll give 5 stars" button — users call it deceptive, plus three ads in a row just to use a tool.

product.title: Export degrades video quality
product.minus: Users complain the picture noticeably worsens after editing, the codec changes, and some lost 1080p 30fps export — a dealbreaker for content.

product.title: Stagnation: no updates, and the features people want are missing
product.minus: Even fans note it isn't evolving — they ask for more music, multi-track audio, fade in/out, picture-in-picture, a proper gallery browser and the desktop/tablet-only features.

product.title: Audio drifts out of sync, and there's no audio extraction
product.minus: Even happy users flag audio-sync problems — some work around it with another app — and ask for audio extraction so it becomes "all in one".

product.title: Storage balloons, and projects vanish when switching phones
product.minus: The app hoards tens to hundreds of gigabytes that can't be located and cleared, and on a new phone — even after a full data transfer — all projects disappear.

product.title: A safe TikTok alternative for kids with strict parents
product.plus: The number-one reason people love it: parents allow Zoomerang where TikTok is banned, and kids call it a safe, fun "kid TikTok".

product.title: Ready-made templates and effects are the main source of fun
product.plus: People love the huge library of templates, trends and filters: find a clip you like, press a button, and make your own video with no editing skills.

product.title: Paywall cuts into basic features — even saving your video
product.minus: The core pain: coins and Pro lock editing, saving and even keeping your own video. Users are furious that you can't save your clip without a subscription — and these are kids with no money of their own.

product.title: Can't log in or sign up — servers and bans
product.minus: A frequent disaster: sign-up and login break down — server errors, expired sessions, verification codes that don't arrive, accounts banned for no reason and gone for good.

product.title: Too many ads
product.minus: A recurring gripe even from high-raters: ads everywhere, and even seeing who viewed your profile demands watching two ads.

product.title: Crashes and freezes eat your finished video
product.minus: A painful pattern: the app crashes or freezes mid-build and all the work is lost — clips fall out of order, nothing posts, hours of filming gone.

product.title: Better than CapCut for simple editing — or just a copy of it
product.plus: Many directly compare it to CapCut and find Zoomerang simpler and more fun thanks to ready templates. But some see the opposite: it's a CapCut clone and CapCut is better.

product.title: Android lags behind iOS on features
product.minus: A steady complaint: Android is missing what iOS has — stories, the new jiggly text animation, longer comments. Android is forever playing catch-up.

product.title: Hard cap on video length — only seconds allowed
product.minus: Fans' top wish: make a full-length video or go live. Clips are capped at 30 seconds / a minute, and extending length only happens by buying coins for a measly 10 seconds.

product.title: Can't post or change your profile picture
product.minus: Even happy users get stuck on the basics: posting spins forever and never publishes, and the profile photo won't change, leaving it blank.

product.title: Support stays silent and fixes nothing
product.minus: A sharp pain for paying users: paid for a subscription and nothing works, emails go unanswered for days, and the reply is "wait" — though a few report being helped quickly.

product.title: The AI pivot disappoints veterans and feels overpriced
product.minus: Long-time users mourn that human-made creative templates were swapped for "AI slop", the app is being pulled toward business, and the AI effects themselves are pricey and weak by a specialist's standards.

product.title: An easy, approachable on-ramp to editing for beginners
product.plus: A genuine strength for newcomers: it teaches editing from scratch, you can film without an account, much is free — and kids make their very first videos.

product.title: Near-zero learning curve — a beginner ships a clip in minutes
product.plus: The thing people praise most: the interface is clear from the first open — you can cut, undo, mute and rearrange without a tutorial. As a first-ever video editor, it's an ideal start.

product.title: The lifetime purchase doesn't survive a new device or a reset
product.minus: The most painful complaint from paying users: they bought "for life", switched phones or reformatted — and the app demands payment again, brings back the watermark, locks pro features. There's no way to move the subscription across devices.

product.title: Hangs and crashes at the worst moment — during the save
product.minus: The app stalls on export, crashes right as you save, kicks you out mid-edit, or dies with a "failed to optimize" error. The finished clip is lost and the work is wasted.

product.title: The paywall hits the basics — letters and the watermark
product.minus: Some users hit a pro wall on the most elementary things: on-screen text, removing the watermark, filters. Being asked to pay right on launch reads as "everything's paid" and drives people off.

product.title: The free version genuinely suffices — export without paying
product.plus: The counterpoint to the paywall gripes: many praise exactly the generous free tier — you can build and export a clip for free, filters are unlocked, your own music works. For some people there's no need to pay at all.

product.title: Audio is the weak spot: it vanishes, distorts, and warps the video
product.minus: A recurring technical pain: the sound disappears after moving to a new phone, distorts slightly on added clips, and sometimes the video itself warps along with the audio.

product.title: Turns amateur footage into something "like a film" — people are proud of the result
product.plus: The core value lives up to the name: people wanted a tool to make their videos look cinematic, and they get quality picture, filters, transitions, voiceover. They praise the output even after years of use.

product.title: A backbone for bloggers and streamers — built for YouTube content
product.plus: A distinct loyal audience — content creators: they cut clips, fails and shorts for YouTube daily and credit this app for their channel and subscriber growth.

product.title: The music library is a copyright trap: the tracks can't be used
product.minus: The built-in music is copyright-protected and unusable for publishing, and some tracks have to be downloaded ahead of time to work offline later. Several users ask for a wider song selection.

product.title: Stumbles on long and heavy videos
product.minus: A clear performance ceiling: clips over 10-30 minutes lag or won't render, and export bloats the file dozens of times over — a 22MB edited video comes out as 1-2GB.

product.title: Export-time ads annoy even satisfied users
product.minus: Even high-rating users complain: every time you export a project, an ad pops up. It's not a blocker, but it's the one thing souring the experience for an otherwise loyal audience.

product.title: Missing PIP, refreshed FX, and next-level tools
product.minus: Power users hit a feature ceiling: they ask for picture-in-picture, audio spectrum, text animation, refreshed FX and AI assistance — the app feels un-updated for a while and is starting to fall behind rivals.

product.title: Ads pop up at every single action
product.minus: The app's defining pain: ads interrupt nearly every editing step, irritating even users who otherwise like the editor.

product.title: A full CapCut replacement without a VPN
product.plus: The top reason users love it: CapCut-level capability without a VPN and without the bloat, which rescued many people's editing workflow.

product.title: Professional effects and transitions out of the box
product.plus: Users rave about the effects, smooth transitions and animations that give an "After Effects" look even to beginners.

product.title: Easy entry for beginners
product.plus: Praised as an editor that's easy to pick up from scratch, letting even inexperienced creators get a decent result fast.

product.title: Pro features unlock by watching ads, not paying
product.plus: A big draw is that the watermark, effects and 4K export can be unlocked by watching a couple of ads instead of paying.

product.title: "Free" turns into paid after the trial
product.minus: Some users feel misled: it's pitched as free, but after a 3-day trial it asks for 39.95, leaving them feeling it's "only about making money".

product.title: Lags and hangs on low-end phones
product.minus: On low-RAM devices the app hangs and bogs the phone down, especially after new features were added, frustrating owners of budget handsets.

product.title: Music cuts out in the middle of editing
product.minus: A concrete workflow bug: audio suddenly stops mid-edit, forcing a restart of the app and breaking the user's flow.

product.title: AI-video upload and export fail with errors
product.minus: Several users hit errors uploading AI videos, removing the watermark, and an "Ad loading fail" screen, leaving core functions simply not working.

product.title: Development feels frozen — no updates for ages
product.minus: Loyal users want new features and stickers (like troll faces) but complain there hasn't been an update in over a year.

product.title: Export quietly drops the video quality
product.minus: Despite a 4K promise, some users notice the finished video comes out lower quality and loses on frame sizing.

product.title: The paywall crept up: what was free yesterday now costs money
product.minus: The single most common complaint: features that were free for years now demand Pro. Users flatly say it «used to be a good-free editing app» and now you «have to pay for everything».

product.title: The pay-gate is hidden until export — after hours of work
product.minus: What stings most is the «trap» mechanic: you spend hours editing with supposedly free elements, and payment is only demanded at export. A tiny Pro icon is hidden so you don't notice.

product.title: Basic actions locked behind Pro: even extracting audio from a video
product.minus: It's not paying itself that enrages people, but that elementary operations got walled off — extracting sound, importing your own audio. Users see it as an insult to common sense.

product.title: Crashes, hangs and won't open — especially after updates
product.minus: Stability is shaky: the app freezes at a load percentage and crashes, and after updates it stops opening entirely, just showing the logo. Multiple updates in a row fail to fix the bug.

product.title: The gallery won't load: phone content has to be «coaxed» in
product.minus: A recurring import bug: the app won't show phone files no matter what permissions it has, and you must leave and re-enter several times before the gallery appears.

product.title: AI tools shoved in your face — and they burn credits without warning
product.minus: Some users hate the AI saturation («EditPilot», story mode): features are pushed, then silently eat hundreds of credits with no confirmation or price warning, and deliver poor results.

product.title: Subscription auto-charges, with cancelling or refunds nearly impossible
product.minus: Billing reads as abusive: a one-time payment attempt turns into a recurring monthly auto-charge that can't be refunded or cancelled — even deleting the account, users say, doesn't stop it.

product.title: Ads and watermark: the free tier costs you time and a CapCut brand
product.minus: Even on the free path you hit ads at export (which waste your time and then don't even work) and a watermark you can't remove without paying.

product.title: Autosave saves your work: nothing lost on a crash or dead battery
product.plus: A favorite among loyal users: autosave catches an app close or a laptop dying mid-edit — you reopen exactly where you left off, with no data loss.

product.title: AI subtitles and auto-captions: hours of manual work vanish
product.plus: The standout practical win for those who stay: auto-captions transcribe speech accurately even through noise, catch words over background screaming, and save hours of weekly manual work.

product.title: Low barrier to entry: a no-experience newbie makes a decent video
product.plus: A core strength is the gentle learning curve: all main tools are upfront, the «import → edit → export» logic is intuitive, and someone who never learned editing quickly gets a decent result.

product.title: Templates and Beat Sync: a finished clip in minutes, beat-matched edits with no fuss
product.plus: Templates load reliably and let you turn out a custom-looking clip in a couple of minutes, while Beat Sync maps clips to the music automatically — rhythmic edits with no manual effort.

product.title: Fast export and smooth playback even with heavy effects
product.plus: Performance gets praised with specifics: a 10-minute 4K video exports in under 4 minutes, and playback stays smooth even with stacked effects and on low-end phones.

product.title: Keyframe animation and velocity effects: pro-grade smooth moves and slow-mo
product.plus: Advanced yet accessible tools: keyframing makes TikTok zooms buttery smooth and velocity edit cleanly smooths slow-mo in Shorts — and it all comes easily even to those who never tried it before.

product.title: One-tap Auto Enhance: dull footage turns bright and «professional»
product.plus: Auto Enhance is loved for instant results: one tap brightens, sharpens and «polishes» footage, turning dull clips into bright, high-quality ones with no manual color work.

product.title: Subscription costs more than the big-name competitors
product.minus: The pricing shocks people: $20 a week when famous services charge $50 a month, plus complaints about Rs.1300 a week on the very first video — users flatly call it overpriced.

product.title: You can't try anything without paying — card required up front
product.minus: No trial: the app demands a credit card before you do anything, and people compare it to being forced to buy a car you weren't allowed to test-drive.

product.title: The 100 signup credits actually let you make a video
product.plus: Against rival apps that claim to be free but aren't, this one hands you 100 credits just for signing up, and a video costs about 29 — enough to genuinely try it out.

product.title: Effortless onboarding: clear and fast on the first try
product.plus: The recurring refrain of the happy reviews is "easy to use": beginners start making videos right away without a struggle, and the interface doesn't scare off first-timers.

product.title: Output praised for realism and "makes whatever you want"
product.plus: When a video lands, people rave about how realistic the content is and that the generator produces exactly what they asked for — a rare hit for AI clips.

product.title: A go-to for storytelling: voiceovers, styles, info videos
product.plus: Content creators value the spread of settings — different voiceovers and styles — and see the app as genuinely needed for stories and informative videos.

product.title: You can't upload your own photos — guts the whole product
product.minus: The lack of personal-photo upload is a dealbreaker for some: without your own source image the app is "just not worth it," and they explicitly ask for the feature.

product.title: Since Sora 2 left, it spits out slideshows instead of video
product.minus: It used to make good video on the Sora 2 engine, but since that shut down it only produces photos with a narration — users call it a slideshow and point to Kling and Veo instead.

product.title: No way to cancel the subscription — they keep charging
product.minus: There's no cancel button in the app: a user emails again and again while money keeps being taken — other apps offer cancellation, and the absence of it is infuriating.

product.title: Generation stalls at 96% and never finishes
product.minus: Videos get stuck pending: one user waited half an hour at 96% and still got nothing, and separately the finished video won't upload to TikTok because of a bug.

product.title: Credits promise one thing, then demand more money
product.minus: The advertised credit price doesn't hold: with 7 credits per scene promised, a user with a balance is still pushed to buy more, and others lose coins without knowing how.

product.title: Clips are too short — 3 seconds a scene
product.minus: Even happy users trip over the length: videos run 3 seconds, and people ask for at least a 3-minute trial so there's something to show.

product.title: Ads promise object removal, but the app can't do it
product.minus: People install after an ad or a Google search showing object removal, watermark removal, or noise cleanup, then find a plain video editor without those features and feel deceived.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and refusals to refund
product.minus: The loudest complaint: cards get charged for a yearly subscription even after cancelling in Google Play, and refund requests get bounced between the app and Google, citing the fine print.

product.title: Trial charges hit immediately and can't really be cancelled
product.minus: The free trial turns into a trap: money is taken almost immediately, while cancellation supposedly takes 30 days, so trying it without paying is effectively impossible.

product.title: Degraded from "the best" to laggy and freezing
product.minus: Long-time users agree: a couple of years ago this was the best mobile editor, but after recent updates it freezes on a single cut, lags frame by frame, and crashes while saving.

product.title: The AI features people came for are broken or gone
product.minus: AI conversion stalls at 99% with "Something went wrong", voice swap won't get past training, and for some the AI video and AI cartoon tools vanished from a paid Pro account.

product.title: An "Enter text here" box bug locks up the whole app
product.minus: A specific recurring bug: opening a project shows a text-input box at the bottom that won't go away and blocks every other tap — restarting the phone and reinstalling don't fix it.

product.title: Audio desyncs on even the simplest cut
product.minus: Even basic trimming breaks sync: the audio drifts off the picture, especially on longer videos, and the app turns laggy and unresponsive.

product.title: Export fails: black frames, import errors, no download
product.minus: Hours of work collapse at the finish line: parts of the clip export as a black screen with audio only, videos import as pictures, import fails with an error, and the finished video just won't download.

product.title: Watermark stays even for paying subscribers
product.minus: Although this is a paid app, the Lightricks watermark lands on every video and doesn't go away even after a year's payment, while support ignores the requests.

product.title: Pro is lost moving iOS→Android, and the Android build is stripped down
product.minus: Switching from iPhone to Android drops the lifetime and Pro purchase, and the Android build itself is missing key features (no-pause audio, auto-captions, effects) that iOS has.

product.title: For the happy ones — powerful yet easy to use
product.plus: When it works, it's praised as one of the best mobile editors: flexible, high quality, with a low learning curve, friendly navigation, and tools like pitch-shifting audio when you change speed.

product.title: Forced sign-up and almost everything locked behind pay
product.minus: Many are annoyed that a mandatory email sign-up is required just to see the interface, that spam follows, and that almost every effect and tool demands a subscription — for a simple editor it feels like overkill.

product.title: Chokes on modern phones and 4K
product.minus: On new flagships (Pixel 10 Pro, S22 Ultra) the app won't process 4K, the preloader freezes forever on high-res footage, and it oddly runs better on older phones and iPhone.

product.title: Android is the abandoned step-sibling of iOS
product.minus: By far the loudest complaint: on iOS it's the reference weather app, but the Android build goes years without updates and ships a fraction of the features. iPhone switchers feel cheated.

product.title: No update since 2023
product.minus: Users literally count versions: iOS is on 6.x while Android is stuck on 2.x since June 2023. The dead update log reads as a signal the project is abandoned.

product.title: The subscription feels like a scam
product.minus: Paying the same price as the full iOS version for an abandoned app feels like theft to many, especially when premium adds no real value.

product.title: Basic features locked behind a paywall — radar and widgets
product.minus: Radar, maps and even widgets — free standard features elsewhere — are locked behind the subscription here, which users find brazen.

product.title: The AI's snark and humor is what users love
product.plus: The single reason people adore the app is the witty, abusive AI character that calls you a meatbag and brightens every launch.

product.title: Forecast accuracy splits users sharply
product.minus: Some praise the accuracy, but many report the app showing sun during pouring rain and temperatures off by 5-10 degrees from reality.

product.title: The widget is useless — empty space, broken refresh, paywalled
product.minus: Even after paying for the widget, users get a huge blank area under the snark quote, no customization, the wrong temperature units, and updates only when the app is opened.

product.title: No notifications — a dealbreaker for a primary weather app
product.minus: The Android build can't send notifications: the app doesn't even appear in the system list or request permission, so it can't serve as a primary weather app.

product.title: Location detection and search are broken
product.minus: The app stubbornly shows New York instead of the user's real location, fails to find GPS, and won't let you set a city manually — fatal for a weather app.

product.title: Vulgar and offensive ad banners
product.minus: The free version surfaces ads for sexbots and hot assassins — wildly out of place in a weather app and unsafe for kids; even after paying to remove ads, banners flash on launch.

product.title: The recent UI redesign helped, but stripped features
product.minus: The long-awaited update refreshed the UI, but many say it removed features (hourly precipitation, secret locations) and at first broke widgets and caused launch crashes.

product.title: The snark sometimes tips into politics and crude offense
product.minus: Some users delete the app over its political jabs, disrespect toward religion, or vulgar audio that blares on launch with no obvious way to mute it.

product.title: Comparing forecast models is the killer feature people stay for
product.plus: What hooks the pros: you can line up different weather models side by side and decide which to trust — something ordinary weather apps just don't offer.

product.title: The go-to tool for sailors, fishermen and pilots
product.plus: For anyone whose life and work hinge on weather at sea and in the air, Windy is the benchmark: timing sailing passages, offshore fishing, flight planning.

product.title: It saves lives during typhoons and cyclones
product.plus: In tropical regions the app works as a personal early-warning system: people track typhoon paths and prepare ahead where official services fall short.

product.title: Accuracy increasingly disagrees with reality — especially on wind
product.minus: The most painful complaint: wind is consistently underreported and temperature and rain miss the mark — for people paying premium precisely for accuracy, it guts the whole point.

product.title: The free tier has been gutted to a useless static map
product.minus: Long-time users are furious: things that used to be free — forecasts, zooming into your own area, hourly forecasts — moved behind the paywall, leaving the free app "no better than a static map."

product.title: The subscription feels overpriced and like money down the drain
product.minus: Prices have been raised repeatedly and many don't see what they're paying for: for occasional use, or where the forecast misses anyway, premium feels like overpaying — and they don't renew.

product.title: The 'my location' button vanished — and it drives people up the wall
product.minus: An update removed the familiar feature that showed your own spot on the map: now people have to hunt for themselves on every open, and the pleas to bring the button back keep coming.

product.title: Updates bring blank screens, crashes and a bloated UI
product.minus: Recent updates broke the app for some: grey/blank screens, constant crashes, half-screen popups and a "bloated" menu instead of the old simplicity.

product.title: Support goes silent — even on paying subscribers
product.minus: When something breaks there's no one to reach: emails go unanswered for months, and the canned "email support" reply reads like a bot brush-off.

product.title: Forced accounts and a too-dark heat palette annoy users
product.minus: Two distinct irritants: you're now forced to create an account or enable location just to save favorites, and the map renders extreme heat as near-black, which confuses and angers people.

product.title: Depth of data and gorgeous visualization — that's the love
product.plus: Even skeptics admit it: more layers, models and weather parameters than you'll ever need, and the animated wind and rain maps look stunning and read at a glance.

product.title: No plain written forecast — just maps and graphs
product.minus: The paradox of a powerful weather tool: for all its data there's no simple written "take an umbrella" forecast anywhere, and users are literally calling for AI to generate one.

product.title: Full-screen ads with fake close buttons you can't dismiss
product.minus: The dominant complaint: full-screen ads pop up after every tap, and the close "X" is fake — tapping it dumps you into the app store or the advertised site. Often there's no way to close the ad at all, forcing a force-stop and restart of the app.

product.title: Ads stand between you and the radar during dangerous weather
product.minus: What stings most is that an ad fires exactly when you urgently need the radar with a tornado or storm closing in. Users say the app puts advertising ahead of access to life-saving information, and in a dangerous moment that's unacceptable.

product.title: The paid account keeps logging you out — you pay and still see ads
product.minus: Premium+ subscribers report the app logs them out several times a day, and after each logout it shows the ads they paid to remove. Reinstalling and removing battery restrictions doesn't fix it.

product.title: Forecast accuracy has dropped — especially rain and temperature
product.minus: Long-time users note the forecast no longer matches reality: it shows "no rain" while it pours, the temperature is off by several degrees, and an 80% rain chance contradicts a totally dry hourly view.

product.title: Once-free features moved behind a paywall — including the widget and alerts
product.minus: People who bought the app or premium years ago lost widgets, hourly forecasts, the persistent status-bar temperature, and even lightning tracking — all locked behind a new Premium+ tier. It reads as plainly taking away what was already paid for.

product.title: The widget and status-bar temperature won't refresh without manually opening the app
product.minus: The whole point of the widget is a glance, but it shows stale data until you open the app itself. The status-bar and lock-screen temperature also freezes, sometimes showing a blank value or an icon instead of degrees.

product.title: The app freezes, won't open, and the support "fix" is always reinstall
product.minus: Users report slow loading (over 30 seconds), white screens, freezes, and having to force-kill the app several times a day. The standard support reply — "reinstall and allow everything" — frustrates many and doesn't help.

product.title: Data harvesting, telemarketing, and forced account creation
product.minus: Some users are outraged by how much data the app collects and sells to third parties — dozens of brokers fire telemetry on every launch. It forces account creation and cookie consent, and after installing, some started getting spam calls and texts.

product.title: Minute-by-minute rain forecast (MinuteCast) is what keeps people loyal
product.plus: The standout strength: minute-level accuracy, especially the next-hour rain forecast. Users plan walks, motorbike rides, and outdoor work around it and say MinuteCast is reliably more accurate than their local meteorologist.

product.title: Pinpoint local accuracy and depth of data — the reason for long-term loyalty
product.plus: Happy users praise accuracy for their exact location (not the next town over) and the depth of data: radar, air quality, allergens, humidity, dew point. For painters, farmers, and hobby meteorologists it's a working tool trusted for years.

product.title: A long logo animation at startup that can't be turned off
product.minus: An added logo animation drags out launch: you have to wait just to see the weather. Premium subscribers are also greeted by a "celebration" Premium+ congratulation animation, with no way to disable it.

product.title: Lightning alerts are too loud and intrusive, with no volume control
product.minus: The lightning alert sound is alarmingly loud, especially through earbuds, with no way to lower it. On top of that a notification fires for every single strike — during a storm the phone buzzes every few minutes, driving people to delete it.

product.title: Critical alerts don't arrive — tornado warnings paywalled or just silent
product.minus: The most dangerous failure: people don't get tornado warnings even with sirens blaring and storms all around. Some life-saving alerts are locked behind the paywall, and government alerts only show up sometimes — the app can't be relied on in an emergency.

product.title: Spam of irrelevant news and non-weather alerts
product.minus: The app pushes notifications about things unrelated to local weather: news stories, a "red alert for blight," messages about deaths in another country. Turning these off in settings doesn't work, even though people try.

product.title: The week starts on Sunday, with no option for Monday
product.minus: A small but nagging UI limitation: in the daily forecast the week is hard-coded to start on Sunday, with no option to switch to Monday — awkward for those who treat Monday as the start of the week.

product.title: Accuracy from local personal weather stations is the main selling point
product.plus: Users come back for years specifically for the reliability: the app pulls data from registered nearby stations, and the forecast for their area beats competitors and the phone's built-in weather.

product.title: The vanished location pin on the radar is a widespread pain point
product.minus: After an update the dot showing where you are on the radar map disappeared; even tapping the location icon doesn't help. For travelers and for judging your position relative to a storm it's critical — some call it dangerous and a reason to delete the app.

product.title: Radar and maps with fronts and precipitation are a beloved feature
product.plus: The maps with radar, surface fronts, and storm tracking help users plan ahead and see incoming weather; the radar tracking feature is called awesome.

product.title: Ads flood the screen and cover the weather itself
product.minus: Ads stuck at the top can't be dismissed, and for some users banners cover the entire page — a weather app is pointless if you can't see the weather, and some uninstall over it.

product.title: Years-long loyalty: "my go-to for 10+ years"
product.plus: A huge share of five-star reviews come from decade-long users who tried other apps and keep coming back; for many it's the only weather app left on their phone.

product.title: The future-radar forecast was removed or locked behind a subscription
product.minus: You used to scroll the radar forward to see what was coming; now the map only shows the past 1-2 hours up to now, and some don't get future radar even with a premium subscription — for many that was the headline feature.

product.title: Saved locations vanish and the app crashes more often
product.minus: Users lose all their saved locations overnight — repeatedly — and after updates the app starts crashing regularly even after reinstalling, which never used to happen.

product.title: Depth of data: graphs, almanac, pressure, your own weather station
product.plus: Power users love the depth: temperature graphs, barometric pressure, sun and moon rise/set times, the ability to connect your own weather station, and drilling into detail when you want it.

product.title: Slow loading and freezes ruin everyday use
product.minus: The app takes 5-6 seconds to load, and sometimes won't load weather data for 5-10 minutes; it fully reloads when defocused, and users end up switching to another app rather than waiting.

product.title: Uncontrollable notifications fire for no reason
product.minus: Dozens of pointless notifications a day — sometimes just because you opened the app, with no weather alert at all; there's no setting for which alerts you get, and sounds fire seemingly at random.

product.title: The redesigned interface became cluttered and less usable
product.minus: After the redesign long-time users complain it's clunky and unintuitive: hard to find the switch between hourly, weekly, and 10-day forecast, the display is overwhelming, and they liked the old version better.

product.title: The paid subscription doesn't deliver and takes money for nothing
product.minus: After buying premium, people don't get the promised data — future radar, front information — or stay stuck on basic; paying for a 15-day forecast feels pointless when even today's can be wrong.

product.title: They removed the radar widget — the app's main, namesake feature
product.minus: The June update stripped the live-radar home-screen widget — the exact reason most people installed the app. A mass exodus: "it's in the bloody name", "the only reason I had this app". Many uninstall on the spot.

product.title: The widget wasn't dropped — it was paywalled, and users call it greed and a scam
product.minus: A free feature was moved to premium with no notice — users call it "scummy", "greedy goblins", and bail before anything else gets stripped. The subscription is also sold per-platform without transparency.

product.title: Radar accuracy is what users genuinely love, year after year
product.plus: The top praise is real local accuracy: "hasn't let me down in 7 years", "scary accurate" rain radar. People rely on it for weather decisions for years.

product.title: It keeps people safe in real severe weather — tornadoes, hurricanes, tsunamis
product.plus: Not just casual weather: people shelter in their cellar by this radar during tornadoes, track hurricanes, and get tsunami warnings while travelling. For many it's a genuine safety tool.

product.title: The ads are intrusive and outright inappropriate
product.minus: Not just monetization noise: complaints about pornographic ads, near-nude women, content that looks like human trafficking, and "investing" spam. People uninstall specifically over this.

product.title: Clean visuals and layer controls make the radar the best-looking for many
product.plus: For those who don't hit the bad ads, the graphics win praise: smooth hi-res radar, a beautiful map, layers easy to toggle. Some note ads don't bother them at all.

product.title: The forecast is the weak spot: strong radar data, confusing prediction
product.minus: The app's strength is real-time radar, but the actual forecast is called hard to understand, frequently off, and clumsy in the UI. People miss a future-radar and a predicted storm path.

product.title: Updates wipe settings and break paid purchases
product.minus: Frequent weekly updates reset layers and notifications, and paid "no ads" plus hurricane tracking stop working even after "restore purchases". Reinstalling is painful — the setup is complex.

product.title: Years of loyalty — it's people's go-to app for years on end
product.plus: A huge share of reviews come from long-time users: 7, 10, 12 years on one app, recommending it to friends, always coming back after trying others. Useful to truckers, cyclists, storm spotters.

product.title: Notifications are unmanageable and the app shuts without permissions
product.minus: Notification spam can't be filtered by category — it's all or nothing. And without notification and location permission the app simply closes when opened from the widget.

product.title: The free tier is generous — radar, alerts, and even space stuff
product.plus: Even without a subscription you get a lot: radar every 10 minutes, instant flash-flood alerts, forecasts, earthquakes, plus Mars and Moon views. For many it's more than enough.

product.title: The radar widget was buggy even before removal — stale and self-vanishing
product.minus: Even while it existed, the widget misbehaved: showed radar 12+ hours old, went blank when enlarged, and vanished and reappeared on its own. Clearing cache and restarting didn't help.

product.title: Zero ads is the number-one reason people switch
product.plus: Over and over, people name the absence of ads as the deciding factor: the forecast opens instantly with no fullscreen video before you can see it, and they leave WeatherBug, AccuWeather and The Weather Channel for exactly this.

product.title: The forecast routinely contradicts the sky outside
product.minus: The most painful complaint: under a clear sky the app shows rain or thunderstorms, and during a drought it paints precipitation every hour. People say outright they can't plan their day even a night ahead, and they blame the data, not the design.

product.title: A beautiful, clean interface with graphs instead of a column of numbers
product.plus: Design and presentation are a love affair of their own: a clean layout, readable temperature and precipitation graphs, and landscape backgrounds that shift with the time of day. For many, this visual clarity beats the "bunch of numbers" rivals throw at them.

product.title: Picking your data provider is a built-in feature
product.plus: The ability to switch between several weather providers is prized in its own right: you can pick the most accurate one for your area and compare forecasts. For many it's a rare feature the big rivals don't offer.

product.title: Rich, highly configurable widgets
product.plus: Dozens of widgets in different information configurations are a point of pride. You can surface only what you want (temp, humidity, precipitation) without the date or time, and the widgets refresh reliably.

product.title: The radar and precipitation map miss real rainfall
product.minus: Separately from the forecast, people complain about the radar: it shows activity where there's none, and the reverse — light rain during a downpour. Switching providers doesn't help, which undermines trust in the map regardless of source.

product.title: Free and donation-funded — people want to pay anyway
product.plus: The "free, donate if you want" model earns rare gratitude: users volunteer to donate and thank the developer personally, while a small contribution unlocks all providers. It reads as a product built "to help humanity."

product.title: It fails to warn about tornadoes and severe danger
product.minus: The most dangerous failure: people sit under a tornado warning or in an actual tornado while the app stays silent. For a weather service a missed storm alert isn't cosmetic — it's grounds to uninstall on the spot.

product.title: Light on battery and doesn't hog the background
product.plus: After apps that drained the battery and ate hundreds of megabytes on a single trip, Weawow feels light: fast startup, minimal permissions, no resource hogging and no background tracking.

product.title: Data depth that rivals paid "premium" features
product.plus: For weather nerds the app delivers on detail: a two-week precipitation forecast, an air-quality index with a graph, moon phases, sun data, and an interactive map where you tap any point — all without the paywall the big services put on it.

product.title: Data gaps: no pollen, no lightning, no watch app
product.minus: Even happy users list what's missing: no pollen data for allergy sufferers, no lightning-strike alerts, and no companion watch app. For part of the audience this closes off the very scenarios they install a weather app for.

product.title: Recent bugs: frozen temperature and broken location
product.minus: Longtime fans hit regressions: the temperature "freezes" for the whole day after switching units from F to C, the forecast stops updating, and GPS clings to an outdated address system. People stress it "used to work great" — these are new breakages.

product.title: Finger-swipe weather animation is the single reason people love it
product.plus: Scrubbing temperature, wind, precipitation and cloud maps with a finger to watch fronts move through time is the thing that keeps people for years and makes them call it the best weather app.

product.title: Forecast is off: "shows pouring rain while the sky is cloudless"
product.minus: A recurring complaint: the radar and models paint rain and storms when it's dry and clear outside (or the reverse), often wildly off — which guts the whole point of a "forecast" app.

product.title: A hands-on developer who replies personally and fixes bugs — but it's one person
product.plus: People value that the author (Duane) answers support himself, fixes issues fast and builds the app "for himself" — a rare kind of human touch and trust in this category.

product.title: No ads, no trackers — ethical privacy as a brand value
product.plus: A love-letter in itself: no ads, no trackers, no needless data collection — for many that alone is reason to buy Pro out of gratitude rather than need.

product.title: The widget is a favorite feature, but updates keep breaking it
product.minus: The widget is praised for packing a lot into a small space, yet after updates it stops auto-refreshing, throws size errors, or breaks under Android 15 — a once-stable feature turned into a source of frustration.

product.title: A blank blue void: data just stops loading
product.minus: A painful failure mode: instead of a map and forecast there's an empty blue void, and refreshing, reinstalling or rebooting the phone fixes nothing; for longtime users it drags on for days.

product.title: Steep learning curve: powerful, but it scares newcomers off at the door
product.minus: The interface isn't a "normal" weather app but a model toolkit: without reading the help, people can't decode the wavy lines, colors and symbols, can't find basics, and bail within minutes. Fans counter: once you get it, you never go back.

product.title: Many models and raw data straight from met services — a geek's paradise
product.plus: A core strength for enthusiasts: choosing between ECMWF, NOAA, HRRR, NAM, GFS, CMC and comparing models by season and location — Pro adds high resolution and frequent updates, and people consider it a fair price.

product.title: Indispensable for planning outdoor activities
product.plus: The loyal core are those who plan hikes, cycle rides, fishing, sailing and boating trips, storm chasing and typhoon tracking by it: the radar overlays and 10-16 day forecast genuinely drive their decisions.

product.title: Version 4 killed what people loved in v3: new graphics are "uncomfortable for the eyes"
product.minus: Longtime users roll back to v3.424: the new cloud animation feels foggy and jerky, the wind scale got clipped, and the bloated interface gets called "visual diarrhea" — updates degrading what already worked.

product.title: Subscription instead of one-time buy — plus the threatened radar removal
product.minus: A sore spot for veterans: a once-paid upgrade "vanished" into an annual model, Pro features are subscription-only, the free tier refreshes just four times a day, and worst of all — the announced removal of radar data by January 2026 in an app with "Forecast" in its name.

product.title: A "Stand with Ukraine" banner in a weather app angers part of the audience
product.minus: A notable niche gripe: users are irritated by a political banner inside a weather app and ask it to go back to neutral — to them it sits outside the product's job.

product.title: Missing basics: "feels like", alerts and auto-refresh
product.minus: Even fans flag gaps versus a regular weather app: no "feels like", no severe-weather push alerts, and the forecast doesn't refresh on open — you have to hit "refresh" manually.

product.title: The developer's rude replies to criticism push people away
product.minus: The flip side of the "hands-on author": some users find the developer's replies to criticism arrogant and rude, even accusing them of "threats" via a star rating — and it becomes a reason to leave.

product.title: Full-screen video ads hijack the app and make it impossible to use
product.minus: Full-screen ads pop up every few seconds, with a timer, sound and often from Temu — you can't close them, can't get through settings, and many uninstall before they ever get to see whether the app is any good.

product.title: The radar lies: shows rain where it's dry, and dry where it's pouring
product.minus: The map shows a downpour when the sky is clear and misses real rain or even a typhoon — accuracy has become wrong "not sometimes, always," which defeats the entire point of a radar app.

product.title: Accurate rain start/stop forecasting is the core reason people love it
product.plus: When the radar works, it accurately shows incoming rain ahead of time and tells you when and how hard it'll hit — invaluable for cyclists, motorcyclists and anyone planning their day and work around the weather.

product.title: Subscription dark patterns: free trials charge you with no refund
product.minus: The "accept" button on the free trial charges you without consent, the trial silently bills you for a whole year, and the promised one-week refund never comes — a textbook subscription scam.

product.title: The radar widget and server connection constantly break
product.minus: The radar widget throws "Connection Error" for months, a server error blocks the radar for whole countries, and even reinstalling doesn't fix it — all while many of these users are paying.

product.title: False rain push notifications that can't be turned off
product.minus: The app fires rain alerts when there's no trace of rain on the radar or in the sky, spams bogus flood warnings twice a day, and gives no way to switch them off — the notifications become pure noise.

product.title: Paying doesn't fix things — features keep moving behind new paywalls
product.minus: Even premium users get a slow, inaccurate app, and previously paid features get clawed back: the radar horizon was cut to 25 minutes, AQI was locked behind a subscription — people feel cheated after paying.

product.title: Intrusive data collection and dozens of third-party trackers with no easy opt-out
product.minus: The app contacts up to 25 "companies" in the background, shares location with third parties, and disabling it means manually unchecking hundreds of vendors — enough for many to uninstall on sight.

product.title: Radar coverage gaps: whole regions and countries simply aren't covered
product.minus: Across Africa, islands and parts of Asia there's either no radar at all or it misses much of the local Doppler network — the app is useless exactly where people hoped to rely on it most.

product.title: Best-in-Europe detail: Doppler velocities for enthusiasts and radar history
product.plus: For weather enthusiasts it's the best app out there: one of the few with Doppler velocities for the EU, deep radar history (6 hours free, up to 48 on premium) and unique detail for planning.

product.title: Post-update degradation: lag, overheating and battery drain
product.minus: Recent updates break what worked for years: the animation stutters, maps won't scroll, the phone overheats, and the app eats 10% of the battery a day — long-time users say the tool got "over-engineered" to death.

product.title: Clean interface and widgets — for the lucky ones without bugs
product.plus: Those who get past the bugs love the simple, intuitive interface, the tidy home-screen widgets, and how much even the free version offers — several call it the best weather app available.

product.title: The $19.99 → $79.99 yearly price jump feels like betrayal
product.minus: A 4x jump in the yearly price with no new features is the number-one reason for mass cancellations; people who paid for years are unsubscribing and calling it a rip-off.

product.title: What used to be free is now behind a paywall
product.minus: Basic things — future radar, forecasts beyond a few hours, world weather — were gradually pulled from the free tier and locked behind a subscription, even though they used to be open to everyone.

product.title: Weather and radar accuracy has visibly degraded over the past couple of years
product.minus: Long-time users say the forecast and radar have started getting it wrong: rain is promised when there is none, the radar lags real time, and the location drifts miles off.

product.title: Accurate forecasting — what people genuinely love it for
product.plus: For those it works for, this is the most accurate and trustworthy weather app they have: truckers, pilots, contractors and fishermen rely on it for planning for years and find it more accurate than local TV.

product.title: Indispensable for those whose work and safety depend on weather
product.plus: Truckers, RV campers, roofers, mobile mechanics and people in hurricane country use it daily to plan routes and get storm warnings — literally as a survival tool.

product.title: The lightning tracker has been broken for over a year
product.minus: Many paid specifically for the lightning map — and it has shown no strikes for a year or more despite claims it was fixed; for fishermen and outdoor workers this is a critical loss.

product.title: Lifetime and one-time purchases suddenly stop being recognized
product.minus: People who bought a "lifetime" license or pro years ago now get hit with subscription demands again; what they paid for simply stops being recognized, sometimes repeatedly.

product.title: Full-screen ads intrude at the worst possible moment
product.minus: Long unskippable video ads with sound launch even during severe-weather and tornado warnings, when life and safety are on the line; a couple of taps and you're back in the ads.

product.title: A subscription wall with no close button traps the app
product.minus: The subscription screen pops up the moment you open the app, often with no visible close button; even tapping a storm alert leads to a subscribe wall, forcing you to force-kill the app.

product.title: Charges after cancellation and no way to unsubscribe
product.minus: Users cancel and still get charged; there is nowhere in the app to cancel, money keeps draining even after uninstalling, and refunds are refused.

product.title: Charging for "NOAA" data that is public domain
product.minus: Many are angry at the very idea of charging for NOAA data that taxpayers funded and that other apps offer for free; on top of that it's "not actually NOAA" but a third-party wrapper.

product.title: Hangs on "fetching data" exactly when it's needed most
product.minus: The app gets stuck on the loading screen and an endless "fetching data" spinner, or falsely claims no internet — often in the middle of a hurricane, while other apps work fine.

product.title: Asked to rate and buy premium before you've even used it
product.minus: Right after install, before opening any feature, the user is hit with an upgrade-to-premium demand and a request to leave a review — which reads as a scam and ruins the first impression.

product.title: Skyla AI assistant is forced on with no way to turn it off
product.minus: A recent update added the floating Skyla AI chatbot icon that can't be dismissed or hidden; users keep saying "it's a weather app, why does it need AI" and threaten to uninstall unless a toggle appears.

product.title: Ads take over the screen and block access to the weather
