product.title: You only see the price after messaging — no filtering by cost
product.minus: There are a million filters except the one that matters — price. The total only shows after you message the sitter, so with multiple pets you can't budget without messaging people just to cancel.

product.title: Support is an AI wall of copy-paste replies
product.minus: On any problem support is either a "real person" who turns out to be a bot, or the same canned reply on a loop. Cases get closed, future emails get ignored, and reviews get identical boilerplate responses.

product.title: Accounts get banned for no reason — and income vanishes
product.minus: A profile suddenly disappears from search or gets blocked with no explanation, sometimes before setup is even done. Be honest about a bite or a sick pet and the whole account is closed; appeals hit a wall of "it's our policy".

product.title: When something goes wrong with the pet, Rover washes its hands
product.minus: The advertised "Trust & Safety" collapses in a real emergency: a dog gets attacked, a sitter extorts money, a pet is left caged. Sitters are deemed contractors, claims go unpaid, and the ability to leave a negative review is removed.

product.title: Can't log in, and the app is "incompatible" with an older phone
product.minus: Login works in the browser but the app loops "invalid email or password" on every device. After updates the app declares older phones incompatible, cutting the sitter off from bookings and earned money entirely.

product.title: Calendar and bookings can only be edited one day at a time
product.minus: Availability has to be set day by day — you can't apply the same hours across a week or different dog sizes per service. Once a booking is accepted you can't change it, or it flips into a "host cancel".

product.title: Deleting your account is deliberately made nearly impossible
product.minus: There's no delete button in the app — only a multi-page quest on desktop. Removing card and personal data is just as hard, and it reads as a deliberate trick to keep users from leaving.

product.title: Sitters bail at the last minute, and the calendar lies
product.minus: Sitters marked "available" agree and then cancel right before the date or go MIA, leaving the owner with no pet care. There's no way to gauge real reliability from a profile beforehand.

product.title: When it works, it's an easy way to find care fast
product.plus: Complaints aside, many value the core: profiles with reviews, last-minute booking, check-in/out notifications. You can go where the pet can't and still feel at ease.

product.title: For a sitter it can become a real career and income
product.plus: Those who commit reach the top of their city, get so many requests they have to turn people down, and make substantial income. The platform genuinely brings clients and pays out.

product.title: The app hangs on the splash screen and won't load for weeks
product.minus: The single most common complaint: on launch the app shows a blue splash screen with a dog and logo — and goes no further. People reinstall, clear cache, switch phones, but for months see only «down for maintenance» or an endless spinner.

product.title: Logging in is an endless loop of «ruh roh» errors
product.minus: You can't use the app without signing in — but login constantly fails with «something went wrong» or «ruh roh», even after repeated password resets. Often it forces you to log in every few minutes or on every open.

product.title: Booking grooming and vet appointments can't be completed
product.minus: The «schedule appointment» button does nothing, the screen freezes, and the form loops you in circles: you fill in the pet profile, it dumps you back to the same screen with empty fields. Stores lose booked customers; people end up booking by desktop or phone.

product.title: Search returns a blank screen with no images or products
product.minus: You search for food — the app says «N results» but shows a blank screen with numbers down the left edge and nothing clickable. Product images don't load, so without the exact name you can't find anything.

product.title: The app hijacks the browser — so why have it at all?
product.minus: Once installed, the app blocks the website: tapping a product in the browser force-launches the app, while signing in «in the app» opens a web page. It's a closed loop, and many say the site works fine and the app is pointless.

product.title: Brutal slowness: loading screens are an exercise in patience
product.minus: Every action — opening a product, the cart, checkout — takes forever, regardless of network, and has dragged on for years with no fix. Often it's faster to get in the car and drive to the store than to wait on the app.

product.title: Vital Care: they say it's cancel-anytime, then lock you in for a year
product.minus: Store staff promise Vital Care is cancel-anytime, but support says it's a one-year contract with no early exit and the card can't be removed. The cancel tab also often won't load — some keep paying $10/mo for another 11 months.

product.title: Rewards get lost: a 3-coupon cap and points that expire fast
product.minus: The loyalty program frustrates as much as the bugs: points must be manually «claimed», they expire fast, and the app won't let you apply more than three rewards at once. In-store purchases aren't tracked, and people lose tens of dollars.

product.title: Items are «in stock» — until you reach checkout
product.minus: The app shows items as available, lets you add them to cart, then at checkout or after payment reveals they're out of stock — orders get cancelled for no reason. Online prices are also higher than in-store, which feels deceptive.

product.title: After checkout you get pushed credit cards and third-party offers
product.minus: After finishing an order for pet food, users get pitched an airline credit card, Sirius XM or AAA. It reads as unprofessional and «scam-like», and push notifications constantly nudge you to spend more.

product.title: The pet profile is useless — the data isn't saved
product.minus: The app makes you build a pet profile but then makes you re-enter the same info for every appointment. Pets can't be removed via the app, birthdays shift by a day, and there's no vet history — people ask for a separate Vetco app.

product.title: When it works — a convenient «store-nearby in one place»
product.plus: For loyal customers the value is real: order in-app and pick up in store, same-day delivery, checking stock before a trip, barcode-scan to re-buy and price-matching. Many call it «the best of both worlds».

product.title: Vital Care discounts and rewards genuinely save money — when they land
product.plus: Those for whom the program works praise the tangible savings: rewards on repeat food purchases, member discounts, three-day hold on online orders. Some users even flipped their rating from 1 to 5 after updates fixed the rewards bugs.

product.title: Stores and staff rescue what the app drops
product.plus: Again and again people separate a great in-store experience from a failing app: friendly staff who know their dogs by name, help with new breeds, grooming and Vetco vet services. The store often fixes what the app broke.

product.title: The app crawls: every action takes minutes
product.minus: The single most common pain is brutal slowness. Opening hangs, taps register after 15-20 seconds, and booking a visit that should take three minutes stretches to 15-45. People say it's faster to just call the clinic than wait for the app to respond.

product.title: White screen of death: the app just won't open
product.minus: For a huge share of users the app simply won't launch — a blank white (sometimes black) screen appears on tap and nothing else. Reinstalling, clearing cache, restarting the phone don't help; the only fallback is the website.

product.title: The update broke everything: what worked, stopped
product.minus: Many pin the breakage to a specific update: appointments vanished, records won't open, buttons stopped responding. The refrain is "undo the update" — it used to work, and the redesign killed it.

product.title: Buttons hide behind the Android navigation bar
product.minus: A textbook layout miss: the app's bottom nav sits underneath Android's system buttons (Pixel, Samsung, Motorola). Profile, calendar icons and the chat box are physically covered — untappable, leaving the app half-dead specifically for Android users.

product.title: Endless password reset: login is impossible
product.minus: After the update the app repeatedly demands a new password, then rejects every compliant one with "something went wrong." People do 4-5 resets and give up — there's simply no way into the account.

product.title: Records and documents unavailable right when needed
product.minus: The core feature — the pet's medical history — fails: records often don't display, and downloads sit "pending" for a day then reset to nothing. The absurd result: to learn your own pet's data you still have to phone the clinic.

product.title: Booking collapses at the final screen
product.minus: Even when it loads, booking itself is unreliable: it offers slots that don't exist, can't find the right clinic, freezes on the last step or throws "something went wrong" — and the clinic later says the booked slot was never open.

product.title: You can't pay the plan in-app — it bounces you to the website
product.minus: Many keep the app for one thing — paying the Wellness plan — and that's exactly what fails: the pay link goes to the website, which links to another website. After the update in-app payment vanished entirely, leaving only autopay.

product.title: You can't properly edit the pet profile
product.minus: Basic editing is missing: you can't fix a birthday, weight or microchip, add a new pet by ID, or remove an ex's name from the account. The app also keeps deselecting your pet on the dashboard and forgetting entered info.

product.title: The in-clinic doctors and staff are genuinely loved
product.plus: Against the hatred of the app, the Banfield clinics themselves draw warm 5-stars: doctors and techs treat pets as their own, call back after visits, are gentle with anxious and "spicy" animals, and support owners through the hardest goodbyes.

product.title: When it works, a handy hub for records and booking
product.plus: The minority for whom the app launches value the concept: everything in one place — records, visit history, booking, med refills, specialist chat. Booking without waiting for the clinic to open and 24/7 access to data are genuinely convenient.

product.title: The Wellness plan: a great idea with a dark side of cancellation and charges
product.minus: The Optimum Wellness Plan is praised as a cheaper alternative to insurance, but cancelling becomes a trap: charges continue after autopay is turned off, owners are billed for the "rest of the year" — even after the pet has died. Some flatly call it a scam.

product.title: Years of free records suddenly locked behind a paid subscription
product.minus: People kept free records for years, then access to their own data was shut behind a subscription. Users feel betrayed: they were promised "free forever" and now their pets' history is held hostage.

product.title: Free plan cut to one pet — the rest of the data is lost
product.minus: In multi-pet households the free version now shows only one pet. The other profiles with all their history are simply inaccessible — and that was the main reason people chose the app.

product.title: The October 2023 update wiped or corrupted accumulated data
product.minus: After moving to the new version records transferred only partially, with wrong dates, or vanished entirely — vaccines, medications, weight. People lost years of medical history with no warning and no way to export.

product.title: Reminders stopped firing — and that's the whole reason for the app
product.minus: Notifications for deworming, vaccines and medications no longer fire. People miss critical treatments and fall back to handwritten notes or Google Calendar — the core function failed.

product.title: The new version is slow, crashes constantly and logs you out
product.minus: Every page takes 20 seconds to load, the app freezes, crashes on login and keeps logging you out. Opening it to quickly check something at the vet is now impossible.

product.title: Tasks don't save and are sorted backwards
product.minus: New tasks don't show up, completed ones don't land in records, and the list is ordered so the nearest task is at the bottom while an event a year ahead sits on top. Task management is effectively broken.

product.title: The weight graph displays upside-down and age is miscalculated
product.minus: After the update the weight graph is drawn backwards by date, the weight on the home screen is wrong, and the pet's age is miscalculated (adds a month). Basic health tracking shows false numbers.

product.title: The paid subscription is expensive and the odd payment flow looks suspicious
product.minus: Around 55-70 euros a year for a simple data log strikes people as outrageous — more than Netflix. On top of that, payment goes through a separate page rather than Google, which feels suspicious.

product.title: Intrusive offer pop-ups that can't be closed
product.minus: On launch a "grab my offer" screen pops up with no close button, and photo-contest banners were added later. Ads and subscription prompts now block the app itself.

product.title: It used to be the most complete health tracker for every kind of pet
product.plus: Before the changes it was the gold-standard health database: medications, vaccines, vet visits, weight, supplies — all in one place, for dogs, cats, reptiles, birds, with the flexibility to fit any species.

product.title: A lifesaver for medication and treatment reminders
product.plus: Users' main love is the reminders: deworming, vaccines, flea drops, scheduled meds. Owners of chronically ill and senior pets call it indispensable.

product.title: Responsive support fixes glitches and restores lost data
product.plus: Despite the botched launch, many note the support team actually responds, fixes bugs and restores lost records — some users raised their rating precisely because of this.

product.title: Glitches and crashes make the app barely usable
product.minus: The app freezes, crashes, spins the loading bone forever and forces phone restarts — users report the same bugs for years and the company fixes nothing.

product.title: The walkers and sitters themselves are nearly always great
product.plus: Set the app aside and the service shines: caring, professional people who send photos and updates, with dogs coming home happy and worn out.

product.title: There is no real support — only an AI bot and a looping recording
product.minus: Reaching a human is impossible: the phone plays a recording sending you back to the app, and the AI chat just gives up when it can't help — which is every time.

product.title: The app auto-assigns a stranger without your approval
product.minus: Even if you only wanted to browse or pick a walker you know, after 24 hours Wag picks a random person for you and hands them your home address.

product.title: A 40% cut leaves walkers earning below minimum wage
product.minus: Wag takes 35-40% on top of the walker's pay, so independent-contractor walkers net almost nothing after taxes and expenses — the Uber/Lyft trap all over again.

product.title: You can't delete your account without handing over a photo ID
product.minus: To delete your account Wag demands a photo of your ID — though none was needed to sign up; users call it data harvesting and locking people in to pad subscriber numbers for investors.

product.title: Old reports and rating prompts resurface for months
product.minus: Every time you open it the app pulls up a walk report from six months or a year ago and forces you to rate it again, blocking access to what you actually need; a bug known for years.

product.title: Sign-up and login simply never go through
product.minus: People can't log in, never get the verification code, get stuck on the terms page or the pet-name field — and codes only come by email, never text.

product.title: Endorsing a friend is turned into a paid app-download funnel
product.minus: Just to endorse a friend you're forced to install the app, hand over your phone and address, then pay to 'upgrade' the endorsement — users call it a scheme for downloads and data harvesting.

product.title: Paid checks and fees just to try to become a walker
product.minus: Anyone hoping to earn must first pay $40-50 for a background check, only to find there are no jobs in their area — or that the app won't even let them register as a walker.

product.title: The price is hidden until you book — and then it climbs
product.minus: You can't see the cost before booding, boarding and daycare run well above rivals, and the price for the same walker can suddenly jump on later days.

product.title: Billing double-charges and fires off false past-due notices
product.minus: Cards get charged twice or asked to pay again the next day at a higher price, payments are declined for no reason with past-due alerts, and refunds are nearly impossible to get.

product.title: Real-time walk tracking is a genuine delight
product.plus: When the app does work, people love watching the walk live like a Lyft ride, seeing when the dog has done its business, and getting daily photo reports.

product.title: A lifesaver at the last minute and during health troubles
product.plus: The service is prized most when a walk is needed urgently, on demand, or when the owner is sick or recovering from surgery — Wag finds someone fast where others say good luck.

product.title: Too few caregivers nearby — almost no one to book
product.minus: In smaller areas there are only a handful of caregivers, requests sit unanswered or get denied, and the person you want can't be booked for months.
